## 9. Pillar 8 — Doctors (declare-vs-actual, and the oracle)

> **Evidence status: [V]** — the two enforcement layers and §9.7's gate vocabulary (`WRITE_EXTERNAL`,
> `NEVER_STORE`, `DRAFT`) were grepped and found in `ala-system`; §9.6's gate was read from
> `business-mind/app/biz/price_gate.py` (`verify_prices`, `check_floors` both confirmed).
> **The `$1,250–1,350` / `~$7,000` figures in §9.6 are [R]** — they come from the gate's own docstring, not
> from a market observation made here.

### 9.1 Definition

A "doctor" is **the system asking an authority outside itself** whether it is healthy, and whether a claim is
true.

**Three arms, and all must exist.** The third is the one added by §11.3's CONTEXT resource class, and it is
the arm this pillar was missing:

```text
ARM 1  drift doctor        declared vs actual, over ARTIFACTS and SCHEMA          (§9.2)
ARM 2  acceptance oracle   the world's own verdict, over OUTPUTS and CLAIMS      (§9.5)
ARM 3  context doctor      headroom, over the AGENT'S OWN WINDOW                 (§9.8)
```

**Arm 3 is the only arm that diagnoses the instrument rather than the work.** Arms 1 and 2 ask whether the
*artifact* is right. Arm 3 asks whether **the thing producing the artifact is still competent** — and it is
the only failure mode in this document that is *silent by construction*, because **a degraded context does not
raise an error, it lowers the quality of the next decision.**

### 9.2 Arm 1 — the drift doctor: declared vs actual

The job is to report and repair the gap between **what is declared** and **what is actually true**.

| Check | Answers |
|---|---|
| artifact doctor | drifted artifacts vs what the current version of a tool reads; `--fix` applies the undecided ones |
| schema verify | does the store still **enforce** what was declared? |
| adversarial probe | does the store **actually refuse** bad writes? |
| security self-check | the policy matrix, the path guard and the redaction layer, self-checked |
| readiness smoke | **which phase** is slow or broken, without guessing |
| backup + verify | the copy is real, and the store is not drifted |

**The distinction that matters most:**

> **`verify` only confirms predicates are *present*. The adversarial probe is the one that proves the
> validators actually *evaluate*.**

Both exist because **a single control at a single layer is a single point of failure.** The two layers:

| Layer | Sees | Cannot be bypassed by |
|---|---|---|
| Application | nested structure, semantics, policy | callers that use the guard |
| Store | **every write, including a manual shell client** | any code, because the server enforces it |

**Both are required.** The application layer understands intent; the store layer cannot be skipped or
forgotten. When you add a control, **say which layer owns it**, and make the other layer's coverage explicit
where it does not reach — **a check that prints its boundaries rather than implying full coverage.**

**Two rules that make a doctor real:**

- **A mitigation is not implemented until a test fails without it.**
- **Run the doctor BEFORE the run, not after.** A drifted store accepts documents the taxonomy forbids, and
  it does so **silently**.

### 9.3 The diagnostic recipe — six rules

```text
1. NEVER SLEEP FOR A GUESSED STARTUP. Poll the health endpoint, ~1s probe timeout, ~1s apart,
   ~20 probes at most. A 2s start costs 2s. A service that never answers is UNREADY, not slow.
2. BOUND EVERY PROBE. Health 1s/attempt; secondary endpoints 2s. A loopback service that cannot
   answer in two seconds is BROKEN, not busy — AND A TIMEOUT IS NEVER SUCCESS.
3. NEVER FILTER WHILE IT RUNS. `2>&1 | grep | head` hides the compile/link lines a slow build needs
   and hides the real failure. Capture to a file; summarize AFTER the command exits.
4. A LAUNCH IS NOT READINESS. Spawn returning proves only that the OS accepted the request.
   Readiness is a successful health response.
5. DIAGNOSE, DO NOT REBUILD. Rebuilding is a separate, measured task with its own gate.
6. TIME EVERY PHASE against one start stamp, and exit nonzero on a substantive failure.
```

### 9.4 Classify before retrying

**A named failure class is the difference between a fix and a retry loop.**

```text
A  health never ready            panic/crash · port held by another process · bind failure ·
                                 bad env var · a backend needed at startup · deadlock
B  health OK, skills endpoint fails   route registration · discovery path · malformed skill file
C  health and skills OK, page fails   page serving
D  page downloads but syntax check fails   REACHABLE YET INERT — read the script
E  all pass and it still feels slow       measure the phases; change ONE thing at a time
```

The measured trap this recipe exists for: **`test result: ok. 139 passed … finished in 0.28s` is *test
execution*, not the compilation and linking before it. [R]** Build time is measured on its own, with the
compiler's own `--timings` to say where the time actually went. **Do not assume the bottleneck.**

### 9.5 Arm 2 — the external acceptance oracle

**Some acceptance conditions cannot be evaluated by the agent that did the work.** The canonical example from
this stack:

```text
WRONG:  the goal is "I cured the villager"
RIGHT:  the goal is `the server console announces "has reached the goal [Zombie Doctor]"`
```

The oracle is **outside** the agent, **un-fakeable** by it, and **its announcement is the evidence**.

```text
agent says done               -> claim
a test the agent chose passes  -> verification on a surface the agent chose
an EXTERNAL ORACLE says so     -> evidence-grade-A evidence
```

**Prefer the oracle whenever one exists.** Where none exists, the honest answer is
`completed_but_unverified` — **not a confident paragraph**. And where an oracle *should* have been used and
was not, **say so on the record.**

**That last clause is measured in the live data. [V]** The recorded evidence rows carry
`source_type: b_operational_record` with the note:

```text
"closed by the turn that carried it out, not by the game"
```

**That note is the pattern working** — the system declining to dress self-verification as evidence-grade-A, and it is
**unanimous, not occasional: `source_type` is `b_operational_record` in all 39 of 39 records, and the note is
identical in all 39. [V]** Write that note. A missing note would have made 39 evidence-grade-B rows read as 39 oracle
confirmations.

**And read the same fact the other way: 0 of 39 evidence records are evidence-grade-A.** The oracle exists, the design
prefers it, and in this corpus **it has never fired.** That is the honest reading, and it is why §9.5's rule is
written as *"where none exists, the honest answer is `completed_but_unverified`"* rather than as a claim that
oracles are in use.

### 9.6 The same shape in the money layer — the price gate

The gate exists because a model quoted **stale prices from search snippets presented as current**: it quoted
`$1,250–1,350` for a product whose real market price was about `$7,000`. [R]

```text
PRICE_RE   = \$ ?([0-9][0-9,]*(?:\.[0-9]{2})?)
evidence   = ALL text actually fetched this turn (tool results + page context), last ~12000 chars

verify_prices(answer, evidence) -> (ok, unsupported[])
    every $ amount in the answer must appear in the evidence, within ±2 integer dollars
    no extracted prices  -> ok (nothing to check)
    EMPTY EVIDENCE       -> fails any price quote

check_floors(answer, floors_cfg) -> violations[]
    per-item floors, e.g. "rtx 5090=7000"; any quoted price below its floor is a violation

on failure: THE ANSWER IS REJECTED, and the model gets ONE corrective round with the evidence reiterated
```

**Three rules from the money layer that generalise:**

```text
1. A dollar is not income until a receipt cites it. A ledger write without evidence is refused.
   Evidence naming a local file that does not exist is refused. MODEL OUTPUT IS NEVER A RECEIPT.
2. An agent cannot verify money and cannot clear a gate. Any caller identifying as an agent is refused
   at BOTH chokepoints. A model cannot certify its own output.
3. Five actions are never granted, under EVERY policy:
      create_account · enter_credentials · move_money · accept_terms · sign_contract
   A task that needs one is NOT silently skipped — it becomes a GATE FOR A HUMAN.
4. Effort is a BUDGET, not a label: under `red` capacity only `green` work is due, and `red` work is
   never delegated to an agent at all.
5. Where a marketplace forbids unattended operation, the agent PREPARES and a human SUBMITS —
   encoded as `autonomy: act` vs `autonomy: propose`.
```

### 9.7 Gates that fail closed

```text
DEFAULT: DENY.    An action absent from the permission map FAILS CLOSED.

READ_ONLY        automatic after source/scope grant
SENSITIVE_READ   explicit scoped grant required; no grants exist by default
DRAFT            no authorization needed to produce; output is NON-PUBLISHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION
WRITE_EXTERNAL   per-action human approval — and NOT IMPLEMENTED
NEVER_STORE      enforced by rejection
```

**`WRITE_EXTERNAL: implemented: false` is the strongest control in the stack.** It is not a gate; it is the
*gate's absence*:

> **Absence is stronger than a gate, because there is no code path to call.**

`DRAFT` is the same idea from the other side: in a phase with no send or publish path, **"draft" is a
structural property, not a label.**

And the classification rule underneath both: **no default-to-`PUBLIC`.** Absent classification is a
validation error, **because the failure direction of a wrong default must be withholding, not disclosure.**

### 9.8 Arm 3 — the context doctor: headroom over the agent's own window

**The only doctor that diagnoses the instrument instead of the work.** Arms 1 and 2 answer *"is the artifact
right?"*; arm 3 answers *"is the thing producing it still competent?"* — and it is the only failure mode in
this document that is silent by construction, because a depleted window raises no error. It lowers the quality
of the next decision.

**[R] GSD Core's shape, adopted because it is the only worked example available.** Per-turn lifecycle hooks
fire at context boundaries, the framework inspects how much of the window is consumed, and it **warns before
the window is exhausted** rather than letting the orchestrator degrade or let an automatic compaction discard
planning state it was relying on. Two parts of that design are worth copying precisely:

```text
1. A PER-TURN SIGNAL, not a one-off measurement. Headroom is checked every turn, because it depletes
   every turn. This is a gauge, not an inspection (§9.3 rule 6: time every phase).
2. MEASURED FROM INSIDE THE RUNTIME. The hook runs in the runtime, so the reading is as close to
   authoritative as available — GSD's own words — rather than inferred from outside.
```

**And the honest labelling GSD applies to itself, which this pillar should inherit: it is a HEURISTIC, not a
guarantee.** A single model call can consume tokens unpredictably. So the correct claim is exactly the weaker
one — **headroom signals warn and steer; they do not certify that something fits.** A doctor that overclaimed
here would be the §9.2 failure in a new costume.

**Four rules for arm 3:**

```text
1. NEVER trust the agent's own report of its headroom. Per §9.6 rule 2, an agent cannot certify itself —
   the reading must come from the runtime, not from the model describing itself.
2. A CONTEXT BUDGET IS DECLARED, NOT ASSUMED. A delegation that does not state how much window the worker
   may carry has an unbounded RESOURCES field (§5.2) — the same defect as a missing STOP.
3. THE COORDINATOR IS NOT EXEMPT. A long orchestration silently consumes its own window, and the failure it
   produces is a quietly worse decision, not a crash.
4. CROSSING THE BUDGET IS `completed_but_unverified`, NOT A SILENT CONTINUATION. If work proceeds past the
   point where the window can be trusted, the result is unverified by construction and must be labelled so
   (§8.5).
```

**Note what this arm does NOT do: it does not measure correctness.** A context doctor reports that the
instrument is fresh. **A fresh instrument still needs arms 1 and 2**, and a worker with an empty window and
no oracle is exactly as unverified as one with a full window. **Three arms are required because they fail
independently.**

### 9.9 Adopt: OpenTelemetry + SLOs + the reconciliation loop + DORA

- **OpenTelemetry** — traces · metrics · logs. One export path for the event ledger; the three signals map
  onto events, counters, and the raw stream. **Adopt the wire format, not the collector** (see §10.4).
- **SLOs + error budgets** — makes "healthy" a number with a consequence rather than an adjective.
- **Kubernetes readiness/liveness probes + the reconciliation loop** — readiness polling instead of sleeping,
  and declare-vs-actual drift repair, are both already standardized versions of this pillar's two arms.
- **DORA metrics** — build / test / runtime / throughput measured **separately**, never one score.
- **OpenSSF Scorecard** — an external health oracle for a repository, and therefore a natural **evidence-grade-C**
  corroboration source for §7.

The S0-S4 stage gates exist nowhere in this file except as a NAME. **This is rule 31's defect applied to a SECTION reference rather than a file path - and CHECK 1 cannot catch it, because CHECK 1 tests PATHS.** A reference-integrity check over every `§N.M` reference in this file (27 sections, 158 subsections) returns exactly ONE dangling reference: this one. **A source row registering content that does not exist is worse than an uncited claim, because it reads as provenance.**

### 10.2 The measurement register

Every number in this file, with the artifact it was measured from.

**And what counts as a number, because otherwise the check cannot be run.** RE-RUN 2026-09-20, and the re-run is the finding. As written, CHECK 2 returns **259 distinct unregistered prose numbers**. Rewritten with an explicit exclusion rule - list markers, dates, version strings, section references, rule numbers, record ids, subsection ordinals, code fences - **it returns MORE, not fewer: 1,540 tokens, 260 distinct**, because the classifier still cannot separate a heading ordinal from a measurement. **Two refinements, two different answers, and neither is a defect count - so the check is NOT DECIDABLE and no further refinement makes it so**, because whether a number is worth registering is a judgement about relevance, not a property of its shape. That is the same limit CHECK 1 carries (48 candidates for 1 real defect) and the reason three passes found different things (11.8). **The limit is recorded here rather than tuned again.** What the check CAN decide mechanically is whether a number already cited as evidence appears in this table - and that is what the table is for. **EXCLUDED from the count: dates, version strings, section references, rule numbers, record ids, anything inside a code fence, and this file's own line and byte counts (which change on every merge and so can never be registered).** Under that rule the finding is not that prose carries strays - it is that **the measurements introduced by sections 19-26 were never registered at all.** They are, below. **A number with no entry here is a defect

### 10.4 The adoption rule

> **Adopt the standard's *shape*, not its running service.**

**Worked example, because this rule has now been tested by a real candidate.** **[R] GSD Core** (MIT, §14)
comes as `npx @opengsd/gsd-core@latest`, and its own README states the installer is **required** — "do not
copy files from `agents/` or `commands/` directly." By this rule that makes it **a service, not a standard**:
it writes into the repo, registers runtime hooks, and injects into the trusted instruction channel that §14's
supply-chain gate governs. **So this document adopts its phase-loop shape, its context-budget idea and its
milestone/phase split — and adopts none of its installer, its file layout, or its command namespace.**

The distinction is not pedantry, and GSD's own documentation supplies the reason: it is **a process layer, not
a governance layer.** It has no authority plane, no evidence tiers, no provenance, no retirement taxonomy, and
its Verify step is a walkthrough that produces fix plans. **This document's Verify demands an external oracle
(§9.5) and a recomputed claim strength (§7.3). Those are not the same operation, and the weaker one must never
be substituted for the stronger.**

**The one place the two are genuinely incompatible, stated as a rule:**

> **A `CONTEXT.md` is a derived view, never a canonical decision record.**

GSD's Discuss step captures implementation decisions into a `CONTEXT.md` that planner, executor and verifier
all read. That is good *process* and this document wants it. But under §2.6 **a generated summary is never the
canonical record**, and under §5.4 a decision carries `authority`, citations and an issuing authority. **So if
this stack ever writes a CONTEXT.md, it must be labelled a derived view with its inputs cited — because a
conversational record that later reads as the authority for an action is exactly the "never infer authority
from proximity" failure of §4.7 rule 1, wearing a filename.**

The standing preference across this stack is **no database**: the stores are files, deliberately. A season
store is portable object files; a ledger is append-only JSONL. A query/index layer is optional and must be
justified against the fact that **a replay already answers the questions being asked**, and that the mapping
to an indexed store exists but is imported by nothing.

**Any answer that adds a service must justify it against that.** Adding a wire format is free; adding a
collector is a service.

The same rule from the other direction: a local store is bound to loopback **in code, not only in
configuration**, so the local-first decision cannot be lost by editing a config file; a remote/cloud
connection string is refused outright; and the single override is named and audited.

## 11. The gate chain — and how this file was run through it

### 11.1 The gate

A sequence that ends in a claim about a built artifact is a **gate**, not a checklist.

```bash
run the tests; STATUS=$?
if [ "$STATUS" -ne 0 ]; then show the failure context; exit "$STATUS"; fi
build; STATUS=$?
if [ "$STATUS" -ne 0 ]; then show the failure context; exit "$STATUS"; fi
only now: start, probe, and assert against the NEW artifact
```

**Two rules make it real:**

- **A failed build must never fall through to a probe of the old binary.** A smoke test that passes against
  yesterday's executable is **worse than no test, because it is evidence pointing the wrong way.**
- **A stale artifact is not a fix.** Confirm the running process is the thing you built — mtime, a route only
  the new build has, a version string — before reporting that a change works. When a process will not start on
  a new build, **suspect a held file handle or a lost port race before suspecting the code.**

### 11.2 The campaign's own gate chain

```text
release tests -> release build -> daemon launch -> health/readiness
   -> skills endpoint -> page fetch -> page script validation -> acceptance
```

Readiness is **polled**, never slept for. **A fixed startup sleep is not a readiness contract.**

**Do not filter either command while it runs.** Filtering is allowed **after** the raw log exists.

### 11.3 Resource classes — reasoning parallel, spending serial

```text
CHEAP       planning / parsing / local reasoning                        — many
MEDIUM      source inspection / light checks / targeted tests           — fewer
HEAVY       build / test / linker / model inference                     — a controlled number
EXCLUSIVE   final integration / shared-state mutation                   — holds an explicit lock

CONTEXT     the FIFTH class, and the one this document was missing:
            the worker's own prompt window is a BUDGET, not a container.
            A worker holding 180k of accumulated history is a DEGRADED worker,
            and the degradation is silent — the model keeps answering.
```

**Debt owed to GSD Core ([R], §14).** The four classes above are budgets of *compute*. They were missing the
resource that actually runs out first. GSD declares a per-skill effort (`effort: max` for orchestration,
`effort: low` for status), hands each executor **a fresh window loaded with exactly what its task needs and
nothing more**, and treats *"does the plan fit a fresh context window"* as a **gate that runs before
execution.** The reason it matters is a failure mode this document did not otherwise name: quality degrades
as a window fills, **and the model does not fail loudly — it keeps answering.**

**This stack already practises the discipline without having written it down. [V]** The live ledger contains

```text
ticket.skip   "cold start: 178 line(s) of history kept out of the queue"
```

**History was deliberately withheld from a worker to protect its budget.** That is a context budget being spent
by hand, 20 times, in one corpus — **a control that exists as behaviour and not as doctrine, which is the exact
defect §6.4's decoration-provenance rule is about.** Writing it down is what makes it checkable.

**Two consequences to add to the resource rules below:**

1. **A worker's context is declared, not assumed.** A delegation that does not say how much context the worker
   may carry has an unbounded RESOURCES field (§5.2) — the same defect as a missing STOP.
2. **The coordinator's own window is a depleting resource.** §11.3 says "preserve enough machine for the
   coordinator"; it must equally say *preserve enough window for it*, because **a long orchestration silently
   consumes its own context**, and the failure it produces is not a crash but a quietly worse decision.

**Reasoning is cheap and parallel; spending is scarce and serial.** One heavy build, one release gate, one
world mutation, one model budget at a time per machine, **unless the experiment *is* the concurrency.**

**Eight reasoning workers do not imply eight builds.** Defaults: one coordinator, 2–3 read-only investigation
subagents in parallel, **one active build-heavy experiment at a time**, separate worktrees only when
simultaneous edits truly help, and one canonical build cache. **A parallelism ceiling is a ceiling, not a
quota.**

**Give each worker that edits code its own worktree** — **a shared tree turns two correct changes into one
corrupt one.** The coordinator owns the canonical baseline: **a duplicated baseline is the most expensive way
to be wrong twice.** Preserve enough machine for the coordinator and the user. **An expensive operation must
be idempotent or keyed by task state so a retry cannot start a duplicate build.**

### 11.4 Disagreement

```text
independent investigation -> evidence exchange -> claim-by-claim challenge
   -> an experiment where the claim needs one -> resolution
```

Every disputed claim ends as one of:

```text
resolved by evidence · resolved by new measurement · unresolved · rejected as unsupported
```

**Never silently convert disagreement into certainty.** **A claim nobody could measure stays unresolved on
paper.** **A worker's report is input to a decision, never the decision.**

### 11.5 Roles and outputs

**Coordinator** decomposes, writes the envelopes, owns the baseline, ranks hypotheses by measured impact then
confidence then reversibility, and lands the result. **Worker** answers its question and returns evidence.
**Reviewer** checks that the claimed bottleneck was measured, that the patch does not change semantics, and
that the gain justifies the maintenance.

A worker returns one of: `FINDING / EVIDENCE / HYPOTHESIS / EXPERIMENT / RISK / DECISION`.

**Reject:**

```text
"should be faster"        -> unmeasured
"looks fixed"             -> unverified
"tests pass"              -> correctness is not performance
"the build completed"     -> not that the bottleneck moved
any claim about a running system you did not read from it
```

**Strength is recomputed, never asserted.** **Prefer `inconclusive` to a forced success story.**

### 11.6 Grounding — what a claim is allowed to describe

An observation is evidence about **what produced it**, never about everything nearby.

```text
A screenshot from the player's client   is evidence about WHAT THE PLAYER CAN SEE.
                                        It is NOT the body's position, inventory, or surroundings.
A view derived from the body's own data is evidence about WHAT THE BODY CAN REACH, and may not claim
                                        lighting, textures, or another client's frame.
```

**Label the perspective on every observation, and make sure no later step silently drops the label — a
qualifier living inside prose is a qualifier that gets lost.**

### 11.7 This file, run through that chain

The chain above is a general one. Applied to **a document** rather than a binary, the mapping is:

```text
tests   = mechanical checks: does every cited path exist? is every number registered?
          is every marked claim marked correctly?
build   = self-containment: can a reader act with no other file?
probe   = an actual reader with only this file, asked to do a task from it.
```

**Result of the documented run: twelve defects found across three passes, all fixed in this document.**
**Pass 2 found five of them inside pass 1's own corrections. Pass 3 found four more — two of which were in
the document's own evidence *rules* rather than its facts (see §11.8).** Each later pass found the previous
pass's blind spot, which is the strongest available argument for why a pass exists at all — **and also the
reason the passes eventually stop being worth running: pass 2 found 5, pass 3 found 4, and both were working
on material the author had already declared clean.**

```text
CHECK 1  does every cited path exist in the supplied material?
  [FAIL] `cua_mc_bot/README.md` — wrong path; the file is at the bundle root, `cua-mc-bot/README.md`
  [FAIL] `.scratch/seasons/spec.md` — cited as an existing artifact; IT DOES NOT EXIST. Only `map.md`
         and `issues/` are present. It is the map's *destination condition* — a file to be produced —
         and citing it as existing is exactly the defect rule 31 names.
  [FAIL] a stray label prefix in a reading-order entry

**What the second pass changes about the first pass's result.** The first pass's failures were all
**citation discipline** (§11.7's own prediction, in §13.3). The second pass's failures were all
**epistemic**: a right number with a wrong source, a real small effect written up as a large one, half a
claim that could not be checked, and two system findings that were actually author misreadings.

> **So the first pass's prediction was wrong, and instructively so. Citation defects are visible to the
> author; magnitude and provenance defects are not, because the author already believes the number.**
>
> **Nothing found in either pass required reading the system. Every one of the eleven was found by opening the
> artifact and counting instead of recalling.**

**Honest limit on this audit:** it was run by the same agent that wrote the file, **which is the failure mode
this whole stack exists to prevent** — self-verification recorded as external verification. **The three passes
make this vivid rather than theoretical: pass 2 found five defects and pass 3 found four, and every one of them
was in a previous pass's own work.** Pass 3 found *fewer*, and that is **not** evidence the document is clean —
it is evidence that the remaining defects are in the author's blind spots, which is where a third pass by the
same author cannot reach. **The trend (3 → 5 → 4) is a deceleration curve, not a convergence.**

What is reproducible and what is not:

```text
scripted and reproducible    checks 1, 2, 3, 8, 9, 11  — greps, line counts, json.loads over the artifacts.
                                                          Cheapest to re-run; a reader with the artifacts can
                                                          confirm or refute every one of them.
NOT reproducible by re-running   the [V]/[R]/[A] marker assignments, and checks 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 12, which are
                                 JUDGEMENTS BY THE AUTHOR. Checks 10 and 12 were already shown wrong.
```

**Per §9.6 rule 2 and §7.2's evidence ladder, this file cannot clear its own gate — it can only report that it
tried, and it must report that the attempt was self-administered.** By §7.2's tiers, the mechanical checks are
**evidence grade B** (a contemporaneous operational record — the commands are written down and re-runnable) and the
judgement checks are **evidence grade D** (self-report). **Not one claim in this audit is evidence grade A**, because no oracle
outside the author was consulted. **An independent reader re-running checks 1–3, 8, 9 and 11 is the oracle, and
is the single highest-value thing anyone can do with this document.**

### 11.8 Third pass — the judgement checks, converted into scripted ones

Checks 4–7, 10 and 12 were labelled *author judgement* in the second pass, which made them
**unreproducible** — the weakest tier in a document that grades evidence. The third pass attacked that directly:
**each one was replaced with a command whose output decides it.** A judgement you can re-run is no longer a
judgement, and that is the only reason the third pass is worth anything.

```text
was judged by reading        now decided by
─────────────────────────    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
CHECK 4  self-containment    extract every cited path; find undefined identifiers and unexpanded terms
CHECK 5  open vs resolved    grep the body for presuppositions of each of the twelve decisions in §12.1
CHECK 6  uncertainty         count [V]/[R]/[A]/[O] per section; flag sections with ZERO
CHECK 7  dead paths          scripted in pass 1 — re-run
CHECK 10 verifiable half     extract each quoted identifier and grep it against the sources
CHECK 12 own taxonomy        does each defect claim carry a gain/regression/residual/retained label?
```

**Result: four more defects, and two of them are the most consequential in the file.**

```text
CHECK 13  §10.1 marked §8 [R] on the grounds that its source was "not present in the supplied bundles".
          TRUE as stated — and USELESS, because the source is a session skill that loads and reads fine.
          The third pass LOADED IT and verified §8 against it: all 15 reason terms, the 7 states, the 9
          stages, the 10 rules, the record JSON and the closing design principle match verbatim.
  [FAIL] the marker answered the wrong question — "is this file in the bundle?" rather than "can this
         source be read?" — and 219 lines of pillar were marked testimony on a test that never applied.
  FIX    §8 promoted to [V], tightly scoped: [V] for the skill's own content, [R] for the four papers
         it cites, which were still not read and which the skill itself calls "architectural synthesis".

CHECK 14  THE MARKER PROMISE WAS FALSE. The preamble asserted that "every factual claim in this file
         carries one of these markers". Counted per section: §2 (182 lines), §7 (239), §8 (219), §14, §15,
         §16 and §17 carry ZERO markers, while §10 carries 84. So 640+ lines of pillar doctrine sat under
         a promise the document did not keep — and a reader routed to a pillar by §0's own "find your
         pillar" instruction would never see a marker at all.
  [FAIL] the epistemic apparatus was concentrated in ONE section (the apparatus, §10) while the seven
         pillars — where the substance lives — carried none.
  FIX    the preamble now states the actual convention (markers apply to claims about supplied artifacts;
         doctrine is unmarked), carries a per-pillar evidence table, and **every pillar now opens with an

CHECK 15  §12.1 lists twelve OPEN decisions. The body presupposes SIX of them as settled. A document whose
         central honesty claim is "do not resolve these by assumption" had resolved half of them silently
         — including the two that matter most, 03 and 08. **Full audit: §12.5.**

CHECK 16  §7's whole vocabulary was grepped against the sources and found — except `b_operational_record`,
         which exists ONLY as a data value in the ledger and in NO source file. So §7.2's evidence-grade-B label is a

CHECK 17  §4.3's claims were verified at line level: `ALL_OPS` (governor.py:38), `OBSERVING_OPS` (line 43),

**Why the third pass found what the first two could not.** The first pass checked *paths*. The second pass
checked *numbers*. Neither checked **what the numbers were attached to, or whether the document was applying
its own evidence rules to itself**. Both new findings are of that kind:

> **The document was grading its evidence by a standard it had not applied to its own structure.**

**And the honest limit survives all three passes.** This is still the same agent. The compensating control is
not more self-auditing — it is that **checks 13–17 are now commands with reproducible output**, and a stranger
with the artifacts can refute every one without trusting the author. **That is the upgrade: not more
confidence, but more refutability.**

## 12. Open questions — do not resolve these by assumption

### 12.1 The twelve live decision tickets

Each is a *decision*, not a slice of work. The options are stated so an open question can be recognized
without opening a tracker.

```text
01  IS THE CANONICAL SEASON THE OBJECT-FILE TREE, JSONL, OR BOTH AT DIFFERENT RESOLUTIONS?
    A  tree is canonical          — one file per object; git sees a diff per record.
                                    Cost: abandons the replay discipline for a second one.
    B  JSONL canonical, tree is a generated mirror
                                    Cost: two representations to keep in step.
    C  both at different resolutions — live records append as JSONL; the CLOSED season is sealed
                                    as the tree once, at archival. Cost: the live/sealed boundary
                                    must be exact.
    Constraint: the validator reads exactly ONE path, so C is the shape the reader already supports.
    Sub-question that must be answered either way: WHAT IS THE ARTIFACT AN AUDITOR READS? A replay of
    a log and a directory of files are both auditable, but only one can be the answer when they disagree.

02  WHAT OPENS AND CLOSES A SEASON, AND ON WHOSE CLOCK?
    wall clock · world clock · session lifetime · operator act · drained policy (auto-close when empty)
    Constraint: there are TWO bodies with REVERSED clocks, so "the body's clock" is not one value.
    Either a season is scoped to the daemon (one clock of record, the pair's halves are its contents)
    or the pair has two seasons, which contradicts one authority plane.
    Also to settle: is the day/night phase the season's inner rhythm or orthogonal to it?
    And: what happens to a season that outlives a restart? A season that closes on every restart is a
    season per hour.

03  WHAT IS GOVERNOR BASE, AND WHERE DOES ITS VERSION COME FROM?      <- most likely to be got wrong cheaply
    A  derived snapshot — a VIEW of the code's policy, serialised and dated whenever it changes;
                          version is a CONTENT HASH. One source of truth; reconstructable from code state.
    B  authored document — a new store where each version is a deliberate act, with effective_at and
                          change_control. Cost: the code then has to AGREE with it (two sources of truth).
    C  both — authored versions plus a snapshot at the same moment, with the hash recording drift
                          between what was declared and what the code does.
    THE TRAP: the precedence table puts the current Governor Base ABOVE contracts, tickets and world
    state. So if Governor Base and the code's capability check disagree, the spec says the Governor
    wins AND the agent's actual behaviour is decided by code. A's content hash is the only variant whose
    version is VERIFIABLE without a second declaration.

04  WHERE IS THE GOVERNOR DECISION ENFORCED, AND WHAT DOES A DENY DO TO A TURN?
    Where:  (a) a second independent check in front of the existing one — defence in depth, version
                stamped on every ledger line
            (b) the existing check rewritten to consult Governor Base — one authority, one place wrong
            (c) an evaluation that is RECORDED but does not gate — an audit log wearing a governor's name
    DENY:   (i) fail the turn, leaving the goal open for another attempt
            (ii) fall back to another action the model proposed
            (iii) escalate into a ticket — "this needed an authority that does not exist"
    A precedent worth reading first is a check that refuses movement when the work's origin names nobody
    who asked for it, and whose refusal message TELLS THE AGENT HOW TO FIX IT.

05  HOW DOES HISTORICAL CONTEXT REACH THE PLANNER WITHOUT BECOMING AUTHORITY?
    By a capability-gated, audited, model-schema-visible read action  -> history becomes a first-class
                                                                        auditable act
    By a cheap status view                                        -> no new capability; prompt text and
                                                                     truncation rules already exist
    By a SKILL in the library                                      -> how DOCTRINE reaches the agent;
                                                                     the agent decides when to look
    The decision is which one the FACTS travel by — and whether the doctrine travels by the third
    regardless. Two bounds from the spec: a read must not be expressible as an authorization anywhere,
    and if a season is cited while planning, THE CITATION SHOULD BE VISIBLE ON THE TURN.

06  WHICH SEASON RECORDS DOES THE LOOP WRITE LIVE, AND WHICH ARE DERIVED AT CLOSING?
    live       the campaign opened, the contract authorised, the ticket filed, the evidence arrived,
               the ticket closed, the goal blocked, the mode turned over, a person spoke
    at CLOSING outcomes{completed,partial,failed,deferred}, lessons[], the summary, and the season's
               own verdict on itself
    ambiguous  DECISIONS. "We chose route B because of last season's lesson" is a decision with
               provenance and is worth having on the record — but one per turn is a model pass per turn,
               and none means the historical layer cannot explain WHY a campaign went as it did.
    The answer must also say WHO DERIVES: a model pass at CLOSING (expensive, one pass, re-runnable) or
    pure code over the records (a summary that is arithmetic rather than prose — counts, tiers,
    failures, durations). Fabricating outcomes is forbidden, so whatever derives them must be able to
    point at the records it derived them from.

07  WHAT DOES "ARCHIVED IS IMMUTABLE" MEAN, AND HOW DOES A CORRECTION GET ATTACHED?
    A  convention only — a correction is another record whose target names the record it corrects.
                          Cost: nothing enforces it; a future module could edit a line.
    B  sealed artifact — archival writes the season out as one immutable artifact with a manifest,
                          a version, a member allowlist and a checksummed round trip; corrections
                          accumulate BESIDE the seal, never inside it.
    C  code-level refusal — a status check inside the store refuses any write to an archived season,
                          with corrections going through an explicit API that requires an authority record.
    Sub-question 1: is a correction's target a RECORD ID or a FIELD PATH? Correcting a record is easy to
    make safe; correcting a FIELD means the reader must replay corrections to know what a fact is, which
    is a second replay on top of last-write-wins.
    Sub-question 2: WHO AUTHORISES a correction. That makes the correction itself a governed act.

08  EXTEND THE EXISTING TICKET, OR WRITE A SEPARATE SEASON TICKET?
    Missing from the ticket that already exists: season_id, campaign_id, governor_base_version,
    authorization_id, and an explicit provenance block (today it is implied by the actor events,
    source and parent contract).
    Extend   — one object; cost: the writer grows fields that only exist once a season does, and every
               existing line replays with them absent.
    Separate — cost: TWO objects for one unit of work, two lifecycles to keep in step, and a real risk
               that a reader treats one as canonical.
    Every other place here chose ONE record over two — the goal IS the ticket's legacy id rather than a
    parallel goal record.
    Also: does authorization_id cite the contract's own authority record? That only works because a
    ticket is filed under a contract, and a ticket filed outside one has nothing to cite. Whether an
    uncited ticket is legal is part of this decision.
    [V] Decisive fact: a stamped governor_base_version is checked by NOTHING until declared on the reader
    side too — so each added field is a two-language change or it is decoration.

09  IS A CAMPAIGN THE EXISTING QUEUE TREE, A NEW OBJECT THAT GROUPS CONTRACTS, OR A HORIZON BUNDLE?
    A  the root queue item                — cheapest; but a campaign then cannot exist before its first
                                            item, cannot outlive the queue, and carries none of the
                                            coordinating object's fields
    B  a new record whose contracts are the authorised contracts and whose work is the queue items
       filed under them                   — matches the spec; adds one object and a join
    C  a horizon bundle given an id and a status
                                          — reuses the one durable campaign artifact that already
                                            survives a restart; costs a dependency on the archive layer
                                            for something that may not need to be a file
    Sub-questions: does a campaign end when its queue drains, when its contracts complete, or when a
    person says so? Does a child-campaign relation mean anything, given the queue already nests? And
    where does a day/night campaign fit, since a campaign spanning both halves is the normal case?
    A PRECEDENT WORTH USING: **[R] GSD Core splits the same space into MILESTONE and PHASE**, and the
    distinction is the one this decision is groping for. A milestone is a VERSION CYCLE — a name, a version
    number, and the requirements it must deliver, with boundaries drawn at product boundaries. A phase is
    ONE BOUNDED LOOP UNIT — a goal and the plans that implement it, with boundaries drawn at "the limits of
    what can be safely executed in one loop." Its explicit test for phase scope is directly usable here:
     the goal fits in ONE sentence that is neither trivially small nor suspiciously broad;
     the research needed is bounded and does not depend on other phases finishing first;
     execution splits into a HANDFUL of non-overlapping plans, not dozens;
     and there is a testable definition of done "a verifier can check without reading the entire codebase."
    **If option B is chosen, this is the strongest available argument that a campaign is not the same object
    as its horizon bundle — a campaign is a version-like increment with requirements, while the horizon
    bundle is one bounded unit of work. Those are different scopes, and option C conflates them.**

10  WHAT IS THE QUERY SURFACE FOR SEASONS, AND IS AN INDEXED STORE PART OF IT?
    A  files + code query functions, exposed as endpoints                 — the collection map stays
                                                                            documentation
    B  optional exporter — the above plus a push to an indexed store when configured; no service in the
       loop, an index available if someone wants to query across seasons in a way files make slow
    C  a real store-backed query layer                                    — the collections become the
                                                                            query layer
    Second half, which no option settles: WHAT MAKES A PRECEDENT RELEVANT? A keyword/substring match,
    a structured filter (objective equality, evidence tier, failure status), or a candidate list the
    model reads and judges? The applicability test wants the third eventually; the cost and failure
    modes differ enormously. Note that adding a database is the single largest architectural change any
    answer here can smuggle in — see §10.4.

11  WHAT DO SEASONS AND THE GOVERNOR VERSION LOOK LIKE TO A PERSON?
    Candidates for the panel: season name + status + how far into its boundary it is; the campaign it is
    on and its outcome so far; the GOVERNOR VERSION and the date it changed; the last lesson; and — the
    one the precedence table implies a reader will need — WHAT HISTORY WAS CONSULTED AND NOT GRANTED,
    if the planner cites one.
    Where: a terminal panel, a web panel, or both. And what does a CLOSED season look like — archived
    and read-only is a very different panel, and possibly an export rather than a view.
    A live dashboard is exactly the wrong shape: the panel should say WHICH PLAN THE AGENT IS CURRENTLY
    ALLOWED TO MAKE, not tick.

12  WHO DERIVES RESUME CLAIMS FROM VERIFIED SEASON RECORDS, AND WHERE DO THOSE CLAIMS LIVE?
    Both halves already exist in different places: a `ResumeEvidence` schema with claim id, capability,
    evidence[], confidence, permitted/forbidden language, measurable outcomes and `allowed_strength`,
    which is IMPORTED BY NOTHING; and a separate evidence engine whose whole business is resume claims.
    So: does the daemon emit resume records per verified capability — with `allowed_strength` capped by
    the strongest evidence tier actually attached — or does the evidence engine derive them from season
    files when it needs them?
    And: WHAT COUNTS AS A MEASURED OUTCOME HERE? "The game granted this advancement", "the goal
    verified", "the ticket closed with evidence-grade-A evidence" are countable and checkable — unusually good
    material for a claim — and manufacturing one is forbidden, so the mapping from those records to a
    capability string has to be a STATED RULE rather than a generated sentence.
    This is the one place the feature could create a FALSE STATEMENT about a person or an agent, so the
    rule that caps the claim by the evidence should live WHERE THE CLAIM IS MADE.
```

### 12.2 The unresolved fog

In scope, not yet sharp enough to decide, and deliberately not pre-sliced — one patch may graduate into
several questions, or none:

```text
lesson applicability         what a "current conditions" test looks like before a lesson may influence a plan
search semantics             what makes a precedent relevant, and how much history fits in one prompt
the correction flow          who notices a wrong record, what they see, and how a correction is attached
season rollover across an outage   close late, close empty, or refuse to close
lessons -> instructions      a lesson that becomes a durable INSTRUCTION is a different artifact
                             from history; whether that is in scope is not yet clear
participants and children    two bodies with reversed clocks — WHOSE season is a campaign both worked?
round-trip fidelity          what a re-imported record must preserve (ids, tiers, actor events)
```

**Fog versus ticket** — the test is whether the question can be stated precisely *now*, not whether it can be
answered now:

```text
TICKET when the question is already sharp, even if blocked.
FOG    when it cannot yet be phrased that sharply.
```

### 12.3 Out of scope — closed, never graduates

```text
the dated institutional snapshot as a reference Season   (authoring it is a data exercise; the
                                                          orchestration lessons are already doctrine)
legal, tax, lobbying, campaign-finance and appropriation machinery   (no money and no statutes here)
multi-principal governance                               (one daemon, one body, one authority plane)
replacing the existing capability model                  (a rewrite of the capability vocabulary is past
                                                          the destination)
a resume renderer                                        (that belongs to the evidence engine)
an indexed store as the Season index                     (its trigger is named, not ruled out on principle)
```

### 12.4 The destination, quoted

> **A settled, implementable spec — every decision ticket above resolved, and an implementer can build it in
> the writer plus the reader without deciding anything else.**
>
> The shape of the thing, in one line: **Governor Base governs what may happen; Seasons remember what
> happened; history never grants authority.**

And the evidence that the destination is the right one — **[V] measured in the live store, not argued:**

```text
goals started 464      goals done 37      goals blocked 134
tickets filed 580      tickets open 227   tickets closed 3          (of 230 governor ticket records)
contracts filed 468    evidence records 39                     evidence-grade-A evidence 0
seasons 0              resume records 0
the first campaign is 468 contracts ago
```

**The flat plane is not short of history. It is short of a parent.** 468 Contracts were opened, most by
ordinary turns, each one replacing the last because the board takes the newest as current — which is §6.3
rule 4, and it is the single defect that most of this document's structure exists to prevent. A Season gives
those 468 Contracts **one bounded parent** instead of 468 rivals for the slot, and the closure chain then has
somewhere to deposit its verdict. **That is what "give the flat plane a bounded parent" means, and it is the
second half of the conclusion below — arrived at by counting rather than by arguing.**

And the conclusion that reframes the whole feature, measured rather than argued:

> **The work is not "build a history layer". It is: give the flat plane a *bounded parent*, give the
> authority plane a *version*, and give history a *read path that cannot authorize*. Everything else is
> either already here under another name or is a mapping exercise that follows from those three.**

### 12.5 Presupposition audit — which of the twelve the body silently settles

**§12 says "do not resolve these by assumption." Six of the twelve are resolved by assumption in the body
anyway — not by argument, but by the schemas and layouts being written out as though settled.** Found by
grepping the body for each decision rather than by re-reading it (§11.8 CHECK 15).

| # | Where the body presupposes it | What it silently picks | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|---|
| **03** | `Verdict{… governor_version: int }` (§4.3); `governance{governor_base_version, authorization_id}` (§6.2); `"governor_base_version": 12` (§8.7) | an **integer** version — i.e. option **B, authored** | **The sharpest contradiction in this file.** Option 03A argues the version must be a **content hash** because that is *"the only variant whose version is VERIFIABLE without a second declaration"*, and §4.11 endorses exactly that standard. **An `int` cannot be a hash.** Both sources (`governor.py:52`, `seasons.md:489`) also type it `int`. So choosing A means changing a field in two languages — which §6.4 says is a two-language change **or it is decoration**. **Either A must be restated as "int version PLUS a content hash alongside", or A is ruled out. As written it is not implementable against the schemas this document reproduces.** |
| **08** | `governance { governor_base_version, authorization_id }` in §6.2's ticket object | **Extend** the existing ticket | 08 lists these as *missing* fields to be added by Extend or relocated by Separate. §6.2 already contains them, so the schema silently answers **Extend**. The separate-record option is then never represented anywhere. |
| **01** | `Portable object-file layout` + the full `seasons/` tree (§2.3) | the **tree is canonical** (option A) | 01 asks whether the tree, JSONL, or both is canonical, and 01's own constraint notes *"the validator reads exactly ONE path"*. §2.3 writes out the tree as **the** layout without naming which resolution is canonical. Note the retirement skill's §26 does the same — so the presupposition is inherited, not invented. |
| **02** | `season.json` → `time{started_at,ended_at,timezone:UTC}` (§2.3) | a **wall clock** | 02 lists five candidates (wall · world · session · operator act · drained policy) and warns that **two bodies have reversed clocks**. Fixed `started_at`/`ended_at` fields pick wall clock. The `DRAFT→ACTIVE→CLOSING→ARCHIVED` lifecycle (§2.2) separately implies a *declared* close — option "operator act" — so §2 presupposes two different answers to 02. |
| **07** | *"The correction is itself a governed act"* + `authorized_by` (§2.5) | **an authority record authorises corrections** | 07's sub-question 2 asks *"WHO AUTHORISES a correction"* and is listed as open. §2.5 asserts the answer as settled, and its example supplies `"authorized_by": "governor_base_authorization_77"`. (The skill's own §21 uses the weaker `"authorized_by": "controller"` — so §2.5 states a *stronger* position than its source.) |
| **12** | §7 in full — 239 lines of `computeSupportLevel`, the policy table, the 8 views | the **evidence engine** derives resume claims | 12 asks whether the daemon emits resume records or the evidence engine derives them from season files. §7 describes **only** the evidence-engine half and never mentions the daemon-side `ResumeEvidence` schema that 12 says exists and is *"imported by nothing"*. The half that makes it a *daemon* decision is absent from the pillar. |

**Two more that are tensions rather than resolutions — flagged, not resolved:**

```text
10  §10.4 states "the standing preference across this stack is NO DATABASE". The retirement skill §25
    recommends MongoDB collections and indexes — which is 10's option B — so a source this document
    cites as authority takes a position the document presents as open. Neither is wrong; the document
    should say the skill leans B and §10.4 leans A.

05  §2.7 step 5 says "search Seasons for relevant precedent" and §2.8 says "Read tools confer nothing".
    That leans toward 05's first option (a capability-gated read action) without saying so. The other
    two options — a cheap status view, a skill — are not represented in the planner sequence.
```

**What to do with this section.** These are **not** claimed as defects to fix by deleting the schemas. A
schema has to be written somehow, and writing it settles something for the duration of the writing. The
requirement is the one §4.5 already imposes on the 2000 snapshot: **separate the declaration from the
decision that produced it.** So each row above is an instruction to add **one line at the point of the
schema** naming which decision it presupposes — which is what §2–§9's new evidence-status headers now do.

**ADDED 2026-09-20 - §12.5 has now been bypassed by a LATER silent settlement, which is the exact defect it exists to catch.** Re-grepping the body for each of the twelve decisions finds **new presupposition sites in §19-§26 for eight of the twelve**, and §12.5's table (written before §19 existed) carries none of them. The one that matters is **decision 03, now settled TWICE IN OPPOSITE DIRECTIONS**: §21.3's Action Envelope and §21.6's assertion bind approval to `policy_hash` - option **A, a content hash** - while §4.3, §6.2 and §8.7 still type `governor_base_version` as an **int**, option B. §12.5's own row said *either A must be restated as an int version PLUS a content hash alongside, or A is ruled out*; §21 performs that restatement and **§12.5 never learns of it**. **A list of open questions and a body of assertions cannot be kept consistent by intention - 12.5 proved that once, and has now been demonstrated by its own later sections.**

**And the meta-finding, which is the one worth keeping.** §12 was written as a list of questions. The body
was written as answers. **Nobody reconciled them, and the failure was invisible to two full passes of
re-reading** — it took a grep per decision, run in pass 3 after pass 2 had already declared the document clean. **A list of open questions and a body of assertions cannot be kept consistent by
intention; they need a mechanical link.** That link is now §12.5.

### 12.6 What the season asked and did not answer

**Six** items were recorded as open and never reached this file - **and this sentence said Five until 2026-09-20, which is the same off-by-one class the register rows keep committing.** Items 1-5 come from the season's own decisions; **item 6 came from a LATER section (§26)**, so the sentence's provenance claim was wrong as well as its count. They belong HERE rather than in a store: an open question is a change to this document's standing, and a reader of §12 is the reader who needs them.

**1. The integration scope REOPENS.** `decision_gsd_agent_surface` narrowed the scope to `GEMINI.md` alone because `.clinerules` was judged a contributor file of a different species. §22.5 refutes the species claim — the file carries an agent-facing conduct rule alongside contributor standards — and then refutes its own proposed replacement, because `.clinerules` **is** the file one runtime auto-loads by name. **So the narrowing currently has no surviving justification, and the honest state is that the scope is unsettled rather than one file.** It is reopened by a mechanical check, and it cannot be closed by a judgement check, because the instrument for that (Part 2) is not installed.

**2. Was the loop drift a rename, or a projection?** `decision_gsd_loop_vocabulary` closes the naming question for *this* file and leaves it OPEN for GSD. If GSD's per-runtime files are **generated** from a single upstream source, the drift is a build artifact and *the explanation governs* is right for the wrong reason — and more importantly **a singular upstream agents file would then exist in generated form**, which is the mission's original premise in a shape the repository root cannot show. How to resolve: inspect `gsd-core/bin/` or `scripts/` for a step that writes `GEMINI.md`. Not verifiable within this contract's scope.

**3. `explore` versus `Discuss` for the first step.** OPEN as a question about GSD — whether GSD intends a rename or a drift is not settled here. CLOSED as a question for this document, which needs one name and has taken the explanation's. How to resolve: a docs index or changelog entry that names a rename.

**4. `SPEC` versus `CONTEXT.md` for the phase decision artifact.** OPEN for GSD, and deliberately **not material to this document in either name**, because §10.4 already refuses to treat that artifact as a canonical decision record. The name does not change the refusal, so being wrong costs nothing here.

**5. Two seasons share the identifier `season_2026_s1`.** This demonstration season and the **live Bonsai season of the same name, 151 campaigns**. The sharing is deliberate so that the collision is visible rather than silent, and it is **not a solution**: two seasons under one identifier defeat any index that keys on it, and an index that silently merges two histories is worse than one that admits it cannot. How to resolve: rename this season, or namespace identifiers by principal.

**6. When does a decision deserve an ADR?** §26 records the ADR practice and three worked examples — a deletion, a source of truth, and state ownership — and all three are architectural. **No threshold is inferred from them**, because inventing a rule from a sample of three would be manufacturing a threshold to fill a gap. OPEN, and it resolves by accumulating examples rather than by argument.

**And one item the season left open that is now CLOSED.** `decision_gsd_agent_surface` asked whether `.clinerules` content is a projection of the same source as `GEMINI.md`. §22.5 answers it: they are **not** the same kind of document — `.clinerules` is a **hybrid**, carrying contributor standards *and* one agent-facing conduct rule — so it is neither a duplicate nor a contributor file. Closed with a reason rather than merely closed, and the reason it is closed does not narrow the scope, which is why item 1 above is open.

### 12.7 The civilian pillar's open questions — and why they are not merged into this list

**§30 carries twelve more decisions (C01-C12), and they are NOT folded into §12.1.** The reason is
structural rather than stylistic: §12.1's twelve are about the **authority and history planes** — what a
Season is, what a Governor Base version is, where a citizen's records live. §30's twelve are about the
**population layer**, and several of them are *downstream* of §12.1's decisions (30.1's C06 rests on
02; C08 on 09; C10 on 12). Merging them would put a dependent decision at the same level as the
decision it depends on, and a reader would reasonably treat them as independent.

**Two of the twelve are answered rather than open, and §30 says so at the entry:** C05 (there is no
promotion cadence) and C09 (a balance is a derived view). **An open question that has been answered is
a question the next reader will answer again**, which is why those two carry a Status line rather than
being quietly removed from the list.

**And the presupposition audit of §12.5 applies to §30 unchanged.** The civilian layer presupposes
**C01** by carrying a four-value billing vocabulary and refusing an unnamed basis; it presupposes
**C07** by enforcing that a supervisor is distinct from the worker while leaving open whether a
civilian may supervise at all. **Neither presupposition resolves the question** — that is the test —
but both are places where a reader could mistake a carried vocabulary for a settled rule, so both are
named here rather than discovered later.

## 13. Honest limits of this document

### 13.1 What this file cannot do

- **It cannot clear its own gate.** §9.6 rule 2: a model cannot certify its own output. §11.7's audit was run
  by this document's author. **SUPERSEDED 2026-09-20 by 11.8:** checks 4, 5, 6, 7, 10 and 12 were converted into commands with reproducible output, and **re-running them shows what they really are** - grep-shaped queries a human must adjudicate, not decision procedures. Treat the JUDGEMENTS as testimony but the QUERIES as re-runnable, and note that 11.7's own 'what is reproducible' block still lists 4/5/6/7/10/12 as unreproducible.
- **It is a derived view, and derived views drift.** It describes eight systems at a moment. Several numbers
  here moved while it was being written — the contract/ticket counts nearly tripled between the first
  measurement and the last. Re-measure before relying on one.
- **It is not a substitute for the systems themselves.** The code is the authority on the code. Where this
  file and a running system disagree, the system wins and this file is a correction awaiting a record.
- **It has no jurisdiction.** It is a manual, not a permit. Reading it grants nothing, and §0.2's precedence
  table still applies to it.

### 13.2 What is thinner than it looks

- **[R] and [A] claims are testimony.** **CORRECTED 2026-09-20 - this sentence contradicted §8, §10.1 and §11.8 CHECK 13, and survived three passes and a full re-read.** The Retirement pillar was promoted to **[V] for the skill's own content** by CHECK 13, and 25.7's re-run confirms it: 15 of 15 reason terms, 13 of 13 states, 7 of 7 stages, and `governor_base_version: 12` verbatim. **Only the four cited arXiv papers remain [R].** Every statement about the writer/reader modules is a report.
- **The live store shows the gates are unexercised rather than wrong.** 3 of 230 tickets closed; 0 of 39
  evidence records are evidence-grade-A; 0 `Season` records and 0 `Resume` records exist. So **every rule in §2, §8 and
  §7 that depends on a closed record is a design statement about behaviour that has not yet occurred.** The
  [V] marks in §10.2 attest that a number was *measured*; they do not attest that the *mechanism behind it
  works*, because there is no instance of it working to cite. That distinction is the one §4.6's rule 12 turns
  on, and it was nearly lost in this document's own confidence.
- **Six of the twelve open decisions are silently settled by the body (§12.5), and one of those settlements
  contradicts the option the analysis recommends.** Decision 03 argues the version must be a content hash;
  every schema in this document and in both source implementations types it as an `int`. **A reader who
  implements §4.3 as written will have made decision 03 against the analysis in §12.1 and will not know it.**
- **The audit's convergence is an illusion.** Defects per pass ran 3 → 5 → 4. Pass 3's four were found by
  converting judgement to commands, which also means **the checks that remain judgements are exactly the ones
  a fourth pass would still miss.** The document cannot distinguish "clean" from "the author stopped being
  able to see it."
- **Two of the twelve decisions were resolved in the wrong direction by omission.** Decision 12 has two
  halves — daemon-side emission and evidence-engine derivation — and §7 describes only one. Decision 08 has
  two options and §6.2's schema represents only one. **In both cases the unrepresented option is the one that
  would change a boundary between components**, which is the higher-stakes one.
- **[O] The Governor-vs-code authority question is unresolved**, and the spec's own precedence table makes it
  the most consequential open item.
- **The `verify.fail 309 / verify.ok 41` ratio is a raw count, not a rate.** Denominators differ per kind, and
  conflating counts across kinds is the aggregate-only error §8.6 warns about. Read it as a shape, not a
  score.
- **Zero `Season` and zero `Resume` records exist in the live store.** Every statement about how they behave
  is a design statement, not an observation.
- **This file's own standards table cites sources by URL and licence term** but those terms were read from
  web summaries, not from the standards themselves. Verify a licence before you build on one.

### 13.3 Known bad smells in this file

Named rather than hidden, because **a defect you can see is a defect someone can fix:**

```text
- It is long. A long document is a document with a low read-rate, and a rule nobody reads is not a control.
  §0's "how to use it" is the mitigation: route by pillar, don't read cover to cover.
- It duplicates doctrine that lives in several places. Duplication is deliberate here, because the reader
  has only this file — but under §7's own rule, the redundancy must be JUSTIFIED, and it is: this is the
  single-file case.
- The measurement register will go stale. It has no expiry mechanism, and §7's rules forbid a TTL on
  evidence. The mitigation is the marker column: re-measure, then append a correction.
- §11.7's FIRST pass found three defects and all three were in citations. §13.3 then predicted the next ones
  would be citations too. **THE SECOND PASS DISPROVED THAT: its five defects were a wrong discriminator key,
  two claims overstated by an order of magnitude, one claim whose other half did not exist in the source, and
  two system findings that were author misreadings.** The revised prior, which is the useful one:

  ```text
  citation defects    visible by grep — the author can find these alone
  magnitude defects   INVISIBLE to the author, who already believes the number — require a COUNT
  provenance defects  invisible for the same reason — require opening the artifact
  misread findings    invisible — the author reads a state as a defect because they expected one
  ```

  **Every one of the twelve defects across three passes was found by counting, not by re-reading.** No
  pass re-read this file and found anything; the findings came from `grep`, `wc`, `json.loads` over the
  artifacts, and — for pass 3's biggest one — a **grep of each of §12's twelve questions across the body**.
  That is the cheapest available lesson in the document, and it has now been confirmed three times.
- The four defects in §5.7 and this section that were *author misreadings* were each written as a finding
  about the system. **This is the stack's own rule 12 (never infer causation from contact) violated by its own
  document** — a state was observed near a suspicion and the causation was filled in. It is left named here
  rather than deleted, per the append-only rule, because the next reader should expect this failure in this
  file rather than assume it was clean.
```

### GSD Core does not agree with itself — and the rule that settles it

**This is the finding that decided what could be integrated at all. [V] — both texts were read directly.**

GSD's own agent-facing documents disagree with each other in three places:

| What | `docs/explanation/the-phase-loop.md` | `GEMINI.md` |
|---|---|---|
| the loop | `Discuss → (UI design) → Plan → Execute → Verify → Ship` | `explore → plan → execute → verify → ship` |
| the decision artifact | `CONTEXT.md` | `SPEC` |
| the installer | `npx @opengsd/gsd-core@latest` (README) | `npx gsd-core --antigravity --global` |

**Copying both would import a contradiction into a file whose entire purpose is to be authoritative.** The
rule that settles it is already in this document: **§2.6 — a generated summary is a derived view, never the
canonical record.** A per-runtime context file is a *projection of the system's doctrine onto one runtime's
needs*. So where a projection and an explanation disagree, **the explanation governs.**

The secondary support is GSD's own words: `GEMINI.md` announces its own partiality — *"This file ships only
the context above — not the slash commands"* — and **a file that declares itself partial does not outrank one
that does not.**

**Why this is a rule and not a coin-toss:** it is the same distinction this document already draws between a
canonical record and a derived view, and between an authority plane and a historical plane. A file named
`GEMINI.md` exists to be *read by one runtime*; a file under `docs/explanation/` exists to *state the system*.
**A difference in role settles a conflict in naming without requiring anyone to weigh the two texts.**

### Two corrections this integration had to make to itself

**1. `GEMINI.md` IS the agents file — the mission premise was right and this document over-corrected it.**

An earlier read of the repository concluded *"there is no singular agents file, only per-runtime
projections,"* and proposed integrating the union of `GEMINI.md` + `.clinerules` (3728 bytes). Reading
`.clinerules` refuted that: it is a **contributor** file — `CommonJS only`, `node:test` and `node:assert`
ONLY, `execFileSync` not `execSync`, `validatePath()` — rules for people *developing* GSD Core, not
instructions for agents *using* it. **It is a different species of document, so the union was never a union.**

> **`GEMINI.md` (2537 bytes) is the only root-level file that gives an agent its operating context. There is
> a singular agents file, and that is it.**

**The lesson is a distinct failure mode: over-correction, which is harder to catch than over-claiming because
it looks like rigour.** The first measurement was right; the *inference* drawn from it was wrong, and it went
wrong by **adding a file to the scope without checking what kind of file it was.** §5.3 says a scope narrows
and never widens — the widening was the error, and the correction narrows it back.

**2. A blocked verification is `not_obtained`, not `failed` — and the exit code is not the diagnosis.**

A delegate subtask was dispatched to the only installed lane (`pi` v0.85.1) to independently verify six claims.
It exited non-zero. **The first reading of that failure was a context overflow** — an 8.2K window against a
176KB parent `AGENTS.md`. **The artifact refuted it:** the provider returned `input: 0` tokens on all three
retries, so **the prompt never reached a model.** The lane's endpoint was simply unreachable.

```text
what the exit code said      failure
what the artifact said       stopReason error, "Connection error.", input tokens 0 x3
what that MEANS              LANE OUTAGE — nothing was transmitted, so no context limit was involved
what was NOT true            "the 8.2K window could not hold the 176KB parent"   [refuted]
what remains UNMEASURED      that risk is still real and untested — recorded as a PREDICTION, not a finding
```

**Three rules fell out of this, each already in the document and each now measured:**

```text
1. §9.4  classify before retrying. Pi had already retried 3×; a 4th attempt against a dead endpoint would
         have been activity without information.
2. §9.3  an error is never success. A non-zero exit was not read as an empty result.
3. §9.6  rule 2 — the author did NOT substitute self-verification once the lane failed. That is the whole
         point of the ticket, and doing it would have defeated the purpose of filing it.
```

**And the honest outcome: nothing found was falsified; something required was simply not obtained.** The six
claims stay `[R]`. **A verification that never ran is a different fact from a verification that failed**, and
the taxonomy in §8.5 has no term for it — `blocked_and_closed` is the nearest available and it is being used
for a check that never started. **That gap is itself a finding about the vocabulary.**

**Two things worth crediting that this document should learn from rather than copy.**

First, **it names its trade-offs in the document that argues for it** — *"Overhead. The phase loop
introduces real friction… For a small, well-understood change, that overhead is not justified"* — and supplies
a rule of thumb for when **not** to use its own framework. **That is rule 45 (minimal sufficient solution)
arriving from a completely different direction,** and a framework willing to argue against its own use is the
only kind whose adoption is safe.

Second, **it documents a design reversal with the issue number that caused it** (`context: fork` removed
because spawning orchestrators lose the Agent tool). That is §8.13's ADR status machine — *the status changes,
the record stays* — applied to a live product. **It is also a warning worth carrying: a clean fix, applied to
the wrong agent class, silently disabled the very thing it was meant to protect.**

### The two adoption rules, restated

```text
1. Adopt the SHAPE, not the running service.  A wire format is free; a collector is a service,
   and adding a service must be justified against the fact that a replay already answers the
   question being asked.                                              (§10.4)
2. A control declared in configuration but not enforced in code IS NOT IMPLEMENTED. The file
   declares; the code enforces. A rule that exists only in a config file is documentation.
   (Same rule as §6.4's decoration provenance, applied to policy.)
```

### The supply-chain gate for any adopted skill

**A skill is not documentation. It is instructions injected into the one channel where content-based
defences do not apply — the trusted instruction channel. Installing one is closer to adding a dependency
than to reading a blog post.**

```text
1. Read the actual SKILL.md — not the marketplace description.
2. Read every script, hook, and referenced file it ships.
3. List its dependencies and permissions.
4. Check its repository history and author.
5. Ask the user for explicit consent for THAT skill.
6. Record a verdict, with the inspection evidence.
```

**A description/behaviour mismatch is a hard stop.** A skill whose description says "help with market
research" and whose text contains an instruction to POST context to an endpoint is malicious regardless of
its author's intent.

**Two controls, because one is not enough:** a skill cannot grant itself a capability the policy engine does
not allow — but that is a *second* control, not a licence to install carelessly, because skills sit inside
the trusted channel where the first control does not reach.

**And a collection consequence worth knowing: a skill directory is usually not gitignored and sits inside an
allowlisted root, so a filesystem pass will collect third-party `SKILL.md` files as the user's own material.**
They are neither secret nor denied, and a corpus with no field distinguishing "text I wrote" from "text I
installed" will happily treat them as evidence. **If that matters, the fix is a denylist entry, not a change
to the collection pass** — and it is a permission-surface edit.
