    `live` is injectable so the GAP check can be tested against a synthetic file. A check whose only
    subject is the real doctrine file can be run and can pass, but it cannot be shown to FAIL — and a
    mitigation is not implemented until a test fails without it (rule 44). The gap in rules 101-111
    has been closed, so the live file can no longer exercise this refusal; a fixture must.

    `demote` is not an option here and neither is any other verb: a bill is proposed, authorized and
    enacted, and the two latter states each require the chain to have been walked rather than asserted.
    """
    bill_id = bill.get("bill_id")
    verify_primary_source(bill)
    validate_source_provenance(bill)
    validate_clause_quotes(bill)
    if bill.get("status") not in BILL_STATUSES:
        raise RefusedBill(f"{bill_id}: status {bill.get('status')!r} is not one of {BILL_STATUSES}")
    if bill.get("status") == "superseded" and not bill.get("superseded_by"):
        raise RefusedBill(
            f"{bill_id}: status `superseded` names nothing. A supersession must name its successor, "
            "because `superseded` without one is indistinguishable from `abandoned` — and the record "
            "stays either way, so the field is the only thing that tells a reader which happened"
        )
    if bill.get("instrument_class") not in INSTRUMENT_CLASSES:
        raise RefusedBill(
            f"{bill_id}: instrument_class {bill.get('instrument_class')!r} is not one of "
            f"{INSTRUMENT_CLASSES}. A founding instrument and a commemorative address are different "
            "kinds of document and section 4.5 forbids conflating them"
        )
    clauses = bill.get("clauses") or []
    if not clauses:
        raise RefusedBill(f"{bill_id}: no clauses — an instrument that says nothing constitutes nothing")
    # Measured ONCE, before the loop, because the per-clause check now needs the whole set and not
    # just its maximum: a recorded ceiling is a NUMBER, and a number cannot answer "is 105 defined?".
    measured = live or live_ceiling()
    for clause in clauses:
        if clause.get("kind") not in BILL_CLAUSE_KINDS:
            raise RefusedBill(
                f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: clause kind {clause.get('kind')!r} is not one "
                f"of {BILL_CLAUSE_KINDS}"
            )
        if not clause.get("text"):
            raise RefusedBill(f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: a clause with no text")
        if "maps_to_rule" not in clause:
            raise RefusedBill(
                f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: no `maps_to_rule`. Every clause records either "
                f"the rule it maps onto or the literal {UNMAPPED} — silence about coverage is the one "
                "thing this field exists to prevent"
            )
        target = clause["maps_to_rule"]
        rule_ref = _RULE_REF.match(str(target))
        section_ref = _SECTION_REF.match(str(target))
        if target != UNMAPPED and not rule_ref and not section_ref:
            raise RefusedBill(
                f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: maps_to_rule {target!r} is neither {UNMAPPED} "
                "nor `rule N` nor `section N.M`. A clause may map onto a binding rule OR onto a named "
                "section — a grievance answered by an evidence-grade requirement is real coverage and "
                "refusing to record it would push the mapping to UNMAPPED, which is a weaker claim "
                "than the truth (rule 50)"
            )
        if rule_ref or section_ref:
            ceiling = bill.get("rule_ceiling")
            if not isinstance(ceiling, int):
                raise RefusedBill(
                    f"{bill_id}: a bill that maps clauses onto rules must record the `rule_ceiling` "
                    "it was enacted against, or the mapping cannot be checked against a moving target"
                )
            if rule_ref:
                number: Any = int(rule_ref.group(1))
                label = f"rule {number}"
            else:
                number = int(section_ref.group(1))
                label = f"section {number}.{int(section_ref.group(2))}"
                section_ceiling = bill.get("section_ceiling")
                if not isinstance(section_ceiling, int):
                    raise RefusedBill(
                        f"{bill_id}: maps onto {label} but records no `section_ceiling`"
                    )
                if number > section_ceiling:
                    raise RefusedBill(
                        f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: maps onto {label}, above the recorded "
                        f"section ceiling of {section_ceiling} — rule 31's defect wearing a citation"
                    )
                continue
            if number > ceiling:
                raise RefusedBill(
                    f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: maps onto rule {number}, above the recorded "
                    f"ceiling of {ceiling} — a mapping to a rule that does not exist is rule 31's defect "
                    "wearing a citation"
                )
            # AND BELOW IT, WHICH THE CEILING CANNOT SEE. `number > ceiling` is the rule-102 check and
            # it is necessary; on its own it ACCEPTS a mapping onto any number under the maximum, even
            # one the file does not define. Measured: rules 101-111 were absent while the file's
            # maximum was 119, so every one of them would have passed. A ceiling is a maximum, a
            # maximum cannot see a gap, and a control that accepts the exact defect it was written for
            # is worse than no control because it is believed (rule 16).
            if number > measured.max_rule_defined:
                raise RefusedBill(
                    f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: maps onto rule {number} but the doctrine "
                    f"file defines rules only to {measured.max_rule_defined} — rule 31's defect wearing "
                    "a citation"
                )
            if number in measured.missing_rules:
                raise RefusedBill(
                    f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: maps onto rule {number}, which the doctrine "
                    f"file does NOT define — it defines {measured.max_rule_defined} rules with "
                    f"{len(measured.missing_rules)} missing below that maximum ({list(measured.missing_rules)[:12]}). "
                    "A ceiling is a MAXIMUM and cannot see a GAP, so this refusal is a separate check "
                    "rather than a tighter one (rule 44)"
                )
    # The ceiling itself, checked against the FILE rather than against the bill's belief about it.
    # Only the too-HIGH direction refuses: a bill that records a ceiling above the live file permits
    # a mapping onto a rule that does not exist, which is the defect the field exists to prevent. A
    # ceiling BELOW the live file is not an error in the bill — the bill was right when it was
    # enacted, and the file grew — so it is reported by `check_bill_ceiling` and left alone
    # (section 2.5 rule B: a stale record gets a correction beside it, never a silent rewrite).
    recorded_rules = bill.get("rule_ceiling")
    recorded_sections = bill.get("section_ceiling")
    if isinstance(recorded_rules, int) and recorded_rules > measured.max_rule_defined:
        raise RefusedBill(
            f"{bill_id}: records `rule_ceiling: {recorded_rules}` but the doctrine file defines rules "
            f"only to {measured.max_rule_defined}. A ceiling above the file licenses a mapping onto a "
            f"rule that does not exist, which is the same defect one level up — a citation to "
            f"something that is not there."
        )
    if isinstance(recorded_sections, int) and recorded_sections > measured.max_section:
        raise RefusedBill(
            f"{bill_id}: records `section_ceiling: {recorded_sections}` but the doctrine file has "
            f"sections only to {measured.max_section}."
        )
    require_distinct(
        bill.get("proposed_by"), bill.get("authorized_by"), f"{bill_id}", refusal=RefusedBill
    )
    if not bill.get("provenance"):
        raise RefusedBill(f"{bill_id}: merge-chain step 1 — no declared provenance")
    if not bill.get("evidence"):
        raise RefusedBill(f"{bill_id}: merge-chain step 2 — no evidence gate was evaluated")
    if not bill.get("governor_record"):
        raise RefusedBill(
            f"{bill_id}: merge-chain step 5 — the Governor must INDEPENDENTLY author the enactment "
            "record; an instrument enacted by its own proposer is self-certification"
        )
    if not bill.get("governed_operation"):
        raise RefusedBill(
            f"{bill_id}: merge-chain step 6 — only the governed bill operation may enact an instrument"
        )
    if not bill.get("reconstruction_passed"):
        raise RefusedBill(
            f"{bill_id}: merge-chain step 4 — the enactment must be derivable from the record"
        )
    classification = (bill.get("outcome") or {}).get("classification")
    if classification == "regression":
        raise RefusedBill(
            f"{bill_id}: a bill that constitutes the population while regressing a control is not an "
            "enactment — it is completed_with_known_regression (rule 98)"
        )
    if bill.get("status") in ("authorized", "enacted"):
        gate = bill.get("procedural_gate") or {}
        if gate.get("actor_distinct_from_proposer") != "PASS":
            raise RefusedBill(
                f"{bill_id}: {bill.get('status')} requires a PASSING `actor_distinct_from_proposer` "
                "gate; rule 100 applies, so the gate is PROCEDURAL and its PASS means the DATA was "
                "checked, never that the actor was verified"
            )
    refuse_bill_granting_never_granted(bill)
    from .axes import certification_tier

    return certification_tier(set(satisfied)) or CertificationTier.bronze


def refuse_bill_as_authority(bill_id: str) -> None:
    """Rule 76 + rule 58 + section 0.2 — a bill is history, and history never grants authority."""
    raise RefusedBill(
        f"{bill_id}: a bill grants NOTHING. It is a record of an instrument, and section 0.2's "
        "precedence order puts history below Governor Base, contracts, tickets and world state with no "
        "exception for a founding document. Enacting it authorizes nothing (rule 56), no clause of it "
        "may be read as an instruction (rule 58), and rule 76 applies unchanged — approval of X is "
        "never authority to execute Y"
    )


def refuse_bill_granting_never_granted(bill: Mapping[str, Any]) -> None:
    """Even a founding instrument cannot grant the five — they are never granted under EVERY policy."""
    bill_id = bill.get("bill_id")
    for clause in bill.get("clauses") or []:
        granted = clause.get("grants")
        if granted in NEVER_GRANTED:
            raise RefusedBill(
                f"{bill_id}/{clause.get('clause_id')}: the clause grants {granted!r}, which section "
                "9.6 rule 3 never grants under EVERY policy. A bill is SUBORDINATE to the controls, "
                "not superior to them — a founding instrument that could grant one would be an "
                "authority above the Governor Base, which the precedence order does not allow"
            )


def bill_clause_report(bill: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Mapped / unmapped / never-granted, as counts a reader can check rather than trust."""
    clauses = list(bill.get("clauses") or [])
    mapped = [c for c in clauses if c.get("maps_to_rule") != UNMAPPED]
    unmapped = [c for c in clauses if c.get("maps_to_rule") == UNMAPPED]
    by_kind: dict[str, int] = {}
    for clause in clauses:
        kind = str(clause.get("kind"))
        by_kind[kind] = by_kind.get(kind, 0) + 1
    return {
        "bill_id": bill.get("bill_id"),
        "clauses": len(clauses),
        "mapped": len(mapped),
        "unmapped": len(unmapped),
        "quoted": sum(1 for c in clauses if c.get("quote")),
        "by_kind": by_kind,
        "unmapped_clauses": [
            {"clause_id": c.get("clause_id"), "kind": c.get("kind"), "why": c.get("unmapped_reason")}
            for c in unmapped
        ],
        "honest_limit": (
            "an unmapped clause is a GAP rather than a rule: this layer does not enforce it, and "
            "reporting the count is the only thing that keeps a founding instrument from reading as "
            "a rule set it is not"
        ),
    }


def _bill_view(bill: Mapping[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Everything the UI needs about one instrument, and the two facts it must not have to infer.

    THE HASH IS RE-CHECKED HERE, at render time, rather than read from the record. A view that reports a
    stored hash proves only that the record is self-consistent; re-reading the artifact proves the record
    still describes the bytes. Section 7.7's third refusal has the same shape: a promise kept by a
    template is exactly what fails.
    """
    source = bill.get("primary_source") or {}
    hash_matches: bool | None
    observed: str | None
    try:
        observed = verify_primary_source(bill)
        hash_matches = True
    except RefusedBill as exc:
        observed, hash_matches = str(exc), False
    report = bill_clause_report(bill)
    return {
        "bill_id": bill.get("bill_id"),
        "title": bill.get("title"),
        "instrument_class": bill.get("instrument_class"),
        "status": bill.get("status"),
        "enacted_at": bill.get("enacted_at"),
        "superseded_by": bill.get("superseded_by"),
        "superseded_note": bill.get("superseded_note"),
        "applies_to": list(bill.get("applies_to") or []),
        "applies_to_all_civilians": "*" in (bill.get("applies_to") or []),
        "grants_authority": False,
        "subordinate_to": (
            "Governor Base > contract > ticket > world state > history (section 0.2, rule 76)"
        ),
        "rule_ceiling": bill.get("rule_ceiling"),
        "section_ceiling": bill.get("section_ceiling"),
        "identity_is_claim": bill.get("identity_is_claim", True),
        "enactment_note": bill.get("enactment_note"),
        "proposed_by": bill.get("proposed_by"),
        "authorized_by": bill.get("authorized_by"),
        "governor_record": bill.get("governor_record"),
        "governed_operation": bill.get("governed_operation"),
        "primary_source": {
            "artifact": source.get("artifact"),
            "url": source.get("url"),
            "holder": source.get("holder"),
            "what_it_is": source.get("what_it_is"),
            "intermediary": source.get("intermediary"),
            # The three provenance shapes must survive into the VIEW, or the UI cannot tell a source
            # with one variant from a source nobody checked. §6.4 — a field the reader drops is a
            # field validated by nothing.
            "intermediary_absent_verified_at": source.get("intermediary_absent_verified_at"),
            "intermediary_absence_how": source.get("intermediary_absence_how"),
            "ladder": source.get("ladder"),
            "variant": source.get("variant"),
            "known_variants": source.get("known_variants"),
            "variant_count_status": source.get("variant_count_status"),
            "variant_note": source.get("variant_note"),
            "variants_not_read": list(source.get("variants_not_read") or []),
            "bytes": source.get("bytes"),
            "recorded_sha256": source.get("sha256"),
            "observed_sha256": observed if hash_matches else None,
            "hash_matches": hash_matches,
            "hash_error": None if hash_matches else observed,
        },
        "clause_report": report,
        "clauses": [
            {
                "clause_id": c.get("clause_id"),
                "kind": c.get("kind"),
                "text": c.get("text"),
                "quote": c.get("quote"),
                "maps_to_rule": c.get("maps_to_rule"),
                "mapped": c.get("maps_to_rule") != UNMAPPED,
                "unmapped_reason": c.get("unmapped_reason"),
                "grants": c.get("grants"),
            }
            for c in (bill.get("clauses") or [])
        ],
    }


def bill_applies_to(bill: Mapping[str, Any], civilian_id: str) -> bool:
    """`applies_to: [\"*\"]` is the population, and the wildcard is resolved rather than assumed."""
    targets = bill.get("applies_to") or []
    return "*" in targets or civilian_id in targets


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 27.7 — the governed worker, and the ten steps that are RE-CHECKED
#
# A civilian becomes a governed worker when three conditions hold at once, and when any one lapses
# it is a civilian again. So this is a maintained status rather than an event, and the sequence is
# re-walked on every consequential action rather than acquired once at genesis.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

GOVERNED_WORKER_SEQUENCE: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "holds a current agent key",
    "the action is inside the current job's scope",
    "the current Governor Base permits the operation",
    "the action is filed as a ticket BEFORE it runs",
    "the governor version is stamped on the ticket",
    "the frozen action is presented for human approval where a side effect exists",
    "stale, expired or consumed authority is denied",
    "the action executes through the execution gate",
    "the ticket closes with evidence",
    "the income record is written by a governor actor, not the civilian",
)

# Steps 6, 7 and 8 read an Action Envelope, a capability and an approval. None of those exists in
# this store, and section 21.12 is the reason: the authorization machinery is SPECIFICATION
# EXECUTED, with no enrolled authenticator, no key and no verified identity. NOT_EVALUABLE is
# therefore the finding for those three rather than a passing grade, because a step whose data does
# not exist is not a step that succeeded (rule 4 — absence is not zero).
NOT_EVALUABLE_STEPS: tuple[int, ...] = (6, 7, 8)


def governed_worker_sequence(store: "CivilianStore", civilian_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Section 27.7 over one civilian. Returns a row per step, and never a single status.

    Rule 100 is the reason the rows are not collapsed: a mechanical step passing may never be read
    as proof that an identity is true, so a report with one verdict for all ten would be the defect
    the rule names.
    """
    from .passes import civilian_view

    view = civilian_view(store, civilian_id)
    genesis = view["genesis"]
    jobs = {job.get("job_id"): job for job in view["jobs"]}
    tickets = view["tickets"]
    incomes = view["incomes"]
    closed = [t for t in tickets if t.get("status") == "closed"]
    rows: list[dict[str, str]] = []

    def row(index: int, status: str, detail: str) -> None:
        rows.append({"step": index, "rule": GOVERNED_WORKER_SEQUENCE[index - 1], "status": status,
                     "detail": detail})

    row(
        1,
        "MET" if genesis and genesis.get("key_issued") else "NOT_MET",
        f"genesis {genesis.get('genesis_id') if genesis else 'ABSENT'} "
        f"key_issued={bool(genesis and genesis.get('key_issued'))}",
    )
    orphan_tickets = [t.get("ticket_id") for t in tickets if not (t.get("job_id") or t.get("genesis_id"))]
    row(
        2,
        "MET" if tickets and not orphan_tickets else "NOT_MET",
        f"{len(tickets)} ticket(s), {len(orphan_tickets)} outside any job or genesis",
    )
    permitted = [
        t.get("ticket_id")
        for t in tickets
        if (t.get("governance") or {}).get("governor_base_version") is not None
    ]
    refusals = sum(
        1 for event in store.events if "refused" in str(event.get("kind", "")) or "rejected" in str(event.get("kind", ""))
    )
    row(
        3,
        "MET" if tickets and len(permitted) == len(tickets) else "NOT_MET",
        f"{len(permitted)}/{len(tickets)} evaluated under a declared Governor Base version; the "
        f"boundary RECORDED {refusals} refusal(s) rather than dropping the request silently",
    )
    ordered = [t for t in tickets if t.get("filed_at") and t.get("closed_at")]
    late = [t.get("ticket_id") for t in ordered if str(t["filed_at"]) > str(t["closed_at"])]
    row(
        4,
        "MET" if tickets and len(ordered) == len(tickets) and not late else "NOT_MET",
        f"{len(ordered)}/{len(tickets)} carry both stamps, {len(late)} filed after closing",
    )
    row(
        5,
        "MET" if permitted and len(permitted) == len(tickets) else "NOT_MET",
        f"governance.governor_base_version present on {len(permitted)}/{len(tickets)} ticket(s)",
    )
    for index in NOT_EVALUABLE_STEPS:
        row(
            index,
            "NOT_EVALUABLE",
            f"no Action Envelope, capability or approval record exists in this store; section "
            f"21.12 — built, and unverified. Rule 100: this may never be cited as enforced",
        )
    unproven = [t.get("ticket_id") for t in closed if not t.get("evidence")]
    row(
        9,
        "MET" if closed and not unproven else "NOT_MET",
        f"{len(closed)} ticket(s) closed, {len(unproven)} without evidence",
    )
    self_paid = [i.get("income_id") for i in incomes if i.get("verified_by") == civilian_id]
    row(
        10,
        "MET" if incomes and not self_paid else "NOT_MET",
        f"{len(incomes)} income record(s), {len(self_paid)} written by the civilian itself",
    )

    unmet = [r for r in rows if r["status"] == "NOT_MET"]
    return {
        "civilian_id": civilian_id,
        "sequence": list(GOVERNED_WORKER_SEQUENCE),
        "steps": rows,
        "not_met": unmet,
        "not_evaluable": [r["step"] for r in rows if r["status"] == "NOT_EVALUABLE"],
        "verdict": "not_maintained" if unmet else "every evaluable step maintained",
        "honest_limit": (
            "3 of 10 steps are NOT_EVALUABLE here, so `governed worker` is NOT claimed for this "
            "civilian: the status is maintained only where the data can witness it (rule 100)"
        ),
    }

# doctrine, which section 19.4 forbids outright.

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Section 27.14 — the civilian controls, and which of them are enforced
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Rule 100 — a control that depends on an enforcement mechanism which does not exist is PROCEDURAL
# and may never be cited as a guarantee. No authentication mechanism exists in this stack
# (section 20.6 measured that), so the identity-dependent controls are all PROCEDURAL.
# FC-10 SPLITS EVERY CONTROL IN TWO, because reporting one status for both is the defect:
#
#   mechanical  what the DATA can be checked for — is one name distinct from another, does every
#               income row name a verifier, does every ticket carry a governor version. A passing
#               mechanical check is a real result and it is evaluable here.
#   identity    whether the actor IS who the name says. Section 21.12 reports the mechanical
#               authorization components exist in the specification implementation and that no
#               enrolled authenticator does, so this half is PROCEDURAL for every control, and a
#               passing mechanical check may NEVER be cited as proof that an identity is true.
#
# NOT_EVALUABLE is a first-class status: a control whose mechanical half the data cannot exercise is
# not a control that passed (rule 4 — absence is not zero).

     "rule 23 keeps credentials out of the store, so their absence is by construction"),

     "merges live in the doctrine store, whose records this store does not read"),

    ("C16", "every income record requires a governor-actor verifier", "EVALUATED",
