```python
def _next_order() -> int:
    return max((fragment.order for fragment in g.load_fragments()), default=-1) + 1


def _target_for(section: str, fragments: list) -> g.DoctrineFragment | None:
    """The fragment this migration ALREADY wrote for this section, whatever its order.

    THIS IS THE BUG THE FIRST VERSION HAD, kept here as the fix rather than quietly changed. The
    first version computed its target as `max(order) + 1`, so the SECOND run appended a second copy of
    sections 27-30 at frag_33-36 instead of updating frag_29-32: the next order is not an identity, it
    is a POSITION, and a position moves every time the thing it points at is appended to. An idempotent
    migration has to recognise its own output by what it IS — the section name plus `authored_for` —
    and never by where the output happened to land. `repair` exists because the tool made the mess.
    """
    return next(
        (f for f in fragments if f.section == section and f.fragment_id in _OURS), None
    )


def _ours() -> dict[str, str]:
    """fragment_id -> the section it carries, for every fragment this migration authored."""
    found: dict[str, str] = {}
    for path in sorted(doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR.glob("frag_*.json")):
        record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if record.get("authored_for") == AUTHORED_FOR:
            found[record["fragment_id"]] = record["section"]
    return found


_OURS: dict[str, str] = {}


def _planned() -> tuple[doctrine.Partition, int]:
    """Partition the authored input and report where its blocks would land. Writes nothing."""
    text = "".join((INPUT_DIR / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8") for name in INPUTS)
    part = doctrine.partition(text)
    if "".join(block.body for block in part.blocks) != text:
        raise SystemExit("   the authored input does not reassemble byte for byte; refusing")
    if not part.fence_balanced:
        raise SystemExit(f"   {part.fence_lines} fence markers is an odd count; refusing")
    if part.phantom_headings:
        raise SystemExit("   a heading inside a fence in the authored input; refusing")
    return part, _next_order()


def _anchor_problems(fragment_id: str, anchor: str, already: str | None = None) -> list[str]:
    """An anchor must exist EXACTLY ONCE, unless the patch already ran \u2014 then it must not appear.

    Idempotence is the point. A migration that appends a pointer twice produces a file that reads as
    two rules where there is one, and the second pass would be the pass that broke it. So each patch
    records a distinctive fragment of its own REPLACEMENT, and `already` is checked first.
    """
    path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fragment_id}.json"
    if not path.exists():
        return [f"{fragment_id}: fragment does not exist"]
    body = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["body"]
    if already and already in body:
        return []
    if anchor not in body:
        return [f"{fragment_id}: anchor not found: {anchor.strip()[:60]!r}..."]
    if body.count(anchor) != 1:
        return [f"{fragment_id}: anchor appears {body.count(anchor)} times; ambiguous"]
    return []


def _duplicates() -> dict[str, list[str]]:
    """Sections this migration authored MORE THAN ONCE. A non-empty result is a defect it made."""
    seen: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for fragment_id, section in sorted(_ours().items()):
        seen.setdefault(section, []).append(fragment_id)
    return {section: ids for section, ids in seen.items() if len(ids) > 1}


def _repair() -> int:
    """Remove the duplicates this tool created, keep the newest revision, and make orders dense.

    Reported rather than silent: the repair names every fragment it deletes, every order it changes,
    and refuses if a fragment it did not author would have to move.
    """
    global _OURS
    _OURS = _ours()
    duplicates = _duplicates()
    if not duplicates:
        print("   no duplicate sections; nothing to repair")
        return 0
    kill: list[str] = []
    for section, ids in duplicates.items():
        # The newest revision wins: the later run carries the later authored input.
        keep = sorted(ids, key=lambda fid: json.loads(
            (doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fid}.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["order"]
        )[-1]
        for fid in ids:
            if fid != keep:
                kill.append(fid)
        print(f"   {section[:50]:50s} keep {keep}  delete {[f for f in ids if f != keep]}")
    for fragment_id in kill:
        (doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fragment_id}.json").unlink()
        print(f"   DELETED   {fragment_id}")

    # Dense orders, in sequence. A fragment this migration did not author must not move.
    fragments = sorted(g.load_fragments(), key=lambda f: f.order)
    moved = 0
    for wanted, fragment in enumerate(fragments):
        if fragment.order == wanted:
            continue
        path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fragment.fragment_id}.json"
        record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        if record.get("authored_for") != AUTHORED_FOR:
            print(f"   REFUSED   {fragment.fragment_id} would move and was not authored here; stopping")
            return 1
        new_id = f"frag_{wanted:02d}"
        target = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{new_id}.json"
        if target.exists():
            print(f"   REFUSED   {new_id} already exists; stopping")
            return 1
        record["fragment_id"] = new_id
        record["order"] = wanted
        record["renumbered_by"] = AUTHORED_FOR
        target.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        path.unlink()
        print(f"   RENUMBERED {fragment.fragment_id} -> {new_id}")
        moved += 1
    print(f"   REPAIRED  {len(kill)} deleted, {moved} renumbered")
    print(f"   duplicates now     {_duplicates() or 'none'}")
    return 0


def _check_anchors() -> list[str]:
    """Every patch anchor must exist BEFORE anything is written."""
    problems: list[str] = []
    # Entries may carry a third element: an explicit applied-marker. Where one exists it is used for
    # the "is this already applied" test, exactly as `apply` does, or the pre-flight check and the
    # patch would disagree about the same entry.
    for entry in PATCHES:
        fragment_id, anchor, replacement, *rest = entry
        marker = rest[0] if rest else replacement[:60]
        problems.extend(_anchor_problems(fragment_id, anchor, already=marker))
    for table, fragment_id in ((PREAMBLE_PATCHES, "frag_01"), (REGISTER_PATCHES, "frag_12")):
        for entry in table:
            anchor, replacement, *rest = entry
            marker = rest[0] if rest else replacement[:60]
            problems.extend(_anchor_problems(fragment_id, anchor, already=marker))
    return problems


def _live_section_range() -> tuple[int, int]:
    """The file's REAL numbered-section range, measured over the built file, fence-aware.

    Read from `AGENTS.md` rather than from the fragment store, because the claim being checked is about
    the file a reader holds. A fragment-derived range would only prove the store agrees with itself.
    """
    text = recon.GOD_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    numbers: list[int] = []
    in_fence = False
    for line in text.splitlines():
        if FENCE.match(line):
            in_fence = not in_fence
            continue
        if in_fence:
            continue
        match = re.match(r"^## (\d+)\.", line)
        if match:
            numbers.append(int(match.group(1)))
    if not numbers:
        return (-1, -1)
    return (min(numbers), max(numbers))


def _preamble_range_problems() -> list[str]:
    """The § convention paragraph's stated range must equal the file's real range. **Both halves.**

    THIS IS THE INVARIANT THE PATCH LIST COULD NOT SEE, and the reason it exists is a measured defect
    rather than a hypothetical one. `PREAMBLE_PATCHES` held two entries that corrected the preamble's
    stated range from 0-26 to 0-30. A later pass appended section 31 and corrected the same two lines
    to 0-31. From then on the two entries reported `anchor not found` — the file had moved PAST their
    target — and the status output carried that as two permanent false alarms.

    A patch list is a claim about a file that goes stale whenever another patch moves the file, and
    nothing in the tool could distinguish "my anchor is missing, something is wrong" from "my anchor
    is missing because a later pass already went further". This check does distinguish them, because it
    tests the PROPERTY rather than a string: whatever wrote the line, the stated range must be the real
    one, in both places the convention paragraph states it.

    Two sites, not one. The paragraph asserts the range twice — once in prose and once in the § legend —
    and the second was missed the first time for exactly that reason: a check that found one site would
    have reported this paragraph clean while half of it contradicted the other half.
    """
    low, high = _live_section_range()
    if low < 0:
        return ["no numbered sections found in the built file; the range cannot be checked"]
    want = f"{SECT}{low}{DASH}{SECT}{high}"
    text = recon.GOD_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
    problems: list[str] = []
    # The prose half. A stale range here is what §12's own convention paragraph exists to prevent.
    if f"This file runs {want}." not in text:
        found = re.search(r"This file runs ([^.]*\.)", text)
        problems.append(
            f"the preamble's stated range does not match the file: states "
            f"{found.group(0) if found else 'nothing'!r}, file has {want}"
        )
    if f"this file has {want} only)" not in text:
        problems.append(f"the § convention legend does not state '{want} only'")
    # A range that names only ONE of the two sites is the exact shape the second one was missed by.
    if text.count(f"{want}") < 2:
        problems.append(
            f"' {want}' appears {text.count(want)} time(s); the convention paragraph states the range "
            "in two places, so a single occurrence means one of them was left behind"
        )
    return problems


def _append_state() -> list[tuple[str, str, bool]]:
    """Which INSTRUMENT_APPENDS have actually landed. **The control that was missing.**

    `instruments` is a SEPARATE MODE from `migrate`, and nothing checked that it had ever been run.
    Measured 2026-09-21: six authored inputs — §27.18, rules 101-111, §30.6 and §30.7, about 30 KB of
    doctrine — were absent from BOTH the store and the file, while being cited fourteen times in the
    file and fully implemented in code. No command reported it, so no operator could see it, and the
    file's own `DERIVED True` said the record was intact. `DERIVED` means the file matches its
    fragments; it says nothing about whether the fragments are the right ones.

    A mode that must be run separately, with nothing reporting whether it has been, is a mode that
    gets forgotten. That is rule 111's defect — a check the next reader cannot see — one level up.
    """
    out: list[tuple[str, str, bool]] = []
    for fragment_id, name in INSTRUMENT_APPENDS:
        addition = (INPUT_DIR / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        marker = addition.lstrip("\n").split("\n", 1)[0]
        path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fragment_id}.json"
        body = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))["body"] if path.exists() else ""
        out.append((fragment_id, marker, marker in body))
    return out


def _status() -> int:
    global _OURS
    _OURS = _ours()
    part, next_order = _planned()
    sections = [block.section for block in part.blocks]
    print("   CIVILIAN DOCTRINE")
    print(f"   authored input      {len(INPUTS)} file(s) in doctrine_input/")
    print(f"   sections            {len(sections)}")
    for name in sections:
        target = _target_for(name, g.load_fragments())
        where = f"updates {target.fragment_id}" if target else f"new at order {next_order}"
        print(f"     {name[:58]:58s} {where}")
    duplicates = _duplicates()
    if duplicates:
        print(f"   DUPLICATE SECTIONS  {duplicates}  <- run `repair`")
    print(f"   would start at      order {next_order}")
    missing = [expected for expected in EXPECTED_SECTIONS
               if not any(name.startswith(expected.split()[0]) for name in sections)]
    print(f"   expected sections   {'all present' if not missing else 'MISSING ' + str(missing)}")
    problems = _check_anchors()
    print(f"   patch anchors       {'all present and unique' if not problems else 'PROBLEMS'}")
    for problem in problems:
        print(f"     {problem}")
    # AND THE INVARIANT THE ANCHOR LIST CANNOT EXPRESS. Reported NEXT TO the anchors rather than
    # instead of them, because they answer different questions: an anchor asks "is my literal still
    # here", and this asks "is the file's stated range still true". The measured case that produced it
    # is two entries reporting `anchor not found` forever because a later pass moved further than they
    # aimed, which the anchor list could not tell apart from a real breakage.
    low, high = _live_section_range()
    print(f"   built file range    {SECT}{low}{DASH}{SECT}{high}  (measured, fence-aware)")
    range_problems = _preamble_range_problems()
    print(f"   preamble range      {'matches the file, in both places' if not range_problems else 'PROBLEMS'}")
    for problem in range_problems:
        print(f"     {problem}")
    existing = {fragment.fragment_id for fragment in g.load_fragments()}
    collisions = [f"frag_{index:02d}" for index in range(next_order, next_order + len(sections))
                  if f"frag_{index:02d}" in existing]
    print(f"   id collisions       {collisions or 'none'}")

    # AND THE MODE THAT NOTHING WAS CHECKING. `migrate` and `instruments` are two halves of one
    # migration, and only one of them had a report. Six authored subsections sat unappended because of
    # it, so their state is printed here — on the command an operator already runs.
    appends = _append_state()
    absent = [(fid, marker) for fid, marker, present in appends if not present]
    print(f"   instrument subsect. {len(appends) - len(absent)} of {len(appends)} appended")
    for fragment_id, marker, present in appends:
        print(f"     {'present' if present else 'ABSENT '}  {fragment_id}  {marker[:60]!r}")
    if absent:
        print("   ABSENT means the authored subsection has NEVER been appended. `migrate` is a different")
        print("   mode and does not append it: run `python civilians_doctrine.py instruments`.")
    print("   nothing written - this was a check")
    return 0 if not problems and not collisions and not missing and not absent else 1


def _migrate() -> int:
    problems = _check_anchors()
    if problems:
        for problem in problems:
            print(f"   {problem}")
        return 1
    global _OURS
    _OURS = _ours()
    part, next_order = _planned()
    source_hash = sha256_hex(
        "".join((INPUT_DIR / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8") for name in INPUTS).encode("utf-8")
    )
    appended: list[str] = []
    updated: list[str] = []
    unchanged: list[str] = []
    for block in part.blocks:
        target = _target_for(block.section, g.load_fragments())
        if target is None:
            # A section that has never been migrated lands after everything that has.
            order = _next_order()
            fragment_id = f"frag_{order:02d}"
        else:
            order, fragment_id = target.order, target.fragment_id
        path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fragment_id}.json"
        existing = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if path.exists() else None
        if existing is not None and existing.get("authored_for") != AUTHORED_FOR:
            print(f"   REFUSED   {fragment_id} exists and was not authored for {AUTHORED_FOR}")
            return 1

        # ORDER SAFETY, and it is a CORRECTION rather than a feature. `migrate` REWRITES a fragment's
        # body from its authored input, and `instruments` APPENDS subsections to that same fragment —
        # so running migrate after instruments deleted every appended subsection SILENTLY. The two
        # modes were not order-safe and nothing reported the loss: measured 2026-09-21, three fragments
        # carried `authored_for` with `patched_for: None`, which is what "the append was wiped, or was
        # never made, and no record can tell you which" looks like. So the rewrite now RE-APPLIES the
        # appends that were present before it, and REFUSES if it is about to drop one it cannot read.
        body = block.body
        restored: list[str] = []
        if existing is not None:
            tail = existing["body"]
            for append_fragment, append_name in INSTRUMENT_APPENDS:
                if append_fragment != fragment_id:
                    continue
                append_path = INPUT_DIR / append_name
                if not append_path.exists():
                    print(f"   REFUSED   {fragment_id} carries {append_name}, whose input is gone, so "
                          "restoring it is impossible — writing would silently delete it")
                    return 1
                addition = append_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
                marker = addition.lstrip("\n").split("\n", 1)[0]
                if marker in tail and marker not in body:
                    body = body.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n" + addition.lstrip("\n")
                    restored.append(append_name)

        record = {
            "fragment_id": fragment_id,
            "order": order,
            "section": block.section,
            "body": body,
            "block_sha256": sha256_hex(body.encode("utf-8")),
            "lines": f"0-{body.count(chr(10))}  (appended; span is indicative only)",
            "authored_from": f"seasons/impl/doctrine_input/ (sha256 {source_hash[:12]}...)",
            "authored_for": AUTHORED_FOR,
            "status": "[O] proposed" if block.section.startswith(("29.", "30.")) else "doctrine",
        }
        if restored:
            print(f"   RESTORED  {fragment_id}  {', '.join(restored)}  (a rewrite would have dropped "
                  "them; migrate and instruments are now order-safe)")
        if existing is None:
            appended.append(fragment_id)
        elif existing["body"] != body:
            record["revisions"] = existing.get("revisions", 0) + 1
            updated.append(fragment_id)
        else:
            record["revisions"] = existing.get("revisions", 0)
            unchanged.append(fragment_id)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    if appended:
        print(f"   APPENDED  {', '.join(appended)}")
    if updated:
        print(f"   UPDATED   {', '.join(updated)}  (authored input changed since the last run)")
    if unchanged:
        print(f"   UNCHANGED {', '.join(unchanged)}")
    duplicates = _duplicates()
    if duplicates:
        print(f"   DUPLICATE SECTIONS  {duplicates}  <- run `repair`")
        return 1

    def apply(fragment_id: str, anchor: str, replacement: str, label: str, marker: str | None = None) -> None:
        """Replace `anchor` with `replacement` once, and be able to do it AGAIN later.

        THE IDEMPOTENCE KEY IS NOW EXPLICIT, and that is a correction. It used to test
        `replacement[:60] in before`, which is a heuristic with two failure modes, and this pass hit
        both:

          * a replacement that BEGINS WITH ITS OWN ANCHOR — an append, or an update to a row that
            shares a prefix with it — was reported "already applied" the FIRST time it ran, so the
            patch silently did nothing. That is how the instrument register rows were skipped.
          * an update to a row this tool had already written could never be applied at all, because
            the new value and the old value share their first sixty characters. A tool that cannot
            update its own output twice is the same defect class as the reuse guard in `civilians.py`
            that skipped the refusals on a re-run.

        So a caller may pass `marker`: the exact substring that proves the patch is applied. Where none
        is given the old prefix heuristic stands, because the existing patches that embed their anchor
        depend on it.
        """
        path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fragment_id}.json"
        record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        before = record["body"]
        already = (marker in before) if marker is not None else (replacement[:60] in before)
        if already:
            print(f"   SKIPPED   {fragment_id}  {label} (already applied)")
            return
        record["body"] = before.replace(anchor, replacement, 1)
        record["block_sha256"] = sha256_hex(record["body"].encode("utf-8"))
        record["lines"] = f"0-{record['body'].count(chr(10))}  (patched; span is indicative only)"
        if AUTHORED_FOR not in record.setdefault("patched_for", []):
            record["patched_for"].append(AUTHORED_FOR)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"   PATCHED   {fragment_id}  {label}  +{len(record['body']) - len(before)} bytes")

    # Each table's entries may carry a third element: the marker that proves the patch is applied.
    # Unpacked here rather than at every declaration, so a patch that needs one says so in one place.
    def run(table, fragment_id: str, label: str) -> None:
        for entry in table:
            anchor, replacement, *rest = entry
            apply(fragment_id, anchor, replacement, label, rest[0] if rest else None)

    for entry in PATCHES:
        fragment_id, anchor, replacement, *rest = entry
        apply(fragment_id, anchor, replacement, "civilian pointer", rest[0] if rest else None)
    run(PREAMBLE_PATCHES, "frag_01", "falsified claim about this file")
    run(REGISTER_PATCHES, "frag_12", "re-measured register row")
    return 0


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The founding instruments (§27.18, rules 101-108, and the questions they leave open)
#
# These are SUBSUBSECTIONS of sections that already exist, so they are APPENDED TO A FRAGMENT
# rather than migrated as new top-level sections. Appending has no anchor, and that is the point: an
# anchor is a string that must exist exactly once, and the tail of a fragment is the one position that
# cannot drift when earlier text is edited. The idempotence check is the heading itself, so a second
# run reports SKIPPED instead of writing the subsection twice — which is the failure the first version
# of this tool made at the section level (see `_target_for`).
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

INSTRUMENT_APPENDS: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...] = (
    ("frag_29", "civilians_2718.md"),          # §27.18
    ("frag_31", "civilians_rules_101.md"),     # §29, rules 101-108
    ("frag_32", "civilians_30_instruments.md"),  # §30.6
    # The third instrument — appended AFTER the three above, so a run of `instruments` applies them in
    # document order and each append lands at the tail of its fragment. Order matters here in a way it
    # did not before: the §27.18 append ends with a paragraph about the enacted instruments, and the new
    # subsections below it must follow that paragraph rather than split it.
    ("frag_29", "civilians_2718_third.md"),        # §27.18, the farewell counsel
    ("frag_31", "civilians_rules_109.md"),        # §29, rules 109-111
    ("frag_32", "civilians_30_third.md"),        # §30.7
    # THE PROGRESSION INSTRUMENTS. Twelve bills were enacted, three of them in classes the vocabulary
    # did not have, so the widening and the twelve are recorded in the SAME subsection that established
    # that a founding document grants nothing — because the widening is the answer to a question that
    # subsection raised and left open: what do you do with a document the vocabulary cannot type?
    #
    # Appended last, so it follows the third instrument's subsections rather than splitting them.
    ("frag_29", "civilians_2718_pipeline.md"),     # §27.18, the progression instruments and the widening
    # THE CITY PLAN AND THE IDLE JOB LAYER USED TO BE AN ENTRY HERE, AND ITS REMOVAL IS THE POINT.
    #
    # It read `("frag_33", "city_jobs.md")`, and it was wrong in BOTH halves by the time anyone looked:
    #
    #   the NAME     city_jobs.md does not exist. The input is `city_jobs_layer.md`, and a declared path
    #                that does not exist is rule 31's defect - the one this corpus keeps finding in prose
    #                and had now written into a constant. `status` could not run at all while it stood,
    #                which is how it surfaced: a crash, not a silent wrong answer, and only because this
    #                mode reads the file on every call.
    #   the FRAGMENT frag_33 is §31. §32 and §33 were SPLIT onto frag_34 and frag_35 when the partition
    #                invariant (one fragment per block) forced two sections apart, and §33 is already
    #                present in frag_35.
    #
    # **AND THE OBVIOUS FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN THE WORSE BUG.** Correcting only the filename leaves a
    # liveness anchor pointing at the wrong fragment, and the append's marker (`## 33. The idle job
    # layer...`) is ABSENT from frag_33 - so the run would have found the marker missing, concluded the
    # append had not landed, and written §33's full text into §31. Measured before the edit: marker in
    # frag_35 True, marker in frag_33 False, which is exactly the pair of readings that makes a
    # name-only fix destructive. An anchor that is stale in its id tests as "not yet done" forever.
    #
    # So the entry is REMOVED rather than repaired, and the removal is recorded here rather than in a
    # commit message: the section authoring in `city_doctrine.py` now owns §32 and §33, one fragment
    # each, and a second tool appending the same text is the two-writers-one-region defect this module
    # already carries a scar from.
)


def _instruments() -> int:
    ok = True
    for fragment_id, name in INSTRUMENT_APPENDS:
        path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fragment_id}.json"
        if not path.exists():
            print(f"   REFUSED   {fragment_id} does not exist")
            ok = False
            continue
        record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        addition = (INPUT_DIR / name).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        if not addition.endswith("\n"):
            addition += "\n"
        # The heading is the marker: every input file begins with one, and it is the only part of the
        # text that is guaranteed unique inside the fragment.
        marker = addition.lstrip("\n").split("\n", 1)[0]
        if marker in record["body"]:
            print(f"   SKIPPED   {fragment_id}  {marker[:64]!r} (already applied)")
            continue
        if record.get("authored_for") not in (AUTHORED_FOR, None) and "patched_for" not in record:
            print(f"   REFUSED   {fragment_id} was not authored or patched here; refusing to append")
            ok = False
            continue
        before = record["body"]
        body = before.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n" + addition.lstrip("\n")
        record["body"] = body
        record["block_sha256"] = sha256_hex(body.encode("utf-8"))
        record["lines"] = f"0-{body.count(chr(10))}  (appended; span is indicative only)"
        record.setdefault("patched_for", [])
        if AUTHORED_FOR not in record["patched_for"]:
            record["patched_for"].append(AUTHORED_FOR)
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"   APPENDED  {fragment_id}  {marker[:56]!r}  +{len(body) - len(before)} bytes")
    if ok:
        print("   now run: python migrate.py rebuild")
    return 0 if ok else 1


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    mode = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if mode == "status":
        return _status()
    if mode == "migrate":
        return _migrate()
    if mode == "repair":
        return _repair()
    if mode == "instruments":
        return _instruments()
    print("   usage: python civilians_doctrine.py [status|migrate|repair|instruments]")
    return 2


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

#### `godplan/plans.py`

```python
"""The overlay's plan store, its pure adjudicator, and its convergent situation digest.

Specification: AGENTS.md section 31 — **the overlay is a LENS, never a legislator.**
Design input: the corrected `3DUI.MD` v2 and `Civilians_lifestyle_UI_Implementation_plan.md`,
with FC-3D-01 .. FC-3D-15 applied.

THE INVARIANT, stated once because everything here derives from it:

    The moment this module DECIDES a control's status, STAMPS a ticket, ASSIGNS a locus into
    the civilians store, or CREATES / PROMOTES / RETIRES a civilian, it has left the lens and
    violated section 19.4.

So the shape is forced:

  * `adjudicate()` is a PURE function of `(proposal, DoctrineSnapshot, StoreSnapshot)`. It
    mutates nothing it is given — `PlanProposal` and the snapshot tuples are frozen, so
    purity is structural rather than promised, and a test checks it over a generated batch.
  * Every player action is a `PlanProposal`, persisted in a SEPARATE, explicitly
    NON-AUTHORITATIVE store rooted at `seasons/plans/`. The civilian store and the doctrine
    store are never written by anything in this module.
  * `PlanStore.save()` refuses any path that resolves inside the civilians store, the doctrine
    store, or the god file. **The guard is code, not a convention** (rule 43).
  * A control's status is READ from `civilians.analyze()`'s `_mechanical_status` output and is
    never recomputed here. Placing or removing a service node changes no status; the test
    `test_node_removal_changes_no_status` is what holds that, and it is the test that would
    fail if this module ever started deciding.
  * An ANSWERED decision renders as answered because the DOCTRINE declares it answered
    (`civilians.ANSWERED_DECISIONS`), not because the view inferred it from the options text.
    FC-3D-15 in section 31.3 is the finding: the layer carried no answered flag, so a view
    that wanted the distinction would have had to decide it. The flag now exists as data.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO. There is no persisted governed merge of a plan into doctrine, no
identity verification (R7 / rule 100), and no resolution of any open C* or fog item. Those are
silver and above, and section 31.5 lists them as explicit non-goals rather than omissions.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from dataclasses import dataclass, field, fields, is_dataclass
from enum import Enum
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Mapping, Sequence

from .canonical import jcs, sha256_hex
from .idle import derive_idle_jobs, idle_summary, idle_yield
from .civilians import (
    ANSWERED_DECISIONS,
    AUTONOMY_MODES,
    BILLING_BASES,
    CIVILIAN_DECISIONS,
    CivilianStore,
    FOG_ITEMS,
    JOB_END_REASONS,
    NEVER_GRANTED,
    OUT_OF_SCOPE,
    RESIDUAL_RISKS,
    _refused_records,
    analyze,
)
from .reconstruct import DOCTRINE_DIR, GOD_FILE

# parents[0]=godplan [1]=impl [2]=seasons [3]=the project root. An earlier version used
# parents[2] as the PROJECT root, which made PLANS_ROOT resolve to `seasons/seasons/plans` and
# made CIVILIANS_ROOT name a directory that does not exist — so the write guard was guarding the
# wrong path and `overlay.py seed` wrote one level too deep. The CLI output is what caught it, and
# `test_the_guard_names_the_real_civilians_root` is the test that now holds it.
SEASONS_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
PROJECT_ROOT = SEASONS_ROOT.parent
PLANS_ROOT = SEASONS_ROOT / "plans"
CIVILIANS_ROOT = SEASONS_ROOT / "civilians"

# Anything a plan must never be able to reach. Kept as an explicit tuple so the guard is auditable
# and cannot quietly grow into "paths I found inconvenient" (the store.py lesson).
PROTECTED_ROOTS: tuple[Path, ...] = (CIVILIANS_ROOT, DOCTRINE_DIR, GOD_FILE)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Refusals — a first-class outcome, per section 17 rule 3
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class RefusedPlan(Exception):
    """Base for every refusal in the overlay. A refusal is a decision, not an error."""


class RefusedStoreWrite(RefusedPlan):
    """The plan store was pointed at a protected root. There is no write path there."""


class RefusedAuthorityClaim(RefusedPlan):
    """A plan tried to assert authority. Plans propose; Governor Base authorises."""


class RefusedForbiddenField(RefusedPlan):
    """A field the doctrine does not have, and that a governed merge would be needed to add."""


class RefusedUnnamedBasis(RefusedPlan):
    """An income allocation that does not name its basis (C01's vocabulary)."""


class RefusedNeverGranted(RefusedPlan):
    """A plan would carry one of the five never-granted actions."""


class RefusedOutOfScope(RefusedPlan):
    """A plan would cross a section 30.3 wall."""


class RefusedResolution(RefusedPlan):
    """A plan tried to resolve an open — or an already ANSWERED — doctrine question."""


class RefusedControlDecision(RefusedPlan):
    """A plan tried to set a control's status. C9-C20 are read, never decided."""


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The forbidden-field vocabulary
#
# Section 15.1 of the overlay plan, and section 27 of the pillar. Each entry is a field the
# doctrine does NOT have. `balance` is forbidden because C09 is ANSWERED (a balance is a
# derived view); the housing fields are forbidden because no such schema exists — the
# disposition recorded in section 31.4, where `house.md` is the physical reference that shows
# how much machinery a real dwelling needs and confirms none of it is in this pillar.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


FORBIDDEN_FIELDS: tuple[str, ...] = (
    "dwelling_id",
    "capacity",
    "quality_tier",
    "housing",
    "housing_ref",
    "balance",
    "stored_balance",
    "reputation",
    "skill_score",
    "tax",
    "salary",
    "payroll",
)

FORBIDDEN_FIELD_REASON: dict[str, str] = {
    "dwelling_id": "no housing schema exists (section 27, FC-3D-06); a real dwelling is a physical assembly, see house.md",
    "capacity": "co-location is fog (section 30.2); inventing capacity resolves a fog item by assumption",
    "quality_tier": "not in any schema; locus height is the GRADE step, not a quality tier",
    "housing": "no housing schema exists",
    "housing_ref": "no housing schema exists",
    "balance": "C09 is ANSWERED: a balance is a derived view over the income ledger",
    "stored_balance": "C09 is ANSWERED: a stored balance is a second source of truth",
    "reputation": "section 30.3 out of scope, and rule 6 forbids scalar skill ratings",
    "skill_score": "rule 6 — no scalar skill ratings, ever",
    "tax": "section 30.3 wall; no statutes here",
    "salary": "a civilian earns per ticket against a job rate, not a salary",
    "payroll": "section 30.3 wall; money is integers and a civilian is not an employee",
}


def refuse_forbidden_fields(node: Any, _path: str = "$") -> None:
    """Refuse any forbidden field NAME or KEY anywhere in a proposal or view model."""
    if isinstance(node, Mapping):
        for key, value in node.items():
            if isinstance(key, str) and key in FORBIDDEN_FIELDS:
                raise RefusedForbiddenField(
                    f"{_path}.{key}: {FORBIDDEN_FIELD_REASON[key]}. A PR adding this field is "
                    "refused without a governed merge (rule 65)"
                )
            refuse_forbidden_fields(value, f"{_path}.{key}")
    elif isinstance(node, (list, tuple)):
        for i, value in enumerate(node):
            refuse_forbidden_fields(value, f"{_path}[{i}]")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The plan side — proposals. All frozen: purity is structural, not promised.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class ZoneKind(Enum):
    """Six zone kinds, each mapped to a REAL field. No housing, no commercial, no industrial."""

    JOB = "job"                    # keyed to `job` / `JOB_CLASSES`

    EVIDENCE = "evidence"          # income record, C13/C16
    RETIREMENT = "retirement"      # retirement record, section 8.5 taxonomy

ZONE_KANJI: dict[ZoneKind, str] = {

    ZoneKind.GENESIS: "\u5275",     # so — genesis

}

ZONE_DOCTRINE_ANCHOR: dict[ZoneKind, str] = {

# kind -> class, populated once the classes below exist. Declared here so the `.update(...)`
# after `ResolveProposal` has something to update: placing the declaration BELOW the update threw
# `NameError: _PROPOSAL_BY_KIND is not defined`, which is the module failing to import at all.
_PROPOSAL_BY_KIND: dict[str, type] = {}


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ZoneProposal:
    zone: ZoneKind
    tiles: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]
    note: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class NodeProposal:
    node: NodeKind
    tile: tuple[int, int]
    note: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class PathProposal:
    start: tuple[int, int]
    end: tuple[int, int]
    carries: str
    note: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class BudgetProposal:
    basis: str | None
    weight: int
    note: str = ""


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class InspectProposal:
    entity_ref: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ResolveProposal:
    question_id: str


_PROPOSAL_BY_KIND.update(
    {
        "ZoneProposal": ZoneProposal,
        "NodeProposal": NodeProposal,
        "PathProposal": PathProposal,
        "BudgetProposal": BudgetProposal,
        "InspectProposal": InspectProposal,
        "ResolveProposal": ResolveProposal,
    }
)


PlanProposal = (
    ZoneProposal | NodeProposal | PathProposal | BudgetProposal | InspectProposal | ResolveProposal
)


def proposal_dict(proposal: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Canonical JSON view of a proposal. Used for hashing and for the forbidden-field scan."""
    if not is_dataclass(proposal):
        raise RefusedPlan(f"{type(proposal).__name__} is not a PlanProposal")
    out: dict[str, Any] = {"kind": type(proposal).__name__}
    for f in fields(proposal):
        value = getattr(proposal, f.name)
        out[f.name] = value.value if isinstance(value, Enum) else value
    return out


def proposal_id(proposal: Any) -> str:
    """Content-addressed, so re-proposing the same plan is the SAME plan (rule 77's discipline)."""
    return "plan_" + sha256_hex(jcs(_jsonable(proposal_dict(proposal))))[:12]


def proposal_from_dict(data: Mapping[str, Any]) -> "PlanProposal":
    """Rehydrate a proposal from its stored form.

    The plan store is JSON, so a loaded proposal is a dict until it is rehydrated. Without this,
    `build_view` would be handed dicts and `adjudicate` would refuse them — which is what happened:
    `overlay.py view` raised `dict is not a PlanProposal`. Coercion is explicit per class rather
    than inferred from annotations, because an inferred coercion would silently accept a wrong
    shape and the whole point of this module is that nothing is accepted by accident.
    """
    kind = str(data.get("kind", ""))
    cls = _PROPOSAL_BY_KIND.get(kind)
    if cls is None:
        raise RefusedPlan(f"{kind!r} is not a PlanProposal this system knows (rule 65)")
    if cls is ZoneProposal:
        return ZoneProposal(
            zone=ZoneKind(str(data["zone"])), tiles=tuple(tuple(t) for t in data["tiles"]), note=str(data.get("note", ""))
        )
    if cls is NodeProposal:
        return NodeProposal(
            node=NodeKind(str(data["node"])), tile=tuple(data["tile"]), note=str(data.get("note", ""))
        )
    if cls is PathProposal:
        return PathProposal(
            start=tuple(data["start"]), end=tuple(data["end"]), carries=str(data["carries"]), note=str(data.get("note", ""))
        )
    if cls is BudgetProposal:
        basis = data.get("basis")
        return BudgetProposal(
            basis=None if basis is None else str(basis), weight=int(data.get("weight", 0)), note=str(data.get("note", ""))
        )
    if cls is InspectProposal:
        return InspectProposal(entity_ref=str(data.get("entity_ref", "")))
    return ResolveProposal(question_id=str(data.get("question_id", "")))


def _jsonable(value: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(value, Enum):
        return value.value
    if isinstance(value, tuple):
        return [_jsonable(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, Mapping):
        return {str(k): _jsonable(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_jsonable(v) for v in value]
    return value


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The view side — walls and fog, mapped from doctrine, never invented
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

GRID = 24


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Region:
    """A view-only rectangle. `label` is doctrine text; `kanji` is chrome (pillar P4)."""

    region_id: str
    kind: str  # "wall" | "fog"
    kanji: str
    label: str
    citation: str
    x0: int
    y0: int
    x1: int
    y1: int

    def contains(self, tile: tuple[int, int]) -> bool:
        x, y = tile
        return self.x0 <= x <= self.x1 and self.y0 <= y <= self.y1


_WALL_KANJI = (
    ("payroll", "\u7d66"),  # 給
    ("tax", "\u7a0e"),      # 税
    ("benefit", "\u76ca"),  # 益
    ("guild", "\u7d44"),    # 組
    ("reputation", "\u8a55"),  # 評
    ("market", "\u5e02"),   # 市
)

_FOG_KANJI = ("\u5951", "\u8077", "\u627f", "\u6587", "\u8a3a", "\u5f15")


def _kanji_for(label: str, table: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...], fallback: str) -> str:
    low = label.lower()
    for needle, glyph in table:
        if needle in low:
            return glyph
    return fallback


def regions(snapshot: "DoctrineSnapshot | None" = None) -> tuple[Region, ...]:
    """The wall and fog layout, as a PURE FUNCTION OF DOCTRINE.

    Walls come one-per section 30.3 out-of-scope item, as a band along the northern edge.
    Fog comes one-per section 30.2 item, as interior blobs. Neither set is chosen here: the
    count is `len(OUT_OF_SCOPE)` and `len(FOG_ITEMS)`, so a doctrine change moves the geometry
    and the view cannot drift from it. The positions are a stated view mapping (chrome), which
    is why they live in this module and not in doctrine.
    """
    walls: list[Region] = []
    for i, label in enumerate(OUT_OF_SCOPE):
        x0 = 1 + i * 4
        walls.append(
            Region(
                region_id=f"wall_{i + 1:02d}",
                kind="wall",
                kanji=_kanji_for(label, _WALL_KANJI, "\u58c1"),
                label=label,
                citation="section 30.3 out of scope",
                x0=x0,
                y0=0,
                x1=min(x0 + 2, GRID - 1),
                y1=0,
            )
        )
    # Fog sits in two rows BELOW the buildable area, so the ward the player plans in starts clear.
    # Sizing is a view decision (chrome); the COUNT is `len(FOG_ITEMS)`, so doctrine still drives it.
    fog: list[Region] = []
    for i, label in enumerate(FOG_ITEMS):
        x0 = 2 + (i % 3) * 7
        y0 = 13 + (i // 3) * 7
        fog.append(
            Region(
                region_id=f"fog_{i + 1:02d}",
                kind="fog",
                kanji=_FOG_KANJI[i % len(_FOG_KANJI)],
                label=label,
                citation="section 30.2 fog of war",
                x0=x0,
                y0=y0,
                x1=min(x0 + 2, GRID - 1),
                y1=min(y0 + 2, GRID - 1),
            )
        )
    return tuple(walls) + tuple(fog)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Snapshots — what the adjudicator is allowed to see
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ControlStatus:
    control: str
    requirement: str
    mechanical_status: str
    identity_status: str


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DoctrineSnapshot:
    """Everything the adjudicator may read from doctrine. Immutable by construction."""

    doctrine_hash: str
    sections: tuple[str, ...]
    answered_decisions: frozenset[str]
    open_decisions: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]          # (id, question)
    fog: tuple[str, ...]
    out_of_scope: tuple[str, ...]
    never_granted: tuple[str, ...]
    billing_bases: tuple[str, ...]
    autonomy_modes: tuple[str, ...]
    job_end_reasons: tuple[str, ...]
    residual_risks: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]
    control_status: tuple[ControlStatus, ...]
    regions: tuple[Region, ...]

    @property
    def mechanical_distribution(self) -> dict[str, int]:
        out: dict[str, int] = {}
        for row in self.control_status:
            out[row.mechanical_status] = out.get(row.mechanical_status, 0) + 1
        return out

    def decision_ids(self) -> tuple[str, ...]:
        return tuple(sorted({d for d, _ in self.open_decisions} | set(self.answered_decisions)))


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class StoreSnapshot:
    """Everything the adjudicator may read from the civilians store. Read-only."""

    store_hash: str
    civilians: tuple[str, ...]
    jobs: tuple[str, ...]
    tickets: tuple[str, ...]
    orders: tuple[str, ...]                    # distinct proposer names
    authorizers: tuple[str, ...]               # distinct authorizer names
    verifiers: tuple[str, ...]                 # distinct income verifier names
    promotions: tuple[str, ...]
    retirements: tuple[str, ...]
    refused: tuple[str, ...]                   # ids the store refuses ON PURPOSE
    events: int
    record_count: int

    def has_distinct_authorizer(self, proposer: str | None = None) -> bool:
        """A distinct authorizer exists when at least one authorizer name is not the proposer."""
        return any(name != proposer for name in self.authorizers)


def _digest(value: Any) -> str:
    return sha256_hex(jcs(_jsonable(value)))


def doctrine_snapshot(store: CivilianStore | None = None) -> DoctrineSnapshot:
    """Build the doctrine snapshot from the live layer. Reads only; the hash covers the content."""
    civic = store if store is not None else CivilianStore.load()
    analysis = analyze(civic)
    answered = frozenset(ANSWERED_DECISIONS)
    open_decisions = tuple(
        (d[0], d[1]) for d in CIVILIAN_DECISIONS if d[0] not in answered
    )
    controls = tuple(
        ControlStatus(
            control=row["control"],
            requirement=row["requirement"],
            mechanical_status=row["mechanical_status"],
            identity_status=row["identity_status"],
        )
        for row in analysis["controls"]
    )
    sections = tuple(
        sorted(
            {
                p.name
                for p in DOCTRINE_DIR.glob("*.json")
                if _fragment_mentions_civilians(p)
            }
        )
    )
    snap = DoctrineSnapshot(
        doctrine_hash="",
        sections=sections,
        answered_decisions=answered,
        open_decisions=open_decisions,
        fog=tuple(FOG_ITEMS),
        out_of_scope=tuple(OUT_OF_SCOPE),
        never_granted=tuple(NEVER_GRANTED),
        billing_bases=tuple(BILLING_BASES),
        autonomy_modes=tuple(AUTONOMY_MODES),
        job_end_reasons=tuple(JOB_END_REASONS),
        residual_risks=tuple((r[0], r[1]) for r in RESIDUAL_RISKS),
        control_status=controls,
        regions=regions(),
    )
    return _replace_hash(snap)


def _replace_hash(snap: DoctrineSnapshot) -> DoctrineSnapshot:
    payload = {
        "answered": sorted(snap.answered_decisions),
        "open": list(snap.open_decisions),
        "fog": list(snap.fog),
        "out_of_scope": list(snap.out_of_scope),
        "never_granted": list(snap.never_granted),
        "billing_bases": list(snap.billing_bases),
        "controls": [(c.control, c.mechanical_status, c.identity_status) for c in snap.control_status],
        "regions": [(r.region_id, r.kind, r.x0, r.y0, r.x1, r.y1) for r in snap.regions],
    }
    from dataclasses import replace as _dc_replace

    return _dc_replace(snap, doctrine_hash=_digest(payload))


def _fragment_mentions_civilians(path: Path) -> bool:
    try:
        data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    except (OSError, json.JSONDecodeError):
        return False
    section = str(data.get("section", ""))
    return section.startswith(("27.", "28.", "29.", "30.", "31."))


def store_snapshot(store: CivilianStore | None = None) -> StoreSnapshot:
    """Build the store snapshot. Reads only; never writes."""
    civic = store if store is not None else CivilianStore.load()
    civic.validate()
    recs = civic.records
    civilians = tuple(sorted(k for k in recs if k.startswith("civilian_")))
    jobs = tuple(sorted(k for k in recs if k.startswith("job_")))
    tickets = tuple(sorted(k for k in recs if k.startswith("ticket_")))
    promotions = tuple(sorted(k for k in recs if k.startswith("promotion_")))
    retirements = tuple(sorted(k for k in recs if k.startswith("retirement_")))
    orders: set[str] = set()
    authorizers: set[str] = set()
    verifiers: set[str] = set()
    for kind_keys, keys in (("promotion", promotions), ("genesis", tuple(sorted(k for k in recs if k.startswith("genesis_"))))):
        for key in keys:
            rec = recs.get(key, {})
            for fname in ("proposed_by", "authorized_by", "authorizer", "proposer"):
                val = rec.get(fname)
                if isinstance(val, str):
                    (orders if fname in ("proposed_by", "proposer") else authorizers).add(val)
    for key in sorted(k for k in recs if k.startswith("income_")):
        val = recs.get(key, {}).get("verified_by")
        if isinstance(val, str):
            verifiers.add(val)
    for key in jobs:
        val = recs.get(key, {}).get("supervisor_id")
        if isinstance(val, str):
            authorizers.add(val)
    # Refused records STAY in the store (rule 65), so this reports them rather than filtering.
    # They are the tutorial's first lesson: a refusal is data (section 9.2 of the overlay plan).
    refused = tuple(sorted(stem for stem, _reason in _refused_records(civic)))
    snap = StoreSnapshot(
        store_hash=sha256_hex(jcs(_jsonable((sorted(recs), sorted(civic.events, key=lambda e: str(e)))))),
        civilians=civilians,
        jobs=jobs,
        tickets=tickets,
        orders=tuple(sorted(orders)),
        authorizers=tuple(sorted(authorizers)),
        verifiers=tuple(sorted(verifiers)),
        promotions=promotions,
        retirements=retirements,
        refused=refused,
        events=len(civic.events),
        record_count=len(recs),
    )
    return snap


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The adjudication — three outcomes, and never a fourth
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AcceptedView:
    """Consistent with the current view. No store mutation; the plan store may highlight tiles."""

    highlighted_tiles: tuple[tuple[int, int], ...]
    note: str

    kind = "accepted_view"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Deferred:
    """An open question, an answered question, or a fog region applies. Surfaces a ticket."""

    decision_ticket: str
    reason: str

    kind = "deferred"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Rejected:
    """A rule forbids this. A citation is mandatory."""

    citation: str
    rule: str

    kind = "rejected"


Adjudication = AcceptedView | Deferred | Rejected


def _decode(value: Any) -> Any:
    if isinstance(value, tuple):
        return [_decode(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [_decode(v) for v in value]
    return value


def adjudicate(
    proposal: PlanProposal,
    doctrine: DoctrineSnapshot,
    store: StoreSnapshot,
) -> Adjudication:
    """PURE. Deterministic. Mutates nothing. Returns an outcome; never a store write.

    The rule order is deliberate: a proposal is checked for forbidden fields first, because a
    proposal carrying a field the doctrine does not have is a scope-widening attempt and must
    not be reasoned about any further.
    """
    refuse_forbidden_fields(proposal_dict(proposal))

    if isinstance(proposal, ResolveProposal):
        return _adjudicate_resolve(proposal, doctrine)
    if isinstance(proposal, InspectProposal):
        return AcceptedView((), f"read-only inspection of {proposal.entity_ref}")
    if isinstance(proposal, BudgetProposal):
        return _adjudicate_budget(proposal, doctrine)
    if isinstance(proposal, PathProposal):
        return _adjudicate_path(proposal, doctrine, store)
    if isinstance(proposal, NodeProposal):
        return _adjudicate_node(proposal, doctrine)
    if isinstance(proposal, ZoneProposal):
        return _adjudicate_zone(proposal, doctrine, store)
    raise RefusedPlan(f"{type(proposal).__name__} is not a PlanProposal this system knows")


# -- one rule per proposal kind -------------------------------------------------------


def _adjudicate_resolve(proposal: ResolveProposal, doctrine: DoctrineSnapshot) -> Adjudication:
    """A resolution is a governed merge. The overlay has no resolve button."""
    qid = proposal.question_id
    if qid in doctrine.answered_decisions:
        return Rejected(
            citation="section 30.1",
            rule=(
                f"{qid} is ANSWERED. Re-opening an answered question is how an answered question "
                "gets re-opened; the overlay quotes the answer and offers no resolution"
            ),
        )
    if qid in {d for d, _ in doctrine.open_decisions}:
        return Deferred(
            decision_ticket=qid,
            reason=(
                f"{qid} is OPEN. Resolution is a governed merge and lives outside the overlay "
                "(section 19.4); the plan is deferred to the decision ticket"
            ),
        )
    return Rejected(
        citation="section 30.1 / 30.6",
        rule=f"{qid} is not a decision this system carries; an invented question id is a defect (rule 65)",
    )


def _adjudicate_budget(proposal: BudgetProposal, doctrine: DoctrineSnapshot) -> Adjudication:
    if proposal.basis is None or proposal.basis == "":
        raise RefusedUnnamedBasis(
            "an income allocation must name its basis. While C01 is open the four bases are a "
            f"VOCABULARY ({', '.join(doctrine.billing_bases)}), and an unnamed basis is refused "
            "because the vocabulary exists precisely so it can be"
        )
    if proposal.basis not in doctrine.billing_bases:
        return Rejected(
            citation="section 30.1 C01",
            rule=f"{proposal.basis!r} is not one of the four billing bases; C01 is open and the vocabulary is closed",
        )
    if proposal.weight < 0:
        return Rejected(citation="section 30.1 C01", rule="a negative allocation is not an allocation")
    return AcceptedView(
        (),
        f"allocation over {proposal.basis} recorded as a PROPOSAL; C01 is open, so no rate is applied "
        "and no balance is stored (C09 ANSWERED: balance is a derived view)",
    )


def _adjudicate_path(
    proposal: PathProposal, doctrine: DoctrineSnapshot, store: StoreSnapshot
) -> Adjudication:
    if proposal.carries in doctrine.never_granted:
        return Rejected(
            citation="section 9.6 rule 3",
            rule=(
                f"{proposal.carries!r} is one of the five never-granted actions. A task that needs it "
                "becomes a GATE FOR A HUMAN; the task is not silently skipped and the overlay never grants it"
            ),
        )
    crossed = _crossings(proposal, doctrine.regions)
    wall = next((r for r in crossed if r.kind == "wall"), None)
    if wall is not None:
        return Rejected(citation=wall.citation, rule=f"the path crosses the {wall.label!r} wall (section 30.3)")
    fog = next((r for r in crossed if r.kind == "fog"), None)
    if fog is not None:
        return Deferred(
            decision_ticket="fog",
            reason=f"the path crosses a fog region: {fog.label}",
        )
    return AcceptedView((), f"authority path visualised as carrying {proposal.carries!r}; it moves nothing")


def _adjudicate_node(proposal: NodeProposal, doctrine: DoctrineSnapshot) -> Adjudication:
    wall = next((r for r in doctrine.regions if r.kind == "wall" and r.contains(proposal.tile)), None)
    if wall is not None:
        return Rejected(
            citation=wall.citation,
            rule=f"a service node cannot stand on the {wall.label!r} wall; it is out of scope (section 30.3)",
        )
    fog = next((r for r in doctrine.regions if r.kind == "fog" and r.contains(proposal.tile)), None)
    if fog is not None:
        return Deferred(
            decision_ticket="fog",
            reason=f"a service node in a fog region would be asserting an answer: {fog.label}",
        )
    return AcceptedView(
        (proposal.tile,),
        f"{NODE_VISUAL_ONLY[proposal.node]} \u2014 and {NODE_MUST_NOT[proposal.node]}. "
        "Placing this node changes no mechanical status",
    )


def _adjudicate_zone(
    proposal: ZoneProposal, doctrine: DoctrineSnapshot, store: StoreSnapshot
) -> Adjudication:
    if not proposal.tiles:
        return Rejected(citation="section 31.2", rule="a zone with no tiles is a proposal to do nothing")
    wall = next(
        (r for r in doctrine.regions if r.kind == "wall" and any(r.contains(t) for t in proposal.tiles)),
        None,
    )
    if wall is not None:
        return Rejected(
            citation=wall.citation,
            rule=(
                f"the zone touches the {wall.label!r} wall. Zoning across an out-of-scope boundary is "
                "refused with a citation, not deferred"
            ),
        )
    fog = next(
        (r for r in doctrine.regions if r.kind == "fog" and any(r.contains(t) for t in proposal.tiles)),
        None,
    )
    if fog is not None:
        return Deferred(
            decision_ticket="fog",
            reason=f"the zone touches a fog region and is deferred, never pre-sliced: {fog.label}",
        )
    # A zone whose class of work needs a distinct authorizer that the store does not hold.
    if proposal.zone in (ZoneKind.GENESIS, ZoneKind.AUTHORITY) and not store.has_distinct_authorizer():
        return Deferred(
            decision_ticket="C17" if proposal.zone is ZoneKind.GENESIS else "C15",
            reason=(
                "the store holds no authorizer distinct from the proposer, so the ARROW the zone would "
                "draw does not exist. Rule 97: a promotion requires a distinct authorizer, and rule 62 "
                "extends the same requirement to a genesis"
            ),
        )
    if proposal.zone in (ZoneKind.EVIDENCE,) and not store.verifiers:
        return Deferred(
            decision_ticket="C16",
            reason="the store holds no governor-actor verifier, so an evidence locus would highlight nothing",
        )
    return AcceptedView(
        tuple(sorted(proposal.tiles)),
        f"{proposal.zone.value} locus proposed over {len(proposal.tiles)} tile(s), anchored to "
        f"{ZONE_DOCTRINE_ANCHOR[proposal.zone]}. ACCEPTED AS A VIEW: this assigns no locus into the "
        "store and creates no entity. The next ingestion pass re-derives which REAL loci fall inside "
        "the highlight, and the player sees the overlap",
    )


def _crossings(proposal: PathProposal, regs: Sequence[Region]) -> tuple[Region, ...]:
    """Sample the path over its bounding box; deterministic, and deliberately coarse."""
    x0, y0 = proposal.start
    x1, y1 = proposal.end
    lo_x, hi_x = sorted((x0, x1))
    lo_y, hi_y = sorted((y0, y1))
    hits: list[Region] = []
    for r in regs:
        if r.x1 < lo_x or r.x0 > hi_x or r.y1 < lo_y or r.y0 > hi_y:
            continue
        hits.append(r)
    return tuple(hits)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The view — a derived render model. Read-only, and it reads rather than decides.
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def build_view(
    store: CivilianStore | None = None,
    plan: Sequence[Any] = (),
    doctrine: DoctrineSnapshot | None = None,
    tick: int = 0,
) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The city view: a PURE function of `(store, plan, doctrine, tick)`.

    Control statuses are copied from the doctrine snapshot, which copied them from
    `civilians.analyze()`. Nothing in `plan` can change one — that is what
    `test_node_removal_changes_no_status` checks.

    **`tick` is an argument rather than a clock read**, and that is the whole reason the idle layer can
    exist without its fiction reaching a record. `PLAN_JOBS.md` §5 fixes the ordering: a tick advances
    the CLOCK, and the view's idle yields are a function of the tick the view was DERIVED at. So the
    producer writes only when the store or the plan moved, the surface re-reads the view and
    interpolates the rest, and no wall clock is consulted anywhere (§16.1's rule, which is what removed
    `generated_at`). A view that read `time.time()` here would be non-deterministic — two derivations
    over an unchanged store would differ, and the watcher would fire forever on its own output.
    """
    civic = store if store is not None else CivilianStore.load()
    doc = doctrine if doctrine is not None else doctrine_snapshot(civic)
    sn = store_snapshot(civic)
    records = civic.records

    loci = []
    avatars = []
    for cid in sn.civilians:
        rec = records.get(cid, {})
        grade = str(rec.get("unit_grade", "genesis"))
        height = _grade_height(grade)
        jobs = [k for k in sn.jobs if records.get(k, {}).get("civilian_id") == cid]
        loci.append(
            {
                "civilian_id": cid,
                "tile": _tile_for(cid),
                "height": height,
                "occupancy": 1,
                "grade_class": str(rec.get("job_class", "")),
                "job_class_source": "JOB_CLASSES holds the four promotion stages, not a job taxonomy",
                "multi_civilian": False,
            }
        )
        avatars.append(
            {
                "civilian_id": cid,
                "lifecycle_state": str(rec.get("lifecycle_state", "")),
                "unit_grade": grade,
                "certification_tier": str(rec.get("certification_tier", "")),
                "genesis_id": rec.get("genesis_id"),
                "has_job": bool(jobs),
                "income_basis": _income_basis(records, cid),
                "self_witness_genesis": True,
            }
        )

    outcomes = [_adjudication_dict(adjudicate(p, doc, sn)) for p in plan]

    jobs = derive_idle_jobs(records, sn.civilians, tick)

    return {
        # The tick these yields were computed at, carried so a consumer can tell a fresh view from a
        # stale one instead of assuming. It is `0` by default because the DEFAULT is the convergent
        # baseline, and a caller that wants a live reading asks for one explicitly.
        "derived_at_tick": tick,
        "view": "civilian-overlay:city",
        "derived_view": True,
        "authoritative": False,
        "doctrine_hash": doc.doctrine_hash,
        "store_hash": sn.store_hash,
        "grid": {"size": GRID, "projection": "isometric", "tilt": 30, "rotation": 45},
        "loci": loci,
        "avatars": avatars,
        "regions": [
            {
                "region_id": r.region_id,
                "kind": r.kind,
                "kanji": r.kanji,
                "label": r.label,
                "citation": r.citation,
                "rect": [r.x0, r.y0, r.x1, r.y1],
            }
            for r in doc.regions
        ],
        "controls": [
            {
                "control": c.control,
                "requirement": c.requirement,
                "mechanical_status": c.mechanical_status,
                "identity_status": c.identity_status,
            }
            for c in doc.control_status
        ],
        "mechanical_distribution": doc.mechanical_distribution,
        "residual_risks": [{"id": i, "risk": t} for i, t in doc.residual_risks],
        "never_granted": [
            {"action": a, "kanji": k, "citation": "section 9.6 rule 3"}
            for a, k in zip(
                doc.never_granted,
                ("\u53e3", "\u8a8d", "\u9001", "\u540c", "\u5951"),
            )
        ],
        "fog": [r.label for r in doc.regions if r.kind == "fog"],
        "out_of_scope": [r.label for r in doc.regions if r.kind == "wall"],
        "monuments": [
            {
                "id": d,
                "question": q,
                "state": "answered" if d in doc.answered_decisions else "open",
                "resolve_available": False,
                "citation": "section 30.1",
            }
            for d, q in doc.open_decisions
        ]
        + [
            {"id": d, "question": None, "state": "answered", "resolve_available": False, "citation": "section 30.1"}
            for d in sorted(doc.answered_decisions)
        ],
        # THE AUTHORIZED FICTION (PLAN_JOBS.md, section 33). A SEPARATE top-level key, never merged
        # into `loci` — marking rule 2, and the marking is structural rather than described because a
        # fiction counted as a locus would make the civilian count wrong everywhere it is read. Each
        # job cites an anchor that already exists, so the number of idle producers is bounded by the
        # number of real records and the ward cannot grow by fiction (refusal 7).
        "idle_jobs": [
            {
                "idle_id": j.idle_id,
                "kind": j.kind.value,
                "kanji": j.kind.glyph,
                "fiction": True,
                "civilian_id": j.civilian_id,
                "anchor_id": j.anchor_id,
                "tile": list(j.tile),
                "base_yield": j.base_yield,
                "assigned_at_tick": j.assigned_at_tick,
                # The value AT THE TICK THIS VIEW WAS DERIVED AT. A surface may render it directly when
                # its clock is at that tick, and must otherwise compute `base_yield * (clock -
                # assigned_at_tick)` from the components above — because this number goes stale the
                # moment the clock advances and the view is not re-derived, and a stale number shown as
                # current is the read, not the write, that this whole layer is built to avoid.
                "yield_at_derived_tick": idle_yield(j, tick),
                "lens": j.lens,
                "citation": j.citation,
            }
            for j in jobs
        ],
        "idle_summary": idle_summary(jobs, tick),
        "proposals": outcomes,
        "plan_is_authoritative": False,
        # THE SURFACE'S DATA CONTRACT, and the reason this key exists rather than being hardcoded in
        # the renderer. A HUD that must show the four-way billing split (section 8.1, pending C01)
        # needs the four NAMES, and the names live in a doctrine constant that the view did not carry.
        # A surface that spelled them itself would be inventing doctrine — the exact defect section
        # 31.1 names — so the contract carries them instead, with the C01 state beside them so the
        # renderer cannot present a settled rate. Same reason `grid` carries `tilt` and `rotation`:
        # the camera contract comes from the view, not from the client.
        "billing_bases": list(BILLING_BASES),
        "billing_rate_settled": False,   # C01 is open; no rate may be applied
        "billing_citation": "section 8.1 / C01 open \u2014 an income record must name the basis it used",
        # C19's display value, carried WITH its coverage. A HUD showing "governor v1" and stopping
        # there would present a partial stamp as a complete one, and C19 is the control that exists
        # because a decision must be answerable later - so the number of tickets that actually
        # declare it travels beside the value. A version with no coverage figure is a claim; a
        # version with its coverage is a measurement.
        "governor_base_version": _governor_version_c19(civic),
        "honest_limit": (
            "this view renders what the doctrine and the store already carry. It authorises nothing, "
            "stores no balance (C09 ANSWERED) and cannot resolve an open question. Merge authority is "
            "PROCEDURAL (section 20.6): no authentication mechanism exists"
        ),
    }


def _governor_version_c19(store: CivilianStore) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """C19's display value: the distinct versions, and how many tickets declare one.

    The version alone is not the measurement. C19 requires EVERY ticket to carry the governor
    version it ran under, so the interesting number is the coverage — and a surface that showed
    `governor v1` without it would present the stamp as complete when the audit reports it is not.
    Read from the store, never inferred.
    """
    # `of_type` returns a DICT keyed by record id, so iterating it yields IDS and not records.
    # The first version of this helper did that, and the failure was silent: `0 of 11` is a
    # perfectly plausible reading, so nothing raised and nothing looked wrong — a surface would
    # simply have displayed "governor v — declared on 0 of 11 tickets" with a straight face.
    # `isinstance(t, dict)` was doing the work of a guard and only ever returning False. Every
    # accessor here goes through `.values()`; `test_the_governor_stamp_carries_its_coverage` pins it.
    tickets = list(store.of_type("ticket").values())
    declared: set[int] = set()
    declared_on = 0
    for t in tickets:
        gov = t.get("governance")
        value = gov.get("governor_base_version") if isinstance(gov, dict) else None
        if value is not None:
            declared.add(int(value))
            declared_on += 1
    return {
        "versions": sorted(declared),
        "declared_on": declared_on,
        "of_tickets": len(tickets),
        "citation": "C19 / section 6.2 — every ticket carries the governor version it ran under",
    }


_GRADE_STEPS = ("genesis", "apprentice", "journeyman", "craftsman", "master")


def _grade_height(grade: str) -> float:
    try:
        return 0.4 + 0.25 * _GRADE_STEPS.index(grade)
    except ValueError:
        return 0.4


def _tile_for(civilian_id: str) -> list[int]:
    """Deterministic placement from the id. A view mapping, not an assignment."""
    h = int(sha256_hex(civilian_id.encode("utf-8"))[:8], 16)
    return [1 + (h % (GRID - 2)), 2 + ((h // (GRID - 2)) % (GRID - 4))]


def _income_basis(records: Mapping[str, Any], civilian_id: str) -> str | None:
    for key, rec in sorted(records.items()):
        if key.startswith("income_") and rec.get("civilian_id") == civilian_id:
            basis = rec.get("basis")
            return str(basis) if basis else None
    return None


def _adjudication_dict(outcome: Adjudication) -> dict[str, Any]:
    if isinstance(outcome, AcceptedView):
        return {
            "outcome": "accepted_view",
            "highlighted_tiles": [list(t) for t in outcome.highlighted_tiles],
            "note": outcome.note,
        }
    if isinstance(outcome, Deferred):
        return {"outcome": "deferred", "decision_ticket": outcome.decision_ticket, "reason": outcome.reason}
    return {"outcome": "rejected", "citation": outcome.citation, "rule": outcome.rule}


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The situation digest — convergent, read-only, for an external planner
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def situation_digest(store: CivilianStore | None = None) -> bytes:
    """A read-only digest for the Wayfinder planner. Byte-identical over an unchanged store.

    This is the same discipline as `test_regenerating_the_view_CONVERGES` (section 7.5 of the
    fixed outline): re-running over an unchanged store must not change a byte, because a digest
    that reorders itself between runs cannot be reviewed.
    """
    civic = store if store is not None else CivilianStore.load()
    doc = doctrine_snapshot(civic)
    sn = store_snapshot(civic)
    view = build_view(civic, (), doc)
    payload = {
        "view": "civilian-overlay",
        "authoritative": False,
        "note": (
            "DERIVED VIEW. Regenerated from the store and the doctrine; it is not a record and "
            "nothing here gains authority by being exported (rule 58)"
        ),
        "doctrine_hash": doc.doctrine_hash,
        "store_hash": sn.store_hash,
        "mechanical_status": doc.mechanical_distribution,
        "controls": [
            {
                "control": c.control,
                "requirement": c.requirement,
                "mechanical_status": c.mechanical_status,
                "identity_status": c.identity_status,
            }
            for c in doc.control_status
        ],
        "residual_risks": [{"id": i, "risk": t} for i, t in doc.residual_risks],
        "open_decisions": [d for d, _ in doc.open_decisions],
        "answered_decisions": sorted(doc.answered_decisions),
        "fog": list(doc.fog),
        "out_of_scope": list(doc.out_of_scope),
        "never_granted_gates": list(doc.never_granted),
        "billing_bases": list(doc.billing_bases),
        "civilians_summary": sorted(
            (
                {
                    "id": a["civilian_id"],
                    "state": a["lifecycle_state"],
                    "grade": a["unit_grade"],
                    "has_job": a["has_job"],
                    "income_basis": a["income_basis"],
                }
                for a in view["avatars"]
            ),
            key=lambda r: r["id"],
        ),
        "counts": {
            "civilians": len(sn.civilians),
            "jobs": len(sn.jobs),
            "tickets": len(sn.tickets),
            "promotions": len(sn.promotions),
            "retirements": len(sn.retirements),
            "events": sn.events,
            "records": sn.record_count,
        },
    }
    return jcs(_jsonable(payload))


def digest_sha256(store: CivilianStore | None = None) -> str:
    return sha256_hex(situation_digest(store))


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The plan store — separate, explicitly non-authoritative, and path-guarded
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


@dataclass
class PlanStore:
    """The player's plans. NOT a record. NOT read by the doctrine. NOT under the civilians root.

    The guard is the point: `save()` refuses a path inside the civilians store, the doctrine
    store or the god file, so "the overlay never writes to those" is enforced by code rather
    than by a contributor remembering. Rule 43: a control that exists only in documentation
    is not a control.
    """

    root: Path = PLANS_ROOT
    authoritative: bool = False
    entries: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)        # stored form, as written
    proposals: list[Any] = field(default_factory=list)                 # rehydrated PlanProposal

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if self.authoritative:
            raise RefusedAuthorityClaim(
                "a plan store is never authoritative. Only a governed merge may change doctrine "
                "(section 19.4, rule 56)"
            )

    @staticmethod
    def guard(path: Path) -> Path:
        resolved = Path(path).resolve()
        for protected in PROTECTED_ROOTS:
            p = Path(protected).resolve()
            if resolved == p or p in resolved.parents:
                raise RefusedStoreWrite(
                    f"{resolved} is inside a PROTECTED root ({p}). The overlay has no write path "
                    "to the civilians store, the doctrine store or the god file (section 31.1)"
                )
        return resolved

    def add(self, proposal: Any, outcome: Adjudication | None = None) -> dict[str, Any]:
        entry = {
            "proposal_id": proposal_id(proposal),
            "proposal": _jsonable(proposal_dict(proposal)),
            "authoritative": False,
            "adjudication": _adjudication_dict(outcome) if outcome is not None else None,
        }
        self.entries.append(entry)
        self.proposals.append(proposal)
        return entry

    def save(self, name: str = "plan.json") -> Path:
        target = self.guard(self.root / name)
        target.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        payload = {
            "view": "civilian-overlay:city",
            "store": "plan",
            "authoritative": False,
            "note": (
                "NON-AUTHORITATIVE. This file is not a record, is not read by the doctrine, and "
                "confers nothing. Only a governed merge may promote a plan into doctrine"
            ),
            "proposals": sorted(self.entries, key=lambda p: p["proposal_id"]),
        }
        target.write_text(json.dumps(payload, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
        return target

    @classmethod
    def load(cls, name: str = "plan.json") -> "PlanStore":
        """Load the plan. `entries` are the stored dicts; `proposals` are rehydrated objects."""
        path = cls.guard(PLANS_ROOT / name)
        ps = cls()
        if path.exists():
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            ps.entries = list(data.get("proposals", []))
            ps.proposals = [proposal_from_dict(e["proposal"]) for e in ps.entries if "proposal" in e]
        return ps
```

#### `godplan/idle.py`

```python
"""idle — the authorized fiction layer. Cookie Clicker's shape, this stack's rules.

Spec: `PLAN_JOBS.md` (the plan), doctrine §33 and rules 129–136, `CITY_MAP.md` §2 (the tick contract).

WHY THIS MODULE IS MOSTLY REFUSALS. *"Fake jobs"* has two readings and only one is buildable:

    (a) a job that pretends to be real — its output reaches an income record, a grade, a ticket or a
        resume claim, and is later cited as evidence            -> FORBIDDEN (rules 3, 98, 60; §7.1)
    (b) a declared fiction — non-authoritative BY CONSTRUCTION, marked as fiction, refused at every
        boundary where fiction could become a claim            -> AUTHORIZED by `PLAN_JOBS.md`

**The distinction between (a) and (b) is not a check, it is the absence of a path.** That is the same
move §9.7 already records twice — `DRAFT` is non-publishable by construction and `WRITE_EXTERNAL` is
`implemented: false` because *"absence is stronger than a gate, because there is no code path to call"*.
A declared fiction is `DRAFT` applied to a number, so this module's refusals are written as methods that
RAISE, and a test asserts each raises. A validation somewhere downstream is a place a future edit can
move; a method that refuses is not.

WHAT AN IDLE JOB IS ANCHORED TO, AND WHY THAT IS THE WHOLE DESIGN. Every idle job hangs off a record
```
