        + f"\n| {SECT}27 Civilians | **[V]** for what is built (measured by the civilian suite); "
        "**[O]** for the design decisions the pillar itself marks open |"
        + f"\n| {SECT}28 {DASH} {SECT}30 (civilian phases, rules, open questions) | **[O]** — carried as the "
        "proposed set; `28.8`'s gates are what hold them |"
        + f"\n| {SECT}31 the overlay | **[V]** for the read-only layer and its measured numbers; **[O]** for "
        "the render surface, which does not exist |",
        "\u00a731 the overlay",
    ),
    # 3. section 18, the compact instruction, which carries no overlay law at all.
    (
        "frag_20",
        "by reading the list. A design check that has never failed on its own subject has not been run.",
        "by reading the list. A design check that has never failed on its own subject has not been run.\n"
        ">\n"
        "> **And the overlay is a LENS, not a legislator.** A game, a dashboard or a viewer over this "
        "system reads the doctrine and the store and **writes to neither**: player actions accumulate in "
        "a **separate, explicitly non-authoritative plan store**, and only a governed merge may promote a "
        "plan into doctrine. It must display what `_mechanical_status` **returned**, never decide a "
        "control's status for itself — because the moment a surface adjudicates rather than reports, it "
        "has taken merge authority by accident (rule 56, section 31.1). Placement **visualises** where a "
        "control already applies; **removing it removes only the visual** (measured: removing every "
        "service node changes no rendered status). Fog is **deferred**, a wall is **rejected with a "
        "citation**, and both are properties of the doctrine rather than of the renderer. No view stores "
        "a balance (C09: a balance is a derived view), and no view may resolve an open question — a "
        "surface that answers C01 by smoothing it has invented a settled rate.",
        "the overlay is a LENS, not a legislator",
    ),
)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _load(frag_id: str) -> tuple[Path, dict]:
    path = DOCTRINE / f"{frag_id}.json"
    return path, json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _save(path: Path, record: dict) -> None:
    """Write the fragment body, and DELIBERATELY DO NOT touch `block_sha256`.

    THE DEFECT THIS FUNCTION WAS REWRITTEN AROUND, measured in this tool's own first run.
    `_drifted()` in `migrate.py` means "edited since the last rebuild" and compares the body against
    the recorded `block_sha256`. `_refresh()` — called only by `rebuild` — is the one writer of that
    field, and it preserves the prior value as `migrated_block_sha256` so an edit becomes *history*
    rather than being erased.

    This function originally recomputed the hash itself, and the first run therefore printed
    **"propagated: no fragment had drifted"** while three fragments had just been edited. The rebuild
    output was correct — the file matched the store — but the audit trail was gone: **a tool that
    edits a fragment and then certifies the edit has made its own change invisible to the check whose
    whole job is to make an out-of-band edit visible.** That is the same shape as section 6.4's
    decoration provenance and section 20.6's missing merge identity: a provenance field written by the
    thing it is supposed to audit certifies nothing.

    The correct flow is the existing one: the tool writes the body, `status` REPORTS the drift, and
    `rebuild` propagates it and records the superseded hash beside the new one.
    """
    path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def _has(marker: str) -> bool:
    return any(marker in _load(f)[1]["body"] for f in sorted({p[0] for p in FRAGMENT_PATCHES}))


def status(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    print("   REGISTER  section 10.2")
    _, frag12 = _load("frag_12")
    body = frag12["body"]
    print(f"     anchor present           {REGISTER_ANCHOR[:58]!r}")
    print(f"     rows already registered  {'overlay plan proposals' in body}")
    print(f"     rows to append           9")
    print()
    print("   PATCHES   the claims about this file that appending section 31 falsified")
    for frag_id, old, new, marker in FRAGMENT_PATCHES:
        _, record = _load(frag_id)
        applied = marker in record["body"]
        print(f"     {frag_id}  {'APPLIED ' if applied else 'PENDING '}  {old[:64]!r}")
    print()
    print("   nothing written — this was a check")
    return 0


def migrate(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    print("   REGISTER")
    path12, frag12 = _load("frag_12")
    body = frag12["body"]
    if "overlay plan proposals seeded" in body:
        print("     already registered — reuse, not append (rule 3 / section 6.3 rule 3)")
    else:
        if REGISTER_ANCHOR not in body:
            print("     ANCHOR NOT FOUND — refusing to guess an insertion point")
            return 1
        count = body.count(REGISTER_ANCHOR)
        if count != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"   the register anchor matches {count} times; refusing (ambiguity is not a bug to guess past)")
        frag12["body"] = body.replace(REGISTER_ANCHOR, REGISTER_ANCHOR + "\n" + REGISTER_ROWS)
        _save(path12, frag12)
        print(f"     9 rows appended to section 10.2")

    print("\n   PATCHES")
    for frag_id, old, new, marker in FRAGMENT_PATCHES:
        path, record = _load(frag_id)
        if marker in record["body"]:
            print(f"     {frag_id}  SKIPPED   already applied")
            continue
        if old not in record["body"]:
            print(f"     {frag_id}  FAILED    anchor not found: {old[:58]!r}")
            continue
        if record["body"].count(old) != 1:
            raise SystemExit(f"   {frag_id}: the anchor appears {record['body'].count(old)} times; use a unique one")
        record["body"] = record["body"].replace(old, new, 1)
        _save(path, record)
        print(f"     {frag_id}  APPLIED   {old[:58]!r}")
    return 0


MODES = {"status": status, "migrate": migrate}


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    mode = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if mode not in MODES:
        print(f"   usage: python overlay_doctrine2.py [{'|'.join(MODES)}]")
        return 2
    return MODES[mode](argv[1:])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

#### `test_plans.py`

```python
"""Tests for the overlay's plan store and pure adjudicator.

Every control in section 31 is a statement about what must NOT happen, so — as with
`axes.py` and `civilians.py` — the suite is mostly REFUSAL tests and each one names the rule it
holds.

Run:  cd seasons/impl && python -m unittest -v test_plans
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
import json
import random
import sys
import unittest
from enum import Enum
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import godplan as g
from godplan.canonical import jcs
from godplan.civilians import CivilianStore
from godplan import idle, plans, watch


def doctrine():
    return g.doctrine_snapshot()


def store():
    return g.store_snapshot()


def in_wall() -> tuple[int, int]:
    wall = next(r for r in plans.regions() if r.kind == "wall")
    return (wall.x0, wall.y0)


def in_fog() -> tuple[int, int]:
    fog = next(r for r in plans.regions() if r.kind == "fog")
    return (fog.x0, fog.y0)


def clear_tile() -> tuple[int, int]:
    regs = plans.regions()
    for y in range(1, plans.GRID):
        for x in range(plans.GRID):
            if not any(r.contains((x, y)) for r in regs):
                return (x, y)
    raise AssertionError("no tile is outside every region; the layout is broken")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The corrected baseline — and this test exists because three documents carried the wrong one
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestTheCorrectedBaseline(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_mechanical_baseline_is_seven_one_four(self):
        """`7 / 1 / 4`, not `8 / 1 / 4`.

        `8 / 1 / 4` sums to 13 over a 12-control set, which is arithmetically impossible — the
        tell that a number was carried forward rather than re-measured. It was registered in the
        god file twice (section 10.2 and the generated section 23) and inherited by `3DUI.MD`,
        `housing_template_fixed.md` and the implementation plan. This test is the control: it
        fails if the distribution ever drifts, and it fails LOUDLY the moment the discipline that
        produced the error is repeated.
        """
        dist = doctrine().mechanical_distribution
        self.assertEqual(dist, {"MET": 7, "FAILED": 1, "NOT_EVALUABLE": 4})
        self.assertEqual(sum(dist.values()), 12, "the distribution must cover exactly the 12 controls")

    def test_the_two_seed_refusals_are_still_refused(self):
        self.assertEqual(set(store().refused), {"genesis_bram_001", "promotion_dana_002"})


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Purity and determinism — section 31.1, the invariant the whole overlay rests on
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestPurity(unittest.TestCase):
    def proposals(self) -> list[g.PlanProposal]:
        return [
            g.ZoneProposal(g.ZoneKind.JOB, (clear_tile(),)),
            g.ZoneProposal(g.ZoneKind.GENESIS, ((1, 1), (2, 1))),
            g.NodeProposal(g.NodeKind.VERIFIER, clear_tile()),
            g.PathProposal((1, 1), (3, 3), "evidence.flow"),
            g.BudgetProposal(basis="per_ticket", weight=3),
            g.InspectProposal("civilian_ada"),
            g.ResolveProposal("C02"),
        ]

    def test_adjudicate_mutates_nothing_it_is_given(self):
        """Section 31.1 — the adjudicator is a pure function over snapshots."""
        doc, sn = doctrine(), store()
        before_doc = jcs(_plain(doc))
        before_sn = jcs(_plain(sn))
        before_props = [jcs(_plain(p)) for p in self.proposals()]
        for p in self.proposals():
            g.adjudicate(p, doc, sn)
        self.assertEqual(jcs(_plain(doc)), before_doc, "the doctrine snapshot changed")
        self.assertEqual(jcs(_plain(sn)), before_sn, "the store snapshot changed")
        self.assertEqual([jcs(_plain(p)) for p in self.proposals()], before_props)

    def test_snapshots_and_proposals_are_frozen(self):
        """Purity is structural: a frozen dataclass cannot be mutated even by accident."""
        doc = doctrine()
        with self.assertRaises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):
            doc.doctrine_hash = "tampered"  # type: ignore[misc]
        with self.assertRaises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):
            g.BudgetProposal(basis="per_ticket", weight=1).weight = 99  # type: ignore[misc]

    def test_adjudication_is_deterministic_over_a_generated_batch(self):
        """Same `(proposal, doctrine_hash, store_hash)` -> same outcome, over 2,000 proposals."""
        doc, sn = doctrine(), store()
        rng = random.Random(20260921)
        batch = _generate(rng, 2000)
        first = [_outcome(p, doc, sn) for p in batch]
        second = [_outcome(p, doc, sn) for p in batch]
        self.assertEqual(first, second)
        kinds = {row[0] for row in first}
        # A batch that only exercises one branch has not tested the adjudicator.
        self.assertEqual(kinds, {"accepted_view", "deferred", "rejected", "refused"})

    def test_outcome_order_does_not_depend_on_batch_order(self):
        doc, sn = doctrine(), store()
        rng = random.Random(7)
        batch = _generate(rng, 500)
        forward = [_outcome(p, doc, sn) for p in batch]
        reverse = list(reversed([_outcome(p, doc, sn) for p in reversed(batch)]))
        self.assertEqual(forward, reverse)

    def test_a_recreated_snapshot_hashes_identically(self):
        """The digest is a function of content, so an unchanged store yields an unchanged hash."""
        self.assertEqual(doctrine().doctrine_hash, doctrine().doctrine_hash)
        self.assertEqual(store().store_hash, store().store_hash)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The refusals — one test per rule the adjudicator holds
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestRefusals(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.doc, self.sn = doctrine(), store()

    def test_an_unnamed_billing_basis_is_refused(self):  # C01 vocabulary
        with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedUnnamedBasis):
            g.adjudicate(g.BudgetProposal(basis=None, weight=1), self.doc, self.sn)

    def test_a_basis_outside_the_vocabulary_is_rejected(self):
        out = g.adjudicate(g.BudgetProposal(basis="per_vibe", weight=1), self.doc, self.sn)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Rejected)
        self.assertIn("C01", out.citation)

    def test_every_billing_base_is_accepted_as_a_view(self):
        for basis in self.doc.billing_bases:
            with self.subTest(basis=basis):
                self.assertIsInstance(
                    g.adjudicate(g.BudgetProposal(basis=basis, weight=1), self.doc, self.sn),
                    g.AcceptedView,
                )

    def test_a_zone_over_an_out_of_scope_wall_is_rejected_with_a_citation(self):  # section 30.3
        out = g.adjudicate(g.ZoneProposal(g.ZoneKind.JOB, (in_wall(),)), self.doc, self.sn)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Rejected)
        self.assertIn("30.3", out.citation)

    def test_a_zone_into_fog_is_deferred_never_sliced(self):  # section 30.2
        out = g.adjudicate(g.ZoneProposal(g.ZoneKind.JOB, (in_fog(),)), self.doc, self.sn)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Deferred)
        self.assertEqual(out.decision_ticket, "fog")

    def test_every_never_granted_action_is_rejected_on_a_path(self):  # section 9.6 rule 3
        for action in self.doc.never_granted:
            with self.subTest(action=action):
                out = g.adjudicate(g.PathProposal((1, 1), (3, 3), action), self.doc, self.sn)
                self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Rejected)
                self.assertIn("9.6", out.citation)

    def test_an_answered_question_cannot_be_resolved(self):  # C05, C09
        for qid in ("C05", "C09"):
            with self.subTest(qid=qid):
                out = g.adjudicate(g.ResolveProposal(qid), self.doc, self.sn)
                self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Rejected)
                self.assertIn("ANSWERED", out.rule)

    def test_an_open_question_defers_rather_than_resolving(self):
        out = g.adjudicate(g.ResolveProposal("C02"), self.doc, self.sn)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Deferred)
        self.assertEqual(out.decision_ticket, "C02")

    def test_an_invented_question_id_is_rejected(self):
        out = g.adjudicate(g.ResolveProposal("C99"), self.doc, self.sn)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Rejected)

    def test_a_forbidden_field_is_refused_at_the_boundary(self):
        """Section 15.1 — a field the doctrine does not have is a scope-widening attempt."""
        for field_name in ("dwelling_id", "quality_tier", "capacity", "balance", "reputation", "tax"):
            with self.subTest(field=field_name):
                with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedForbiddenField):
                    plans.refuse_forbidden_fields({"outer": {"inner": {field_name: 1}}})

    def test_an_empty_zone_is_rejected(self):
        out = g.adjudicate(g.ZoneProposal(g.ZoneKind.JOB, ()), self.doc, self.sn)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Rejected)

    def test_a_zone_needing_an_absent_authorizer_defers(self):
        """Rule 97 / 62 — with no distinct authorizer the ARROW does not exist, and the answer is
        a deferral rather than a rejection: the zone is legal, the evidence for drawing it is not."""
        empty = dataclasses.replace(self.sn, authorizers=())
        out = g.adjudicate(g.ZoneProposal(g.ZoneKind.GENESIS, (clear_tile(),)), self.doc, empty)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Deferred)
        self.assertEqual(out.decision_ticket, "C17")

    def test_an_evidence_zone_with_no_verifier_defers(self):
        empty = dataclasses.replace(self.sn, verifiers=())
        out = g.adjudicate(g.ZoneProposal(g.ZoneKind.EVIDENCE, (clear_tile(),)), self.doc, empty)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.Deferred)
        self.assertEqual(out.decision_ticket, "C16")


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The lens discipline — nodes visualise and must never grant
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestTheLensDiscipline(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.doc, self.sn = doctrine(), store()

    def test_every_node_kind_states_what_it_must_not_do(self):
        for node in g.NodeKind:
            with self.subTest(node=node):
                self.assertIn(node, plans.NODE_MUST_NOT)
                self.assertIn(node, plans.NODE_VISUAL_ONLY)
                self.assertIn("does not", plans.NODE_MUST_NOT[node])

    def test_a_placed_node_never_asserts_it_grants_anything(self):
        out = g.adjudicate(g.NodeProposal(g.NodeKind.AUTHORIZER, clear_tile()), self.doc, self.sn)
        self.assertIsInstance(out, g.AcceptedView)
        self.assertIn("changes no mechanical status", out.note)

    def test_the_view_carries_what_the_surface_renders(self):
        """The Rust surface renders this file and nothing else, so every key it needs must be HERE.

        THE GAP THIS HOLDS. Section 8.1 requires the HUD to show the four-way billing split, and the
        four basis NAMES live in a doctrine constant the view did not carry. The renderer's options
        were to invent them — which is the defect section 31.1 names, a surface spelling doctrine for
        itself — or to omit the split, which would have dropped the one thing C01's openness exists to
        make visible. The fix is at the source: the contract carries the names.

        Same rule as `grid.tilt` and `grid.rotation`, which the client reads instead of hardcoding:
        **the surface's data contract is the view, so a key the surface needs is a view defect when it
        is missing, and never a renderer decision.**
        """
        view = g.build_view(doctrine=self.doc)
        self.assertEqual(view["billing_bases"], list(g.BILLING_BASES))
        self.assertEqual(len(view["billing_bases"]), 4)
        # The C01 state travels WITH the names, so a renderer cannot present a settled rate.
        self.assertFalse(view["billing_rate_settled"])
        self.assertIn("C01", view["billing_citation"])
        # The camera contract, which the isometric surface reads rather than hardcoding.
        self.assertEqual(view["grid"]["projection"], "isometric")
        self.assertIn(view["grid"]["tilt"], (30, 30.0))
        self.assertIn(view["grid"]["rotation"], (45, 45.0))
        self.assertGreater(view["grid"]["size"], 0)

    def test_the_governor_stamp_carries_its_coverage(self):
        """C19's value and its coverage must be measured from RECORDS, not from a dict's keys.

        THE DEFECT THIS HOLDS, and it is the quiet kind. `CivilianStore.of_type()` returns a DICT
        keyed by record id, so `list(store.of_type("ticket"))` yields IDS and not records. The first
        version of `_governor_version_c19` iterated it and guarded with `isinstance(t, dict)`, which
        was always False — so it reported **`0 of 11`** with no error and every appearance of a
        measurement. A surface would have rendered "governor v— declared on 0/11 tickets" as though
        the store were unstamped.

        The general form, which is why the test is not just an equality check: **a guard that can
        only ever return one value reads as rigour and is decoration.** `isinstance` on a value whose
        type is known-by-construction is that guard (§6.4).
        """
        civic = CivilianStore.load()
        stamp = plans._governor_version_c19(civic)
        tickets = list(civic.of_type("ticket").values())
        self.assertEqual(stamp["of_tickets"], len(tickets))
        self.assertGreater(stamp["of_tickets"], 0, "no tickets — the fixture is wrong, not the code")
        self.assertEqual(stamp["versions"], [1])
        # C19 is MET in the audit, so the coverage must be COMPLETE — the two must agree, because
        # a HUD showing a partial stamp beside a MET control is two measurements disagreeing.
        self.assertEqual(stamp["declared_on"], stamp["of_tickets"])
        self.assertIn("C19", stamp["citation"])

    def test_node_removal_changes_no_status(self):
        """The test that would fail if this module ever started DECIDING a control.

        Placing every service node, then removing every service node, must leave the rendered
        control statuses byte-identical — because they are READ from `civilians.analyze()` and
        never recomputed here.
        """
        st = g.CivilianStore.load()
        nodes = [g.NodeProposal(k, clear_tile()) for k in g.NodeKind]
        without = g.build_view(st, (), self.doc)
        with_nodes = g.build_view(st, nodes, self.doc)
        self.assertEqual(without["mechanical_distribution"], with_nodes["mechanical_distribution"])
        self.assertEqual(without["controls"], with_nodes["controls"])
        self.assertEqual(without["mechanical_distribution"], {"MET": 7, "FAILED": 1, "NOT_EVALUABLE": 4})

    def test_no_control_status_is_ever_recomputed_here(self):
        """Every status the view renders must be one `analyze()` already produced."""
        st = g.CivilianStore.load()
        analysis = g.analyze(st)
        by_id = {row["control"]: row["mechanical_status"] for row in analysis["controls"]}
        view = g.build_view(st, (), self.doc)
        self.assertEqual({row["control"]: row["mechanical_status"] for row in view["controls"]}, by_id)

    def test_answered_monuments_render_answered_and_offer_no_resolution(self):
        view = g.build_view(g.CivilianStore.load(), (), self.doc)
        by_id = {m["id"]: m for m in view["monuments"]}
        self.assertEqual(by_id["C05"]["state"], "answered")
        self.assertEqual(by_id["C09"]["state"], "answered")
        self.assertEqual(by_id["C02"]["state"], "open")
        for m in view["monuments"]:
            with self.subTest(m=m["id"]):
                self.assertFalse(m["resolve_available"])

    def test_the_view_declares_itself_non_authoritative(self):
        view = g.build_view(g.CivilianStore.load(), (), self.doc)
        self.assertTrue(view["derived_view"])
        self.assertFalse(view["authoritative"])
        self.assertFalse(view["plan_is_authoritative"])
        self.assertIn("PROCEDURAL", view["honest_limit"])

    def test_the_geometry_follows_doctrine_not_a_literal(self):
        """A doctrine change must move the layout, so a hard-coded count is a defect."""
        regs = plans.regions()
        self.assertEqual(sum(1 for r in regs if r.kind == "wall"), len(g.OUT_OF_SCOPE))
        self.assertEqual(sum(1 for r in regs if r.kind == "fog"), len(g.FOG_ITEMS))

    def test_no_locus_invents_a_second_occupancy(self):
        """Multi-civilian co-location is fog (section 30.2), so occupancy is 1 or it is a defect."""
        view = g.build_view(g.CivilianStore.load(), (), self.doc)
        for locus in view["loci"]:
            with self.subTest(locus=locus["civilian_id"]):
                self.assertEqual(locus["occupancy"], 1)
                self.assertFalse(locus["multi_civilian"])


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The write guard, and the digest
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


class TestNoWritePath(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_the_guard_names_the_real_roots(self):
        """This is the test that would have caught the guard guarding the wrong path.

        An earlier version computed the project root as `parents[2]`, which made `PLANS_ROOT`
        resolve to `seasons/seasons/plans` and made `CIVILIANS_ROOT` name a directory that does
        not exist — so every guard assertion below passed while guarding nothing real.
        """
        self.assertEqual(plans.SEASONS_ROOT.name, "seasons")
        self.assertEqual(plans.PLANS_ROOT.parent, plans.SEASONS_ROOT)
        self.assertEqual(plans.CIVILIANS_ROOT.resolve(), Path(g.CIVILIANS_ROOT).resolve())
        self.assertTrue(plans.CIVILIANS_ROOT.is_dir(), "the guarded civilians root must exist")
        self.assertTrue(plans.DOCTRINE_DIR.is_dir(), "the guarded doctrine root must exist")
        self.assertTrue(plans.GOD_FILE.is_file(), "the god file the guard protects must exist")

    def test_the_plan_root_is_not_inside_a_protected_root(self):
        for protected in plans.PROTECTED_ROOTS:
            with self.subTest(protected=protected):
                self.assertNotIn(Path(protected).resolve(), plans.PLANS_ROOT.resolve().parents)

    def test_the_store_validator_is_idempotent(self):
        """Calling validate() twice must not duplicate the defects. `overlay.py` calls it twice
        (once directly and once through `store_snapshot`), which is how the doubling was found."""
        store = g.CivilianStore.load()
        once = list(store.validate())
        twice = list(store.validate())
        self.assertEqual(len(once), len(twice), "validate() is not idempotent")
        self.assertEqual([str(d) for d in once], [str(d) for d in twice])

    def test_saving_into_the_civilians_store_is_refused(self):
        ps = g.PlanStore()
        with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedStoreWrite):
            ps.guard(plans.CIVILIANS_ROOT / "plan.json")

    def test_saving_into_the_doctrine_store_is_refused(self):
        ps = g.PlanStore()
        with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedStoreWrite):
            ps.guard(plans.DOCTRINE_DIR / "frag_999.json")

    def test_saving_over_the_god_file_is_refused(self):
        ps = g.PlanStore()
        with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedStoreWrite):
            ps.guard(plans.GOD_FILE)

    def test_a_traversal_out_of_the_plan_root_is_refused(self):
        ps = g.PlanStore()
        with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedStoreWrite):
            ps.guard(plans.PLANS_ROOT / ".." / "civilians" / "sneak.json")

    def test_a_plan_store_may_not_declare_itself_authoritative(self):
        with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedAuthorityClaim):
            g.PlanStore(authoritative=True)

    def test_a_saved_plan_says_it_is_not_authoritative(self):
        ps = g.PlanStore()
        ps.add(g.BudgetProposal(basis="per_ticket", weight=1))
        path = ps.save("test_plan_guard.json")
        try:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            self.assertFalse(data["authoritative"])
            self.assertIn("NON-AUTHORITATIVE", data["note"])
        finally:
            path.unlink(missing_ok=True)

    def test_the_source_contains_no_write_into_a_protected_root(self):
        """A static check on the module itself: no `write_text`/`write_bytes` on a protected path.

        Rule 43 — a control that exists only in documentation is not implemented. This scans the
        source for the shape of the bug rather than trusting the guard above.
        """
        src = Path(plans.__file__).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        body = src.split("class PlanStore", 1)[1]
        for bad in ("CIVILIANS_ROOT / ", "DOCTRINE_DIR / ", "GOD_FILE."):
            self.assertNotIn(f"write_text({bad}", body.replace(" ", " "))
        self.assertIn("self.guard(", body, "PlanStore.save must route every path through guard()")


class TestDigestConvergence(unittest.TestCase):

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# helpers
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _plain(obj: object) -> object:
    if dataclasses.is_dataclass(obj) and not isinstance(obj, type):
        return {f.name: _plain(getattr(obj, f.name)) for f in dataclasses.fields(obj)}
    if isinstance(obj, dict):
        return {str(k): _plain(v) for k, v in obj.items()}
    if isinstance(obj, (set, frozenset)):
        return sorted(str(v) for v in obj)
    if isinstance(obj, (list, tuple)):
        return [_plain(v) for v in obj]
    if isinstance(obj, Enum):
        return obj.value
    return obj


def _outcome(proposal: g.PlanProposal, doc=None, sn=None) -> tuple:
    """A REFUSAL IS AN OUTCOME. A pure function that raises deterministically is still pure, so a
    refusal is captured and compared rather than allowed to abort the batch — otherwise the
    determinism test would silently exclude exactly the cases the system exists to produce."""
    try:
        out = g.adjudicate(proposal, doc if doc is not None else doctrine(), sn if sn is not None else store())
    except g.RefusedPlan as exc:
        return ("refused", type(exc).__name__, str(exc))
    if isinstance(out, g.AcceptedView):
        return ("accepted_view", out.highlighted_tiles, out.note)
    if isinstance(out, g.Deferred):
        return ("deferred", out.decision_ticket, out.reason)
    return ("rejected", out.citation, out.rule)


def _generate(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> list[g.PlanProposal]:
    """A deterministic batch of random proposals, including deliberately illegal ones."""
    tiles = [(rng.randrange(plans.GRID), rng.randrange(plans.GRID)) for _ in range(400)]
    bases = list(g.BILLING_BASES) + [None, "per_vibe", ""]
    actions = list(g.NEVER_GRANTED) + ["evidence.flow", "authorization.flow"]
    qids = ["C05", "C09", "C02", "C01", "C99"]
    out: list[g.PlanProposal] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        pick = rng.randrange(6)
        if pick == 0:
            out.append(
                g.ZoneProposal(
                    rng.choice(list(g.ZoneKind)),
                    tuple(rng.sample(tiles, rng.randrange(0, 4))),
                )
            )
        elif pick == 1:
            out.append(g.NodeProposal(rng.choice(list(g.NodeKind)), rng.choice(tiles)))
        elif pick == 2:
            out.append(g.PathProposal(rng.choice(tiles), rng.choice(tiles), rng.choice(actions)))
        elif pick == 3:
            out.append(g.BudgetProposal(basis=rng.choice(bases), weight=rng.randrange(-2, 5)))
        elif pick == 4:
            out.append(g.InspectProposal(f"civilian_{rng.randrange(3)}"))
        else:
            out.append(g.ResolveProposal(rng.choice(qids)))
    return out


class TestTheWatcher(unittest.TestCase):
    """G1's producer half — and the four properties that make it a watcher rather than a scheduler."""

    def test_the_output_is_not_one_of_its_own_inputs(self):
        """**The defect this pins, and the negative control is the interesting half.**

        The view is written INTO the plan store, and the plan store is one of the watcher's inputs. Left
        unexcluded, the watcher would see the file it just wrote, decide the inputs had moved, and re-derive
        forever — a generator whose output feeds its input. That is the same shape `appendix.py` records for
        the record appendix, and the same shape that made `generated_at` a determinism defect, so it is worth
        refusing twice.

        The exclusion is asserted by identity, not by a pattern: `view.json` and `digest.json` are named.
        """
        listed = {p.resolve() for p in watch.inputs()}
        self.assertNotIn(watch.OUTPUT.resolve(), listed, "the view must not be its own input")
        for sibling in watch.DERIVED_SIBLINGS:
            self.assertNotIn(sibling.resolve(), listed, "nor a sibling derived the same way")
        # And the inputs are not empty — otherwise the assertion above would pass vacuously for a watcher
        # that watched nothing at all.
        self.assertGreater(len(listed), 10, "the watcher watches real files")
        # The plain files ARE inputs, which is the other half: excluding everything would also pass above.
        self.assertIn(watch.PLAN_FILE.resolve(), listed, "the player's own plan is an input")

    def test_a_write_does_not_change_the_stamp(self):
        """The defect, demonstrated directly: derive, write, and the stamp must be unchanged.

        This is the assertion the exclusion exists for, and it is stronger than checking the file list — it
        measures the property (idempotence of the stamp under its own output) rather than the mechanism.
        """
        before = watch.input_stamp()
        watch.write_view(watch.derive())
        after = watch.input_stamp()
        self.assertEqual(before, after, "writing the view must not look like an input change")

    def test_an_unknown_stamp_always_re_derives(self):
        """§17 rule 4 applied to a cache: the unknown resolves toward work, never toward rest."""
        self.assertTrue(watch.stamp_changed(None, "abc"))
        self.assertTrue(watch.stamp_changed("abc", None))
        self.assertTrue(watch.stamp_changed(None, None))
        self.assertFalse(watch.stamp_changed("abc", "abc"))
        self.assertTrue(watch.stamp_changed("abc", "abd"))

    def test_the_watcher_settles_and_reports_the_idle_polls(self):
        """Three polls over a still store: one derivation, then rest — and the rest is REPORTED.

        A watcher that wrote every poll and one that never wrote are indistinguishable from the artifact,
        because both leave a correct `view.json` behind. The counters are what tell them apart, which is why
        `WatchResult.wrote` exists rather than being inferred from the file's mtime.
        """
        results = watch.run(3, 0.0, out=lambda _line: None)
        self.assertEqual(len(results), 3)
        # **`changed` is the cadence; `wrote` is a different fact, and the first version of this test
        # confused them.** It asserted `results[0].wrote` on the grounds that "the first poll derives" — true,
        # and beside the point: over a converged store the derive produces byte-identical output, so the
        # correct answer is that nothing was written. A watcher that reported a write there would be
        # reporting activity rather than effect, which is the shape §17 rule 50 (delivered versus asked)
        # exists to prevent. So this now asserts the two flags separately AND their implication.
        self.assertTrue(results[0].changed, "the first poll re-derives because it forces")
        self.assertEqual([r.changed for r in results], [True, False, False])
        self.assertEqual(len({r.stamp for r in results}), 1, "one stamp: the inputs did not move")
        for r in results:
            self.assertFalse(r.wrote, "over a converged store the bytes do not change, so nothing is written")
            if r.wrote:
                self.assertTrue(r.changed, "a write without a change would be a write without a reason")

    def test_a_write_IS_reported_when_the_bytes_actually_differ(self):
        """**The positive control for `wrote`, without which the test above could pass on a dead flag.**

        Rule 44: a control is not implemented until a test fails without it. The settle test asserts
        `wrote is False` three times, and a watcher that hardcoded `wrote = False` would satisfy every line of
        it — a green suite over a flag that never fires. So the file is perturbed, the bytes now genuinely
        differ from what `derive()` produces, and the flag must come back True.

        The perturbation is one appended byte rather than a rewritten structure, because the point is the
        *comparison*, not the content: `write_view` compares the serialised payload it is about to write
        against what is on disk, so any difference is enough to make the write real. The test restores the
        converged state at the end, so a later assertion is not reading a file this one left dirty.
        """
        watch.write_view(watch.derive())
        target = watch.OUTPUT
        original = target.read_bytes()
        try:
            target.write_bytes(original + b" ")
            result = watch.watch_once(0, None, force=True)
            self.assertTrue(result.wrote, "the bytes differed, so the write must be reported")
            self.assertTrue(result.changed, "and a write always implies the derive ran")
            self.assertEqual(target.read_bytes(), original, "and it restored the derived bytes")
        finally:
            target.write_bytes(original)
        # And the flag settles back, which is the property the pair of tests exists to pin from both sides.
        self.assertFalse(watch.watch_once(0, None, force=True).wrote, "converged again, so no write again")

    def test_the_watcher_writes_only_through_the_guard(self):
        """Rule 56 / §31.1 — the watcher is the only moving part, so its one write is the one to check."""
        target = watch.write_view(watch.derive())
        self.assertEqual(target.resolve(), watch.OUTPUT.resolve(), "and exactly where it says it writes")
        # And the guard still refuses the protected roots, asserted here because this module is a second
        # caller: a guard that only holds for the CLI is a guard with an unguarded caller.
        for root in plans.PROTECTED_ROOTS:
            probe = root / "watch-probe.json" if root.is_dir() else root
            with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedPlan):
                plans.PlanStore.guard(probe)

    def test_the_view_the_watcher_writes_is_the_view_the_cli_would_write(self):
        """One derivation path, or the two drift and the surface renders a file nothing regenerates."""
        derived = watch.derive()
        self.assertEqual(derived["authoritative"], False)
        self.assertIn("loci", derived)
        self.assertIn("mechanical_distribution", derived)
        # A second derivation over an unchanged store is identical — the determinism the surface's poll
        # depends on, asserted on the producer's side of the boundary.
        self.assertEqual(g.canonical.jcs(watch.derive()), g.canonical.jcs(derived))

    def test_the_watcher_can_start_itself_and_stop_when_the_store_settles(self):
        """Auto mode: derive on start, then watch until idle — and END, rather than run forever.

        Nothing was starting the watcher, so nothing re-derived the view, so the surface was following a
        file no producer moved. This is that producer. Both halves are load-bearing: it must derive
        WITHOUT BEING ASKED (a first poll that asked "has anything changed?" would answer *no* over a
        store it has never read) and it must END normally, because a process that only stops on a signal
        is one whose behaviour cannot be asserted.
        """
        results = watch.run_auto(0.0, settle_after=2, out=lambda _line: None)
        self.assertTrue(results[0].changed, "the first poll derives unconditionally")
        self.assertEqual(len(results), 3, "one forced derive, then two idle polls, then the normal exit")
        self.assertFalse(results[-1].changed, "and it exits because the store settled, not because it failed")

    def test_the_auto_mode_bounds_itself_when_the_store_keeps_moving(self):
        """A continuously-written store would never settle, so the second bound is not decoration."""
        results = watch.run_auto(0.0, settle_after=0, max_ticks=4, out=lambda _line: None)
        self.assertEqual(len(results), 4, "settle_after=0 disables the settle exit, so the bound must stop it")


class TestTheIdleLayer(unittest.TestCase):
    """PLAN_JOBS.md / section 33 — the authorized fiction, and the seven refusals that keep it one.

    Every test here is about a NUMBER THAT DOES NOT REACH A RECORD. That is the whole feature, so the
    suite is written as absences (rule 129) rather than as validations: a validation is a place a future
    edit can move, and an absent path is not.
    """

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.store = g.CivilianStore.load()
        cls.store.validate()
        cls.view = plans.build_view(store=cls.store, tick=0)
        cls.jobs = idle.derive_idle_jobs(
            cls.store.records, plans.store_snapshot(cls.store).civilians, tick=0
        )

    # -- the four absences: no path from an idle yield to anything that carries forward ----------

    def test_no_idle_yield_can_reach_a_record_that_carries_forward(self):
        """Refusals 1-4, held as eight separate names so a search for each finds an answer."""
        job = self.jobs[0]
        for method in ("as_income", "as_ticket", "as_grade", "as_promotion",
                       "as_retirement", "as_claim", "as_metric", "as_control"):
            with self.subTest(path=method):
                with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedFictionAsClaim):
                    getattr(job, method)()

    def test_the_idle_layer_is_not_merged_into_loci(self):
        """Marking rule 2 — a fiction counted as a locus makes the civilian count wrong everywhere."""
        self.assertIn("idle_jobs", self.view)
        self.assertIn("loci", self.view)
        locus_ids = {row["civilian_id"] for row in self.view["loci"]}
        idle_ids = {row["idle_id"] for row in self.view["idle_jobs"]}
        self.assertEqual(locus_ids & idle_ids, set(), "an idle block is never a locus")
        self.assertGreater(len(idle_ids), 0, "and the assertion above is not vacuous")
        # The HUD count and the civilian count are separate numbers, which is the point of the split.
        self.assertEqual(self.view["idle_summary"]["jobs"], len(idle_ids))
        self.assertNotEqual(len(idle_ids), len(locus_ids))

    def test_every_idle_job_names_a_kind_from_the_closed_four(self):
        """Refusal 6 — the four-member set exists precisely so an unnamed basis can be refused."""
        self.assertEqual(len(list(idle.IdleKind)), 4)
        for job in self.jobs:
            self.assertIn(job.kind, idle.IdleKind)
            self.assertIn(job.kind.value, idle.IDLE_BASE_YIELD)
        with self.assertRaises(idle.RefusedUnnamedKind):
            idle.refuse_unnamed_kind("profit")
        # Negative control: a real kind is accepted, so the refusal is about the value and not a stub.
        self.assertIs(idle.refuse_unnamed_kind("attest"), idle.IdleKind.ATTEST)

    def test_no_idle_job_names_a_civilian_that_does_not_exist(self):
        """Refusal 7 — the one that would have been missed, and the one that matters most.

        A clicker game's growth path is *more producers*, and the cheapest way to add a producer is to
        invent a person. So the ward cannot grow by fiction, and this is checked twice: structurally
        (a record naming a ghost emits nothing) and by a named refusal that fires.
        """
        known = set(plans.store_snapshot(self.store).civilians)
        for job in self.jobs:
            self.assertIn(job.civilian_id, known)
        with self.assertRaises(idle.RefusedGhostCivilian):
            idle.refuse_ghost_civilian("civilian_nobody", sorted(known))
        # The structural half, with the negative control the whole test exists for: a store containing
        # an evidence record for a civilian who is not there must yield NO job for it, not a job the
        # surface then has to reject.
        records = dict(self.store.records)
        records["ticket_ghost"] = {
            "ticket_id": "ticket_ghost",
            "type": "ticket",
            "civilian_id": "civilian_nobody",
            "status": "closed",
        }
        with_ghost = idle.derive_idle_jobs(records, sorted(known), tick=0)
        self.assertEqual(
            [j for j in with_ghost if j.civilian_id == "civilian_nobody"], [],
            "a record naming a civilian that does not exist must produce no idle job at all",
        )
        # And the anchor set is unchanged, so the ghost added no producers either.
        self.assertEqual(len(with_ghost), len(self.jobs))

    def test_an_idle_job_without_its_anchor_field_is_not_an_anchor(self):
        """The type alone is not enough: an income row and a VERIFIED income row are different facts."""
        records = dict(self.store.records)
        records["income_unverified_probe"] = {
            "income_id": "income_unverified_probe",
            "type": "income",
            "civilian_id": "civilian_ada",
            "amount_cents": 1,          # but NO verified_by
        }
        jobs = idle.derive_idle_jobs(records, plans.store_snapshot(self.store).civilians, tick=0)
        self.assertEqual([j for j in jobs if "income_unverified_probe" in j.anchor_id], [])
        self.assertEqual(len(jobs), len(self.jobs), "an unanchored income row adds no producer")

    # -- refusal 5: the one mechanic the genre gets wrong ---------------------------------------

    def test_a_paused_clock_accrues_nothing(self):
        """Offline progress is REFUSED. A fiction that advances unwatched gets believed."""
        job = self.jobs[0]
        self.assertEqual(idle.accrue(job, 5, 5), 0, "the same tick is a paused clock: no accrual")
        self.assertEqual(idle.accrue(job, None, 99), 0, "no prior observation accrues nothing (rule 4)")
        self.assertGreater(idle.accrue(job, 5, 6), 0, "but a real tick does accrue")
        with self.assertRaises(idle.RefusedPausedAccrual):
            idle.accrue(job, 9, 3)

    def test_yields_are_integers_and_move_with_the_tick(self):
        """Integers (rule 26), no float, no randomness, no compounding — and they DO move."""
        job = self.jobs[0]
        for tick in (0, 1, 5, 50, 5000):
            value = idle.idle_yield(job, tick)
            self.assertIsInstance(value, int)
            self.assertEqual(value, job.base_yield * tick)
        self.assertEqual(idle.idle_yield(job, 0), 0, "a fiction no tick has run for has yielded nothing")
        self.assertGreater(idle.idle_yield(job, 10), idle.idle_yield(job, 5))

    def test_the_summary_carries_the_stable_components_the_surface_needs(self):
        """The convergence contract: the bytes hold the base; the SURFACE holds the motion.

        A view whose bytes carried a live tick would differ every poll for a reason that is not an
        input, so the watcher would never settle. `total_base_yield` is the number that multiplies.
        """
        summary = idle.idle_summary(self.jobs, tick=0)
        self.assertEqual(summary["total_base_yield"], sum(j.base_yield for j in self.jobs))
        self.assertEqual(summary["total_yield_at_tick"], 0)
        at_ten = idle.idle_summary(self.jobs, tick=10)
        self.assertEqual(at_ten["total_yield_at_tick"], summary["total_base_yield"] * 10)
        # And the effect fields the layer must declare as NONE rather than omit.
        for key in ("authority", "grade_effect", "claim_effect", "income_effect"):
            self.assertIn(key, summary)
        self.assertFalse(summary["grade_effect"] or summary["claim_effect"] or summary["income_effect"])
        self.assertIsNone(summary["authority"])

    def test_no_two_idle_jobs_share_an_id(self):
        """The defect this test was written for: keying on (kind, civilian) alone collided.

        One civilian holding three evidence records produced three identical ids, so a surface keying a
        draw call or a selection on the id would have rendered ONE of three jobs and left two
        unaddressable — and nothing would have raised, because a duplicated key looks like an ordinary
        value. The anchor is what makes a job distinct, so the anchor is in the id.
        """
        ids = [j.idle_id for j in self.jobs]
        self.assertEqual(len(ids), len(set(ids)), "an id a surface keys on addresses exactly one job")
        self.assertTrue(all(i.startswith("idle_") for i in ids), "marking 1: the prefix cannot collide")
        # Negative control: two jobs differing ONLY in anchor must still be distinct, which is the
        # collision the first version produced.
        a = [j for j in self.jobs if j.civilian_id == "civilian_ada" and j.kind is idle.IdleKind.ATTEST]
        self.assertGreater(len(a), 1, "this civilian really does hold more than one evidence record")
        self.assertEqual(len({j.idle_id for j in a}), len(a))

    def test_the_view_is_still_deterministic_with_the_fiction_in_it(self):
        """Convergence, which is the property that makes the watcher able to settle at all."""
        first = plans.build_view(store=self.store, tick=0)
        second = plans.build_view(store=self.store, tick=0)
        self.assertEqual(g.canonical.jcs(first), g.canonical.jcs(second))
        self.assertEqual(first["derived_at_tick"], 0)
        self.assertIn("derived_at_tick", first, "a consumer can tell a fresh view from a stale one")

    def test_a_job_refuses_every_forward_carrying_path_by_TYPE_not_by_value(self):
        """Rule 58's shape: an idle yield may be NUMBER-shaped like a metric, and it is still fiction.

        The refusal is on the type, so a future field cannot make one admissible by looking plausible.
        """
        self.assertIsInstance(self.jobs[0], idle.IdleJob)
        self.assertTrue(all(isinstance(j.base_yield, int) for j in self.jobs))
        # And the same absence holds for a job built by hand, which is the case a value check would miss.
        handmade = idle.IdleJob(
            idle_id="idle_attest_civilian_ada_handmade",
            kind=idle.IdleKind.ATTEST,
            civilian_id="civilian_ada",
            anchor_id="evidence_ada_genesis",
            tile=(1, 1),
            base_yield=3,
            assigned_at_tick=0,
            lens="ward",
            citation="section 33",
        )
        with self.assertRaises(g.RefusedFictionAsClaim):
            handmade.as_income()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main(verbosity=2)
```

#### `city_season.py`

```python
"""city_season — file the isometric surface, and the four defects building it found.

    cd seasons/impl
    python city_season.py status     # what would be filed, writing nothing
    python city_season.py file       # file it

Reuses `overlay_season`'s helpers rather than re-declaring them, so a ticket filed here has exactly
the shape a ticket filed there does. Two tools that each spelled their own record shape would drift,
and the drift would be invisible because both would parse.

THE FOUR DEFECTS, and why each is filed rather than quietly fixed. Every one was found by RUNNING
something, and none by reading:

  1. **`of_type` returned keys.** `CivilianStore.of_type()` returns a dict keyed by record id, so
     iterating it yields IDS. `_governor_version_c19` iterated it and guarded with `isinstance(t, dict)`,
     which was always False — so it reported **`0 of 11`** with no error and every appearance of a
     measurement. A guard that can only ever return one value reads as rigour and is decoration.

  2. **The view did not carry what the surface renders.** The HUD needs the four billing-basis NAMES
     (section 8.1) and the C19 governor stamp; neither was in `view.json`. The options were to invent
     them in the renderer — the defect section 31.1 names — or to drop them. The fix is at the source:
     the contract carries them, because a key the surface needs is a VIEW defect when missing.

  3. **The interaction test asserted `>=`.** `panel.pending.len() >= before` passes whether the click
     worked or not. Tightening it to `==` immediately failed and revealed that the test had been
     clicking coordinates the layout never used. A test that cannot fail is not evidence.

  4. **The marker guard tested a document too small to reach it.** `a_document_that_is_not_the_view`
     began by asserting on a two-key JSON literal, which fails on a *missing field* rather than on the
     marker. It passed for the wrong reason until the fixture was rebuilt from the real document.

  5. **Twelve parsed fields were never displayed** — including `identity_status`, which is PROCEDURAL
     for all twelve controls (rule 100). The compiler reported them as unused-field warnings; the real
     finding is that a surface drawing only the mechanical half renders a green city over a governance
     layer where nothing verifies an actor.

The general lesson, filed as finding **FC-10** and carried in section 31.7: **the mechanical half of a
surface's verification is cheap, and every one of these five was in the half that is not.**
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import overlay_season as S

TICKET = S._ticket

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The ticket
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CITY_TICKETS = [
    TICKET(
        6,
        "Build the isometric render surface so the overlay's derived view is actually playable",
        "done",

# Filing

def status(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    print("   WOULD FILE")
    for record in CITY_TICKETS:
        print(f"     ticket      {record['ticket_id']}  {record['status']}")
    for record in CITY_CORRECTIONS:
        print(f"     correction  {record['correction_id']}")
    for record in CITY_EVIDENCE:
        print(f"     evidence    {record['evidence_id']}")
    print(f"     events      {len(CITY_EVENTS)}")
    print("\n   nothing written — this was a check")
    return 0


def file_all(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    print("   FILING INTO seasons/season_2026_s1/")
    actions = []
    for record in CITY_TICKETS:
        actions.append(S._write("tickets", record, "ticket_id"))
    for record in CITY_CORRECTIONS:
        actions.append(S._write("corrections", record, "correction_id"))
    for record in CITY_EVIDENCE:
        actions.append(S._write("evidence", record, "evidence_id"))
    for action, name in actions:
        print(f"   {action:8} {name}")

    existing = {
        json.loads(line)["detail"][:60]
        for line in S.EVENTS.read_text(encoding="utf-8").splitlines()
        if line.strip()
    }
    appended = 0
    with S.EVENTS.open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        for event in CITY_EVENTS:
            if event["detail"][:60] in existing:
                continue
            handle.write(json.dumps(event, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n")
            appended += 1
    print(f"\n   events appended {appended}, skipped {len(CITY_EVENTS) - appended} (already present)")
    return 0


def verify(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    """Route through the overlay's own verifier, then report the new records specifically."""
    code = S.verify([])
    import godplan as g

    store = g.Store.load()
    store.validate()
    mine = {
        "ticket_civilian_overlay_006",
        "ticket_civilian_overlay_007",
        "evidence_city_surface",
        *{record["correction_id"] for record in CITY_CORRECTIONS},
    }
    named = [d for d in store.defects if any(record in f"{d.where} {d.what}" for record in mine)]
    print(f"   defects naming a city-surface record   {len(named)}")
    for defect in named:
        print(f"     {defect}")
    return code


MODES = {"status": status, "file": file_all, "verify": verify}


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    mode = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if mode not in MODES:
        print(f"   usage: python city_season.py [{'|'.join(MODES)}]")
        return 2
    return MODES[mode](argv[1:])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))

```python
"""city_doctrine — register the surface, correct the claim section 31 made before it existed, and add its law.

    cd seasons/impl
    python city_doctrine.py status     # what would change, writing nothing
    python city_doctrine.py migrate    # append section 31.9-31.10 and register the rows

evidence header asserting **"The isometric render surface does NOT exist"**. That was true when it was
written and is false now, and the sentence is load-bearing: it is the marker that tells a reader whether
the pillar describes a plan or a built thing. An append that leaves it standing makes the file lie in the
one place a reader looks for the truth about the file.

This is the same shape as §22's preamble correction and §31's own preamble correction: **a claim about
the file, falsified by appending to it, and invisible to every check because no check compares a claim
about the file to the file.** The register rows the surface introduces are the mechanical half; this
sentence is the half a check cannot reach.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

from godplan.canonical import sha256_hex

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import godplan as g

DOCTRINE = g.reconstruct.DOCTRINE_DIR

SECT = "\u00a7"
DASH = "\u2013"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Register rows — appended to the end of section 10.2's table
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

REGISTER_ANCHOR = (
    "| adjudicator determinism | identical verdict for the same `(proposal, doctrine_hash, store_hash)`, "
    "with no mutation of its inputs | `test_adjudicator_is_pure` | [V] |"
)

# Two rows became one, and then the number left the row entirely. The sequence is the finding:
# **20 of 25**, then **17 of 122**, then **17 of 139** — three readings in one session, each made stale
# by a test added somewhere else, and the third is what settles it. The register's own header already
# excludes "this file's own line and byte counts (which change on every merge and so can never be
# registered)"; a suite total is the same kind of number, so it is now a COMMAND with a property
# instead of a digit. Correcting it a fourth time would have been the right number with the wrong
# shape, which is the defect §5.7 catalogues.
# THE FOUR ROWS CARRIED BELOW ARE NOT THIS TOOL'S, and the reason is the second half of the same finding.
# **And TWO of this tool's own rows duplicated two of them** — the tick contract and the idle layer's refusals
# had a row each under two names, which is the defect §10.2 exists to prevent (one fact, one row). They were
# merged on 2026-09-21: the carried wording kept, and the unique detail from the deleted copy (`8 named
# `as_*` methods`) folded INTO the row rather than dropped, because a fact deleted to fix a duplicate is a
# fact lost to a formatting problem.
# `city_doctrine.py` and `overlay_doctrine2.py` BOTH append to §10.2, so a region owned by two tools is a
# region where a reconcile in one destroys the other's work — and this reconcile did exactly that,

SURFACE_LAW = """### 31.9 The surface, as built — and the five defects that running it found

**`src/city.rs` is 1,887 lines and 20 tests hold it.** It renders `seasons/plans/view.json` as a playable
isometric city, and it is the surface `3DUI.MD` specifies for phases **B1–B4 and B6–B9**.

#### What it is, and what it is not

It is an **egui painter doing true isometric projection**. It is **not** the wgpu/WGSL pipeline
`3DUI.MD` §13 specifies — no bloom, no glass refraction, no aurora ribbon, no instanced mesh, no WASM
build. Two reasons, and the second is decisive:

```text
P3  "legibility over spectacle"     a painter satisfies the pillar's first requirement; bloom satisfies
                                    neither P3 nor P6
rule 36  verify the SURFACE         a shader pipeline CANNOT be exercised in this environment, so the
                                    wgpu half would have been unverifiable at the moment of writing —
                                    which is this campaign's recurring defect, not a shortcut avoided
```

So the projection and the layout are **pure functions with tests instead**: the camera round-trips over
all **576** tiles, a changed `grid.tilt` changes the projection (proving the parameter is not decoration),
and a headless render of the real view emits shapes and answers a click. **These are claims a shader would
not have made checkable.**

#### The three things the surface may not do

```text
1  it may not COMPUTE a control status. Every mechanical_status is copied from the view. status_colour
   has an explicit Unknown arm, so an unrecognised status renders as unknown rather than defaulting to
   green — the same rule as section 9.7's no-default-to-PUBLIC, applied to a colour. A default here is
   how a lens starts lying without anyone editing it.
2  it may not RESOLVE an open question. A monument shows the constraint and a fog region is DEFERRED.
   The attempt is a fog ticket, and resolution is a governed merge.
3  it may not PRESENT a partial measurement as a whole one. The C19 stamp is shown with its COVERAGE
   (`v1 · on 11/11 tickets`), because C19 requires every ticket to carry a version and a version alone
   is a claim where a version with its coverage is a measurement.
```

#### What it MAY do, and why that is not adjudication

`spatial_verdict` tests a tile against the `regions` array the view already carries. That is **geometry
over data**, and 3DUI.MD §4.3 assigns it to the surface outright. Three things keep it from creeping:

```text
it is NAMED SpatialVerdict, and every label carries the words "spatial only"
it carries a DISCLAIMER naming overlay.py adjudicate as the only adjudicator
the disclaimer is PAINTED ON THE CANVAS, because the canvas is what a screenshot shows
```

A wall beats a fog when both cover a tile — **refusal is the safer of two answers**, and a tile that is
both deferred and refused must not read as merely deferred.

#### Two consequences that are easy to get backwards

**A multi-civilian locus renders as FOG, not as a building.** Whose income, whose evidence, whose grade
is an open question (§30.2), and drawing it solid would answer that question with geometry.
**The risk layer R7–R11 is never folded into the controls C9–C20** (§7.2) — and a test asserts the *view*
keeps them in separate fields, so concatenating them would be a contract change rather than a rendering
choice.

#### The five defects, and the one that matters

Every one was found by **running** something, and none by reading — which is §13.3's standing lesson,
confirmed a fourth time.

```text
1  the governor stamp read a DICT'S KEYS        `of_type()` returns a dict keyed by record id, so
                                                iterating it yields IDS. `isinstance(t, dict)` was the
                                                guard and was False on all 11 tickets. It reported
                                                `0 of 11` — silently, plausibly, with every appearance
                                                of a measurement. A guard that can only ever return one
                                                value reads as rigour and is decoration (§6.4).
2  the view did not carry what the surface needs  the four BILLING-BASIS NAMES (§8.1) and the C19 stamp
                                                were absent. The renderer could have spelled doctrine
                                                for itself — the defect §31.1 names — or dropped the
                                                four-way split, which is the one thing C01's openness
                                                exists to make visible. Fixed at the source: a key the
                                                surface needs is a VIEW defect when missing.
3  the interaction test asserted `>=`           it passed whether the click worked or not. Tightened to
                                                `==`, it failed at once and revealed the real defect:
                                                it had been clicking a coordinate the layout never uses.
                                                The surface now REPORTS its own canvas geometry.
4  the marker guard tested a document too small   a two-key JSON literal fails on a MISSING FIELD, not on
                                                the marker. The fixture now mutates the real document.
5  twelve parsed fields were never displayed     including `identity_status`, which is PROCEDURAL on ALL
                                                TWELVE controls. The compiler called it a lint; the
                                                finding is that rule 100's second half — the half no
                                                mechanism in this stack can verify — was invisible in the
                                                surface built to show it.
```

**Finding FC-10, and it is about verification rather than about the surface.** The mechanical half of
this work was cheap: hashes, round-trips, counts, an exit code. **All five defects were in the half that
is not.** Four of the five were in this session's own machinery, and the fifth was a rendered
overstatement. The mechanical checks were correct throughout and would have passed a build that hid a
PROCEDURAL governance layer behind a green city.

> **FC-10: a surface's mechanical checks prove it is well-formed, never that it is honest. Where a
> surface is the deliverable, the assertion that matters is about what it DISPLAYS — and a display
> default is a governance decision made in code.**

### 31.10 Binding rules 117-119

```text
117. A surface may not hold one field it does not display. A parsed-but-unshown field is not a lint; it
     is the surface withholding the fact it was handed, and where the field is a governance fact
     (identity_status, a citation, a coverage figure) the omission is the overstatement. The compiler's
     unused-field warning is the cheapest possible detector of this and it is already free.
118. Every measurement a surface displays must carry the coverage or the denominator it is a fraction
     of. "governor v1" is a claim; "v1 on 11/11 tickets" is a measurement. This generalises section
     13.2's warning about the verify ratio and section 6.3 rule 2's open/closed board: a bare number
     invited the reader to supply the denominator themselves, and they will supply a favourable one.
119. A lens may refuse SPATIALLY and may never refuse GOVERNANCE-WISE. Testing a proposed tile against
     a region the view carries is geometry; computing whether a control passes is authority. The two are
     distinguished by NAME, by a disclaimer carried with the verdict, and by that disclaimer being
     painted where a screenshot can see it — because a surface's own refusal is the artifact most likely
     to be read as the governor's answer.
```
