pub struct CiviliansPanel {
    analysis: Option<Analysis>,
    source: Option<PathBuf>,
    error: Option<String>,
    selected: usize,
    reload_counter: usize,
}

impl Default for CiviliansPanel {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            analysis: None,
            source: None,
            error: None,
            selected: 0,
            reload_counter: 0,
        }
    }
}

impl CiviliansPanel {
    /// Read the derived view. Returns the error rather than a partial view: a panel that rendered a
    /// partially-parsed analysis would show an empty population as though the population were empty.
    fn read() -> Result<(Analysis, PathBuf), String> {
        let path = locate_analysis().ok_or_else(|| {
            "seasons/civilians/analysis.json was not found — run `python civilians.py analyze`".to_owned()
        })?;
        let raw = fs::read_to_string(&path)
            .map_err(|error| format!("could not read {}: {error}", path.display()))?;
        let analysis: Analysis = serde_json::from_str(&raw)
            .map_err(|error| format!("{} is not the derived view: {error}", path.display()))?;
        // A PARSE IS NOT A RECOGNITION. Every field here is `#[serde(default)]`, and serde's derived
        // deserializer also accepts a JSON ARRAY by filling the defaults — so `[]` parses cleanly into
        // an empty `Analysis`. Testing for a parse error would therefore have accepted a document that
        // is not this view at all and rendered an empty population, which is indistinguishable from an
        // empty store. The guard is the marker the view itself carries.
        if !analysis.derived_view {
            return Err(format!(
                "{} parsed but does not declare `derived_view: true`, so it is not the view this panel \
                 renders (section 2.6)",
                path.display()
            ));
        }
        Ok((analysis, path))
    }

    pub fn reload(&mut self) {
        match Self::read() {
            Ok((analysis, path)) => {
                self.analysis = Some(analysis);
                self.source = Some(path);
                self.error = None;
            }
            Err(error) => {
                self.analysis = None;
                self.error = Some(error);
            }
        }
        self.reload_counter += 1;
    }

    pub fn render(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui) {
        if self.analysis.is_none() && self.error.is_none() {
            self.reload();
        }
        ui.horizontal(|ui| {
            ui.heading("Civilians");
            ui.separator();
            if ui.button("Reload analysis").clicked() {
                self.reload();
            }
            if let Some(path) = &self.source {
                ui.small(format!("{} (read {}×)", path.display(), self.reload_counter));
            }
        });

        if let Some(error) = &self.error {
            ui.colored_label(egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60), error);
            return;
        }
        let Some(analysis) = self.analysis.clone() else {
            return;
        };

        // The view is not a record, and the panel says so where a reader will see it rather than in a
        // doc comment: a UI that presented a derived view as the store would be the §2.6 defect.
        ui.colored_label(
            egui::Color32::from_rgb(230, 218, 127),
            format!(
                "DERIVED VIEW — not canonical (§2.6) · store digest {} · {} records · {} defects",
                analysis.store_digest.chars().take(16).collect::<String>(),
                analysis.counts.civilians,
                analysis.counts.defects,
            ),
        );
        ui.small(&analysis.derived_view_note);
        ui.separator();

        self.render_bills(ui, &analysis);
        ui.separator();
        self.render_population(ui, &analysis);
    }

    fn render_bills(&self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, analysis: &Analysis) {
        ui.heading(format!("Founding instruments ({})", analysis.bills.len()));
        ui.small(&analysis.bills_note);
        ui.add_space(4.0);
        for bill in &analysis.bills {
            let source = &bill.primary_source;
            let badge = if source.hash_matches {
                egui::Color32::from_rgb(76, 220, 76)
            } else {
                egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60)
            };
            let header = format!(
                "{} · {} · {} · {} clauses ({} mapped, {} UNMAPPED)",
                bill.bill_id,
                bill.instrument_class,
                bill.status,
                bill.clause_report.clauses,
                bill.clause_report.mapped,
                bill.clause_report.unmapped,
            );
            egui::CollapsingHeader::new(header)
                .id_salt(format!("bill_{}", bill.bill_id))
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label(&bill.title);
                    // READ FROM THE RECORD, not asserted by the panel. `grants_authority` is false for
                    // every bill and the field exists so the falsehood is checkable rather than
                    // implied — a UI that printed the claim regardless of the value would be exactly
                    // the "promise kept by a template" that §7.7's third refusal is about.
                    ui.colored_label(
                        if bill.grants_authority {
                            egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60)
                        } else {
                            egui::Color32::from_rgb(230, 218, 127)
                        },
                        format!(
                            "grants_authority: {} — subordinate to {}",
                            bill.grants_authority, bill.subordinate_to
                        ),
                    );
                    if bill.applies_to_all_civilians {
                        ui.small("applies_to: * — resolved per civilian, never shown as a wildcard");
                    }
                    if let Some(successor) = &bill.superseded_by {
                        ui.colored_label(
                            egui::Color32::from_rgb(120, 190, 255),
                            format!("SUPERSEDED BY {successor} — not refused, and the record stays (§8.2)"),
                        );
                    }
                    if let Some(note) = &bill.enactment_note {
                        ui.small(note);
                    }
                    ui.add_space(4.0);
                    ui.horizontal(|ui| {
                        ui.colored_label(
                            badge,
                            if source.hash_matches {
                                format!("sha256 re-read OK · {} bytes · ladder {}", source.bytes, source.ladder)
                            } else {
                                "ARTIFACT HASH MISMATCH — rule 2".to_owned()
                            },
                        );
                    });
                    if let Some(error) = &source.hash_error {
                        ui.colored_label(egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60), error);
                    }
                    ui.monospace(&source.artifact);
                    ui.small(format!("holder: {}", source.holder));
                    ui.small(format!("url: {}", source.url));
                    // THREE provenance shapes, rendered differently. Collapsing them is how a source
                    // nobody checked comes to look like a source with one variant, which is the whole
                    // reason the third instrument carries an absence instead of a number.
                    match (&source.intermediary, source.known_variants) {
                        (Some(relay), _) if relay == "NOT_STATED" => {
                            ui.colored_label(
                                egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 160, 60),
                                "intermediary: NOT STATED — the chain STOPS here, it does not continue",
                            );
                            ui.small(format!(
                                "absence verified {} · {} ·",
                                source.intermediary_absent_verified_at.as_deref().unwrap_or("UNDATED"),
                                source.intermediary_absence_how.as_deref().unwrap_or("no method recorded"),
                            ));
                        }
                        (Some(relay), _) => {
                            ui.small(format!("intermediary (required at ladder C): {relay}"));
                        }
                        (None, _) => {}
                    }
                    match source.known_variants {
                        Some(count) if count > 1 => {
                            ui.small(format!(
                                "variant {:?} of {count} — an unnamed copy is refused",
                                source.variant.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "NONE".into()),
                            ));
                        }
                        Some(_) => {}
                        None => {
                            // Not a blank line and not a zero. The unnamed-variant check CANNOT be
                            // applied to this source, and the panel says which check it cannot run.
                            ui.colored_label(
                                egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 160, 60),
                                format!(
                                    "variant count: NOT ESTABLISHED ({}) — the unnamed-variant check \
                                     cannot be applied, so it is unknown and not 1",
                                    source.variant_count_status.as_deref().unwrap_or("unrecorded"),
                                ),
                            );
                            if let Some(note) = &source.variant_note {
                                ui.small(note);
                            }
                        }
                    }
                    ui.small(format!(
                        "quotes verified verbatim: {}/{}",
                        bill.clause_report.quoted, bill.clause_report.clauses
                    ));
                    ui.add_space(4.0);
                    for clause in &bill.clauses {
                        let color = if let Some(reason) = &clause.unmapped_reason {
                            ui.colored_label(egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 160, 60), "UNMAPPED");
                            ui.label(format!("{}  ({})", clause.text, clause.kind));
                            ui.small(format!("why: {reason}"));
                            continue;
                        } else {
                            egui::Color32::from_rgb(180, 220, 160)
                        };
                        ui.colored_label(color, format!("{} → {}", clause.clause_id, clause.maps_to_rule));
                        ui.label(&clause.text);
                        ui.small(format!("\u{201c}{}\u{201d}", clause.quote));
                    }
                    ui.add_space(4.0);
                    ui.small(&bill.clause_report.honest_limit);
                });
        }
    }

    fn render_population(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, analysis: &Analysis) {
        ui.heading(format!("Population ({})", analysis.civilians.len()));
        if analysis.civilians.is_empty() {
            ui.small("no civilians in the store");
            return;
        }
        if self.selected >= analysis.civilians.len() {
            self.selected = 0;
        }
        ui.horizontal_wrapped(|ui| {
            for (index, civilian) in analysis.civilians.iter().enumerate() {
                let label = format!(
                    "{} · {} · grade {}",
                    civilian.civilian_id, civilian.lifecycle_state, civilian.unit_grade
                );
                ui.selectable_value(&mut self.selected, index, label);
            }
        });
        ui.separator();

        let civilian = &analysis.civilians[self.selected];
        if !civilian.jobs.is_empty() {
            ui.label(format!("Jobs ({})", civilian.jobs.len()));
            for job in &civilian.jobs {
                ui.monospace(format!(
                    "{}  {}  supervisor {}  band {}  {}c  {} ticket(s) closed",
                    job.job_id,
                    job.status,
                    job.supervisor_id.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "—".into()),
                    job.effort_band.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "—".into()),
                    job.amount_cents.unwrap_or(0),
                    job.tickets_closed,
                ));
            }
            ui.small(
                "A supervisor is a civilian, so §27.7's control C12 has a job to compare rather than a \
                 field it cannot evaluate.",
            );
            ui.add_space(6.0);
        }

        egui::Grid::new("civilian_identity")
            .num_columns(2)
            .spacing([18.0, 4.0])
            .show(ui, |ui| {
                ui.label("lifecycle");
                ui.monospace(&civilian.lifecycle_state);
                ui.end_row();
                ui.label("job class");
                ui.monospace(&civilian.job_class);
                ui.end_row();
                ui.label("unit grade");
                ui.monospace(format!(
                    "{} (the F..SSS ladder — S is stronger than A, §19.2)",
                    civilian.unit_grade
                ));
                ui.end_row();
                ui.label("certification tier");
                ui.monospace(format!(
                    "{} (a requirement set, not a confidence scale, §19.1)",
                    civilian.certification_tier
                ));
                ui.end_row();
                ui.label("income");
                ui.monospace(format!(
                    "{} cents {} · verified by a governor record, never self-certified (§9.6)",
                    civilian.income.total_cents, civilian.income.currency
                ));
                ui.end_row();
            });

        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label(format!("Tickets ({})", civilian.tickets.len()));
        for ticket in &civilian.tickets {
            ui.monospace(format!(
                "{}  {} / {}  job {}  governor v{}",
                ticket.ticket_id,
                ticket.status,
                ticket.verify_status,
                ticket.job_id.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "—".into()),
                ticket
                    .governor_base_version
                    .map(|version| version.to_string())
                    .unwrap_or_else(|| "—".into()),
            ));
            ui.small(format!("evidence: {}", ticket.evidence.join(", ")));
        }
        ui.small(
            "A ticket is filed BEFORE the work runs and records the governor version it was evaluated \
             under, so \"why was this allowed at the time?\" is answerable later (§6.3).",
        );

        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label("Instruments applying to this civilian");
        ui.small(
            "A bill grants nothing: it is listed so it can be read and audited (§0.2, rule 76). \
             The wildcard is resolved per civilian rather than shown.",
        );
        for reference in &civilian.bills {
            ui.monospace(format!(
                "{}  {}  {} clauses  {} mapped  {} UNMAPPED",
                reference.bill_id, reference.status, reference.clauses, reference.mapped, reference.unmapped
            ));
        }

        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label(format!("Claims ({})", civilian.claims.len()));
        if civilian.claims.is_empty() {
            ui.small("no claims");
        }
        for claim in &civilian.claims {
            let label = format!(
                "{} · {} · {}",
                claim.claim_id,
                claim.computed_level.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "no level".into()),
                if claim.resume_safe { "resume-safe" } else { "WITHHELD" }
            );
            egui::CollapsingHeader::new(label)
                .id_salt(format!("claim_{}", claim.claim_id))
                .show(ui, |ui| {
                    ui.label(&claim.statement);
                    if let Some(reason) = &claim.computed_reason {
                        ui.small(format!("computed because: {reason}"));
                    }
                    if let Some(withheld) = &claim.withheld_reason {
                        ui.colored_label(egui::Color32::from_rgb(230, 218, 127), format!("withheld: {withheld}"));
                    }
                    if let Some(ignored) = &claim.ignored_assertion {
                        ui.colored_label(
                            egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60),
                            format!("asserted strength DISCARDED, reported as ignoredAssertion: {ignored}"),
                        );
                    }
                    if !claim.forbidden_words.is_empty() {
                        ui.colored_label(
                            egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60),
                            format!("forbidden words without evidence: {}", claim.forbidden_words.join(", ")),
                        );
                    }
                    if !claim.digits_without_metric.is_empty() {
                        ui.colored_label(
                            egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60),
                            format!(
                                "digits with no metric on this claim's own evidence (§7.7 refusal 2): {}",
                                claim.digits_without_metric.join(", ")
                            ),
                        );
                    }
                    ui.small(format!("evidence: {}", claim.evidence.join(", ")));
                    ui.small(format!(
                        "origin: {}",
                        claim.origin.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "derived".into())
                    ));
                });
        }

        if !civilian.income.records.is_empty() {
            ui.add_space(6.0);
            ui.label(format!("Income records ({})", civilian.income.records.len()));
            for record in &civilian.income.records {
                ui.monospace(format!(
                    "{}  {}c  ticket {}  verified by {}",
                    record.income_id, record.amount_cents, record.ticket_id, record.verified_by
                ));
                ui.small(format!("measured from {}", record.source_artifact));
            }
            ui.small(
                "A dollar is not income until a receipt cites it, and a civilian cannot certify its own \
                 income (§9.6 rule 1).",
            );
        }

        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label("Promotions and retirement");
        for promotion in &civilian.promotions {
            let regression = promotion.classification.as_deref() == Some("regression");
            ui.colored_label(
                if regression {
                    egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60)
                } else {
                    egui::Color32::from_rgb(76, 220, 76)
                },
                format!(
                    "{} {} {} → {} · {}",
                    promotion.promotion_id,
                    promotion.verb,
                    promotion.from_grade,
                    promotion.to_grade,
                    if regression {
                        "REFUSED: an attempt with a regression is a retirement, not a promotion (rule 98)"
                    } else {
                        "authorized by the Governor, not by the civilian"
                    }
                ),
            );
        }
        if let Some(retirement) = &civilian.retirement {
            ui.label(format!(
                "{} · {} · final grade {} / tier {} · {}",
                retirement.retirement_id,
                retirement.retirement_reason,
                retirement.final_unit_grade,
                retirement.final_certification_tier,
                retirement.career_result
            ));
        }

        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label("Backward pass — result back to the Governor Base version (§27.12)");
        for chain in &civilian.backward_chain {
            let color = if chain.verdict == "OK" {
                egui::Color32::from_rgb(76, 220, 76)
            } else {
                egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60)
            };
            ui.colored_label(color, format!("{} · {} · {} steps", chain.civilian_id, chain.verdict, chain.steps.len()));
            for step in &chain.steps {
                ui.monospace(format!("  {}  {}", step.status, step.chain));
            }
        }

        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label("Forward pass (§27.13)");
        for arrow in &analysis.forward_pass.arrows {
            let color = match arrow.status.as_str() {
                "OK" => egui::Color32::from_rgb(76, 220, 76),
                "BLOCKED" => egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60),
                _ => egui::Color32::from_rgb(150, 150, 150),
            };
            ui.colored_label(color, format!("{:>2}. {} → {} · {}", arrow.index, arrow.from, arrow.to, arrow.status));
            ui.small(&arrow.detail);
            if let Some(class) = &arrow.block_class {
                ui.small(format!("block class: {class}"));
            }
        }

        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label("Controls — the mechanical half and the identity half (§27.14, rule 100)");
        ui.small(
            "One status for both halves is the defect FC-10 names: the data can be checked here, and \
             whether the actor was really the actor cannot.",
        );
        for control in &analysis.controls {
            ui.monospace(format!(
                "{}  mechanical: {}   identity: {}",
                control.control, control.mechanical_status, control.identity_status
            ));
            ui.small(&control.requirement);
        }

        ui.add_space(6.0);
        ui.label(format!("Store defects ({})", analysis.defects.len()));
        for defect in &analysis.defects {
            let color = match defect.severity.as_str() {
                "blocking" => egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 60, 60),
                "medium" => egui::Color32::from_rgb(200, 160, 60),
                _ => egui::Color32::from_rgb(150, 150, 150),
            };
            ui.colored_label(color, format!("[{}] {}", defect.severity, defect.r#where));
            ui.small(&defect.what);
        }
    }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::CiviliansPanel;
    use crate::civilians;

    /// Parse the REAL derived view. This is the check a schema drift would fail: the Python view and
    /// these structs are two languages describing one file, and §6.4's rule — every added field is a
    /// two-language change or it is decoration — has no enforcement unless something parses the file.
    #[test]
    fn parses_the_real_derived_view() {
        let (analysis, path) = CiviliansPanel::read().expect("the derived view should parse");
        assert!(analysis.derived_view, "the view must declare itself derived (section 2.6)");
        assert!(!analysis.store_digest.is_empty(), "a view that cannot name its inputs is not checkable");
        assert!(!analysis.civilians.is_empty(), "{} held no civilians", path.display());
        // The count is compared against the view's OWN `counts.bills`, not a literal. This asserted
        // `4` until the progression pipeline took the corpus to sixteen, and a literal here makes every
        // corpus change a Rust edit — which is exactly how a cross-language field goes unchecked.
        // Comparing the list against the count tests the property that matters instead: the two halves
        // of one JSON document agree.
        assert_eq!(
            analysis.bills.len(),
            analysis.counts.bills,
            "the bill list and the view's own bill count disagree — one of them is lying"
        );
        assert!(!analysis.bills.is_empty(), "the view held no bills at all");
        // And every record declares a sanctioned class, which is the field the widened vocabulary
        // lives in. §6.4 — an added field is a two-language change or it is decoration — has no
        // enforcement unless a READER on the other side exercises it.
        for bill in &analysis.bills {
            assert!(
                crate::civilians::INSTRUMENT_CLASSES.contains(&bill.instrument_class.as_str()),
                "{} declares unsanctioned instrument_class {:?}",
                bill.bill_id,
                bill.instrument_class
            );
        }
    }

    /// The provenance states must remain DISTINGUISHABLE after the trip through JSON, because a
    /// source nobody checked and a source with one variant are otherwise the same shape (§17 rule 4).
    #[test]
    fn an_unestablished_provenance_stays_unestablished() {
        let (analysis, _) = CiviliansPanel::read().expect("the derived view should parse");
        let farewell = analysis
            .bills
            .iter()
            .find(|b| b.bill_id == "bill_farewell_1796")
            .expect("the farewell counsel should be in the view");
        assert!(
            farewell.primary_source.known_variants.is_none(),
            "an unestablished variant count must not arrive as a number"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            farewell.primary_source.variant_count_status.as_deref(),
            Some("not_found"),
            "and it must say WHY it is unknown, or unknown reads like zero"
        );
        assert_eq!(
            farewell.primary_source.intermediary.as_deref(),
            Some("NOT_STATED")
        );
        assert!(
            farewell.primary_source.intermediary_absent_verified_at.is_some(),
            "an undated absence is a claim about every future version of the page"
        );
        // and the three sources whose counts WERE established must still read as numbers
        for id in ["bill_declaration_1776", "bill_articles_1781", "bill_gettysburg_1863"] {
            let bill = analysis.bills.iter().find(|b| b.bill_id == id).expect(id);
            assert!(
                bill.primary_source.known_variants.is_some(),
                "{id} lost a count that was established"
            );
        }
    }

    /// The two facts the panel exists to show, asserted rather than rendered.
    #[test]
    fn no_instrument_grants_authority_and_every_clause_is_quoted() {
        let (analysis, _) = CiviliansPanel::read().expect("the derived view should parse");
        for bill in &analysis.bills {
            assert!(!bill.grants_authority, "{} claims to grant authority", bill.bill_id);
            assert!(bill.primary_source.hash_matches, "{} cites bytes that moved", bill.bill_id);
            assert_eq!(
                bill.clause_report.quoted,
                bill.clauses.len(),
                "{} has a clause whose quote was not verified",
                bill.bill_id
            );
            for clause in &bill.clauses {
                assert!(!clause.quote.is_empty(), "{} has a clause with no quote", bill.bill_id);
                if !clause.mapped {
                    assert!(
                        clause.unmapped_reason.is_some(),
                        "{} {} is unmapped and gives no reason",
                        bill.bill_id,
                        clause.clause_id
                    );
                }
            }
        }
    }

    /// A parse is not a recognition, and this test is the measured reason the guard exists.
    #[test]
    fn a_document_that_is_not_the_view_is_refused_by_the_marker() {
        // `[]` DOES parse — serde fills every defaulted field from a sequence — so a parse-error test
        // would have passed a document that is not this view at all.
        let from_a_sequence = serde_json::from_str::<civilians::Analysis>("[]")
            .expect("serde accepts a sequence for a fully-defaulted struct");
        assert!(from_a_sequence.civilians.is_empty());
        assert!(!from_a_sequence.derived_view, "and it does NOT claim to be the view");

        let unknown = serde_json::from_str::<civilians::Analysis>("{\"unexpected\": true}")
            .expect("unknown fields are ignored");
        assert!(!unknown.derived_view);
    }

    /// The condition `read()` refuses on, asserted directly so the guard cannot be removed silently.
    #[test]
    fn the_real_view_carries_the_marker_the_guard_tests() {
        let (analysis, _) = CiviliansPanel::read().expect("the derived view should parse");
        assert!(analysis.derived_view);
        assert!(!analysis.derived_view_note.is_empty());
    }
}

/// Walk up from the UI directory (and the executable) to the project root and find the store.
fn locate_analysis() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut starts = Vec::new();
    if let Ok(current) = std::env::current_dir() {
        starts.push(current);
    }
    if let Ok(executable) = std::env::current_exe() {
        if let Some(parent) = executable.parent() {
            starts.push(parent.to_owned());
        }
    }
    starts.push(PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")));

    for mut current in starts {
        loop {
            let candidate = current.join("civilians").join("analysis.json");
            if candidate.is_file() {
                return Some(candidate);
            }
            let canonical = current.join("seasons").join("civilians").join("analysis.json");
            if canonical.is_file() {
                return Some(canonical);
            }
            if !current.pop() {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    None
}
