#### `rust-ui/src/city.rs`

```rust
//! city.rs — the isometric surface for the overlay's derived view.
//!
//! Spec: `3DUI.MD` (市民都市 SHIMIN TOSHI, `civilian-overlay:city`), phases B1–B4 and B6–B9; doctrine
//! sections 31.1–31.6. Reads `seasons/plans/view.json` and nothing else, and writes only to the
//! non-authoritative plan store.
//!
//! # What this module is allowed to do, and what it must never do
//!
//! The doctrine's line (section 31.1, rule 56, rule 112) is that a surface **reports**; it never
//! **adjudicates**. Three consequences shape every function here, and each has a test that fails
//! without it:
//!
//! 1. **A control status is copied, never computed.** Every `mechanical_status` the renderer draws is
//!    the string from the view. `status_colour` has an explicit `Unknown` arm, so an unrecognised
//!    status renders as *unknown* rather than defaulting to green — the same rule as section 9.7's
//!    "no default-to-PUBLIC", applied to a colour. A default here would make an unread status look
//!    like a passing one.
//!
//! 2. **Spatial refusal is not adjudication.** `spatial_verdict` tests a tile against the `regions`
//!    array the view already carries. That is geometry over data, and 3DUI.MD §4.3 explicitly assigns
//!    it to the surface ("a zone that touches a fog region is deferred, not accepted"). It is named
//!    `SpatialVerdict` and it carries a disclaimer, because the governor's own verdict comes from
//!    `python overlay.py adjudicate` — and a UI that showed its own geometry as the governor's answer
//!    would have taken merge authority by accident.
//!
//! 3. **The camera comes from the view.** `tilt` and `rotation` are read from `grid`, not hardcoded, so
//!    the projection contract lives in one place. A client that hardcoded 30° would silently disagree
//!    with a view that changed its mind.
//!
//! # The honest limit of this surface
//!
//! It is an **egui painter** doing true isometric projection, **not** a wgpu/WGSL pipeline. `3DUI.MD`
//! §13 specifies a 14-pass GPU renderer with bloom and glass refraction; that is not built, and this
//! module does not claim it. Two reasons, stated rather than implied:
//!
//! * **P3 ranks legibility above spectacle.** Every visual encoding here maps to a named doctrine
//!   status, which is the pillar's first requirement and its second is "no visual without a source".
//!   Bloom is in §13 and is the *last* thing §13 needs.
//! * **A GPU pass cannot be verified in this environment.** Rule 36 says verify the SURFACE rather than
//!   the API behind it, and a pipeline nobody can look at is exactly the artifact that would be
//!   declared done on the strength of its own build log. The projection and the layout are pure
//!   functions with tests instead; a shader would have neither.

use std::collections::BTreeMap;
use std::fs;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};

use eframe::egui;
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The derived view — serde model mirroring seasons/plans/view.json
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Grid {
    pub projection: String,
    pub rotation: f32,
    pub tilt: f32,
    pub size: i32,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Avatar {
    pub civilian_id: String,
    pub lifecycle_state: String,
    pub unit_grade: String,
    pub certification_tier: String,
    pub has_job: bool,
    pub income_basis: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub self_witness_genesis: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Locus {
    pub civilian_id: String,
    pub grade_class: String,
    pub height: f32,
    /// The view's own note that `JOB_CLASSES` is the promotion ladder and not a job taxonomy. Carried
    /// into the tooltip rather than dropped, because it is the reason the surface must not label a
    /// locus with an invented job class.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub job_class_source: String,
    pub tile: [i32; 2],
    pub occupancy: u32,
    pub multi_civilian: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Control {
    pub control: String,
    pub requirement: String,
    pub mechanical_status: String,
    pub identity_status: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct RegionRec {
    pub region_id: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub label: String,
    pub citation: String,
    pub kanji: String,
    /// `[x0, y0, x1, y1]`
    pub rect: [i32; 4],
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Monument {
    pub id: String,
    pub question: Option<String>,
    pub state: String,
    pub citation: String,
    pub resolve_available: bool,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Gate {
    pub action: String,
    pub kanji: String,
    pub citation: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct Risk {
    pub id: String,
    pub risk: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct ProposalRec {
    pub outcome: String,
    pub note: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub highlighted_tiles: Vec<[i32; 2]>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct GovernorStamp {
    pub versions: Vec<i64>,
    pub declared_on: u32,
    pub of_tickets: u32,
    pub citation: String,
}

/// One authorized fiction, as the view carries it. **Read-only, and never a locus.**
///
/// Every field here is either an identity or a STABLE component. There is deliberately no
/// `current_yield` field on this struct: a number computed by the producer would be correct only at the
/// tick the view was derived at, and the surface's clock runs on afterwards — so a stale value rendered
/// as current is exactly the read, rather than the write, that `PLAN_JOBS.md` is built to avoid.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct IdleJobRec {
    pub idle_id: String,
    pub kind: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub kanji: String,
    /// Always `true`, and carried anyway. A consumer that had to infer "is this fiction?" from the key
    /// it arrived under would be one rename away from rendering a fiction as a citizen.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub fiction: bool,
    pub civilian_id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub anchor_id: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tile: [i32; 2],
    pub base_yield: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub assigned_at_tick: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub yield_at_derived_tick: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub lens: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub citation: String,
}

/// The HUD's fiction numbers. Every one is reported AS a fiction count.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct IdleSummary {
    #[serde(default)]
    pub fiction: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub glyph: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub tick: i64,
    pub jobs: u32,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub per_kind: BTreeMap<String, u32>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub total_base_yield: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub total_yield_at_tick: i64,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub grade_effect: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub claim_effect: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub income_effect: bool,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub honest_limit: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub citation: String,
}

impl IdleSummary {
    /// The fiction's yield **at the surface's own clock**, computed from the stable base.
    ///
    /// This is the whole of "everything moves": the producer writes the base once, the surface
    /// multiplies by the clock it already advances, and the number on screen changes every tick without
    /// a single write to any store. `PLAN_JOBS.md` §5 — *a tick advances the CLOCK; the view's idle
    /// yields are a function of the tick the view was derived at* — implemented on the reading side,
    /// which is the side that is allowed to move.
    ///
    /// `clock` is a count of ticks the clock actually ran, so a paused clock passes the same value it
    /// last passed and the yield stands still. That is refusal 5 discharged by the arithmetic rather
    /// than by a check: there is no wall-clock term to subtract for elapsed real time.
    pub fn yield_at(&self, clock: i64) -> i64 {
        self.total_base_yield * clock.max(0)
    }

    /// The fiction count, named as fiction. The HUD shows this beside the civilian count and never
    /// folded into it (marking rule 2).
    pub fn fiction_count(&self) -> u32 {
        self.jobs
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Deserialize)]
pub struct CityView {
    pub view: String,
    pub derived_view: bool,
    pub authoritative: bool,
    pub plan_is_authoritative: bool,
    pub doctrine_hash: String,
    pub store_hash: String,
    pub honest_limit: String,
    pub grid: Grid,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub avatars: Vec<Avatar>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub loci: Vec<Locus>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub controls: Vec<Control>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub regions: Vec<RegionRec>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub monuments: Vec<Monument>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub never_granted: Vec<Gate>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub residual_risks: Vec<Risk>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub fog: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub out_of_scope: Vec<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub proposals: Vec<ProposalRec>,
    pub billing_bases: Vec<String>,
    pub billing_rate_settled: bool,
    pub billing_citation: String,
    pub governor_base_version: GovernorStamp,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub mechanical_distribution: BTreeMap<String, u32>,
    /// The tick these idle yields were computed at. Carried so a consumer can tell a fresh view from a
    /// stale one instead of assuming — the same discipline as the governor stamp's coverage figure.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub derived_at_tick: i64,
    /// **The authorized fiction, in its own key.** Never merged into `loci`: an idle block counted as a
    /// locus would make the civilian count wrong everywhere it is read, and the count is the number the
    /// whole overlay is trusted for.
    #[serde(default)]
    pub idle_jobs: Vec<IdleJobRec>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub idle_summary: Option<IdleSummary>,
}

impl CityView {
    /// The distribution the HUD displays — **the declared one**, never a recount.
    ///
    /// The renderer could count `controls`, and it would agree today. It must not, because the whole
    /// point of the field is that the view states a number and the surface shows that number: if the
    /// two ever disagreed, the disagreement is a finding about the *view*, and a renderer that
    /// silently recomputed would erase it.
    pub fn distribution(&self) -> (u32, u32, u32) {
        let get = |key: &str| self.mechanical_distribution.get(key).copied().unwrap_or(0);
        (get("MET"), get("FAILED"), get("NOT_EVALUABLE"))
    }

    pub fn governor_label(&self) -> String {
        let versions = if self.governor_base_version.versions.is_empty() {
            "v—".to_owned()
        } else {
            self.governor_base_version
                .versions
                .iter()
                .map(|v| format!("v{v}"))
                .collect::<Vec<_>>()
                .join(",")
        };
        format!(
            "{versions} · on {}/{} tickets",
            self.governor_base_version.declared_on, self.governor_base_version.of_tickets
        )
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Spatial refusal — geometry over the view's regions, NOT a control verdict
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A **view-level** spatial outcome. Explicitly not the governor's verdict.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
pub enum SpatialVerdict {
    /// No region of interest on any proposed tile.
    Clear,
    /// Touches a `fog` region: the doctrine has not decided, so the proposal is deferred.
    Deferred { region_id: String, citation: String, label: String, kanji: String },
    /// Touches a `wall` region: out of scope, refused, with the citation attached.
    Rejected { region_id: String, citation: String, label: String, kanji: String },
    /// No tiles proposed at all.
    Empty,
}

impl SpatialVerdict {
    /// The label that must accompany the verdict wherever it is shown, so the surface's own geometry
    /// is never read as the governor's answer. 3DUI.MD §14 and section 31.1 both turn on this.
    pub fn label(&self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Self::Clear => "CLEAR (spatial only)",
            Self::Deferred { .. } => "DEFERRED (spatial only)",
            Self::Rejected { .. } => "REJECTED (spatial only)",
            Self::Empty => "EMPTY",
        }
    }

    pub const DISCLAIMER: &'static str = "view-level spatial refusal only — the governor's verdict comes from `python overlay.py adjudicate`; this surface never adjudicates a control (section 31.1, rule 112)";

    pub fn citation(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            Self::Deferred { citation, .. } | Self::Rejected { citation, .. } => Some(citation),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    pub fn region_id(&self) -> Option<&str> {
        match self {
            Self::Deferred { region_id, .. } | Self::Rejected { region_id, .. } => Some(region_id),
            _ => None,
        }
    }
}

/// The region covering a tile, if any. A wall beats a fog when both somehow overlap, because refusal
/// is the safer of the two answers and a tile that is both deferred and refused must not read as
/// merely deferred.
pub fn region_at(tile: (i32, i32), regions: &[RegionRec]) -> Option<&RegionRec> {
    let mut fog: Option<&RegionRec> = None;
    for region in regions {
        let [x0, y0, x1, y1] = region.rect;
        if tile.0 >= x0 && tile.0 <= x1 && tile.1 >= y0 && tile.1 <= y1 {
            match region.kind.as_str() {
                "wall" => return Some(region),
                "fog" => fog = fog.or(Some(region)),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    fog
}

pub fn spatial_verdict(tiles: &[(i32, i32)], regions: &[RegionRec]) -> SpatialVerdict {
    if tiles.is_empty() {
        return SpatialVerdict::Empty;
    }
    let mut deferred: Option<&RegionRec> = None;
    for tile in tiles {
        if let Some(region) = region_at(*tile, regions) {
            match region.kind.as_str() {
                "wall" => {
                    return SpatialVerdict::Rejected {
                        region_id: region.region_id.clone(),
                        citation: region.citation.clone(),
                        label: region.label.clone(),
                        kanji: region.kanji.clone(),
                    }
                }
                "fog" => deferred = deferred.or(Some(region)),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
    }
    match deferred {
        Some(region) => SpatialVerdict::Deferred {
            region_id: region.region_id.clone(),
            citation: region.citation.clone(),
            label: region.label.clone(),
            kanji: region.kanji.clone(),
        },
        None => SpatialVerdict::Clear,
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Status colour — with NO default to MET
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum StatusColour {
    Met,
    Failed,
    NotEvaluable,
    /// **The identity axis's own word.** Added after measuring the live view: all twelve controls carry
    /// `identity_status: "PROCEDURAL"` on that axis and none carries `NOT_EVALUABLE`, so before this arm
    /// existed every identity reading fell through to `Unknown` and all twelve painted as unreadable.
    /// Twelve false alarms is the mirror of the defect `Unknown` exists to prevent.
    Procedural,
    /// A status string the surface does not recognise. Rendered as neither passing nor failing,
    /// because "I cannot read this" and "this passed" must never look the same (§9.7's no
    /// default-to-PUBLIC, and the reason this arm exists rather than a `_ => Met`).
    Unknown,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Glyph {
    Filled,
    Triangle,
    Diamond,
    /// Two statuses previously shared `Diamond` (`NotEvaluable` and `Unknown`), which defeats the whole
    /// point of a colour-blind supplement: shape has to distinguish the cases colour cannot.
    Hollow,
    Question,
}

pub fn status_colour(status: &str) -> StatusColour {
    match status {
        "MET" => StatusColour::Met,
        "FAILED" => StatusColour::Failed,
        "NOT_EVALUABLE" => StatusColour::NotEvaluable,
        "PROCEDURAL" => StatusColour::Procedural,
        _ => StatusColour::Unknown,
    }
}

/// §12.4's colour-blind supplement: status is carried by shape as well as colour, so the overlay is
/// readable without distinguishing green from amber.
///
/// **The mapping is injective** — asserted by a test. It was not, and two pairs shared a shape:
/// `NotEvaluable`/`Unknown` both drew a diamond, so an unreadable status and an unevaluable one were
/// indistinguishable without colour, which is exactly the reader the supplement is for.
pub fn status_glyph(status: &str) -> Glyph {
    match status_colour(status) {
        StatusColour::Met => Glyph::Filled,
        StatusColour::Failed => Glyph::Triangle,
        StatusColour::NotEvaluable => Glyph::Diamond,
        StatusColour::Procedural => Glyph::Hollow,
        StatusColour::Unknown => Glyph::Question,
    }
}

pub fn status_glyph_char(glyph: Glyph) -> &'static str {
    match glyph {
        Glyph::Filled => "\u{25cf}",
        Glyph::Triangle => "\u{25b2}",
        Glyph::Diamond => "\u{25c7}",
        Glyph::Hollow => "\u{25cb}",
        Glyph::Question => "?",
    }
}

/// The one mapping from a status word to a UI colour, **derived from `theme` rather than restated**.
///
/// Every arm reads a named token. It used to hold literals, which made a THIRD copy of the palette: the
/// shader constants in `theme`, the `Color32` UI constants in `theme`, and these tuples — and the
/// `PROCEDURAL` value existed in two of the three with no test between them. Literals are how a palette
/// becomes three palettes that agree until one is edited.
fn status_rgb(colour: StatusColour) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
    fn to_u8(c: [f32; 3]) -> (u8, u8, u8) {
        (
            (c[0] * 255.0).round() as u8,
            (c[1] * 255.0).round() as u8,
            (c[2] * 255.0).round() as u8,
        )
    }
    match colour {
        StatusColour::Met => to_u8(crate::theme::MET),
        StatusColour::Failed => to_u8(crate::theme::FAILED),
        StatusColour::NotEvaluable => to_u8(crate::theme::NOT_EVALUABLE),
        StatusColour::Procedural => to_u8(crate::theme::PROCEDURAL),
        StatusColour::Unknown => to_u8(crate::theme::UNKNOWN_STATUS),
    }
}

/// The status colour as an egui colour.
///
/// Public because the HUD needs it and because a second mapping from `StatusColour` to RGB is how two
/// views of one status start disagreeing — §31.1's defect with a wrapper around it.
pub fn status_tint(colour: StatusColour, alpha: u8) -> egui::Color32 {
    let (r, g, b) = status_rgb(colour);
    egui::Color32::from_rgba_unmultiplied(r, g, b, alpha)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The plan store — the ONLY path this surface writes, and it is non-authoritative
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PendingProposal {
    pub tool: String,
    pub kind: String,
    pub tiles: Vec<[i32; 2]>,
    pub spatial_verdict: String,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub spatial_citation: Option<String>,
    #[serde(default)]
    pub spatial_region: Option<String>,
    pub adjudicated: bool,
    pub note: String,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
pub struct PendingStore {
    pub view: String,
    pub authoritative: bool,
    pub adjudicated: bool,
    pub note: String,
    pub source: String,
    pub tick: u64,
    pub proposals: Vec<PendingProposal>,
}

impl PendingStore {
    fn empty() -> Self {
        Self {
            view: "civilian-overlay:city".to_owned(),
            authoritative: false,
            adjudicated: false,
            note: "PROPOSED IN THE SURFACE (3DUI.MD section 15.2). This is the non-authoritative plan \
                   store: no record here is a store record, nothing reads it to authorise an action, \
                   and only a governed merge may promote any of it into doctrine (rule 60)."
                .to_owned(),
            source: "rust-ui city surface".to_owned(),
            tick: 0,
            proposals: Vec::new(),
        }
    }
}

/// Append proposals to the pending plan store. Returns how many were written.
///
/// The surface writes here and **nowhere else**. `test_the_surface_writes_only_under_the_plan_store`
/// pins the root, because a UI that grew a second write path would be the exact thing section 31.1
/// exists to prevent, and it would grow one for a reasonable-sounding reason.
pub fn commit_to(path: &Path, proposals: &[PendingProposal], tick: u64) -> Result<usize, String> {
    let mut store = match fs::read_to_string(path) {
        Ok(raw) => serde_json::from_str::<PendingStore>(&raw)
            .map_err(|error| format!("{} is not the pending store: {error}", path.display()))?,
        Err(_) => PendingStore::empty(),
    };
    store.tick = tick;
    let written = proposals.len();
    store.proposals.extend_from_slice(proposals);
    if let Some(parent) = path.parent() {
        fs::create_dir_all(parent).map_err(|error| format!("could not create {}: {error}", parent.display()))?;
    }
    fs::write(
        path,
        serde_json::to_string_pretty(&store).map_err(|error| error.to_string())?,
    )
    .map_err(|error| format!("could not write {}: {error}", path.display()))?;
    Ok(written)
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Path resolution
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A cheap identity for the derived view, so a tick can ask "has it changed?" without reading it.
///
/// **Length alone is not an identity.** An edit that swaps a word for another of the same length
/// leaves the byte count untouched, and a poll keyed on length would report "unchanged" about a view
/// that had in fact been re-derived. `(len, mtime)` is still a *hint* rather than a hash — the honest
/// statement is that it can miss a same-length edit within a filesystem's timestamp resolution, and
/// the cost of that miss is one late poll, not a wrong render, because the next poll catches it.
/// A hash comparison is deliberately not used: a poll is on the frame path, and reading the whole
/// file every tick to decide whether to read the whole file would be the wrong shape.
pub fn file_stamp(path: &Path) -> Option<(u64, u64)> {
    let meta = std::fs::metadata(path).ok()?;
    let mtime = meta
        .modified()
        .ok()
        .and_then(|t| t.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).ok())
        .map(|d| d.as_nanos() as u64)?;
    Some((meta.len(), mtime))
}

/// Does a poll need to do anything, given what was on disk last time?
///
/// Pure, so the decision is testable without touching a filesystem — and total, because `None` on
/// either side means "we cannot compare", which must poll rather than assume. **An absent stamp is
/// not evidence of an unchanged file**, the same rule as §17 rule 4 (an unobserved metric is absent,
/// never 0) applied to a cache: the safe direction of an unknown is to re-read.
pub fn stamp_differs(previous: Option<(u64, u64)>, current: Option<(u64, u64)>) -> bool {
    match (previous, current) {
        (Some(a), Some(b)) => a != b,
        _ => true,
    }
}

/// How many ticks pass between two polls. **A poll is IO and a tick is not**, so the two cadences are
/// deliberately not the same number: at 10 Hz the surface would otherwise stat the view ten times a
/// second to learn nothing ten times.
///
/// Floors at one, so a rate slower than 1 Hz still polls every tick rather than never — a poll that
/// can be rounded to zero is a poll that stops running when the player asks for less motion.
pub fn poll_interval_ticks(hz: f32) -> u64 {
    if !hz.is_finite() || hz <= 0.0 {
        return 1;
    }
    (hz.round() as u64).max(1)
}

/// Walk up from the UI directory and the executable to find `seasons/plans/view.json`. Mirrors
/// `civilians::locate_analysis`, deliberately: two locators that disagreed about the root would find
/// two different projects.
pub fn locate_view() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut starts = Vec::new();
    if let Ok(current) = std::env::current_dir() {
        starts.push(current);
    }
    if let Ok(executable) = std::env::current_exe() {
        if let Some(parent) = executable.parent() {
            starts.push(parent.to_owned());
        }
    }
    starts.push(PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")));

    for mut current in starts {
        loop {
            for candidate in [
                current.join("plans").join("view.json"),
                current.join("seasons").join("plans").join("view.json"),
            ] {
                if candidate.is_file() {
                    return Some(candidate);
                }
            }
            if !current.pop() {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

/// The pending plan store beside the view it fills. Derived from the view's own directory so the two
/// cannot drift apart, and asserted to live under the plan store root.
pub fn pending_path(view_path: &Path) -> PathBuf {
    view_path.with_file_name("pending.json")
}

pub fn read_view(path: &Path) -> Result<CityView, String> {
    let raw = fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|error| format!("could not read {}: {error}", path.display()))?;
    let view: CityView =
        serde_json::from_str(&raw).map_err(|error| format!("{} is not the derived view: {error}", path.display()))?;
    recognise_view(view, &path.display().to_string())
}

/// The recognition half of reading a view, split out so a test can drive it from a string.
///
/// **A parse is not a recognition** (the same guard `civilians.rs` carries): every field is defaulted
/// where it can be, so `{}` parses cleanly into an empty view and would render an empty city that is
/// indistinguishable from an empty doctrine. The markers the view carries are the guard, and a
/// surface that checked only that the JSON parsed would be showing the player nothing while reporting
/// success.
fn recognise_view(view: CityView, source: &str) -> Result<CityView, String> {
    if !view.derived_view {
        return Err(format!(
            "{source} parsed but does not declare `derived_view: true`, so it is not the view this surface renders (section 2.6)"
        ));
    }
    if view.view != "civilian-overlay:city" {
        return Err(format!(
            "{source} declares view {:?}, not `civilian-overlay:city`",
            view.view
        ));
    }
    Ok(view)
}

/// Parse a view from a string, applying **the same recognition** `read_view` applies.
///
/// Test-only, and deliberately not a second implementation of the guards: a fixture helper that
/// skipped them would let the suite assert things about a view the real reader would refuse, so every
/// scene test would be verifying an unreachable surface.
#[cfg(test)]
pub fn parse_view_for_test(json: &str) -> Result<CityView, String> {
    let view: CityView = serde_json::from_str(json).map_err(|error| format!("fixture is not the view: {error}"))?;
    recognise_view(view, "fixture")
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The tools the player may propose with
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

pub const ZONE_KINDS: [&str; 6] = [
    "job", "genesis", "evidence", "retirement", "authority", "contract",
];

pub const NODE_KINDS: [&str; 6] = [
    "verifier", "authorizer", "genesis", "retirement", "ticket_display", "control_relay",
];

pub const ZONE_KANJI: [&str; 6] = ["職", "創", "証", "引", "権", "契"];
pub const NODE_KANJI: [&str; 6] = ["検", "認", "創", "退", "記", "統"];

/// 3DUI.MD §4.2: what each zone kind may be anchored to, and what it explicitly is not. Carried so the
/// tool palette can state its own refusal — a zone described only by its name invites the player to
/// assume it grants the thing it is named after.
pub fn zone_anchor(kind: &str) -> &'static str {
    match kind {
        "job" => "the `job` field — and JOB_CLASSES is the promotion ladder, NOT a job taxonomy",
        "genesis" => "the genesis contract (rule 95) — a genesis needs a distinct authorizer (C17)",
        "evidence" => "income verification (C13/C16) — MET green only while a verifier is present",
        "retirement" => "the retirement record and section 8.5's taxonomy (C20)",
        "authority" => "authorizer fields (rules 62, 97) — distinctness is the point",
        "contract" => "job contracts and the autonomy mode (act or propose)",
        _ => "no doctrine anchor",
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Tests — the projection, the spatial refusal, and the discipline the surface must not break
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    fn view() -> CityView {
        let path = locate_view().expect("seasons/plans/view.json — run `python overlay.py view`");
        read_view(&path).expect("the view must parse and declare its marker")
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // The poll: how a tick notices the season moved without the player doing anything
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    #[test]
    fn an_unknown_stamp_polls_rather_than_assumes() {
        // The same rule as §17 rule 4 — an unobserved value is ABSENT, never a default that reads as
        // good news. Here the default that reads as good news would be "unchanged", and it is the one
        // that would leave a stale city on screen forever.
        assert!(stamp_differs(None, Some((10, 20))));
        assert!(stamp_differs(Some((10, 20)), None));
        assert!(stamp_differs(None, None));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_matching_stamp_needs_no_read_and_a_different_one_does() {
        assert!(!stamp_differs(Some((100, 5000)), Some((100, 5000))));
        assert!(stamp_differs(Some((100, 5000)), Some((100, 5001))), "a touch is a change");
        assert!(
            stamp_differs(Some((100, 5000)), Some((101, 5000))),
            "a same-length edit inside one timestamp tick is missed by design — the next poll catches it"
        );
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_poll_interval_never_rounds_down_to_zero() {
        // A rate below 1 Hz must still poll, or asking for less motion would silently stop the city
        // from following its own store — which is a pause the player never asked for.
        assert_eq!(poll_interval_ticks(0.5), 1);
        assert_eq!(poll_interval_ticks(0.0), 1);
        assert_eq!(poll_interval_ticks(-3.0), 1);
        assert_eq!(poll_interval_ticks(f32::NAN), 1);
        assert_eq!(poll_interval_ticks(1.0), 1);
        assert_eq!(poll_interval_ticks(4.0), 4);
        assert_eq!(poll_interval_ticks(10.0), 10);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_real_view_has_a_stamp_and_a_missing_path_does_not() {
        let path = locate_view().expect("seasons/plans/view.json");
        let stamp = file_stamp(&path).expect("the real view is on disk");
        assert!(stamp.0 > 0, "a derived view is not an empty file");
        assert!(stamp.1 > 0, "and it has a modification time");
        // The negative control: a path that does not exist must not produce a stamp, because a stamp
        // for an absent file would make the next poll compare against a fiction.
        assert!(file_stamp(Path::new("seasons/plans/definitely-not-here.json")).is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn parses_the_real_derived_view() {
        let view = view();
        assert!(view.derived_view);
        assert!(!view.authoritative, "the view must not claim authority");
        assert!(!view.plan_is_authoritative);
        assert_eq!(view.controls.len(), 12);
        assert_eq!(view.never_granted.len(), 5);
        assert_eq!(view.billing_bases.len(), 4);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_document_that_is_not_the_view_is_refused_by_the_marker() {
        // Tests `read_view`, the guard — not serde. The first version of this test asserted on a
        // two-key document and would have passed for the wrong reason: the fixture was too small to
        // reach the guard, so it was testing a missing-field error and calling it a refusal.
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join("city_marker_test");
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();

        // Built from the REAL document rather than a synthetic one, so the fixture cannot be too
        // small to reach the guard — which is exactly how the first version of this test passed
        // while testing a missing-field error.
        let raw = fs::read_to_string(locate_view().unwrap()).unwrap();
        let mut doc: serde_json::Value = serde_json::from_str(&raw).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("not_the_view.json");
        doc["derived_view"] = serde_json::Value::Bool(false);
        fs::write(&path, serde_json::to_string(&doc).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let error = read_view(&path).expect_err("a document without the marker must be refused");
        assert!(error.contains("derived_view"), "{error}");

        // And a document that declares the marker but names another view.
        doc["derived_view"] = serde_json::Value::Bool(true);
        doc["view"] = serde_json::Value::String("civilian-overlay:something-else".into());
        fs::write(&path, serde_json::to_string(&doc).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let error = read_view(&path).expect_err("a differently-named view must be refused");
        assert!(error.contains("civilian-overlay:city"), "{error}");

        // And the real view passes both guards, so the test cannot pass by refusing everything.
        assert!(read_view(&locate_view().unwrap()).is_ok());
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }




    #[test]
    fn a_wall_tile_is_rejected_with_its_citation_and_a_fog_tile_is_deferred() {
        let view = view();
        let wall = view.regions.iter().find(|r| r.kind == "wall").expect("a wall region");
        let fog = view.regions.iter().find(|r| r.kind == "fog").expect("a fog region");
        let wall_tile = (wall.rect[0], wall.rect[1]);
        let fog_tile = (fog.rect[0], fog.rect[1]);

        let rejected = spatial_verdict(&[wall_tile], &view.regions);
        assert!(matches!(rejected, SpatialVerdict::Rejected { .. }));
        assert_eq!(rejected.citation(), Some(wall.citation.as_str()));
        assert!(rejected.label().contains("spatial only"));

        let deferred = spatial_verdict(&[fog_tile], &view.regions);
        assert!(matches!(deferred, SpatialVerdict::Deferred { .. }));
        assert_eq!(deferred.citation(), Some(fog.citation.as_str()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_clear_tile_is_clear_and_an_empty_proposal_is_empty() {
        let view = view();
        let clear = (12, 12);
        assert!(region_at(clear, &view.regions).is_none(), "the fixture tile must be clear");
        assert_eq!(spatial_verdict(&[clear], &view.regions), SpatialVerdict::Clear);
        assert_eq!(spatial_verdict(&[], &view.regions), SpatialVerdict::Empty);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_wall_beats_a_fog_when_both_cover_the_tile() {
        // Refusal is the safer answer, so a tile that is both deferred and refused must not read as
        // merely deferred.
        let regions = vec![
            RegionRec {
                region_id: "fog_x".into(),
                kind: "fog".into(),
                label: "fog".into(),
                citation: "section 30.2".into(),
                kanji: "？".into(),
                rect: [3, 3, 3, 3],
            },
            RegionRec {
                region_id: "wall_x".into(),
                kind: "wall".into(),
                label: "wall".into(),
                citation: "section 30.3".into(),
                kanji: "税".into(),
                rect: [3, 3, 3, 3],
            },
        ];
        match spatial_verdict(&[(3, 3)], &regions) {
            SpatialVerdict::Rejected { region_id, .. } => assert_eq!(region_id, "wall_x"),
            other => panic!("expected a rejection, got {other:?}"),
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn status_glyph_is_injective_so_shape_distinguishes_what_colour_cannot() {
        // §12.4's colour-blind supplement only works if the glyphs are DISTINCT. Measured before this
        // test existed: `NotEvaluable` and `Unknown` both drew a diamond, so an unevaluable control and
        // an unread one were the same shape — which is exactly the pair a shape supplement has to
        // separate, since they differ in nothing else the eye can use.
        use std::collections::HashSet;
        let statuses = ["MET", "FAILED", "NOT_EVALUABLE", "PROCEDURAL", "", "garbage"];
        let glyphs: HashSet<&'static str> = statuses.iter().map(|s| status_glyph_char(status_glyph(s))).collect();
        assert_eq!(glyphs.len(), 5, "five statuses must draw five shapes, got {glyphs:?}");
        // And the unread case is a QUESTION MARK, not a shape that looks like an evaluated one.
        assert_eq!(status_glyph_char(status_glyph("garbage")), "?");
        assert_ne!(status_glyph("NOT_EVALUABLE"), status_glyph(""));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_identity_word_is_distinct_from_every_mechanical_one() {
        // The identity axis's word is `PROCEDURAL` and the mechanical axis's three are MET / FAILED /
        // NOT_EVALUABLE. Both are the view's vocabulary; this pins that the surface keeps them apart and
        // never paints one as the other.
        assert_eq!(status_colour("PROCEDURAL"), StatusColour::Procedural);
        assert_ne!(StatusColour::Procedural, StatusColour::NotEvaluable);
        assert_ne!(status_rgb(StatusColour::Procedural), status_rgb(StatusColour::Unknown));
        assert_ne!(status_rgb(StatusColour::Procedural), status_rgb(StatusColour::Met));
    }

    #[test]
    fn an_unrecognised_status_never_renders_as_met() {
        // The surface's own "no default-to-MET". A default here would make an unread status look like
        // a passing one, which is how a lens starts lying without anyone editing it.
        assert_eq!(status_colour("MET"), StatusColour::Met);
        assert_eq!(status_colour("FAILED"), StatusColour::Failed);
        assert_eq!(status_colour("NOT_EVALUABLE"), StatusColour::NotEvaluable);
        for unknown in ["met", "OK", "", "PARTIAL", "MET ", "unknown"] {
            assert_eq!(
                status_colour(unknown),
                StatusColour::Unknown,
                "{unknown:?} must not be read as a known status"
            );
        }
        assert_ne!(status_colour("dropped"), StatusColour::Met);
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_status_the_view_carries_is_one_the_surface_recognises() {
        // The complement of the test above: the surface refuses to guess, so if the view ever gained a
        // status this build does not know, it must be reported here rather than rendered as a colour.
        let view = view();
        for control in &view.controls {
            assert_ne!(
                status_colour(&control.mechanical_status),
                StatusColour::Unknown,
                "{} carries {:?}, which the surface would render as unknown",
                control.control,
                control.mechanical_status
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_surface_shows_the_declared_distribution_and_does_not_recount() {
        let view = view();
        let (met, failed, not_evaluable) = view.distribution();
        assert_eq!((met, failed, not_evaluable), (7, 1, 4));
        assert_eq!(met + failed + not_evaluable, view.controls.len() as u32);
        // and the impossible figure the design documents carried is now unreachable
        assert_ne!(met, 8, "8 + 1 + 4 exceeds a 12-control set");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_governor_stamp_is_shown_with_its_coverage() {
        // **This asserted the literal `11/11` and went stale the moment the store grew to 23 tickets**
        // — the fixture reads the LIVE `view.json`, so a hardcoded count is a test that fails whenever
        // somebody files a ticket. That is the same defect the Python measurement register kept
        // committing, and the same fix applies: assert the PROPERTY, and let the number be whatever the
        // store says.
        //
        // The property is what C19 actually requires — a version presented WITH the fraction of tickets
        // that declare it, and `declared_on` never exceeding `of_tickets`. `11/11` was the number one
        // day; `23/23` is the number now; neither is the point.
        let view = view();
        let label = view.governor_label();
        assert!(label.contains('v'), "the version itself must appear: {label}");
        let stamp = &view.governor_base_version;
        assert!(
            label.contains(&format!("{}/{}", stamp.declared_on, stamp.of_tickets)),
            "a version without its coverage presents a partial stamp: {label}"
        );
        assert!(
            stamp.declared_on <= stamp.of_tickets,
            "coverage cannot exceed the set it covers: {}/{}",
            stamp.declared_on,
            stamp.of_tickets
        );
        // And the coverage figure must be a real fraction of a non-empty set, so a view with no tickets
        // cannot pass by reporting `0/0`.
        assert!(stamp.of_tickets > 0, "a stamp over no tickets asserts nothing");
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_citation_of_a_c01_split_travels_with_the_split() {
        // C01 is open, so the four names must arrive with the fact that no rate is applied — a HUD
        // showing four names alone would imply a settled formula.
        let view = view();
        assert!(!view.billing_rate_settled);
        assert!(view.billing_citation.contains("C01"));
        assert!(view.billing_bases.contains(&"per_closed_job".to_owned()));
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_surface_writes_only_under_the_plan_store() {
        // 3DUI.MD §15.2 and section 31.1. A UI that grew a second write path would grow it for a
        // reasonable-sounding reason, so the root is pinned rather than trusted.
        let view_path = locate_view().unwrap();
        let pending = pending_path(&view_path);
        let text = pending.to_string_lossy().replace('\\', "/");
        assert!(text.contains("seasons/plans/"), "{text}");
        assert!(!text.contains("seasons/civilians"), "{text}");
        assert!(!text.contains("doctrine"), "{text}");
        assert!(!text.contains("AGENTS.md"), "{text}");
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_committed_pending_store_declares_itself_non_authoritative_and_unadjudicated() {
        // Writes to a temp file, never the real store: a test that mutates the artifact it checks is
        // the defect this whole stack is about.
        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join("city_pending_test");
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
        fs::create_dir_all(&dir).unwrap();
        let path = dir.join("pending.json");
        let proposal = PendingProposal {
            tool: "zone".into(),
            kind: "job".into(),
            tiles: vec![[4, 4]],
            spatial_verdict: "CLEAR (spatial only)".into(),
            spatial_citation: None,
            spatial_region: None,
            adjudicated: false,
            note: "test".into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(commit_to(&path, &[proposal], 3).unwrap(), 1);
        // append, never overwrite
        let second = PendingProposal {
            tool: "node".into(),
            kind: "verifier".into(),
            tiles: vec![[8, 2]],
            spatial_verdict: "CLEAR (spatial only)".into(),
            spatial_citation: None,
            spatial_region: None,
            adjudicated: false,
            note: "test 2".into(),
        };
        assert_eq!(commit_to(&path, &[second], 4).unwrap(), 1);
        let store: PendingStore = serde_json::from_str(&fs::read_to_string(&path).unwrap()).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(store.proposals.len(), 2);
        assert!(!store.authoritative);
        assert!(!store.adjudicated);
        assert!(store.note.contains("non-authoritative"));
        assert_eq!(store.tick, 4);
        let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&dir);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_risk_layer_is_not_folded_into_the_controls() {
        // 3DUI.MD §7.2: R7-R11 are their own layer and must never be merged into C9-C20. The surface
        // holds them in separate fields, and this asserts the view does too, so a UI change that
        // concatenated them would be a change to a contract rather than a rendering choice.
        let view = view();
        assert_eq!(view.residual_risks.len(), 5);
        assert_eq!(view.controls.len(), 12);
        let control_ids: Vec<&str> = view.controls.iter().map(|c| c.control.as_str()).collect();
        for risk in &view.residual_risks {
            assert!(!control_ids.contains(&risk.id.as_str()), "{} appears as a control", risk.id);
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_zone_and_node_kind_states_its_anchor() {
        for kind in ZONE_KINDS {
            let anchor = zone_anchor(kind);
            assert_ne!(anchor, "no doctrine anchor", "{kind} has no anchor");
        }
        assert_eq!(zone_anchor("not_a_kind"), "no doctrine anchor");
        // the JOB_CLASSES conflation the fact-check found must be stated, not smoothed
        assert!(zone_anchor("job").contains("NOT a job taxonomy"));
    }


    #[test]
    fn the_disclaimer_names_the_governor_as_the_only_adjudicator() {
        let text = SpatialVerdict::DISCLAIMER;
        assert!(text.contains("spatial refusal only"));
        assert!(text.contains("overlay.py adjudicate"));
        assert!(text.contains("never adjudicates"));
    }

    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // The authorized fiction (PLAN_JOBS.md / section 33)
    // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    #[test]
    fn the_fiction_yield_moves_with_the_clock_and_only_with_the_clock() {
        // "Everything moves" is this: the producer wrote a base once, and the surface multiplies it by
        // the tick count it already advances. No re-derivation, no poll, no write.
        let view = view();
        let summary = view.idle_summary.as_ref().expect("the view now carries the idle layer");
        assert!(summary.total_base_yield > 0, "a fiction with no base yield cannot move");
        assert_eq!(summary.yield_at(0), 0, "a fiction no tick has run for has yielded nothing");
        assert_eq!(summary.yield_at(1), summary.total_base_yield);
        assert_eq!(summary.yield_at(10), summary.total_base_yield * 10);
        assert!(summary.yield_at(10) > summary.yield_at(9));
        // Negative clock: a paused clock passes what it last passed, and a negative cannot arise — but
        // if one did it must clamp to zero rather than yield a negative fiction into a HUD.
        assert_eq!(summary.yield_at(-5), 0);
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_paused_clock_accrues_nothing_because_no_wall_clock_is_read() {
        // Refusal 5, discharged by the ARITHMETIC rather than by a check: `yield_at` takes a tick count
        // and nothing else, so there is no elapsed-real-time term to subtract. A paused clock passes
        // the same count it last passed, and the yield stands still. This test asserts the shape of
        // the function, not a branch — a deleted branch could not break it.
        let summary = view().idle_summary.expect("idle summary");
        let paused_at = 7_i64;
        assert_eq!(summary.yield_at(paused_at), summary.yield_at(paused_at));
        // Two seconds of wall time cannot enter, because there is no parameter for it.
        assert_eq!(summary.yield_at(11) - summary.yield_at(10), summary.total_base_yield);
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_fiction_is_never_counted_as_a_civilian() {
        // Marking rule 2. The civilian count is the number the whole overlay is trusted for, so an idle
        // block absorbed into it would corrupt the one figure a reader checks first.
        let view = view();
        let loci = view.loci.len();
        let civilians = view.avatars.len();
        let fiction = view.idle_jobs.len();
        assert!(fiction > 0, "the layer is present, so the assertion below is not vacuous");
        assert_ne!(fiction, loci, "the two counts are different numbers, which is why they are separate");
        assert!(view.idle_jobs.iter().all(|j| j.fiction), "every idle job declares itself fiction");
        assert!(view.idle_jobs.iter().all(|j| j.idle_id.starts_with("idle_")));
        // **And the `civilian_id` overlap with loci is REQUIRED, not a defect** — this assertion said the
        // opposite in its first version and failed, which is the useful kind of failure: an idle job hangs
        // off a real record (refusal 7), so its `civilian_id` is by design a civilian that also has a
        // locus. What must never collide is the JOB IDENTITY, because that is what a surface keys on, and
        // what must never merge is the COUNT, because that is what a reader trusts.
        let locus_civilians: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> =
            view.loci.iter().map(|l| l.civilian_id.as_str()).collect();
        assert!(
            view.idle_jobs.iter().all(|j| locus_civilians.contains(j.civilian_id.as_str())),
            "every idle job is anchored to a civilian that really has a locus — that is the anchor rule"
        );
        let idle_ids: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> =
            view.idle_jobs.iter().map(|j| j.idle_id.as_str()).collect();
        let locus_ids: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> =
            view.loci.iter().map(|l| l.civilian_id.as_str()).collect();
        assert!(
            idle_ids.is_disjoint(&locus_ids),
            "no idle id is also a locus id: a shared key is how a surface renders one and drops the rest"
        );
        assert_eq!(idle_ids.len(), fiction, "and the ids are distinct, so the key really addresses all of them");
        assert_eq!(civilians, loci, "one avatar per locus, so the split above is the only difference");
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_idle_job_cites_an_anchor_that_already_exists() {
        // Refusal 7 made visible: the ward cannot grow by fiction, so every job hangs off a record and
        // the job count is bounded by the anchor count.
        let view = view();
        assert!(
            view.idle_jobs.iter().all(|j| !j.anchor_id.is_empty()),
            "an idle job with no anchor is a producer invented from nothing"
        );
        // The anchors point at real things, so no anchor id may be an `idle_` id itself.
        assert!(view.idle_jobs.iter().all(|j| !j.anchor_id.starts_with("idle_")));
        // The four kinds are the closed set, and every one the schema admits is anchored by a different
        // record type — which is what makes `PLAN_JOBS.md` §1's table a design rather than a list.
        let kinds: std::collections::BTreeSet<&str> = view.idle_jobs.iter().map(|j| j.kind.as_str()).collect();
        assert!(!kinds.is_empty());
        for kind in &kinds {
            assert!(
                ["attest", "witness", "tally", "steward"].contains(kind),
                "{kind} is not one of the four closed idle kinds"
            );
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn the_summary_declares_what_the_fiction_is_not() {
        // The view must carry the non-effects explicitly rather than leaving them to be inferred from
        // an absence. An absence is what a defect looks like.
        let summary = view().idle_summary.expect("idle summary");
        assert!(summary.fiction);
        assert!(!summary.grade_effect, "a fiction cannot award a grade");
        assert!(!summary.claim_effect, "a fiction cannot support a claim");
        assert!(!summary.income_effect, "a fiction is not money");
        assert!(summary.honest_limit.contains("not money") || summary.honest_limit.contains("fiction"));
        assert!(summary.citation.contains("PLAN_JOBS") || summary.citation.contains("section 33"));
    }

    #[test]
    fn a_view_from_before_the_idle_layer_still_parses() {
        // The compatibility half, and it is what makes adding three keys safe: `#[serde(default)]` on
        // every new field means an older producer's view — the one written before this layer existed —
        // deserializes to an EMPTY layer rather than failing to load. A surface that refused to open a
        // slightly older view would be a surface that breaks whenever the producer is rolled back.
        let path = locate_view().expect("view.json");
        let mut value: serde_json::Value =
            serde_json::from_str(&std::fs::read_to_string(&path).expect("read")).expect("json");
        let obj = value.as_object_mut().expect("object");
        obj.remove("idle_jobs");
        obj.remove("idle_summary");
        obj.remove("derived_at_tick");
        let older: CityView = serde_json::from_value(value).expect("an older view must still parse");
        assert!(older.idle_jobs.is_empty());
        assert!(older.idle_summary.is_none());
        assert_eq!(older.derived_at_tick, 0, "absent resolves to the convergent baseline, never to a guess");
        // And the renderer must not fall over on a view with no fiction in it: the strip returns early.
        assert_eq!(older.avatars.len(), view().avatars.len(), "the rest of the view is untouched");
    }
}
```

#### `rust-ui/src/knowledge.rs`

```rust
use std::cmp::Reverse;
use std::collections::HashSet;
use std::fs;
use std::path::PathBuf;

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct FileLocation {
    pub source: PathBuf,
    pub start_line: usize,
    pub end_line: usize,
    pub section: String,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub struct ContextPack {
    pub source: PathBuf,
    pub source_bytes: usize,
    pub selected_sections: Vec<String>,
    pub locations: Vec<FileLocation>,
    pub features: Vec<String>,
    pub endpoints: Vec<String>,
    pub commands: Vec<String>,
    pub text: String,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
struct Section {
    title: String,
    body: String,
    start_line: usize,
    end_line: usize,
    terms: HashSet<String>,
}

pub struct KnowledgeBase {
    source: PathBuf,
    sections: Vec<Section>,
}

impl KnowledgeBase {
    pub fn load() -> Result<Self, String> {
        let source = locate_agents_file().ok_or_else(|| {
            "AGENTS.md was not found from the UI directory or its parents".to_owned()
        })?;
        let raw = fs::read_to_string(&source)
            .map_err(|error| format!("could not read {}: {error}", source.display()))?;
        let sections = parse_sections(&raw);
        if sections.is_empty() {
            return Err(format!("{} contains no top-level sections", source.display()));
        }
        Ok(Self { source, sections })
    }

    pub fn context_for(&self, request: &str, budget: usize) -> ContextPack {
        let request_terms = terms(request);
        let mut ranked: Vec<(usize, usize)> = self
            .sections
            .iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, section)| {
                let overlap = request_terms.intersection(&section.terms).count();
                let core = matches!(section.title.as_str(),
                    "0. The frame" |
                    "1. The one principle everything else derives from" |
                    "4. Pillar 3 — Governor Base, and the 2000 snapshot" |
                    "9. Pillar 8 — Doctors (declare-vs-actual, and the oracle)" |
                    "17. The binding rules" |
                    "21. The authorization chain — making the apex control enforced instead of procedural"
                );
                (overlap + usize::from(core), index)
            })
            .collect();
        ranked.sort_by_key(|(score, index)| (Reverse(*score), *index));

        let mut selected = Vec::new();
        let mut used = 0;
        for (score, index) in ranked {
            if score == 0 && !selected.is_empty() {
                break;
            }
            let section = &self.sections[index];
            let block = format!("## {}\n{}\n", section.title, section.body.trim());
            if used + block.len() > budget && !selected.is_empty() {
                continue;
            }
            used += block.len();
            selected.push((index, block));
            if used >= budget {
                break;
            }
        }
        selected.sort_by_key(|(index, _)| *index);

        let selected_sections = selected
            .iter()
            .map(|(index, _)| self.sections[*index].title.clone())
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let locations = selected
            .iter()
            .map(|(index, _)| {
                let section = &self.sections[*index];
                FileLocation {
                    source: self.source.clone(),
                    start_line: section.start_line,
                    end_line: section.end_line,
                    section: section.title.clone(),
                }
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let selected_text = selected
            .iter()
            .map(|(_, block)| block.as_str())
            .collect::<String>();
        let features: Vec<String> = selected_sections
            .iter()
            .map(|title| title.split('—').next().unwrap_or(title).trim().to_owned())
            .filter(|title| !title.is_empty())
            .collect();
        let endpoints = extract_lines(&selected_text, |line| {
            line.contains("/v1/") || line.contains("WRITE_EXTERNAL") || line.contains("NEVER_STORE")
        });
        let commands = extract_lines(&selected_text, |line| {
            let trimmed = line.trim_start();
            trimmed.starts_with("cargo ")
                || trimmed.starts_with("python ")
                || trimmed.starts_with("npm ")
                || trimmed.starts_with("POST /")
        });

        let text = format!(
            "AGENTS.md context (source: {}, {} bytes; selected sections: {})\n\n{}\nCompatible features: {}\nRelevant endpoints/gates: {}\nRelevant commands: {}",
            self.source.display(),
            fs::metadata(&self.source).map(|meta| meta.len()).unwrap_or(0),
            selected_sections.join(", "),
            selected_text,
            if features.is_empty() { "none".to_owned() } else { features.join(", ") },
            if endpoints.is_empty() { "none".to_owned() } else { endpoints.join(" | ") },
            if commands.is_empty() { "none".to_owned() } else { commands.join(" | ") },
        );

        ContextPack {
            source: self.source.clone(),
            source_bytes: fs::metadata(&self.source)
                .map(|meta| meta.len() as usize)
                .unwrap_or(0),
            selected_sections,
            locations,
            features,
            endpoints,
            commands,
            text,
        }
    }
}

fn locate_agents_file() -> Option<PathBuf> {
    let mut starts = Vec::new();
    if let Ok(current) = std::env::current_dir() {
        starts.push(current);
    }
    if let Ok(executable) = std::env::current_exe() {
        if let Some(parent) = executable.parent() {
            starts.push(parent.to_owned());
        }
    }
    starts.push(PathBuf::from(env!("CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR")));

    for mut current in starts {
        loop {
            let candidate = current.join("AGENTS.md");
            if candidate.is_file() {
                return Some(candidate);
            }
            if !current.pop() {
                break;
            }
        }
    }
    None
}

fn parse_sections(raw: &str) -> Vec<Section> {
    let mut sections = Vec::new();
    let mut title = String::new();
    let mut body = String::new();
    let mut start_line = 0;
    for (line_index, line) in raw.lines().enumerate() {
        if let Some(next_title) = line.strip_prefix("## ") {
            if !title.is_empty() {
                sections.push(Section {
                    title: title.clone(),
                    start_line,
                    end_line: line_index,
                    terms: terms(&format!("{} {}", title, body)),
                    body: std::mem::take(&mut body),
                });
            }
            title = next_title.trim().to_owned();
            start_line = line_index + 1;
        } else if !title.is_empty() {
            body.push_str(line);
            body.push('\n');
        }
    }
    if !title.is_empty() {
        sections.push(Section {
            title: title.clone(),
            start_line,
            end_line: raw.lines().count(),
            terms: terms(&format!("{} {}", title, body)),
            body,
        });
    }
    sections
}

fn terms(text: &str) -> HashSet<String> {
    text.to_lowercase()
        .split(|character: char| !character.is_ascii_alphanumeric() && character != '_')
        .filter(|term| term.len() >= 3)
        .map(str::to_owned)
        .collect()
}

fn extract_lines(text: &str, predicate: impl Fn(&str) -> bool) -> Vec<String> {
    let mut lines = Vec::new();
    for line in text.lines().map(str::trim).filter(|line| !line.is_empty()) {
        if predicate(line) && !lines.iter().any(|existing| existing == line) {
            lines.push(line.to_owned());
        }
    }
    lines.truncate(12);
    lines
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::parse_sections;

    #[test]
    fn parses_top_level_sections_without_merging_them() {
        let sections = parse_sections("## 0. One\nGovernor Base\n## 1. Two\nPOST /v1/goto\n");
        assert_eq!(sections.len(), 2);
        assert_eq!(sections[0].title, "0. One");
        assert_eq!((sections[0].start_line, sections[0].end_line), (1, 2));
        assert_eq!((sections[1].start_line, sections[1].end_line), (3, 4));
        assert!(sections[1].body.contains("/v1/goto"));
    }
}
```
