        let hover_tile = pointer_uv.and_then(|uv| self.controls.orbit.tile_at(uv, aspect, extent, size));

        if self.view.is_some() {
            self.handle_drags(ui, response, layout, hover_tile, aspect, extent, size);
        }
        self.controls.hover = hover_tile;

        // ---- cursor ---------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Derived from the state the press handler reads, so it cannot describe a gesture that is not in
        // flight. Set only while the canvas is the hovered region, because egui's rails and buttons set
        // their own icon when they are drawn later in the frame — and a canvas that overrode them would
        // be a surface whose buttons never changed the pointer.
        if response.hovered() {
            let over_chrome = ui
                .input(|i| i.pointer.hover_pos())
                .map(|pos| layout.is_chrome(pos))
                .unwrap_or(false);
            ui.ctx().set_cursor_icon(self.controls.cursor(over_chrome).icon());
        }

        // ---- scroll -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // All three axes of the wheel, because reading only `y` silently discarded two of them: a
        // trackpad's two-finger sideways swipe did nothing at all (which reads as a broken surface
        // rather than as an unbound axis), and the depth band had no pointer path whatsoever.
        if response.hovered() && pointer_uv.is_some() {
            let (scroll, shift, ctrl) =
                ui.input(|i| (i.smooth_scroll_delta, i.modifiers.shift, i.modifiers.ctrl));
            // Screen-down is world +Z for the default camera, but the camera can be rotated, so every pan
            // is taken along the camera's own ground basis rather than along world axes — otherwise
            // panning sideways would feel correct upright and wrong after an orbit.
            let yaw = self.controls.orbit.yaw();

            if ctrl && scroll.y.abs() > 0.1 {
                // Ctrl+scroll is SL-02's depth band. Kept ahead of the other two so a modifier that
                // means one thing here cannot be read as "a pan with an extra key held".
                self.controls.orbit.depth_by(-scroll.y * DEPTH_PER_SCROLL);
            } else {
                if scroll.y.abs() > 0.1 {
                    // Shift+scroll pans the camera's focus instead of zooming. The brief gives the wheel
                    // one meaning (logarithmic zoom, §3.3); this adds the second without taking the first,
                    // because a wheel that always zooms cannot travel — and travelling is what makes a
                    // 24-tile ward navigable at the zoom levels where it does not fit on screen.
                    if shift {
                        let step = scroll.y * PAN_PER_POINT;
                        self.controls
                            .orbit
                            .pan_by(-step * yaw.cos(), -step * yaw.sin(), extent);
                    } else {
                        self.controls.orbit.zoom_by(scroll.y * ZOOM_PER_SCROLL);
                    }
                }
                // The camera's own RIGHT axis, which is `(-sin, cos)` when forward is `(cos, sin)`.
                // A rightward swipe scrolls the view right, which is the *opposite* sign to a rightward
                // drag — dragging moves the world, scrolling moves the eye. Getting this backwards is
                // the kind of error that feels wrong immediately and is hard to name.
                if scroll.x.abs() > 0.1 {
                    let step = scroll.x * PAN_PER_POINT;
                    self.controls
                        .orbit
                        .pan_by(-step * yaw.sin(), step * yaw.cos(), extent);
                }
            }
        }

        self.tick += 1;
    }

    fn handle_drags(
        &mut self,
        ui: &egui::Ui,
        response: &egui::Response,
        layout: Layout,
        hover_tile: Option<[i32; 2]>,
        aspect: f32,
        extent: f32,
        size: i32,
    ) {
        use egui::PointerButton::{Middle, Primary, Secondary};
        let _ = (aspect, extent);

        // Start. Three gestures, each on its own button, so no two can interleave: primary draws with a
        // tool (or orbits with Select), secondary orbits, middle pans.
        if response.drag_started_by(Primary) {
            let over_canvas = ui
                .input(|i| i.pointer.interact_pos())
                .map(|pos| !layout.is_chrome(pos))
                .unwrap_or(false);
            if over_canvas {
                if self.controls.tool.marks_an_area() {
                    if let Some(tile) = hover_tile {
                        self.controls.drag = Drag::Zone {
                            from: tile,
                            to: tile,
                        };
                        self.controls.brush = Some((tile, tile));
                    }
                } else {
                    self.controls.drag = Drag::Orbit;
                }
            }
        }
        if response.drag_started_by(Secondary) {
            self.controls.drag = Drag::Orbit;
        }
        if response.drag_started_by(Middle) {
            self.controls.drag = Drag::Pan;
        }

        // Continue.
        let delta = response.drag_delta();
        match self.controls.drag {
            Drag::Orbit if response.dragged_by(Primary) || response.dragged_by(Secondary) => {
                self.controls
                    .orbit
                    .orbit_by(-delta.x * ORBIT_PER_POINT, delta.y * ORBIT_PER_POINT);
            }
            Drag::Zone { from, .. } if response.dragged_by(Primary) => {
                if let Some(to) = hover_tile {
                    self.controls.drag = Drag::Zone { from, to };
                    self.controls.brush = Some((from, to));
                }
            }
            Drag::Pan if response.dragged_by(Middle) => {
                let yaw = self.controls.orbit.yaw();
                // The drag moves the WORLD, so the focus moves opposite the pointer: dragging right
                // should bring the left of the ward into view, which is what every map does.
                let dx = -delta.x * PAN_PER_POINT;
                let dz = -delta.y * PAN_PER_POINT;
                self.controls
                    .orbit
                    .pan_by(dx * yaw.cos() - dz * yaw.sin(), dx * yaw.sin() + dz * yaw.cos(), extent);
            }
            _ => {}
        }

        // Stop.
        if response.drag_stopped_by(Primary) {
            if matches!(self.controls.drag, Drag::Zone { .. }) {
                // The drag SUCCEEDS into the pending list, so the mouse path needs no second step —
                // and the brush is cleared so the same rectangle is not added twice by a stray Enter.
                self.add_brush_to_pending();
                self.controls.brush = None;
            }
            self.controls.drag = Drag::None;
        }
        if response.drag_stopped_by(Secondary) || response.drag_stopped_by(Middle) {
            self.controls.drag = Drag::None;
        }

        // Click: select. Double-click: centre on it. A double click is a discrete gesture with no drag,
        // and `fraction` is the standard way to detect it without a timer of our own.
        if response.clicked() {
            if let Some(tile) = hover_tile {
                self.controls.selection = Some(tile);
                self.keyboard_focus = false;
            }
        }
        if response.double_clicked() {
            if let Some(tile) = hover_tile {
                self.controls.selection = Some(tile);
                self.focus_selection(size);
            }
        }
        if response.secondary_clicked() {
            self.controls.selection = None;
            self.controls.brush = None;
            self.controls.drag = Drag::None;
        }
    }

    /// Apply a discrete action. The camera actions are handled by `Controls::apply`; everything that
    /// touches this surface's own state lands here.
    fn apply(&mut self, action: Action, extent: f32, grid: (f32, f32, i32)) {
        // Escape escalates, so it is handled **before** the delegation: by the time `Controls::apply` has
        // run, the brush a first Escape should have been about is already gone, and the two levels would
        // collapse into one.
        if action == Action::Cancel && self.dismiss_one_level() {
            return;
        }
        self.controls.apply(action, extent, grid);
        match action {
            Action::Commit => {
                if self.controls.brush.is_some() {
                    self.add_brush_to_pending();
                    self.controls.brush = None;
                } else {
                    self.commit();
                }
            }
            Action::RemoveLastProposal => {
                if let Some(dropped) = self.pending.pop() {
                    self.say(
                        MessageKind::Info,
                        format!(
                            "dropped {} over {} tile(s) — the pending list is a buffer, not a governed act",
                            dropped.kind,
                            dropped.tiles.len()
                        ),
                    );
                }
            }
            Action::CycleSelection | Action::CycleSelectionBack => {
                let candidates = self.locus_tiles();
                let back = action == Action::CycleSelectionBack;
                self.controls.cycle_selection(&candidates, back);
            }
            Action::FocusSelection => {
                self.controls.apply(Action::FocusSelection, extent, grid);
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    /// Close the topmost thing the player opened, and report whether there was one.
    ///
    /// **HIG's rule is that Escape always makes progress and never guesses.** It backs out one level,
    /// from the most modal thing to the least: the panels the player is *reading*, then — via
    /// `Controls::apply` — the brush they are *drawing*, the tool they are *holding*, and the drag that
    /// is *in flight*. Every one of those is a state the player deliberately entered, so escaping it is
    /// never a surprise.
    ///
    /// Returns `false` when no panel is open, which is what lets the caller fall through to the gesture
    /// reset rather than swallowing the key — an Escape that did nothing would be a key that appears
    /// broken exactly when the player most wants out.
    fn dismiss_one_level(&mut self) -> bool {
        // Most-modal first. The help overlay is a full-surface dialog, so it closes before anything
        // drawn underneath it; the rails are always open and are therefore not a level at all.
        for open in [
            &mut self.controls.show_help,
            &mut self.controls.show_ledger,
            &mut self.controls.show_proposals,
            &mut self.controls.show_debug,
        ] {
            if *open {
                *open = false;
                return true;
            }
        }
        false
    }

    fn focus_selection(&mut self, size: i32) {
        if let Some(tile) = self.controls.selection {
            let half = size as f32 * 0.5;
            self.controls.orbit.focus = [tile[0] as f32 - half + 0.5, tile[1] as f32 - half + 0.5];
        }
    }

    /// The loci the view carries, sorted, as the candidate list for Tab cycling.
    ///
    /// Sorted rather than in file order because the cycle must be the same on every run: a cycle that
    /// depends on the order a JSON array happened to be written in is a cycle that changes when the
    /// store is regenerated, and a selection that jumps for no reason reads as a bug.
    fn locus_tiles(&self) -> Vec<[i32; 2]> {
        let mut tiles: Vec<[i32; 2]> = self
            .view
            .as_ref()
            .map(|view| view.loci.iter().map(|locus| locus.tile).collect())
            .unwrap_or_default();
        tiles.sort_unstable();
        tiles.dedup();
        tiles
    }

    fn add_brush_to_pending(&mut self) {
        let tiles = self.controls.brush_tiles();
        if tiles.is_empty() {
            return;
        }
        if self.controls.tool == Tool::Select {
            self.say(
                MessageKind::Refused,
                "no tool is active — pick a zone or node kind, then draw (1–6, 7–9, or [ and ])",
            );
            return;
        }
        let size = self.grid_tuple().2;
        let in_bounds: Vec<[i32; 2]> = tiles
            .iter()
            .copied()
            .filter(|t| t[0] >= 0 && t[1] >= 0 && t[0] < size && t[1] < size)
            .collect();
        if in_bounds.is_empty() {
            self.say(MessageKind::Refused, "the brush is outside the ward");
            return;
        }
        let proposal = self.make_proposal(in_bounds);
        let verdict = proposal.spatial_verdict.clone();
        let kind = proposal.kind.clone();
        let count = proposal.tiles.len();
        self.pending.push(proposal);
        self.say(
            MessageKind::Info,
            format!("{kind} proposed over {count} tile(s) · {verdict} · pending {}, not adjudicated", self.pending.len()),
        );
    }

    fn make_proposal(&self, tiles: Vec<[i32; 2]>) -> PendingProposal {
        let regions = self
            .view
            .as_ref()
            .map(|view| view.regions.as_slice())
            .unwrap_or(&[]);
        let tuple: Vec<(i32, i32)> = tiles.iter().map(|t| (t[0], t[1])).collect();
        let verdict = spatial_verdict(&tuple, regions);
        let (tool, kind) = match self.controls.tool {
            Tool::Zone(i) => ("zone", ZONE_KINDS.get(i).copied().unwrap_or("zone")),
            Tool::Node(i) => ("node", NODE_KINDS.get(i).copied().unwrap_or("node")),
            Tool::Select => ("zone", "unselected"),
        };
        let note = if tool == "node" {
            format!(
                "{kind} placed to VISUALISE where the {} control already applies. It grants nothing and \
                 changes no mechanical status (section 31.4).",
                zone_anchor(kind)
            )
        } else {
            format!(
                "{tool} locus proposed over {} tile(s), anchored to {}. This assigns no locus into the \
                 store and creates no entity (section 31.2).",
                tiles.len(),
                zone_anchor(kind)
            )
        };
        PendingProposal {
            tool: tool.to_owned(),
            kind: kind.to_owned(),
            tiles,
            spatial_verdict: verdict.label().to_owned(),
            spatial_citation: verdict.citation().map(str::to_owned),
            spatial_region: verdict.region_id().map(str::to_owned),
            adjudicated: false,
            note,
        }
    }

    /// **The only write on this surface.** Nothing else in this file opens a file for writing, and a
    /// test asserts that rendering does not either.
    fn commit(&mut self) {
        let Some(source) = self.source.clone() else {
            self.say(MessageKind::Refused, "no view is loaded, so there is nowhere to commit");
            return;
        };
        if self.pending.is_empty() {
            self.say(
                MessageKind::Refused,
                "nothing pending — draw a rectangle first (drag, or Shift+arrow then Enter)",
            );
            return;
        }
        let path = pending_path(&source);
        match commit_to(&path, &self.pending, self.tick) {
            Ok(written) => {
                self.pending.clear();
                self.say(
                    MessageKind::Info,
                    format!(
                        "committed {written} proposal(s) to {} — NOT adjudicated; run `python overlay.py adjudicate`",
                        path.display()
                    ),
                );
            }
            Err(error) => self.say(MessageKind::Refused, format!("commit REFUSED: {error}")),
        }
    }

    fn say(&mut self, kind: MessageKind, text: impl Into<String>) {
        self.message_kind = kind;
        self.message = Some(text.into());
    }

    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    // Render
    // -----------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    pub fn render(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, render_state: Option<&egui_wgpu::RenderState>) {
        if let Some(state) = render_state {
            self.target_format = state.target_format;
        }
        if self.view.is_none() && self.error.is_none() {
            self.reload();
        }

        let rect = ui.available_rect_before_wrap();
        let layout = Layout::of(rect);
        // One allocation for the whole surface. The HUD is painted over the callback rather than laid
        // out around it, which is what lets the scene be full-bleed — and every HUD region is claimed
        // explicitly below, so hand-drawn controls are reachable without fighting the canvas for input.
        let response = ui.allocate_rect(rect, egui::Sense::click_and_drag());

        let view = self.view.clone();
        let (size, aspect, extent) = match &view {
            Some(v) => (
                v.grid.size,
                rect.width() / rect.height().max(1.0),
                scene::grid_extent(v.grid.size),
            ),
            None => (24, rect.width() / rect.height().max(1.0), 1.0),
        };

        if view.is_some() {
            self.handle_input(ui, &response, layout, aspect);
        }

        // ---- the display clock -------------------------------------------------------------------
        // Advanced once per frame, before anything reads it, and it asks for its own frames while it
        // runs. **Requesting repaint is the mechanism, not a workaround**: egui draws on input, and a
        // clock that only advanced when the pointer moved would not be a clock. The request is gated on
        // `running` alone, so a paused surface costs nothing and the rate stays the player's choice.
        let dt = ui.input(|i| i.stable_dt);
        let fresh = self.controls.clock.advance(dt);
        if fresh > 0 {
            self.telemetry.clock_frames += 1;
        }
        self.telemetry.clock_ticks += fresh;
        if self.controls.clock.running {
            ui.ctx().request_repaint();
        }

        // A tick is what asks the city whether it has moved. **Only while the clock runs**: a paused
        // clock means the player has asked the surface to hold still, and a paused clock that kept
        // re-reading the file would be a pause that still polls. The interval is in ticks rather than
        // seconds for the same reason — a poll is IO, and its cadence should follow the clock the
        // player chose rather than a second timer nobody can see or set.
        if self.controls.clock.running && self.poll_due() {
            self.last_poll_tick = Some(self.controls.clock.ticks);
            self.poll_view();
        }

        let frame_start = Instant::now();
        let mut geometry = None;

        if let Some(view) = &view {
            let eye = self.controls.orbit.eye(extent);
            // The recorded proposals' own highlighted tiles. Gathered here rather than in the scene
            // because the layer is a *view* state: the scene is a pure function of (view, options,
            // tiles), and a scene that decided for itself which proposals to show would be a second
            // reader of the view's intent.
            let highlight = self.highlight_tiles(view);
            let options = scene::SceneOptions {
                avatars: true,
                blocks: true,
                volumes: self.controls.show_volumes,
                fog: self.controls.show_fog,
                walls: self.controls.show_fog,
                gates: true,
                monuments: self.controls.show_monuments,
                highlights: !highlight.is_empty(),
                reduced_motion: self.controls.reduced_motion,
            };
            let pulse = self.pulse();
            let built_at = Instant::now();
            let mut built = scene::build_with_highlights(view, &options, eye, pulse, &highlight);
            self.telemetry.scene_build_us = built_at.elapsed().as_micros() as u64;
            self.telemetry.scene_builds += 1;

            // The overlay instances are appended AFTER `build`, then the translucent tail is re-sorted:
            // both are translucent kinds, and the pass has no depth write, so blend order *is* the
            // result — appending them unsorted would make the brush's blend order depend on push order.
            built.instances.extend(surface_overlays(
                self.controls.brush,
                self.controls.tool == Tool::Select,
                self.controls.hover,
                self.controls.selection,
                size,
                pulse,
            ));
            built.sort_translucent_back_to_front(eye);

            self.telemetry.instances = built.total();
            self.telemetry.opaque = built.opaque_count;
            self.telemetry.translucent = built.total().saturating_sub(built.opaque_count);

            geometry = Some(SurfaceGeometry {
                rect,
                aspect,
                extent,
                size,
                centre_tile: self
                    .controls
                    .orbit
                    .tile_at([0.5, 0.5], aspect, extent, size),
                eye,
                zoom: self.controls.orbit.zoom,
                grid: [view.grid.tilt, view.grid.rotation, view.grid.size as f32],
            });

            let params = FrameParams {
                view_proj: self.controls.orbit.view_proj(aspect, extent),
                eye,
                rect_points: [rect.left(), rect.top(), rect.width(), rect.height()],
                // The scene's animation time is the CLOCK's, not the process's. This is what makes
                // pausing pause the city: the aurora, the particles and the ribbon flow all read this
                // uniform, so a paused clock holds the whole scene still while the status pulse — which
                // reads wall time on purpose — keeps warning. See `Clock::default` for why the two are
                // separate rather than one compromise.
                time: self.controls.clock.seconds() as f32,
                reduced_motion: self.controls.reduced_motion,
                grid_size: extent,
                zoom: self.controls.orbit.zoom,
                target_format: self.target_format,
            };
            ui.painter().add(egui::Shape::Callback(
                egui_wgpu::Callback::new_paint_callback(
                    rect,
                    CityCallback {
                        scene: Arc::new(built),
                        params,
                    },
                ),
            ));
        }

        self.geometry = geometry;

        // The HUD. Painted after the callback is queued — egui draws in call order, and a callback is a
        // shape like any other, so the panels land on top of the scene.
        self.draw_hud(ui, &layout, view.as_ref());

        let frame_ms = frame_start.elapsed().as_secs_f32() * 1000.0;
        self.telemetry.last_frame_ms = frame_ms;
        self.telemetry.frames += 1;
    }

    fn draw_hud(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, view: Option<&CityView>) {
        let painter = ui.painter().clone();
        let motion = ui.style().animation_time;
        // One registry per frame, so a control that stops being drawn stops claiming. A registry that
        // persisted across frames would report overlaps that no longer exist — the same "the answer
        // depends on the previous frame" defect the `Layout` doc comment already forbids.
        let mut regions = Regions::new();

        match view {
            // ---- the three states a surface must design, and the one it must state -------------
            None => self.draw_error(ui, layout, &mut regions),
            Some(view) if view.loci.is_empty() && view.avatars.is_empty() => {
                self.draw_empty(ui, layout, view, &mut regions)
            }
            Some(view) => {
                let stats = self.draw_app_bar(ui, layout, view, &mut regions);
                self.draw_left_rail(ui, layout, view);
                self.draw_right_rail(ui, layout, view);
                self.draw_bottom_bar(ui, layout, &stats, &mut regions);
                // The fiction strip is drawn AFTER the rails and BEFORE the toast, and it claims its
                // rectangle like everything else. Ordering matters for the registry and not for the
                // pixels: a claim that collided with a rail would be reported, and drawing it last
                // inside the column is what makes "inside the column" true rather than hoped for.
                self.draw_fiction(ui, layout, view, &mut regions);
            }
        }

        self.draw_toast(ui, layout, motion, &mut regions);

        // ---- exactly one floating panel, and the choice is arithmetic rather than taste ----------
        // The keymap wants 900x560 and the proposals panel 760x520; inside a 1400-point window's
        // column those two cannot both fit. A surface that drew every open panel would draw them on
        // top of one another — the defect `regions.rs` exists to report — so the arbitration is
        // explicit, and the panels the player asked for and did not get are REPORTED in telemetry
        // rather than silently dropped.
        //
        // Where the panel goes is `regions::place`, which is deterministic and total. Its candidates
        // are the centre first, then a ring, so the common case is the centred panel the design
        // always had and the crowded case degrades predictably.
        if let Some(kind) = self.controls.topmost_float() {
            let slot = crate::regions::place(kind.wanted(), layout.float_area, &[]);
            regions.claim(
                format!("float:{}", kind.name()),
                slot,
                ClaimKind::Panel,
            );
            match kind {
                FloatKind::Help => self.draw_help(ui, slot, &mut regions),
                // The ledger is about a specific view, so it cannot be drawn over a load error. The
                // claim happens first, so a skipped panel leaves its slot free rather than reserving it.
                FloatKind::Ledger => {
                    if let Some(view) = view {
                        self.draw_ledger(ui, slot, view, &mut regions)
                    }
                }
                FloatKind::Proposals => self.draw_proposals(ui, slot, view, &mut regions),
                FloatKind::Debug => self.draw_debug(ui, slot, view, &mut regions),
            }
        }

        // §21.4's trust boundary, painted where it cannot be missed rather than put in a tooltip, and
        // on its OWN row: it used to share the action row's last 20 points, so below about 900 points
        // the Add button was drawn over the end of the sentence that states what this surface may not
        // do. Claimed as a readout because it takes no pointer — the overlap it needed fixing for was
        // with a *control*, and the honest fix was to give it a row rather than a z-order.
        if layout.bottom.height() >= 8.0 {
            let band = egui::Rect::from_min_size(
                egui::pos2(layout.bottom.left() + 12.0, layout.bottom.bottom() - DISCLAIMER_H),
                egui::vec2(layout.bottom.width() - 24.0, DISCLAIMER_H),
            );
            regions.claim("disclaimer", band, ClaimKind::Readout);
            let bar = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(layout.bottom);
            bar.text(
                egui::pos2(band.left(), band.center().y),
                egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER,
                crate::city::SpatialVerdict::DISCLAIMER,
                egui::FontId::proportional(10.0),
                theme::INK_SECONDARY,
            );
        }

        self.telemetry.claims = regions.claims().len();
        self.telemetry.refused_claims = regions.overlaps().len();
        self.telemetry.hidden_floats = self.controls.hidden_floats();
        self.regions = regions;
    }

    fn draw_app_bar(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, view: &CityView, regions: &mut Regions) -> String {
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(layout.app_bar);
        paint_panel(&painter, layout.app_bar, Elevation::AppBar, None);
        let mut x = layout.app_bar.left() + 14.0;
        let y = layout.app_bar.center().y;

        // ---- the right run first, because it is what the left run must not reach -----------------
        // The chips are the fixed half: five at the 48-point target. Computing their extent BEFORE
        // anything is painted on the left is the entire fix — the left run grows rightward and the
        // right run grows leftward, and nothing used to compare them. At a 900-point window the title,
        // the badge, the stamp, the frame counter and the honest limit together exceed the ~280 points
        // the chips leave, and the limit text was painted underneath them.
        let chips: [(&str, bool, Action, &str); 5] = [
            ("risks", self.controls.show_risks, Action::ToggleRisks, "G"),
            ("controls", self.controls.show_volumes, Action::ToggleVolumes, "V"),
            ("monuments", self.controls.show_monuments, Action::ToggleMonuments, "M"),
            ("fog", self.controls.show_fog, Action::ToggleFog, "F"),
            ("help", self.controls.show_help, Action::ToggleHelp, "?"),
        ];
        let chips_w = chips.len() as f32 * (TARGET + 6.0);
        let left_limit = layout.app_bar.right() - 10.0 - chips_w - 12.0;

        let mut dropped = 0usize;
        // Identity first, and never dropped: the title and the read-only badge are what this surface
        // IS, and a surface that hid them on a narrow window would be hiding its own stated limit.
        x += text(&painter, x, y, "市民都市 · Civilian City", font_bold(14.0), theme::INK_PRIMARY, egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER).width() + 12.0;
        let badge = egui::Rect::from_min_size(egui::pos2(x, y - 9.0), egui::vec2(96.0, 18.0));
        paint_chip(&painter, badge, theme::ACCENT_UI, "read-only lens");
        x = badge.right() + 14.0;

        // C19, with its COVERAGE. The label comes from the VIEW's own method rather than being
        // reassembled here, so there is one rendering of the stamp rather than two that can drift.
        let stamp = view.governor_base_version.clone();
        let stamp_colour = if stamp.declared_on == stamp.of_tickets {
            theme::INK_PRIMARY
        } else {
            theme::WARN_UI
        };
        let stamp_label = view.governor_label();
        let stamp_w = text_width(&painter, &stamp_label, font_mono(11.0));
        if x + stamp_w <= left_limit {
            x += text(&painter, x, y, &stamp_label, font_mono(11.0), stamp_colour, egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER).width() + 14.0;
        } else {
            dropped += 1;
        }

        // The frame counter and the clock, together, because they are the same fact from two sides:
        // `frame` is how many times this surface has drawn, `clock` is how many ticks it has been told
        // to advance. Abbreviated rather than spelled out — the width left after the identity run is
        // the scarce resource, and the debug panel carries the long form.
        let clock = format!(
            "f{} · clock {} @{:.0}Hz{}",
            self.tick,
            self.controls.clock.ticks,
            self.controls.clock.hz,
            if self.controls.clock.running { "" } else { " paused" }
        );
        let clock_w = text_width(&painter, &clock, font_mono(11.0));
        if x + clock_w <= left_limit {
            x += text(&painter, x, y, &clock, font_mono(11.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY, egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER).width() + 14.0;
        } else {
            dropped += 1;
        }

        // The document's own honest limit, printed verbatim rather than paraphrased: it is a claim the
        // overlay made about what this view cannot tell you, and a surface that summarised it would be
        // editing the limit. Truncated by measured WIDTH and not by character count, because 64
        // characters of proportional text is anywhere between 240 and 480 points.
        for budget in [64usize, 44, 28] {
            let candidate = truncate(&view.honest_limit, budget);
            let w = text_width(&painter, &candidate, egui::FontId::proportional(10.0));
            if x + w <= left_limit {
                text(&painter, x, y, &candidate, egui::FontId::proportional(10.0), theme::INK_DIVIDER, egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER);
                break;
            }
            if budget == 28 {
                dropped += 1;
            }
        }
        self.telemetry.app_bar_dropped = dropped;

        // Right side: the layer toggles. Buttons are the 48-point target wide and `BUTTON_H` tall —
        // MD1's rule is 48 in the axis a finger travels, and a 48x30 chip in a 46-point bar is the
        // honest reading of it. Claimed as controls, so a chip that ever grew into its neighbour would
        // be reported rather than silently drawn over it.
        let mut right = layout.app_bar.right() - 10.0;
        for (label, on, action, chord) in chips {
            let rect = egui::Rect::from_min_size(
                egui::pos2(right - TARGET, y - BUTTON_H * 0.5),
                egui::vec2(TARGET, BUTTON_H),
            );
            right = rect.left() - 6.0;
            regions.claim(format!("app bar: {label}"), rect, ClaimKind::Control);
            if chip_button(ui, rect, label, on, chord, self.keyboard_focus) {
                self.apply(action, 0.0, self.grid_tuple());
            }
        }
        String::new()
    }

    /// The declared distribution, **recounted and compared rather than recounted and shown**.
    ///
    /// The view carries `mechanical` counts; showing the stored number is §31.3's rule (a lens renders
    /// what is there). But a stored count that no longer matches the controls it claims to summarise is a
    /// defect, and the only place it can be caught is where both are in hand — so the HUD shows the
    /// declared figure and marks it when a recount disagrees, rather than silently replacing it.
    fn draw_status_distribution(&self, painter: &egui::Painter, layout: &Layout, view: &CityView) {
        let mut met = 0;
        let mut failed = 0;
        let mut not_evaluable = 0;
        let mut unknown = 0;
        for control in &view.controls {
            match status_colour(&control.mechanical_status) {
                crate::city::StatusColour::Met => met += 1,
                crate::city::StatusColour::Failed => failed += 1,
                crate::city::StatusColour::NotEvaluable => not_evaluable += 1,
                // `PROCEDURAL` is the IDENTITY axis's word. Its appearance on the MECHANICAL axis is
                // therefore a vocabulary defect in the view, not a fifth mechanical status — so it counts
                // as unread and the note below reports it. Mapping it to `not_evaluable` would be this
                // surface inventing a meaning for a word the mechanical axis does not have.
                crate::city::StatusColour::Procedural | crate::city::StatusColour::Unknown => unknown += 1,
            }
        }
        let (d_met, d_failed, d_not_evaluable) = view.distribution();
        let differs = (d_met, d_failed, d_not_evaluable) != (met, failed, not_evaluable);
        let figure = format!("{d_met} / {d_failed} / {d_not_evaluable}");
        let anchor = egui::pos2(layout.right.left() + 14.0, layout.right.top() + 28.0);
        text(
            painter,
            anchor.x,
            anchor.y,
            &figure,
            egui::FontId::monospace(16.0),
            if differs { theme::WARN_UI } else { theme::INK_PRIMARY },
            egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER,
        );
        // The DECLARED figures are shown, and the recount is compared against them rather than shown in
        // their place. A renderer that silently recomputed would erase the only evidence that the view
        // and the controls ever disagreed — and "which of the two is wrong" is not a question the
        // surface is allowed to answer.
        let note = if differs || unknown > 0 {
            format!(
                "DECLARED {d_met} / {d_failed} / {d_not_evaluable} but a recount over the {} controls gives \
                 {met} / {failed} / {not_evaluable} with {unknown} unread — the disagreement is a finding \
                 about the view, and this surface will not resolve it",
                view.controls.len()
            )
        } else {
            format!(
                "declared {d_met} / {d_failed} / {d_not_evaluable} · mechanical only — never a certification",
            )
        };
        paint_wrapped(painter, anchor.x, anchor.y + 13.0, layout.right.width() - 28.0, &note, egui::FontId::proportional(9.0), if differs { theme::WARN_UI } else { theme::INK_SECONDARY });
    }

    /// **The authorized fiction, moving on the surface's own clock.**
    ///
    /// This is the half of `PLAN_JOBS.md` that makes "everything moves" true without a single write:
    /// the producer wrote `total_base_yield` once, and this multiplies it by `clock_ticks` — the count
    /// of ticks the display clock has actually advanced. Nothing here re-derives, re-polls, or touches
    /// a store; it reads a number the view already carried and does arithmetic the surface is allowed
    /// to do (§7.3's display tick).
    ///
    /// **And the pause comes out of the arithmetic rather than out of a check.** A paused clock passes
    /// the same tick count it last passed, so the yield stands still — refusal 5 is discharged by there
    /// being no wall-clock term to subtract, not by a branch somebody could later delete.
    ///
    /// Three things the strip is careful to do, each of which is a refusal made visible:
    ///   * it names the count as **fiction**, and shows it beside — never added to — the civilian count;
    ///   * it carries the citation and the honest limit, so a player reading the number can read what
    ///     it is not;
    ///   * it renders **nothing** when the view carries no summary, rather than a zero. A zero here
    ///     would say "the layer is present and yields nothing", which is a different fact from "there is
    ///     no such layer in this view" (rule 4's direction, applied to a display).
    fn draw_fiction(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, view: &CityView, regions: &mut Regions) {
        let Some(summary) = view.idle_summary.as_ref() else {
            return;
        };
        let clock = self.controls.clock.ticks as i64;
        let yield_now = summary.yield_at(clock);
        let w = 268.0_f32.min(layout.column.width() - 24.0);
        if w < 120.0 {
            return; // a strip too narrow to read is a strip that should not be drawn
        }
        let h = 96.0;
        let rect = egui::Rect::from_min_size(
            egui::pos2(layout.column.right() - w - 12.0, layout.column.top() + 12.0),
            egui::vec2(w, h),
        );
        // The claim, and it is not ceremony: `regions.rs` refuses an overlapping claim and reports it,
        // so a strip placed against a rail or a panel is a reported defect rather than a visual one.
        regions.claim("fiction", rect, ClaimKind::Panel);

        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(rect);
        paint_panel(&painter, rect, Elevation::Drawer, Some(&format!("{} Fiction", summary.glyph)));
        let x = rect.left() + 12.0;
        let mut y = rect.top() + 36.0;
        let row = |painter: &egui::Painter, y: f32, label: &str, value: &str, colour: egui::Color32| {
            painter.text(egui::pos2(x, y), egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP, label, font_mono(10.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY);
            painter.text(egui::pos2(rect.right() - 12.0, y), egui::Align2::RIGHT_TOP, value, font_mono(11.0), colour);
        };
        row(&painter, y, "idle jobs", &format!("{}", summary.fiction_count()), theme::FICTION_UI);
        y += 16.0;
        row(&painter, y, "base / tick", &format!("{}", summary.total_base_yield), theme::INK_PRIMARY);
        y += 16.0;
        // The moving number, and it is labelled with the tick it was computed at. A yield shown without
        // its tick is the same defect as a governor version shown without its coverage.
        row(
            &painter,
            y,
            &format!("yield @ t{}", clock),
            &format!("{}", yield_now),
            theme::FICTION_UI,
        );
        y += 16.0;
        painter.text(
            egui::pos2(x, y),
            egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP,
            &format!("not money · not a metric · not a claim  ({})", summary.citation.split('/').next().unwrap_or("PLAN_JOBS").trim()),
            egui::FontId::proportional(9.0),
            theme::INK_SECONDARY,
        );
    }

    fn draw_left_rail(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, view: &CityView) {
        if layout.left.width() < 1.0 {
            return;
        }
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(layout.left);
        paint_panel(&painter, layout.left, Elevation::Drawer, Some("Inspector"));
        let mut y = layout.left.top() + 40.0;
        let x = layout.left.left() + 14.0;
        let wrap = layout.left.width() - 28.0;

        let selection = self.controls.selection;
        match selection {
            None => {
                painter.text(
                    egui::pos2(x, y),
                    egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP,
                    "Nothing selected.\n\nClick a tile, or press Tab to walk the loci. Shift+arrows draw a \
                     rectangle; Enter adds it to the pending list.",
                    egui::FontId::proportional(11.0),
                    theme::INK_SECONDARY,
                );
            }
            Some(tile) => {
                let region = region_at((tile[0], tile[1]), &view.regions);
                y += text(&painter, x, y, &format!("tile {} , {}", tile[0], tile[1]), font_mono(12.0), theme::INK_PRIMARY, egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP).height() + 8.0;
                // The spatial verdict, IN THE RAIL as well as on the canvas: the canvas label says a
                // refusal happened, and this says which citation produced it.
                let verdict = spatial_verdict(&[(tile[0], tile[1])], &view.regions);
                let colour = match verdict {
                    crate::city::SpatialVerdict::Rejected { .. } => theme::DANGER_UI,
                    crate::city::SpatialVerdict::Deferred { .. } => theme::WARN_UI,
                    _ => theme::INK_PRIMARY,
                };
                y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, wrap, verdict.label(), egui::FontId::proportional(11.0), colour) + 6.0;
                if let Some(citation) = verdict.citation() {
                    y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, wrap, citation, egui::FontId::monospace(10.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY) + 6.0;
                }
                if let Some(region) = region {
                    y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, wrap, &format!("{} · {}", region.region_id, region.kind), font_mono(10.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY) + 10.0;
                }

                if let Some(locus) = view.loci.iter().find(|l| l.tile == tile) {
                    y += 4.0;
                    y = paint_separator(&painter, x, y, wrap) + 8.0;
                    let rows: [(&str, String); 6] = [
                        ("civilian", locus.civilian_id.clone()),
                        ("occupancy", locus.occupancy.to_string()),
                        ("grade class", locus.grade_class.clone()),
                        ("height", format!("{:.2}", locus.height)),
                        ("job source", locus.job_class_source.clone()),
                        ("multi-civilian", locus.multi_civilian.to_string()),
                    ];
                    for (key, value) in rows {
                        y = paint_row(&painter, x, y, wrap, key, &value, self.keyboard_focus);
                    }
                    if locus.multi_civilian {
                        y = paint_wrapped(
                            &painter,
                            x,
                            y + 4.0,
                            wrap,
                            "a multi-civilian job is FOG (section 30.2) — the surface draws one dashed \
                             placeholder rather than inventing the others",
                            egui::FontId::proportional(10.0),
                            theme::WARN_UI,
                        );
                    }

                    // The avatars the view carries for this civilian, if any. Read, never synthesised: a
                    // locus with no matching avatar is a fact about the view, and inventing a lifecycle
                    // state for it would be the surface authoring a record. Nested inside the locus arm
                    // because an avatar is only meaningful *for* a civilian the view names.
                    if let Some(avatar) = view.avatars.iter().find(|a| a.civilian_id == locus.civilian_id) {
                    y += 6.0;
                    y = paint_separator(&painter, x, y, wrap) + 8.0;
                    let rows: [(&str, String); 5] = [
                        ("state", avatar.lifecycle_state.clone()),
                        ("unit grade", avatar.unit_grade.clone()),
                        ("tier", avatar.certification_tier.clone()),
                        ("has job", avatar.has_job.to_string()),
                        (
                            "income basis",
                            avatar.income_basis.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "—".into()),
                        ),
                    ];
                    for (key, value) in rows {
                        y = paint_row(&painter, x, y, wrap, key, &value, self.keyboard_focus);
                    }
                    if avatar.self_witness_genesis {
                        paint_wrapped(
                            &painter,
                            x,
                            y + 4.0,
                            wrap,
                            "R11: this genesis is SELF-WITNESSED — the artifact and its witness are the \
                             same actor (section 7.2's rule that no artifact is the sole witness to itself)",
                            egui::FontId::proportional(10.0),
                            theme::WARN_UI,
                        );
                    }
                    } else if !locus.multi_civilian {
                        y += 6.0;
                        paint_wrapped(
                            &painter,
                            x,
                            y,
                            wrap,
                            "no avatar record accompanies this locus — the view carries a locus without a \
                             civilian, and this surface will not invent one",
                            egui::FontId::proportional(10.0),
                            theme::INK_SECONDARY,
                        );
                    }
                }
            }
        }
    }

    fn draw_right_rail(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, view: &CityView) {
        if layout.right.width() < 1.0 {
            return;
        }
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(layout.right);
        paint_panel(&painter, layout.right, Elevation::Drawer, Some("Governance"));
        // The declared distribution, at the head of the Governance rail (`3DUI.MD` §12.3 puts it
        // top-right). This call was **missing**: the function existed, computed the declared-versus-
        // recounted comparison, and nothing ever invoked it — so the HUD's headline figure was dead code
        // and the view's `mechanical_distribution` was parsed and never read. Found by the compiler's
        // `never used` warning, which is the only reason a dead paint path is visible at all.
        self.draw_status_distribution(&painter, layout, view);
        let x = layout.right.left() + 14.0;
        let wrap = layout.right.width() - 28.0;
        let mut y = layout.right.top() + 84.0;

        // Controls C9-C20 with their glyph — shape as well as colour (§12.4's colour-blind supplement).
        y += paint_separator(&painter, x, y, wrap) + 6.0;
        for control in &view.controls {
            let colour = status_colour(&control.mechanical_status);
            let glyph = status_glyph_char(status_glyph(&control.mechanical_status));
            let tint = status_tint(colour, 235);
            let pulse = if colour == crate::city::StatusColour::Failed && !self.controls.reduced_motion {
                // The amber pulse is the ONLY thing animating at rest, and it means something: a control
                // whose identity half could not be evaluated. `theme::pulse` supplies the rate AND the
                // reduced-motion behaviour (a steady signal, not none), so this arm only turns it into
                // an alpha — one implementation of the pulse, not two.
                let a = (170.0 + 85.0 * self.pulse()) as u8;
                status_tint(colour, a)
            } else {
                tint
            };
            let line = format!("{glyph}  {}", control.control);
            let rect = painter.text(
                egui::pos2(x + 14.0, y),
                egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP,
                &line,
                font_mono(11.0),
                theme::INK_PRIMARY,
            );
            painter.text(egui::pos2(x, y), egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP, &glyph, font_mono(11.0), pulse);
            if self.keyboard_focus && self.controls.selection.is_some() {
                painter.rect_stroke(rect.expand(1.0), 2.0, theme::Elevation::focus_ring());
            }

            // BOTH halves of the control, because rule 100 is that a control has two and one status for
            // both is the defect. The identity half has its OWN word — `PROCEDURAL`, not `NOT_EVALUABLE` —
            // and before this row existed the surface parsed the field and never showed it, so the one
            // fact that matters about every control on this grid was invisible.
            let mut hy = rect.bottom() + 1.0;
            let mech = status_tint(status_colour(&control.mechanical_status), 235);
            let iden = status_tint(status_colour(&control.identity_status), 235);
            let iden_glyph = status_glyph_char(status_glyph(&control.identity_status));
            let first = painter.text(
                egui::pos2(x + 16.0, hy),
                egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP,
                format!("mechanical {}", control.mechanical_status),
                font_mono(9.0),
                mech,
            );
            painter.text(
                egui::pos2(x + 16.0, first.bottom()),
                egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP,
                format!("{iden_glyph} identity  {}", control.identity_status),
                font_mono(9.0),
                iden,
            );
            hy = first.bottom() + 11.0;
            // The requirement, verbatim from the view. Truncating it to a “reading length” would be this
            // surface editing the constraint, and a wrapped constraint is the whole point of a ledger.
            hy = paint_wrapped(&painter, x + 16.0, hy, wrap - 16.0, &control.requirement, egui::FontId::proportional(9.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY);
            y = hy + 6.0;
            if y > layout.right.bottom() - 120.0 {
                painter.text(egui::pos2(x, y), egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP, "· · ·", font_mono(11.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY);
                y += 18.0;
                break;
            }
        }

        y += 2.0;
        y = paint_separator(&painter, x, y, wrap) + 8.0;
        // The four bases, listed with whether a rate is settled. Collapsing them to one number would be
        // the surface inventing the decision C01 has not made, so they are listed and the citation is
        // printed rather than summarised.
        let heading = if view.billing_rate_settled {
            "BILLING BASES (settled)"
        } else {
            "BILLING BASES (C01 open — no settled rate)"
        };
        y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, wrap, heading, font_mono(10.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY) + 4.0;
        for base in &view.billing_bases {
            y = paint_row(&painter, x, y, wrap, "basis", base, false);
        }
        y = paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            x,
            y + 2.0,
            wrap,
            &view.billing_citation,
            egui::FontId::proportional(9.0),
            theme::INK_DIVIDER,
        ) + 6.0;

        y += 2.0;
        y = paint_separator(&painter, x, y, wrap) + 8.0;
        // The five never-granted actions, by name, with the citation. §9.6 rule 3 says a task that needs
        // one becomes a gate for a human — so the SURFACE must be able to say which action is gated, and
        // a gate drawn as a red arch with no label is a refusal nobody can act on.
        y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, wrap, "NEVER GRANTED — every policy, no exception", font_mono(9.0), theme::DANGER_UI) + 3.0;
        for gate in &view.never_granted {
            y = paint_wrapped(
                &painter,
                x,
                y,
                wrap,
                &format!("{}  {}  ·  {}", gate.kanji, gate.action, gate.citation),
                font_mono(9.0),
                theme::INK_PRIMARY,
            );
        }

        y += 4.0;
        y = paint_separator(&painter, x, y, wrap) + 6.0;
        // R7–R11. A residual risk is NOT a control and is never folded into one (§7.2), which is why it
        // gets its own block rather than a fifth column in the distribution above.
        y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, wrap, "RESIDUAL RISKS — outside the control set, never resolvable here", font_mono(9.0), theme::WARN_UI) + 3.0;
        for risk in &view.residual_risks {
            y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, wrap, &format!("{}  {}", risk.id, risk.risk), egui::FontId::proportional(9.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY);
        }

        y += 4.0;
        paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            x,
            y,
            wrap,
            "A control status is COPIED from the view, never computed here. An unread status draws as ? \
             in a colour no status uses; identity is its own word, PROCEDURAL, because no mechanism \
             verifies an actor (rule 100).",
            egui::FontId::proportional(9.0),
            theme::INK_SECONDARY,
        );
    }

    fn draw_bottom_bar(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, _stats: &str, regions: &mut Regions) {
        if layout.bottom.height() < 8.0 {
            return;
        }
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(layout.bottom);
        paint_panel(&painter, layout.bottom, Elevation::Fab, None);

        // ---- the palettes, wrapped into as many rows as the width needs --------------------------
        // The bar's height came from the SAME `palette_columns` call, so a button cannot be drawn past
        // the rows that reserved space for it. Before this, twelve 84-point entries were laid on one
        // row from x=12 and needed 1,020 points: every window narrower than about 1,030 clipped the
        // node palette off the right edge, and a clipped button reads as a missing feature rather than
        // as a layout defect.
        //
        // The row is derived from the running index rather than carried in a cursor, so the zone and
        // node palettes wrap *through* each other instead of each starting a new row.
        let columns = palette_columns(layout.bottom.width());
        let pal_left = layout.bottom.left() + BOTTOM_PAD;
        let pal_top = layout.bottom.top() + BOTTOM_PAD;
        let at = |index: usize| {
            let col = (index % columns) as f32;
            let row = (index / columns) as f32;
            egui::Rect::from_min_size(
                egui::pos2(
                    pal_left + col * (PALETTE_W + PALETTE_GAP),
                    pal_top + row * (PALETTE_ROW_H + PALETTE_ROW_GAP),
                ),
                egui::vec2(PALETTE_W, PALETTE_ROW_H),
            )
        };
        let mut index = 0usize;
        for (i, (kind, kanji)) in ZONE_KINDS.iter().zip(ZONE_KANJI.iter()).enumerate() {
            let rect = at(index);
            regions.claim(format!("zone palette {i}"), rect, ClaimKind::Control);
            let active = self.controls.tool == Tool::Zone(i);
            if palette_button(ui, rect, kanji, kind, self.keyboard_focus, active) {
                self.apply(Action::ZoneTool(i), 0.0, self.grid_tuple());
            }
            index += 1;
        }
        for (i, (kind, kanji)) in NODE_KINDS.iter().zip(NODE_KANJI.iter()).enumerate() {
            let rect = at(index);
            regions.claim(format!("node palette {i}"), rect, ClaimKind::Control);
            let active = self.controls.tool == Tool::Node(i);
            if palette_button(ui, rect, kanji, kind, self.keyboard_focus, active) {
                self.apply(Action::NodeTool(i), 0.0, self.grid_tuple());
            }
            index += 1;
        }

        // ---- the action row, below every palette row --------------------------------------------
        let rows = palette_rows(layout.bottom.width()) as f32;
        let row_top = pal_top + rows * PALETTE_ROW_H + (rows - 1.0) * PALETTE_ROW_GAP + ACTION_ROW_GAP;
        let row_mid = row_top + BUTTON_H * 0.5;

        // Right-aligned: Add, Clear, Commit. Commit is the only writer, so it is the only
        // primary-coloured button on the surface.
        let mut right = layout.bottom.right() - BOTTOM_PAD;
        let commit = egui::Rect::from_min_size(egui::pos2(right - 128.0, row_top), egui::vec2(128.0, BUTTON_H));
        right = commit.left() - 8.0;
        let clear = egui::Rect::from_min_size(egui::pos2(right - 90.0, row_top), egui::vec2(90.0, BUTTON_H));
        right = clear.left() - 8.0;
        let add = egui::Rect::from_min_size(egui::pos2(right - 110.0, row_top), egui::vec2(110.0, BUTTON_H));

        let add_label = match self.controls.brush {
            Some(_) => format!("Add {} tiles", self.controls.brush_tiles().len()),
            None => "Add (draw first)".to_owned(),
        };
        regions.claim("commit", commit, ClaimKind::Control);
        regions.claim("clear brush", clear, ClaimKind::Control);
        regions.claim("add tiles", add, ClaimKind::Control);
        if action_button(ui, commit, &format!("Commit {}", self.pending.len()), true, "Ctrl+S", self.keyboard_focus) {
            self.commit();
        }
        if action_button(ui, clear, "Clear brush", false, "X / Esc", self.keyboard_focus) {
            self.apply(Action::ClearBrush, 0.0, self.grid_tuple());
        }
        if action_button(ui, add, &add_label, false, "Enter", self.keyboard_focus) {
            self.apply(Action::Commit, 0.0, self.grid_tuple());
        }

        // ---- the clock, at the head of the action row -------------------------------------------
        // A transport control belongs with the other actions rather than in the app bar, and the app
        // bar's left run is the run that has to give way on a narrow window. It is the ONLY control on
        // this surface that advances state, and it advances a display count and nothing else.
        let clock_rect = egui::Rect::from_min_size(
            egui::pos2(layout.bottom.left() + BOTTOM_PAD, row_top),
            egui::vec2(196.0, BUTTON_H),
        );
        regions.claim("clock", clock_rect, ClaimKind::Control);
        let running = self.controls.clock.running;
        let clock_label = format!(
            "{} clock {} · {:.1} Hz",
            if running { "pause" } else { "run" },
            self.controls.clock.ticks,
            self.controls.clock.hz
        );
        if action_button(ui, clock_rect, &clock_label, running, ". ,", self.keyboard_focus) {
            self.apply(Action::ToggleClock, 0.0, self.grid_tuple());
        }

        // Everything left of the actions, in priority order, each drawn only if it fits. The budget is
        // measured against the FIRST action button rather than the bar's edge, which is what stops the
        // readout from running under Add — the overlap the disclaimer used to suffer.
        let readout_limit = add.left() - 12.0;
        let mut rx = clock_rect.right() + 12.0;
        let (brush_label, brush_colour) = match self.controls.brush {
            Some((from, to)) => {
                let tiles = self.controls.brush_tiles();
                let verdict = self
                    .view
                    .as_ref()
                    .map(|v| {
                        let tuple: Vec<(i32, i32)> = tiles.iter().map(|t| (t[0], t[1])).collect();
                        spatial_verdict(&tuple, &v.regions).label().to_owned()
                    })
                    .unwrap_or_default();
                (
                    format!(
                        "brush {} , {} → {} , {} · {} tiles · {verdict}",
                        from[0], from[1], to[0], to[1], tiles.len()
                    ),
                    theme::INK_PRIMARY,
                )
            }
            None => (
                "no brush — drag on the ward, or Shift+arrows".to_owned(),
                theme::INK_SECONDARY,
            ),
        };
        if rx + 60.0 <= readout_limit {
            let fitted = truncate_to_width(&painter, &brush_label, font_mono(10.0), readout_limit - rx);
            rx += text(&painter, rx, row_mid, &fitted, font_mono(10.0), brush_colour, egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER).width() + 16.0;
        }

        // The hover/selection readout, so the pointer's target is legible without opening the rail.
        let hover = self
            .controls
            .hover
            .map(|t| format!("hover {} , {}", t[0], t[1]))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "hover —".to_owned());
        let sel = self
            .controls
            .selection
            .map(|t| format!("selected {} , {}", t[0], t[1]))
            .unwrap_or_else(|| "nothing selected".to_owned());
        let readout = format!("{hover} · {sel}");
        if rx + 60.0 <= readout_limit {
            let fitted = truncate_to_width(&painter, &readout, font_mono(10.0), readout_limit - rx);
            text(&painter, rx, row_mid, &fitted, font_mono(10.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY, egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER);
        }
        let _ = &painter;
    }

    fn draw_toast(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, motion: f32, regions: &mut Regions) {
        let Some(message) = self.message.clone() else {
            return;
        };
        let accent = match self.message_kind {
            MessageKind::Info => theme::ACCENT_UI,
            MessageKind::Refused => theme::DANGER_UI,
        };
        // Claimed as a panel: the toast takes the dismiss button's clicks, and it must not sit under a
        // floating panel. `Layout::float_area` excludes this band for exactly that reason, so the two
        // cannot overlap even before the registry is consulted.
        regions.claim("toast", layout.toast, ClaimKind::Panel);
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(layout.toast);
        // MD1's motion rule: a state change is visible within 200ms. `motion` is egui's own animation
        // time, which the reduced-motion path drives to zero rather than this code branching twice.
        paint_grow_in(&painter, layout.toast, motion, accent);
        paint_wrapped_centred(&painter, layout.toast, &message, 11.0, theme::INK_PRIMARY);
        // Dismissible, because a message that cannot be cleared becomes permanent chrome.
        let close = egui::Rect::from_min_size(
            egui::pos2(layout.toast.right() - TARGET, layout.toast.top()),
            egui::vec2(TARGET, layout.toast.height()),
        );
        regions.claim("toast dismiss", close, ClaimKind::Control);
        if chip_button(ui, close, "×", false, "", false) {
            self.message = None;
        }
    }

    /// The error state. **A designed state, not a fallback**: the store being absent is the normal state
    /// on a fresh clone, and the honest answer names the command that fixes it.
    fn draw_error(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, regions: &mut Regions) {
        let error = self.error.clone().unwrap_or_else(|| "no view".to_owned());
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(layout.canvas);
        // Placed through the same helper the floating panels use, so the error card cannot sit under a
        // rail on a narrow window — it was centred on the CANVAS, which at 760 points put 120 of its
        // 560 across the two rails.
        let card = crate::regions::place(egui::vec2(560.0, 190.0), layout.float_area, &[]);
        regions.claim("error card", card, ClaimKind::Panel);
        paint_panel(&painter, card, Elevation::Dialog, Some("no derived view"));
        paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            card.left() + 20.0,
            card.top() + 52.0,
            card.width() - 40.0,
            &error,
            egui::FontId::proportional(12.0),
            theme::DANGER_UI,
        );
        paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            card.left() + 20.0,
            card.top() + 96.0,
            card.width() - 40.0,
            "This surface renders the derived view. It does not read the civilian store \
             directly and it never writes to one — a surface that derived its own view would be a \
             second implementation of the overlay, and the two would disagree in silence.",
            egui::FontId::proportional(11.0),
            theme::INK_SECONDARY,
        );
        let retry = egui::Rect::from_min_size(egui::pos2(card.left() + 20.0, card.bottom() - 46.0), egui::vec2(120.0, BUTTON_H));
        // The retry button sits INSIDE the card's rect, so it is claimed against the scene rather than
        // against the card — a card and its own button are one surface, not two claimants.
        regions.claim("error retry", retry, ClaimKind::Control);
        if action_button(ui, retry, "Retry", true, "", self.keyboard_focus) {
            self.error = None;
            self.reload();
        }
    }

    /// The empty state — **distinct from the error state**, and the distinction is the point: "there are
    /// no loci" and "the file is missing" are different facts, and only one of them is about the store.
    fn draw_empty(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, layout: &Layout, view: &CityView, regions: &mut Regions) {
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(layout.canvas);
        paint_panel(&painter, layout.app_bar, Elevation::AppBar, None);
        let card = crate::regions::place(egui::vec2(520.0, 150.0), layout.float_area, &[]);
        regions.claim("empty card", card, ClaimKind::Panel);
        paint_panel(&painter, card, Elevation::Dialog, Some("no loci to draw"));
        paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            card.left() + 20.0,
            card.top() + 52.0,
            card.width() - 40.0,
            &format!(
                "The view parsed and is not empty — it declares {} controls, {} regions and {} proposals, \
                 and zero loci. So the grid is real and no civilian has a locus in it.",
                view.controls.len(),
                view.regions.len(),
                view.proposals.len()
            ),
            egui::FontId::proportional(12.0),
            theme::INK_PRIMARY,
        );
        paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            card.left() + 20.0,
            card.bottom() - 52.0,
            card.width() - 40.0,
            "Drawing is still available: the overlays, the monuments and the brush all work over an \
             empty ward.",
            egui::FontId::proportional(11.0),
            theme::INK_SECONDARY,
        );
    }

    /// `rect` is the **slot** the frame's registry reserved for this panel, not a rectangle this
    /// function computes. That inversion is the fix for the overlap: a panel that decides its own
    /// placement cannot know what is already on screen, and four panels that each centred themselves on
    /// the canvas drew on top of one another. `regions::place` decides; this paints.
    fn draw_help(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, rect: egui::Rect, regions: &mut Regions) {
        // Two columns, because the keymap alone left the HIG audit with no home at all — `hig_audit()`
        // existed, was tested, and was never shown anywhere. A rule reported as implemented in a function
        // no surface calls is the same defect as a control that exists only in configuration.
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(rect);
        paint_panel(
            &painter,
            rect,
            Elevation::Dialog,
            Some("keys, gestures and the HIG audit — generated from the keymap"),
        );
        let x = rect.left() + 18.0;
        let left_w = rect.width() * 0.52 - 24.0;
        let mut y = rect.top() + 46.0;
        for (group, rows) in Controls::help_groups() {
            y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, left_w, group.to_uppercase().as_str(),font_mono(10.0),
            theme::ACCENT_UI) + 3.0;
            for (chord, desc) in rows {
                let row = egui::Rect::from_min_size(egui::pos2(x, y), egui::vec2(left_w, 17.0));
                paint_key_chip(&painter, egui::pos2(row.left(), row.top() + 2.0), chord);
                painter.text(
                    egui::pos2(row.left() + 104.0, row.top() + 8.0),
                    egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER,
                    desc,
                    egui::FontId::proportional(11.0),
                    theme::INK_PRIMARY,
                );
                y = row.bottom();
            }
            y += 8.0;
            if y > rect.bottom() - 78.0 {
                break;
            }
        }
        // The gestures, which have no key: stated so the help is complete rather than keymap-only. Every
        // gesture is listed here AND has a key path, which is the HIG requirement — `ctrl+wheel` in
        // particular is the only pointer route to SL-02's depth band.
        paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            x,
            rect.bottom() - 62.0,
            left_w,
            "gestures · drag = draw or orbit · right-drag = orbit · middle-drag = pan · wheel = zoom · \
             shift+wheel = pan · ctrl+wheel = eye depth · double-click = centre",
            egui::FontId::proportional(10.0),
            theme::INK_SECONDARY,
        );

        // ---- the HIG spatial audit (§17) -------------------------------------------------
        let audit_x = rect.left() + rect.width() * 0.54;
        let audit_w = rect.right() - 18.0 - audit_x;
        let mut ay = rect.top() + 46.0;
        ay = paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            audit_x,
            ay,
            audit_w,
            "HIG SPATIAL RULES (§17) — each with what was actually done",
            font_mono(10.0),
            theme::ACCENT_UI,
        ) + 6.0;
        for (rule, implemented, what) in crate::controls::hig_audit() {
            // The glyph and the colour both come from the EXISTING status vocabulary rather than from
            // literals here: "met" and "failed" must read the same way on this panel as they do on a
            // control volume, and a second mapping from a status to a colour is how two views of one
            // status start disagreeing. A rule reported as NOT implemented is drawn in the attention
            // colour rather than hidden, because an audit that only prints its passes is not an audit.
            let (glyph, colour) = if implemented {
                (
                    crate::city::status_glyph_char(crate::city::Glyph::Filled),
                    crate::city::status_tint(crate::city::StatusColour::Met, 255),
                )
            } else {
                (
                    crate::city::status_glyph_char(crate::city::Glyph::Triangle),
                    crate::city::status_tint(crate::city::StatusColour::Failed, 255),
                )
            };
            painter.text(
                egui::pos2(audit_x, ay + 6.0),
                egui::Align2::LEFT_TOP,
                glyph,
                font_mono(10.0),
                colour,
            );
            ay = paint_wrapped(
                &painter,
                audit_x + 12.0,
                ay,
                audit_w - 12.0,
                rule,
                egui::FontId::proportional(11.0),
                colour,
            ) + 1.0;
            ay = paint_wrapped(
                &painter,
                audit_x + 12.0,
                ay,
                audit_w - 12.0,
                what,
                egui::FontId::proportional(10.0),
                theme::INK_SECONDARY,
            ) + 8.0;
            if ay > rect.bottom() - 60.0 {
                break;
            }
        }
        let close = egui::Rect::from_min_size(
            egui::pos2(rect.right() - 42.0, rect.top() + 6.0),
            egui::vec2(36.0, BUTTON_H),
        );
        regions.claim("help close", close, ClaimKind::Control);
        if chip_button(ui, close, "×", false, "Esc", self.keyboard_focus) {
            self.controls.show_help = false;
        }
    }

    fn draw_ledger(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, rect: egui::Rect, view: &CityView, regions: &mut Regions) {
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(rect);
        paint_panel(&painter, rect, Elevation::Dialog, Some("decision ledger — C01–C12 and I1–I4"));
        let mut y = rect.top() + 44.0;
        let x = rect.left() + 18.0;
        let wrap = rect.width() - 36.0;
        paint_wrapped(
            &painter,
            x,
            y,
            wrap,
            "A node may be INSPECTED here and never resolved. Resolution is a governed merge, and a node \
             this surface could resolve would be a surface that legislates.",
            egui::FontId::proportional(10.0),
            theme::INK_SECONDARY,
        );
        y += 30.0;
        for monument in &view.monuments {
            let answered = monument.state == "answered";
            let chip = egui::Rect::from_min_size(egui::pos2(x, y), egui::vec2(96.0, 20.0));
            paint_chip(&painter, chip, if answered { theme::INK_PRIMARY } else { theme::ACCENT_UI }, if answered { "answered" } else { "open" });
            painter.text(
                egui::pos2(chip.right() + 10.0, chip.center().y),
                egui::Align2::LEFT_CENTER,
                &monument.id,
                font_mono(11.0),
                theme::INK_PRIMARY,
            );
            // The question, the citation, and — the load-bearing half — whether resolution is
            // available at all. A monument whose question is `None` is one the view declined to
            // state, and the surface says so rather than printing an empty row that reads as a
            // question with no content.
            let mut my = chip.bottom() + 4.0;
            let body = match &monument.question {
                Some(q) => q.replace('\n', " "),
                None => "(the view states no question for this monument)".to_owned(),
            };
            my = paint_wrapped(&painter, chip.right() + 10.0, my, wrap - 106.0, &body, egui::FontId::proportional(11.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY) + 2.0;
            let tail = format!(
                "{} · resolution {}",
                truncate(&monument.citation, 96),
                if monument.resolve_available { "AVAILABLE" } else { "NOT AVAILABLE HERE" }
            );
            my = paint_wrapped(&painter, chip.right() + 10.0, my, wrap - 106.0, &tail, font_mono(9.0), if monument.resolve_available { theme::INK_SECONDARY } else { theme::INK_DIVIDER }) + 2.0;
            y = my + 6.0;
            if y > rect.bottom() - 40.0 {
                paint_wrapped(&painter, x, y, wrap, "· · · , scroll is not implemented here", egui::FontId::proportional(10.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY);
                break;
            }
        }
        let close = egui::Rect::from_min_size(
            egui::pos2(rect.right() - 42.0, rect.top() + 6.0),
            egui::vec2(36.0, BUTTON_H),
        );
        regions.claim("ledger close", close, ClaimKind::Control);
        if chip_button(ui, close, "×", false, "L", self.keyboard_focus) {
            self.controls.show_ledger = false;
        }
    }

    fn draw_proposals(&mut self, ui: &mut egui::Ui, rect: egui::Rect, view: Option<&CityView>, regions: &mut Regions) {
        let painter = ui.painter().with_clip_rect(rect);
        paint_panel(&painter, rect, Elevation::Dialog, Some("proposals — pending in memory, and the view's own record"));
        let x = rect.left() + 18.0;
        let wrap = rect.width() - 36.0;
        let mut y = rect.top() + 44.0;
        if self.pending.is_empty() {
            paint_wrapped(
                &painter,
                x,
                y,
                wrap,
                "Nothing pending. Every entry here is a proposal the surface has NOT adjudicated, and \
                 committing it writes to the plan store only — `overlay.py adjudicate` is what turns a \
                 proposal into an outcome.",
                egui::FontId::proportional(11.0),
                theme::INK_SECONDARY,
            );
        }
        for (index, proposal) in self.pending.iter().enumerate() {
            y = paint_wrapped(
                &painter,
                x,
                y,
                wrap,
                &format!(
                    "{}. {} · {} tiles · {} · adjudicated: {}",
                    index + 1,
                    proposal.kind,
                    proposal.tiles.len(),
                    proposal.spatial_verdict,
                    proposal.adjudicated
                ),
                font_mono(11.0),
                theme::INK_PRIMARY,
            ) + 2.0;
            y = paint_wrapped(&painter, x + 12.0, y, wrap - 12.0, &proposal.note, egui::FontId::proportional(10.0), theme::INK_SECONDARY) + 6.0;
            if y > rect.bottom() - 40.0 {
                break;
            }
        }
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        // The view's OWN recorded proposals, below the pending ones and explicitly separated.
        //
        // Two different things share the word "proposal" and the panel must not let them blur: what the
        // player has drafted and not committed, and what the view has already recorded as a proposal
        // with an outcome. The second was parsed and dropped until this block existed, so the note the
        // overlay wrote — including "ACCEPTED AS A VIEW: this assigns no locus into the store" — had no
        // reader.
        // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
        if let Some(view) = view {
            let highlighted = self.highlight_tiles(view).len();
            y += 6.0;
            y = paint_separator(&painter, x, y, wrap) + 6.0;
            y = paint_wrapped(
                &painter,
                x,
                y,
                wrap,
                &format!(
                    "RECORDED BY THE VIEW — {} proposal(s), {highlighted} distinct tile(s) highlighted \
