        // only bindings 4-6 while the shader sampled `post.intensity` from binding 3. Device creation
        // then failed with
        //
        //     In Device::create_render_pipeline, label = 'composite'
        //       Shader global ResourceBinding { group: 0, binding: 3 } is not available in the pipeline layout
        //
        // and the cost of the mistake was a frame buffer, `composite_buffer`, that was written every
        // single frame and read by nothing — a value with a producer and no consumer, which is what a
        // layout that disagrees with its shader always looks like from the outside.
        let uniform_entry = |binding: u32, visibility: wgpu::ShaderStages| wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry {
            binding,
            visibility,
            ty: wgpu::BindingType::Buffer {
                ty: wgpu::BufferBindingType::Uniform,
                has_dynamic_offset: false,
                min_binding_size: None,
            },
            count: None,
        };
        let texture_entry = |binding: u32| wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry {
            binding,
            visibility: wgpu::ShaderStages::FRAGMENT,
            ty: wgpu::BindingType::Texture {
                sample_type: wgpu::TextureSampleType::Float { filterable: true },
                view_dimension: wgpu::TextureViewDimension::D2,
                multisampled: false,
            },
            count: None,
        };
        let sampler_entry = |binding: u32| wgpu::BindGroupLayoutEntry {
            binding,
            visibility: wgpu::ShaderStages::FRAGMENT,
            ty: wgpu::BindingType::Sampler(wgpu::SamplerBindingType::Filtering),
            count: None,
        };

        let globals_bgl = device.create_bind_group_layout(&wgpu::BindGroupLayoutDescriptor {
            label: Some("globals layout"),
            entries: &[uniform_entry(0, wgpu::ShaderStages::VERTEX_FRAGMENT)],
        });
        let scene_layout = device.create_pipeline_layout(&wgpu::PipelineLayoutDescriptor {
            label: Some("scene layout"),
            bind_group_layouts: &[&globals_bgl],
            push_constant_ranges: &[],
        });

        let post_bgl = device.create_bind_group_layout(&wgpu::BindGroupLayoutDescriptor {
            label: Some("post layout"),
            entries: &[
                texture_entry(1),
                sampler_entry(2),
                uniform_entry(3, wgpu::ShaderStages::FRAGMENT),
            ],
        });
        let post_layout = device.create_pipeline_layout(&wgpu::PipelineLayoutDescriptor {
            label: Some("post pipeline layout"),
            bind_group_layouts: &[&post_bgl],
            push_constant_ranges: &[],
        });

        let composite_bgl = device.create_bind_group_layout(&wgpu::BindGroupLayoutDescriptor {
            label: Some("composite layout"),
            // 3 is `post` — shared with the post pipelines because the shader declares it once and
            // `fs_composite` reads it. Bindings are per layout, not per pipeline: two layouts may name
            // the same number, and each binds its own buffer to it.
            entries: &[
                uniform_entry(3, wgpu::ShaderStages::FRAGMENT),
                texture_entry(4),
                texture_entry(5),
                sampler_entry(6),
            ],
        });
        let composite_layout = device.create_pipeline_layout(&wgpu::PipelineLayoutDescriptor {
            label: Some("composite pipeline layout"),
            bind_group_layouts: &[&composite_bgl],
            push_constant_ranges: &[],
        });

        // ---- pipelines ----
        let make = |label: &str,
                    layout: &wgpu::PipelineLayout,
                    vs: &str,
                    fs: &str,
                    format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
                    depth: Option<(wgpu::TextureFormat, bool)>,
                    blend: Option<wgpu::BlendState>,
                    instanced: bool| {
            let buffers: Vec<wgpu::VertexBufferLayout> = if instanced {
                vec![Vertex::layout(), Instance::layout()]
            } else {
                Vec::new()
            };
            device.create_render_pipeline(&wgpu::RenderPipelineDescriptor {
                label: Some(label),
                layout: Some(layout),
                vertex: wgpu::VertexState {
                    module: &shader,
                    entry_point: vs,
                    buffers: &buffers,
                    compilation_options: Default::default(),
                },
                fragment: Some(wgpu::FragmentState {
                    module: &shader,
                    entry_point: fs,
                    targets: &[Some(wgpu::ColorTargetState {
                        format,
                        blend,
                        write_mask: wgpu::ColorWrites::ALL,
                    })],
                    compilation_options: Default::default(),
                }),
                primitive: wgpu::PrimitiveState {
                    topology: wgpu::PrimitiveTopology::TriangleList,
                    // No back-face culling: the ground quads are single-sided by construction, and the
                    // figures are closed solids whose interior is never visible because depth already
                    // rejects it. Culling would add a second way for a mesh to be invisible.
                    cull_mode: None,
                    ..Default::default()
                },
                depth_stencil: depth.map(|(format, write)| wgpu::DepthStencilState {
                    format,
                    depth_write_enabled: write,
                    depth_compare: if write {
                        wgpu::CompareFunction::Less
                    } else {
                        wgpu::CompareFunction::LessEqual
                    },
                    stencil: Default::default(),
                    bias: Default::default(),
                }),
                multisample: Default::default(),
                multiview: None,
                cache: None,
            })
        };

        let alpha = Some(wgpu::BlendState::ALPHA_BLENDING);
        // The sky is a fullscreen triangle covering everything, drawn FIRST into the scene pass, which
        // carries a `Depth32Float` attachment. It therefore needs a matching depth state — `None` was
        // a device-creation-level `RenderPass::end` failure:
        //
        //     Incompatible depth-stencil attachment format: the RenderPass uses a texture with
        //     format Some(Depth32Float) but the RenderPipeline with 'sky' label uses an attachment
        //     with format None
        //
        // It depth-TESTS and does not depth-WRITE, which is the only pairing that works here. The sky
        // emits `clip = vec4(p, 0.0, 1.0)` — depth 0, the NEAR plane — so writing depth would clear the
        // way for nothing: every later fragment would compare `Less` against 0.0, fail, and the city
        // would be invisible behind its own sky. With the write off, the buffer stays at the cleared far
        // plane and ordinary geometry depth-tests against that instead.
        let sky = make(
            "sky",
            &scene_layout,
            "vs_fullscreen",
            "fs_sky",
            HDR_FORMAT,
            Some((DEPTH_FORMAT, false)),
            None,
            false,
        );
        let city_opaque = make(
            "city opaque",
            &scene_layout,
            "vs_city",
            "fs_city",
            HDR_FORMAT,
            Some((DEPTH_FORMAT, true)),
            alpha,
            true,
        );
        // The translucent variant is the SAME shader with depth-write off. Two pipelines rather than a
        // runtime flag because `depth_write_enabled` is fixed at pipeline creation, and a blend order
        // decided at draw time is a blend order nobody can review.
        let city_translucent = make(
            "city translucent",
            &scene_layout,
            "vs_city",
            "fs_city",
            HDR_FORMAT,
            Some((DEPTH_FORMAT, false)),
            alpha,
            true,
        );
        let bright = make("bright", &post_layout, "vs_fullscreen", "fs_bright", HDR_FORMAT, None, None, false);
        let blur = make("blur", &post_layout, "vs_fullscreen", "fs_blur", HDR_FORMAT, None, None, false);
        let composite = make(
            "composite",
            &composite_layout,
            "vs_fullscreen",
            "fs_composite",
            target_format,
            None,
            None,
            false,
        );

        // ---- scene uniforms ----
        let globals = device.create_buffer_init(&wgpu::util::BufferInitDescriptor {
            label: Some("globals"),
            contents: bytemuck::bytes_of(&Globals {
                view_proj: [[0.0; 4]; 4],
                eye: [0.0; 4],
                light: [LIGHT_DIRECTION[0], LIGHT_DIRECTION[1], LIGHT_DIRECTION[2], 0.0],
                params: [0.0; 4],
            }),
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
        });
        let globals_bg = device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("globals"),
            layout: &globals_bgl,
            entries: &[wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                binding: 0,
                resource: globals.as_entire_binding(),
            }],
        });

        let sampler = device.create_sampler(&wgpu::SamplerDescriptor {
            label: Some("post sampler"),
            address_mode_u: wgpu::AddressMode::ClampToEdge,
            address_mode_v: wgpu::AddressMode::ClampToEdge,
            address_mode_w: wgpu::AddressMode::ClampToEdge,
            mag_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
            min_filter: wgpu::FilterMode::Linear,
            ..Default::default()
        });

        // ---- one vertex and one index buffer for all three meshes ----
        // The three unit meshes live in ONE pair of buffers with three index ranges. One buffer set
        // means one bind path and no per-mesh state; the ranges are what make three draws possible
        // without three buffers.
        let mut vertices: Vec<Vertex> = Vec::new();
        let mut indices: Vec<u32> = Vec::new();
        let mut ranges = [Range::default(); 3];
        for mesh_id in MeshId::ALL {
            let piece = match mesh_id {
                MeshId::Quad => mesh::unit_quad(),
                MeshId::Box => mesh::unit_box(),
                MeshId::Avatar => mesh::avatar(),
            };
            let base = vertices.len() as u32;
            let start = indices.len() as u32;
            ranges[mesh_id.index()] = Range { start, count: piece.indices.len() as u32 };
            vertices.extend_from_slice(&piece.vertices);
            indices.extend(piece.indices.iter().map(|i| i + base));
        }

        let vertex_buffer = device.create_buffer_init(&wgpu::util::BufferInitDescriptor {
            label: Some("city vertices"),
            contents: bytemuck::cast_slice(&vertices),
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::VERTEX,
        });
        let index_buffer = device.create_buffer_init(&wgpu::util::BufferInitDescriptor {
            label: Some("city indices"),
            contents: bytemuck::cast_slice(&indices),
            usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::INDEX,
        });

        Self {
            sky,
            city_opaque,
            city_translucent,
            bright,
            blur,
            composite,
            scene_layout,
            post_layout,
            composite_layout,
            post_bgl,
            composite_bgl,
            globals,
            globals_bg,
            sampler,
            vertex_buffer,
            index_buffer,
            ranges,
        }
    }
}

/// The offscreen chain. One per target size; rebuilt when the size changes.
struct Target {
    width: u32,
    height: u32,
    hdr: wgpu::TextureView,
    depth: wgpu::TextureView,
    bloom_a: wgpu::TextureView,
    bloom_b: wgpu::TextureView,
    /// `src = hdr` for the bright pass.
    bright_bg: wgpu::BindGroup,
    /// `src = bloom_a`, blurring horizontally.
    blur_h_bg: wgpu::BindGroup,
    /// `src = bloom_b`, blurring vertically back into `bloom_a`.
    blur_v_bg: wgpu::BindGroup,
    composite_bg: wgpu::BindGroup,
}

impl Target {
    fn new(
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        renderer: &Renderer,
        width: u32,
        height: u32,
        post_buffers: &[wgpu::Buffer; 3],
        composite_buffer: &wgpu::Buffer,
    ) -> Self {
        let width = width.max(1);
        let height = height.max(1);
        let make = |label: &str, format: wgpu::TextureFormat, w: u32, h: u32, binding: bool| {
            let usage = wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT
                | if binding { wgpu::TextureUsages::TEXTURE_BINDING } else { wgpu::TextureUsages::empty() };
            device
                .create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
                    label: Some(label),
                    size: wgpu::Extent3d { width: w, height: h, depth_or_array_layers: 1 },
                    mip_level_count: 1,
                    sample_count: 1,
                    dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
                    format,
                    usage,
                    view_formats: &[],
                })
                .create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor::default())
        };

        let bw = (width / BLOOM_DIVISOR).max(1);
        let bh = (height / BLOOM_DIVISOR).max(1);

        let hdr = make("hdr", HDR_FORMAT, width, height, true);
        let depth = make("depth", DEPTH_FORMAT, width, height, false);
        let bloom_a = make("bloom a", HDR_FORMAT, bw, bh, true);
        let bloom_b = make("bloom b", HDR_FORMAT, bw, bh, true);

        let bg = |src: &wgpu::TextureView, buffer: &wgpu::Buffer| {
            device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
                label: Some("post"),
                layout: &renderer.post_bgl,
                entries: &[
                    wgpu::BindGroupEntry { binding: 1, resource: wgpu::BindingResource::TextureView(src) },
                    wgpu::BindGroupEntry { binding: 2, resource: wgpu::BindingResource::Sampler(&renderer.sampler) },
                    wgpu::BindGroupEntry { binding: 3, resource: buffer.as_entire_binding() },
                ],
            })
        };

        let composite_bg = device.create_bind_group(&wgpu::BindGroupDescriptor {
            label: Some("composite"),
            layout: &renderer.composite_bgl,
            entries: &[
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry {
                    binding: 3,
                    resource: composite_buffer.as_entire_binding(),
                },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry { binding: 4, resource: wgpu::BindingResource::TextureView(&hdr) },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry { binding: 5, resource: wgpu::BindingResource::TextureView(&bloom_a) },
                wgpu::BindGroupEntry { binding: 6, resource: wgpu::BindingResource::Sampler(&renderer.sampler) },
            ],
        });

        // Bind groups are built into locals BEFORE the struct literal, not inline in it. Inline would
        // be tidier to read and would not compile: a struct's fields are evaluated in written order, so
        // listing `hdr` above `bright_bg: bg(&hdr, …)` moves the view before it is borrowed. The fix is
        // ordering, and the local makes the ordering explicit rather than a rule about field position.
        let bright_bg = bg(&hdr, &post_buffers[0]);
        let blur_h_bg = bg(&bloom_a, &post_buffers[1]);
        let blur_v_bg = bg(&bloom_b, &post_buffers[2]);

        Self {
            width,
            height,
            hdr,
            depth,
            bloom_a,
            bloom_b,
            bright_bg,
            blur_h_bg,
            blur_v_bg,
            composite_bg,
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The resource the callback keeps between frames
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// Everything persistent for the city surface. Stored in egui-wgpu's callback resources, so the
/// shaders are compiled once and the instance buffers are only re-uploaded when the scene changes.
pub struct CityGpu {
    renderer: Renderer,
    target: Option<Target>,
    instance_buffers: [wgpu::Buffer; 3],
    instance_capacity: [usize; 3],
    post_buffers: [wgpu::Buffer; 3],
    composite_buffer: wgpu::Buffer,
    /// A hash of the instance bytes last uploaded. Re-uploading an unchanged scene every frame would
    /// be a real cost for no pixels, and this makes it a measurable one.
    last_scene_key: u64,
    /// Frames rendered, and the last scene's counts. Exposed for the debug overlay so the surface can
    /// report its own telemetry instead of a test guessing it (`3DUI.MD` §17's overlay-metric rule).
    pub frames: u64,
    pub last_counts: scene::SceneCounts,
    pub last_uploaded_bytes: u64,
}

impl CityGpu {
    pub fn new(device: &wgpu::Device, target_format: wgpu::TextureFormat) -> Self {
        let renderer = Renderer::new(device, target_format);
        let uniform = |label: &str| {
            device.create_buffer_init(&wgpu::util::BufferInitDescriptor {
                label: Some(label),
                contents: bytemuck::bytes_of(&Post {
                    texel: [1.0, 1.0],
                    dir: [0.0, 0.0],
                    threshold: BLOOM_THRESHOLD,
                    intensity: BLOOM_COMPOSITE,
                    _pad0: 0.0,
                    _pad1: 0.0,
                }),
                usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::UNIFORM | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
            })
        };
        let post_buffers = [uniform("post bright"), uniform("post blur h"), uniform("post blur v")];
        let composite_buffer = uniform("post composite");
        let instance = |label: &str| {
            device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
                label: Some(label),
                // A zero-sized buffer is invalid; one instance of slack keeps the first frame valid
                // without a special case in the draw path.
                size: (std::mem::size_of::<Instance>() * 64) as u64,
                usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::VERTEX | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
                mapped_at_creation: false,
            })
        };
        Self {
            renderer,
            target: None,
            instance_buffers: [instance("instances quad"), instance("instances box"), instance("instances avatar")],
            instance_capacity: [64, 64, 64],
            post_buffers,
            composite_buffer,
            last_scene_key: 0,
            frames: 0,
            last_counts: scene::SceneCounts::default(),
            last_uploaded_bytes: 0,
        }
    }

    /// Scene bytes -> GPU, only when they changed. Returns whether an upload happened.
    fn upload(&mut self, device: &wgpu::Device, queue: &wgpu::Queue, scene: &Scene) -> bool {
        let groups = scene::partition(scene);
        let key = scene_key(&groups);
        if key == self.last_scene_key {
            return false;
        }
        self.last_scene_key = key;
        let mut bytes = 0u64;
        for (index, group) in groups.iter().enumerate() {
            let needed = group.instances.len().max(1);
            if needed > self.instance_capacity[index] {
                // Grow by doubling rather than to the exact size: a scene that gains one citizen per
                // frame would otherwise reallocate every frame.
                let capacity = needed.next_power_of_two();
                self.instance_buffers[index] = device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
                    label: Some("instances"),
                    size: (std::mem::size_of::<Instance>() * capacity) as u64,
                    usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::VERTEX | wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST,
                    mapped_at_creation: false,
                });
                self.instance_capacity[index] = capacity;
            }
            if !group.instances.is_empty() {
                let data = bytemuck::cast_slice(&group.instances);
                queue.write_buffer(&self.instance_buffers[index], 0, data);
                bytes += data.len() as u64;
            }
        }
        self.last_uploaded_bytes = bytes;
        true
    }

    /// Encode the offscreen chain: sky + geometry into `hdr`, then the bloom pair.
    fn encode_scene(
        &self,
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
        encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder,
        scene: &Scene,
        params: &FrameParams,
        width: u32,
        height: u32,
    ) {
        let Some(target) = self.target.as_ref() else { return };
        let _ = device;
        let r = &self.renderer;

        // ---- uniforms ----
        let globals = Globals {
            view_proj: params.view_proj,
            eye: [params.eye[0], params.eye[1], params.eye[2], 1.0],
            light: [
                LIGHT_DIRECTION[0],
                LIGHT_DIRECTION[1],
                LIGHT_DIRECTION[2],
                params.time,
            ],
            params: [
                if params.reduced_motion { 1.0 } else { 0.0 },
                params.grid_size,
                params.zoom,
                0.0,
            ],
        };
        queue.write_buffer(&r.globals, 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&globals));

        let bw = (width / BLOOM_DIVISOR).max(1);
        let bh = (height / BLOOM_DIVISOR).max(1);
        // FOUR separate uniform buffers, not one rewritten four times. `queue.write_buffer` writes are
        // staged and all take effect before the command buffer runs, so reusing one buffer would give
        // every pass the last value written — the blur would silently become the composite.
        let bright = Post {
            texel: [1.0 / width as f32, 1.0 / height as f32],
            dir: [0.0, 0.0],
            threshold: BLOOM_THRESHOLD,
            intensity: BLOOM_COMPOSITE,
            _pad0: 0.0,
            _pad1: 0.0,
        };
        let blur_h = Post {
            texel: [1.0 / bw as f32, 1.0 / bh as f32],
            dir: [1.0, 0.0],
            threshold: 0.0,
            intensity: 0.0,
            _pad0: 0.0,
            _pad1: 0.0,
        };
        let blur_v = Post { dir: [0.0, 1.0], ..blur_h };
        let composite = Post {
            texel: [1.0 / width as f32, 1.0 / height as f32],
            dir: [0.0, 0.0],
            threshold: 0.0,
            intensity: BLOOM_COMPOSITE,
            _pad0: 0.0,
            _pad1: 0.0,
        };
        queue.write_buffer(&self.post_buffers[0], 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&bright));
        queue.write_buffer(&self.post_buffers[1], 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&blur_h));
        queue.write_buffer(&self.post_buffers[2], 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&blur_v));
        queue.write_buffer(&self.composite_buffer, 0, bytemuck::bytes_of(&composite));

        let groups = scene::partition(scene);

        // ---- pass 1: sky, then geometry ----
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
                label: Some("city scene"),
                color_attachments: &[Some(wgpu::RenderPassColorAttachment {
                    view: &target.hdr,
                    resolve_target: None,
                    ops: wgpu::Operations {
                        load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(wgpu::Color::BLACK),
                        store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
                    },
                })],
                depth_stencil_attachment: Some(wgpu::RenderPassDepthStencilAttachment {
                    view: &target.depth,
                    depth_ops: Some(wgpu::Operations {
                        load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(CLEAR_DEPTH),
                        store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
                    }),
                    stencil_ops: None,
                }),
                timestamp_writes: None,
                occlusion_query_set: None,
            });

            pass.set_pipeline(&r.sky);
            pass.set_bind_group(0, &r.globals_bg, &[]);
            pass.draw(0..3, 0..1);

            pass.set_index_buffer(r.index_buffer.slice(..), wgpu::IndexFormat::Uint32);
            pass.set_vertex_buffer(0, r.vertex_buffer.slice(..));
            pass.set_bind_group(0, &r.globals_bg, &[]);

            for mesh_id in MeshId::ALL {
                let index = mesh_id.index();
                let group = &groups[index];
                let range = r.ranges[index];
                if range.count == 0 || group.instances.is_empty() {
                    continue;
                }
                pass.set_vertex_buffer(1, self.instance_buffers[index].slice(..));

                if group.opaque_count > 0 {
                    pass.set_pipeline(&r.city_opaque);
                    pass.draw_indexed(
                        range.start..range.start + range.count,
                        0,
                        0..group.opaque_count as u32,
                    );
                }
                if group.opaque_count < group.instances.len() {
                    // The translucent tail: same vertex range, instances offset past the opaque ones,
                    // and a pipeline with depth-write off so a volume never occludes what it reports.
                    pass.set_pipeline(&r.city_translucent);
                    let offset = (group.opaque_count * std::mem::size_of::<Instance>()) as u64;
                    pass.set_vertex_buffer(1, self.instance_buffers[index].slice(offset..));
                    pass.draw_indexed(
                        range.start..range.start + range.count,
                        0,
                        0..(group.instances.len() - group.opaque_count) as u32,
                    );
                }
            }
        }

        // ---- pass 2: bright ----
        {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
                label: Some("bloom bright"),
                color_attachments: &[Some(wgpu::RenderPassColorAttachment {
                    view: &target.bloom_a,
                    resolve_target: None,
                    ops: wgpu::Operations {
                        load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(wgpu::Color::BLACK),
                        store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
                    },
                })],
                depth_stencil_attachment: None,
                timestamp_writes: None,
                occlusion_query_set: None,
            });
            pass.set_pipeline(&r.bright);
            pass.set_bind_group(0, &target.bright_bg, &[]);
            pass.draw(0..3, 0..1);
        }

        // ---- pass 3: blur, horizontal then vertical ----
        for (view, bg) in [(&target.bloom_b, &target.blur_h_bg), (&target.bloom_a, &target.blur_v_bg)] {
            let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
                label: Some("bloom blur"),
                color_attachments: &[Some(wgpu::RenderPassColorAttachment {
                    view,
                    resolve_target: None,
                    ops: wgpu::Operations {
                        load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(wgpu::Color::BLACK),
                        store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
                    },
                })],
                depth_stencil_attachment: None,
                timestamp_writes: None,
                occlusion_query_set: None,
            });
            pass.set_pipeline(&r.blur);
            pass.set_bind_group(0, bg, &[]);
            pass.draw(0..3, 0..1);
        }
    }

    /// Composite into whatever pass is current. This is the one place the GPU path touches egui's own
    /// render pass, and it draws a single triangle — which is why the viewport egui sets is enough.
    fn composite_into(&self, pass: &mut wgpu::RenderPass<'_>) {
        let Some(target) = self.target.as_ref() else { return };
        pass.set_pipeline(&self.renderer.composite);
        pass.set_bind_group(0, &target.composite_bg, &[]);
        pass.draw(0..3, 0..1);
    }
}

/// A content hash of the instance data, so an unchanged scene is not re-uploaded.
///
/// FNV-1a over the raw bytes: not cryptographic, and it does not need to be — a collision would mean
/// one stale frame, while a hash that took longer than the upload it avoids would be worse than none.
fn scene_key(groups: &[scene::MeshGroup; 3]) -> u64 {
    let mut hash: u64 = 0xcbf2_9ce4_8422_2325;
    for group in groups {
        hash ^= group.instances.len() as u64;
        hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
        for instance in &group.instances {
            for byte in bytemuck::bytes_of(instance) {
                hash ^= *byte as u64;
                hash = hash.wrapping_mul(0x0000_0100_0000_01b3);
            }
        }
    }
    hash
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The callback
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

/// A frame of the city: the built scene and the parameters, handed to egui as a paint callback.
pub struct CityCallback {
    pub scene: Arc<Scene>,
    pub params: FrameParams,
}

impl CallbackTrait for CityCallback {
    fn prepare(
        &self,
        device: &wgpu::Device,
        queue: &wgpu::Queue,
        screen_descriptor: &ScreenDescriptor,
        encoder: &mut wgpu::CommandEncoder,
        resources: &mut CallbackResources,
    ) -> Vec<wgpu::CommandBuffer> {
        if resources.get::<CityGpu>().is_none() {
            resources.insert(CityGpu::new(device, self.params.target_format));
        }
        let gpu = match resources.get_mut::<CityGpu>() {
            Some(gpu) => gpu,
            None => return Vec::new(),
        };

        // The offscreen target is sized to the CALLBACK RECT rather than the window — see the module
        // doc. `pixels_per_point` comes from the screen descriptor so the size and egui's own viewport
        // arithmetic agree.
        let ppp = screen_descriptor.pixels_per_point.max(0.1);
        let width = (self.params.rect_points[2] * ppp).round().max(1.0) as u32;
        let height = (self.params.rect_points[3] * ppp).round().max(1.0) as u32;
        let needs_target = match &gpu.target {
            Some(target) => target.width != width || target.height != height,
            None => true,
        };
        if needs_target {
            gpu.target = Some(Target::new(
                device,
                &gpu.renderer,
                width,
                height,
                &gpu.post_buffers,
                &gpu.composite_buffer,
            ));
        }

        gpu.frames += 1;
        gpu.last_counts = self.scene.counts;
        gpu.upload(device, queue, &self.scene);
        gpu.encode_scene(device, queue, encoder, &self.scene, &self.params, width, height);
        Vec::new()
    }

    fn paint(
        &self,
        _info: egui::epaint::PaintCallbackInfo,
        render_pass: &mut wgpu::RenderPass<'static>,
        resources: &CallbackResources,
    ) {
        // The one draw that touches egui's own pass. egui-wgpu has already set the viewport to this
        // callback's rect, so a fullscreen triangle lands exactly in the panel — no scissor maths, and
        // nothing to get wrong when the panel is resized.
        if let Some(gpu) = resources.get::<CityGpu>() {
            gpu.composite_into(render_pass);
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Offscreen rendering, for the tests
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

#[cfg(test)]
pub mod testing {
    use super::*;

    /// Render a scene to RGBA8 pixels with no window and no surface.
    ///
    /// This exists so the pipeline can be **exercised** rather than described. It walks the same
    /// `CityGpu` used by the callback through the same passes and reads the result back, which is the
    /// oracle half of rule 83 — the mechanical half being that `naga` parses the WGSL with no GPU.
    pub struct Offscreen {
        pub device: wgpu::Device,
        pub queue: wgpu::Queue,
        pub gpu: CityGpu,
        pub width: u32,
        pub height: u32,
        pub format: wgpu::TextureFormat,
        pub adapter_info: String,
    }

    /// Returns `None` when no adapter is available, so a machine without a GPU reports "not obtained"
    /// rather than a red test that says the pipeline is broken.
    pub fn try_new(width: u32, height: u32) -> Option<Offscreen> {
        use eframe::wgpu;
        let instance = wgpu::Instance::new(wgpu::InstanceDescriptor {
            backends: wgpu::Backends::all(),
            ..Default::default()
        });
        let adapter = futures_lite::future::block_on(instance.request_adapter(&wgpu::RequestAdapterOptions {
            power_preference: wgpu::PowerPreference::HighPerformance,
            compatible_surface: None,
            force_fallback_adapter: false,
        }))?;
        let info = adapter.get_info();
        let (device, queue) = futures_lite::future::block_on(adapter.request_device(
            &wgpu::DeviceDescriptor {
                label: Some("offscreen"),
                required_features: wgpu::Features::empty(),
                required_limits: wgpu::Limits::downlevel_defaults(),
                memory_hints: Default::default(),
            },
            None,
        ))
        .ok()?;
        // `Rgba8UnormSrgb` matches the composite pipeline's expectations and reads back in an order a
        // test can assert on without knowing the platform's preferred surface format.
        let format = wgpu::TextureFormat::Rgba8UnormSrgb;
        let gpu = CityGpu::new(&device, format);
        Some(Offscreen {
            device,
            queue,
            gpu,
            width,
            height,
            format,
            adapter_info: format!("{} ({:?}, {:?})", info.name, info.device_type, info.backend),
        })
    }

    impl Offscreen {
        /// Render one frame and return tightly packed RGBA8 pixels, row-major, top-left origin.
        pub fn render(&mut self, scene: &Scene, params: &FrameParams) -> Vec<u8> {
            // A target the size of the image, driven through exactly the callback's own path.
            self.gpu.target = Some(Target::new(
                &self.device,
                &self.gpu.renderer,
                self.width,
                self.height,
                &self.gpu.post_buffers,
                &self.gpu.composite_buffer,
            ));
            self.gpu.upload(&self.device, &self.queue, scene);

            let out = self.device.create_texture(&wgpu::TextureDescriptor {
                label: Some("offscreen out"),
                size: wgpu::Extent3d {
                    width: self.width,
                    height: self.height,
                    depth_or_array_layers: 1,
                },
                mip_level_count: 1,
                sample_count: 1,
                dimension: wgpu::TextureDimension::D2,
                format: self.format,
                usage: wgpu::TextureUsages::RENDER_ATTACHMENT | wgpu::TextureUsages::COPY_SRC,
                view_formats: &[],
            });
            let out_view = out.create_view(&wgpu::TextureViewDescriptor::default());

            let mut encoder = self
                .device
                .create_command_encoder(&wgpu::CommandEncoderDescriptor { label: Some("offscreen") });
            self.gpu
                .encode_scene(&self.device, &self.queue, &mut encoder, scene, params, self.width, self.height);
            {
                let mut pass = encoder.begin_render_pass(&wgpu::RenderPassDescriptor {
                    label: Some("composite"),
                    color_attachments: &[Some(wgpu::RenderPassColorAttachment {
                        view: &out_view,
                        resolve_target: None,
                        ops: wgpu::Operations {
                            load: wgpu::LoadOp::Clear(wgpu::Color::BLACK),
                            store: wgpu::StoreOp::Store,
                        },
                    })],
                    depth_stencil_attachment: None,
                    timestamp_writes: None,
                    occlusion_query_set: None,
                });
                self.gpu.composite_into(&mut pass);
            }

            // `copy_texture_to_buffer` requires a 256-byte row stride, so the readback buffer is
            // padded and the padding is stripped below.
            let unpadded = self.width * 4;
            let padded = unpadded.div_ceil(256) * 256;
            let buffer = self.device.create_buffer(&wgpu::BufferDescriptor {
                label: Some("readback"),
                size: (padded * self.height) as u64,
                usage: wgpu::BufferUsages::COPY_DST | wgpu::BufferUsages::MAP_READ,
                mapped_at_creation: false,
            });
            encoder.copy_texture_to_buffer(
                wgpu::ImageCopyTexture {
                    texture: &out,
                    mip_level: 0,
                    origin: wgpu::Origin3d::ZERO,
                    aspect: wgpu::TextureAspect::All,
                },
                wgpu::ImageCopyBuffer {
                    buffer: &buffer,
                    layout: wgpu::ImageDataLayout {
                        offset: 0,
                        bytes_per_row: Some(padded),
                        rows_per_image: Some(self.height),
                    },
                },
                wgpu::Extent3d {
                    width: self.width,
                    height: self.height,
                    depth_or_array_layers: 1,
                },
            );
            self.queue.submit(Some(encoder.finish()));

            let slice = buffer.slice(..);
            let (tx, rx) = std::sync::mpsc::channel();
            slice.map_async(wgpu::MapMode::Read, move |result| {
                let _ = tx.send(result);
            });
            self.device.poll(wgpu::Maintain::Wait);
            rx.recv().expect("map callback").expect("map succeeded");
            let view = slice.get_mapped_range();
            let mut pixels = Vec::with_capacity((unpadded * self.height) as usize);
            for row in 0..self.height {
                let start = (row * padded) as usize;
                pixels.extend_from_slice(&view[start..start + unpadded as usize]);
            }
            drop(view);
            buffer.unmap();
            pixels
        }
    }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The two halves of rule 83, both of which were claimed and neither of which existed
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
//
// This module is the defect that a launch found. `naga` was declared as a dev-dependency whose
// comment said *"CPU-only WGSL parsing, so shader correctness is checkable with NO GPU present"*,
// and `Offscreen` was documented as *"the oracle half of rule 83 — the mechanical half being that
// naga parses the WGSL with no GPU"*. **Both statements were false. Nothing called either one.**
//
// The cost was measured rather than argued. `fs_blur` indexed a `let` array with a loop variable,
// which naga refuses, and the shader shipped anyway because no test ever put the WGSL in front of a
// validator — the binary panicked at device creation instead, on the operator's machine:
//
//     In Device::create_shader_module, label = 'city.wgsl'
//       Expression [34] is invalid
//         The expression [6] may only be indexed by a constant
//         Entry point fs_blur at Fragment is invalid
//
// That is rule 83's exact failure: a check *declared* is not a check *run*, and rule 43 says a
// control that exists only in configuration is not implemented. Two tests, one per half.
#[cfg(test)]
mod gpu_pipeline_tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::city::{locate_view, read_view};
    use crate::controls::Orbit;

    /// The entry points the six pipelines are created against, in `Renderer::new`'s own order.
    /// A name here that the shader does not declare is a device-creation panic, so the list is the
    /// contract rather than a sample of it.
    const ENTRY_POINTS: [(&str, naga::ShaderStage); 5] = [
        ("vs_fullscreen", naga::ShaderStage::Vertex),
        ("vs_city", naga::ShaderStage::Vertex),
        ("fs_sky", naga::ShaderStage::Fragment),
        ("fs_city", naga::ShaderStage::Fragment),
        ("fs_bright", naga::ShaderStage::Fragment),
    ];

    /// Parse AND validate the real shader source, with no device and no GPU.
    ///
    /// Parsing alone is not enough: the `fs_blur` defect parsed fine and failed *validation*, which
    /// is why this walks both stages. `Capabilities::all()` mirrors what `wgpu` grants a device on a
    /// capable adapter; the honest limit is that it is a naga-level opinion and not the driver's.
    #[test]
    fn the_shader_parses_and_validates_with_no_gpu() {
        let source = include_str!("../shaders/city.wgsl");
        let module = naga::front::wgsl::parse_str(source)
            .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("city.wgsl does not parse:\n{}", error.emit_to_string(source)));

        naga::valid::Validator::new(
            naga::valid::ValidationFlags::all(),
            naga::valid::Capabilities::all(),
        )
        .validate(&module)
        .unwrap_or_else(|error| panic!("city.wgsl does not validate:\n{error:?}"));

        // And every entry point the pipelines name is really there, so a renamed function is a test
        // failure rather than a panic on the operator's machine.
        for (name, stage) in ENTRY_POINTS {
            let found = module
                .entry_points
                .iter()
                .any(|entry| entry.name == name && entry.stage == stage);
            assert!(found, "the shader must declare `{name}` for {stage:?}");
        }
    }

    /// The exact construct that broke, asserted in isolation so the reason survives a refactor.
    ///
    /// If a future revision reintroduces a dynamic index into a `let` array anywhere in the shader,
    /// the validator above fails — and this test says which construct it was and why it cannot work,
    /// so the next reader does not "simplify" the unrolled kernel back into a loop.
    #[test]
    fn a_let_array_may_not_be_indexed_dynamically() {
        let bad = "@fragment\nfn f(@location(0) uv: vec2<f32>) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {\n\
                   let offsets = array<f32, 3>(0.0, 1.0, 2.0);\n\
                   var sum = 0.0;\n\
                   for (var i = 0u; i < 3u; i = i + 1u) {\n    sum += offsets[i];\n  }\n\
                   return vec4<f32>(sum, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0);\n}\n";
        let module = naga::front::wgsl::parse_str(bad).expect("the construct parses");
        let verdict = naga::valid::Validator::new(
            naga::valid::ValidationFlags::all(),
            naga::valid::Capabilities::all(),
        )
        .validate(&module);
        assert!(
            verdict.is_err(),
            "a `let` array indexed by a loop variable must be refused; if naga now accepts it, the \
             unrolled kernel in fs_blur may be rewritten as a loop again"
        );
    }

    /// The oracle half: render the real scene through the real pipelines and read the pixels back.
    ///
    /// This is the only test that exercises the surface end to end. It is skipped with a printed
    /// reason when the machine has no adapter, so a headless runner reports "not obtained" rather
    /// than a failure that reads as "the pipeline is broken" (§9.5).
    #[test]
    fn the_real_scene_renders_to_pixels() {
        let Some(mut off) = testing::try_new(240, 160) else {
            eprintln!("NOT OBTAINED: no GPU adapter on this machine; the offscreen oracle did not run");
            return;
        };

        let path = locate_view().expect("seasons/plans/view.json — run `python overlay.py view`");
        let view = read_view(&path).expect("the view must parse and declare its marker");

        let extent = scene::grid_extent(view.grid.size);
        let orbit = Orbit::from_grid(view.grid.tilt, view.grid.rotation, view.grid.size);
        let eye = orbit.eye(extent);
        let (w, h) = (off.width, off.height);
        let params = FrameParams {
            view_proj: orbit.view_proj(w as f32 / h as f32, extent),
            eye,
            rect_points: [0.0, 0.0, w as f32, h as f32],
            time: 0.0,
            reduced_motion: false,
            grid_size: extent,
            zoom: orbit.zoom,
            target_format: off.format,
        };

        let scene = scene::build(&view, &scene::SceneOptions::default(), eye, 0.0);
        let pixels = off.render(&scene, &params);

        assert_eq!(
            pixels.len(),
            (w * h * 4) as usize,
            "readback must be tightly packed RGBA8 ({w}x{h})"
        );
        // `[V]` the adapter that produced these pixels, printed so a failing run names the device.
        eprintln!("offscreen oracle ran on {}", off.adapter_info);

        // A frame that rendered nothing is indistinguishable from a pipeline that silently did not
        // draw, so the assertions are about CONTENT rather than about "it did not panic".
        let distinct: std::collections::HashSet<[u8; 3]> = pixels
            .chunks_exact(4)
            .map(|p| [p[0], p[1], p[2]])
            .collect();
        assert!(
            distinct.len() > 8,
            "only {} distinct colours: the scene did not draw (rule 36 — exercise the surface)",
            distinct.len()
        );
        assert!(
            distinct.iter().any(|c| c != &[0, 0, 0]),
            "every pixel is black, so no pass produced output"
        );
    }
}
```

#### `rust-ui/src/gpu/scene.rs`

```rust
//! scene.rs — the derived view turned into GPU instances. Pure, deterministic, no device.
//!
//! # The rule this module obeys above all others
//!
//! **Every instance is placed by something the view already says.** The moment this file chooses a
//! position for a doctrine object out of its own judgement, the surface has stopped rendering the
//! store and started authoring it — which is `3DUI.MD`'s governing constraint and rule 112.
//!
//! That rule has a visible cost here, and the cost is worth naming rather than hiding:
//!
//! *The view carries no geometry for the twelve controls.* `controls` is
//! `{control, requirement, mechanical_status, identity_status}` — twelve records with no `rect`, no
//! tile and no extent. `3DUI.MD` §7.1 asks for them as **overlay volumes**, and a volume needs a
//! position. Three options existed:
//!
//! 1. Invent a sector per control. Refused: that is the surface deciding where authority applies.
//! 2. Draw nothing. Refused as the sole answer, because §7.1 does ask for them and silence would read
//!    as "no controls exist".
//! 3. Place them where the specification *does* place non-spatial doctrine: **on the map perimeter**.
//!    §9.1 puts decision monuments on the perimeter in the HIG arc, and §9.3 puts out-of-scope walls
//!    there too. A control is non-spatial doctrine of the same kind, so a control **column** on the
//!    perimeter is spec-grounded while a control *volume* is not.
//!
//! Option 3 is what is implemented, and it is a **substitute, recorded as one**. The perimeter column
//! says "this control exists and has this status"; it does not claim to say *where* the control
//! applies, because the store never said.
//!
//! # What is placed, and by what
//!
//! | instance | placed by |
//! |---|---|
//! | ground tiles | `grid.size` |
//! | locus blocks | `loci[].tile`, height from `loci[].height` |
//! | citizens | `loci[].tile` (the locus is where a citizen *is*; `avatars[]` carries no position) |
//! | fog volumes | `regions[kind == "fog"].rect` |
//! | out-of-scope walls | `regions[kind == "wall"].rect` |
//! | never-granted gates | `never_granted[]`, on the boundary — §6.4 |
//! | decision monuments | `monuments[]`, on the perimeter arc — §9.1 |
//! | control columns | `controls[]`, on the perimeter — see above |
//! | idle blocks | `idle_jobs[].tile`, a constant height — §33 |
use crate::city::{CityView, IdleJobRec};
use crate::theme;

/// `kind` values. **These must equal the `KIND_*` constants in `city.wgsl`** — a mismatch is not a
/// compile error, it is a wrong colour, which is why [`tests::kinds_agree_with_the_shader_source`]
/// parses the shader text and asserts the agreement rather than trusting a comment.
pub const KIND_TILE: u32 = 0;
pub const KIND_BLOCK: u32 = 1;
pub const KIND_AVATAR: u32 = 2;
pub const KIND_NODE: u32 = 3;
pub const KIND_VOLUME: u32 = 4;
pub const KIND_FOG: u32 = 5;
pub const KIND_GATE: u32 = 6;
pub const KIND_WALL: u32 = 7;
pub const KIND_HOVER: u32 = 8;
pub const KIND_BRUSH: u32 = 9;
/// **An idle block — a declared fiction, and its own kind rather than a `KIND_BLOCK`.**
///
/// The whole authorization for `PLAN_JOBS.md`'s layer is that a fiction is marked STRUCTURALLY, so a
/// consumer cannot mistake it for a real locus. Sharing `KIND_BLOCK` would have made the distinction a
/// convention in a renderer, which is the thing marking rule 4 exists to prevent — and the shader can
/// then give it its own treatment (dashed, desaturated, never a citizen silhouette) rather than a tint
/// applied to the same geometry.
pub const KIND_IDLE: u32 = 10;

pub const STATUS_MET: u32 = 0;
pub const STATUS_FAILED: u32 = 1;
pub const STATUS_NOT_EVALUABLE: u32 = 2;
pub const STATUS_UNKNOWN: u32 = 3;

/// Map a doctrine status string to the code the shader draws. **There is no default arm that returns
/// `MET`** — an unrecognised string becomes `STATUS_UNKNOWN`, which the shader draws in a magenta no
/// status uses, because §31.1's failure is a status that renders as passing when it was never read.
pub fn status_code(status: &str) -> u32 {
    match status {
        "MET" => STATUS_MET,
        "FAILED" => STATUS_FAILED,
        "NOT_EVALUABLE" => STATUS_NOT_EVALUABLE,
        _ => STATUS_UNKNOWN,
    }
}

/// One instance. 64 bytes, 16-byte aligned and padding-free, so `Pod` is sound.
#[repr(C)]
#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, bytemuck::Pod, bytemuck::Zeroable)]
pub struct Instance {
    /// `xyz` world position (the point the thing **stands on**), `w` horizontal scale.
    pub pos_scale: [f32; 4],
    /// `rgb` tint, `a` unused by the opaque pass and kept for a future use rather than repurposed.
    pub tint: [f32; 4],
    /// `x` kind, `y` status code, `zw` reserved.
    pub kind_status: [u32; 4],
    /// `x` vertical height (0 means "use the horizontal scale"), `y` an animated flag,
    /// `z` the Z-scale ratio (0 means 1.0), `w` reserved.
    ///
    /// `z` exists for the kinds whose footprint is not square — a wall's region rect, and the drag
    /// rectangle — and it is the **same slot for both**. An earlier revision put the wall's ratio in
    /// `y`, which is where the pulse lives for a hover/brush overlay, so one field meant two things
    /// depending on the kind. Two meanings in one slot is how a renderer stops being reviewable.
    pub params: [f32; 4],
}

impl Instance {
    pub fn layout() -> eframe::wgpu::VertexBufferLayout<'static> {
        use eframe::wgpu;
        // Locations **4-7**: 0-3 belong to `Vertex`. The two layouts are bound to different slots,
        // so the numbers are what keeps them from colliding rather than the binding order.
        const ATTRS: [wgpu::VertexAttribute; 4] = wgpu::vertex_attr_array![
            4 => Float32x4,
            5 => Float32x4,
            6 => Uint32x4,
            7 => Float32x4,
        ];
        wgpu::VertexBufferLayout {
            array_stride: std::mem::size_of::<Instance>() as wgpu::BufferAddress,
            step_mode: wgpu::VertexStepMode::Instance,
            attributes: &ATTRS,
        }
    }
}

/// Which layers the player has switched on. Every one of these is a *view* control with no authority:
/// switching fog off hides the fog and changes nothing about it (§9.2 — "the overlay must not pre-slice
/// them into fake answers").
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SceneOptions {
    pub avatars: bool,
    pub blocks: bool,
    pub volumes: bool,
    pub fog: bool,
    pub walls: bool,
    pub gates: bool,
    pub monuments: bool,
    /// The recorded-proposal highlight layer. A toggle rather than a list, because the *content* is
    /// supplied as an argument: a layer switch is a `bool` and the tiles it highlights are data, and
    /// folding the two together would make this struct non-`Copy` for no gain.
    pub highlights: bool,
    /// Monotonic seconds, for the pulsing FAILED state and the aurora. Passed in rather than sampled
    /// here so the scene is a pure function of its inputs and a test can produce a fixed result.
    pub reduced_motion: bool,
}

impl Default for SceneOptions {
    fn default() -> Self {
        Self {
            avatars: true,
            blocks: true,
            volumes: true,
            fog: true,
            walls: true,
            gates: true,
            monuments: true,
            highlights: false,
            reduced_motion: false,
        }
    }
}

/// A built frame: the instances, split into the two draws, plus counts for honest telemetry.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct Scene {
    pub instances: Vec<Instance>,
    /// Instances `[0, opaque_count)` are drawn with depth-write; the rest are translucent and drawn
    /// after, depth-tested but not depth-writing, so a volume never occludes a citizen behind it.
    pub opaque_count: usize,
    pub counts: SceneCounts,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, Default, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub struct SceneCounts {
    pub tiles: usize,
    pub blocks: usize,
    pub citizens: usize,
    /// Highlighted tiles emitted for the recorded proposals. Counted separately from `tiles` so the HUD
    /// can tell "the grid is 576 tiles" from "two of them are highlighted", which is the same discipline
    /// as counting citizens by what was emitted rather than by the loop that emitted them.
    pub highlights: usize,
    /// Loci that exist but whose civilian is **fog** — a multi-civilian job, where drawing figures
    /// would mean the surface inventing all but one of them (§30.2). Counted separately from
    /// `citizens` because the HUD shows both, and a telemetry line that called a dashed placeholder a
    /// citizen would be a wrong number presented as a measurement.
    pub fogged_loci: usize,
    pub volumes: usize,
    pub fog: usize,
    pub walls: usize,
    pub gates: usize,
    pub monuments: usize,
    /// Idle blocks emitted. Counted separately from `blocks` and `citizens` for the same reason
    /// `fogged_loci` is: the HUD shows both numbers, and a telemetry line that added fiction to the
    /// civilian count would be a fiction presented as a measurement — the one thing `PLAN_JOBS.md`
    /// refuses.
    pub idle_blocks: usize,
}

impl Scene {
    pub fn total(&self) -> usize {
        self.instances.len()
    }

    /// Translucent instances, farthest first.
    ///
    /// Sorting is done here rather than on the GPU because the translucent pass has no depth write to
    /// resolve overlaps, so blending order *is* the result. Doing it on the CPU also makes the frame a
    /// pure function of the view, which is what §16.1's determinism requirement asks for — regenerating
    /// the view over an unchanged store must produce byte-identical output.
    pub fn sort_translucent_back_to_front(&mut self, eye: [f32; 3]) {
        let tail = &mut self.instances[self.opaque_count..];
        tail.sort_by(|a, b| {
            let da = depth_sq(a, eye);
            let db = depth_sq(b, eye);
            // Total order: distance, then kind, then position, so two instances at the same distance
            // cannot swap between runs and produce a different frame from identical input.
            db.partial_cmp(&da)
                .unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal)
                .then(a.kind_status[0].cmp(&b.kind_status[0]))
                .then(a.pos_scale[0].partial_cmp(&b.pos_scale[0]).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
                .then(a.pos_scale[2].partial_cmp(&b.pos_scale[2]).unwrap_or(std::cmp::Ordering::Equal))
        });
    }
}

fn depth_sq(i: &Instance, eye: [f32; 3]) -> f32 {
    let dx = i.pos_scale[0] - eye[0];
    let dy = i.pos_scale[1] - eye[1];
    let dz = i.pos_scale[2] - eye[2];
    dx * dx + dy * dy + dz * dz
}

/// Which of the three unit meshes an instance draws. Three, not seventy: §6.1's one-draw-call
/// requirement applies to the figures, and the ground and the blocks are each a single instanced
/// mesh rather than a topology per object.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum MeshId {
    Quad,
    Box,
    Avatar,
}

impl MeshId {
    pub const ALL: [MeshId; 3] = [MeshId::Quad, MeshId::Box, MeshId::Avatar];

    pub fn index(self) -> usize {
        match self {
            MeshId::Quad => 0,
            MeshId::Box => 1,
            MeshId::Avatar => 2,
        }
    }

    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            MeshId::Quad => "quad",
            MeshId::Box => "box",
            MeshId::Avatar => "avatar",
        }
    }
}

/// Which mesh draws a given `kind`. A new kind added to `scene.rs` and the shader without a line here
/// falls to `Box`, which is the safest wrong answer: a box is visible and wrong, while an avatar
/// would silently look like a citizen.
pub fn mesh_of(kind: u32) -> MeshId {
    match kind {
        KIND_TILE | KIND_HOVER | KIND_BRUSH => MeshId::Quad,
        KIND_AVATAR => MeshId::Avatar,
        // `KIND_IDLE` falls through to `Box` deliberately. The safest wrong answer for an idle block is
        // a box: it is visible and wrong, whereas an avatar would silently look like a citizen — which
        // is the one confusion this whole layer is built to make impossible.
        _ => MeshId::Box,
    }
}

/// One instanced draw: the instances, and how many of them write depth.
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, PartialEq)]
pub struct MeshGroup {
    /// Opaque instances first, then translucent. The order is load-bearing: the renderer draws
    /// `[0, opaque_count)` with depth-write and the remainder without, so it never needs to sort or
    /// partition anything itself.
    pub instances: Vec<Instance>,
    pub opaque_count: usize,
}

impl MeshGroup {
    pub fn translucent(&self) -> &[Instance] {
        &self.instances[self.opaque_count..]
    }
}

/// Split a built scene into the three instanced draws.
///
/// Filtering **preserves order**, and the scene's own ordering is opaque-first with the translucent
/// tail sorted — so each group comes out opaque-first too, with no second sort and no chance of the
/// two orderings disagreeing. That is the whole reason the sort in [`Scene::sort_translucent_back_to_front`]
/// operates only on the tail.
pub fn partition(scene: &Scene) -> [MeshGroup; 3] {
    let mut groups: [MeshGroup; 3] = Default::default();
    for group in groups.iter_mut() {
        group.instances.reserve(scene.instances.len() / 3 + 1);
    }
    for (index, instance) in scene.instances.iter().enumerate() {
        let mesh = mesh_of(instance.kind_status[0]);
        let opaque = index < scene.opaque_count;
        groups[mesh.index()].instances.push(*instance);
        if opaque {
            groups[mesh.index()].opaque_count += 1;
        }
    }
    groups
}

/// Tile centre in world units. The grid is centred on the origin so the camera target is `(0,0,0)`
/// regardless of `grid.size` — a view that grew from 24 to 40 tiles would otherwise shift the whole
/// city out from under the camera and the fix would be a magic offset per call site.
pub fn tile_world(tile: [i32; 2], size: i32) -> [f32; 3] {
    let half = size as f32 * 0.5;
    [tile[0] as f32 - half + 0.5, 0.0, tile[1] as f32 - half + 0.5]
}

/// The grid extent in world units, used to place the perimeter.
pub fn grid_extent(size: i32) -> f32 {
    size as f32 * 0.5 + 1.0
}

/// A neutral lightness for `grade_class`, scaled by the grade ladder step. The ladder words come from
/// the store; the *step* is what becomes height, and an unknown word gets the lowest step rather than
/// a middle one — an unrecognised grade must not look like a promotion.
pub fn grade_step(grade_class: &str) -> f32 {
    match grade_class {
        "genesis" => 0.35,
        "apprentice" => 0.6,
        "journeyman" => 0.95,
        "craftsman" => 1.35,
        "master" => 1.8,
        _ => 0.35,
    }
}

/// Build one frame. Pure: same view + same options + same eye => same `Scene`, asserted by test.
/// Which kinds are drawn in the translucent pass — depth-tested but not depth-writing.
///
/// The classification lives here, as a function of the kind, rather than being decided by where an
/// instance happened to be pushed. That distinction matters: an earlier revision set
/// `opaque_count = instances.len()` after building everything, which quietly declared a fog volume and
/// a control column **opaque**. Both carry an alpha well below 1, so the depth buffer would have
/// written them as solid and every citizen standing behind one would have vanished — a bug that only
/// a render shows, and one this function makes impossible to reintroduce by reordering a push.
///
/// Gates are deliberately **not** here. A red arch is a barrier the player is meant to see as solid,
/// and at 0.85 alpha with no depth write it would blend against whatever is behind it on the boundary.
pub fn is_translucent(kind: u32) -> bool {
    // `KIND_IDLE` is translucent so it sorts into the tail and reads as something laid ON the city
    // rather than standing IN it. That is the second of the three properties the block's comment
    // claims, and it is asserted by a test — a claim about appearance with no assertion behind it is
    // how the tint and the sort order drift apart.
    matches!(kind, KIND_VOLUME | KIND_FOG | KIND_HOVER | KIND_BRUSH | KIND_IDLE)
}

/// Build a frame with no recorded-proposal highlight.
///
/// Kept as the common case so the six test call sites and any future caller that is not showing the
/// proposal panel do not have to pass an empty slice — a parameter every caller passes `&[]` to is a
/// parameter that has drifted away from being a *choice*.
pub fn build(view: &CityView, options: &SceneOptions, eye: [f32; 3], pulse: f32) -> Scene {
    build_with_highlights(view, options, eye, pulse, &[])
}

/// Build a frame, optionally highlighting the tiles the view's recorded proposals named.
///
/// The tiles are an argument rather than a field of `SceneOptions` because they are *content*, not a
/// layer switch: folding them in would make this struct non-`Copy` for no gain, and the scene would
/// then be carrying the player's selection state.
pub fn build_with_highlights(
    view: &CityView,
    options: &SceneOptions,
    eye: [f32; 3],
    pulse: f32,
    highlight_tiles: &[[i32; 2]],
) -> Scene {
    let mut scene = Scene::default();
    let size = view.grid.size;
    let extent = grid_extent(size);

    // ---- ground ----------------------------------------------------------------
    // One quad per tile. 24x24 = 576 instances, which is nothing for one instanced draw call and
    // keeps the grid line exactly one tile wide at every zoom (the shader derives it from world space).
    for x in 0..size {
        for z in 0..size {
            scene.instances.push(Instance {
                pos_scale: [tile_world([x, z], size)[0], 0.0, tile_world([x, z], size)[2], 1.0],
                tint: [theme::ACCENT[0] * 0.25, theme::ACCENT[1] * 0.25, theme::ACCENT[2] * 0.25, 1.0],
                kind_status: [KIND_TILE, STATUS_MET, 0, 0],
                params: [1.0, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            });
        }
    }
    scene.counts.tiles = (size * size) as usize;

    // ---- the authorized fiction -------------------------------------------------
    // One low, DESATURATED block per idle job, drawn under its own kind so the shader can mark it as
    // fiction rather than as a building. Three deliberate properties, each of which is a refusal made
    // visible rather than a style choice:
    //
    //   * it is SHORTER than any locus block — height is a function of the kind, never of a yield, so a
    //     fiction cannot grow taller by accreting (`CITY_MAP.md` §4: a lens may never be a lever);
    //   * it is TRANSLUCENT, which is `is_translucent(KIND_IDLE)` being true, so it sorts into the tail
    //     and reads as something laid on the city rather than standing in it;
    //   * it is drawn from `idle_jobs` and never from `loci`, so the civilian count cannot absorb it.
    //
    // The tile comes from the view. This module does not place it: two implementations of one placement
    // would be §6.4's defect, and the producer already owns the deterministic one.
    if options.blocks {
        for job in &view.idle_jobs {
            let [x, z] = job.tile;
            if x < 0 || z < 0 || x >= size || z >= size {
                // Refused rather than clamped, and counted: an idle block outside the grid is a finding
                // about the view, so it is dropped visibly (by its absence from the count) instead of
                // being slid onto an in-bounds tile where it would look like it belonged.
                continue;
            }
            let centre = tile_world([x, z], size);
            scene.instances.push(Instance {
                pos_scale: [centre[0], 0.0, centre[2], 0.62],
                tint: [theme::FICTION[0], theme::FICTION[1], theme::FICTION[2], 0.42],
                // `y` is the status slot and it is **0, which is `STATUS_MET`'s code** — safe only
                // because the shader's `KIND_IDLE` branch never reads `status_colour`, and that branch is
                // asserted not to in `the_idle_shader_branch_never_reads_a_status`.
                //
                // **The first version set `STATUS_UNKNOWN` here while this comment claimed "left 0", and
                // the test caught the disagreement rather than the comment.** `STATUS_UNKNOWN` would have
                // rendered a fiction MAGENTA — the shader's alarm colour for an unrecognised status — so
                // the contradiction was not cosmetic: it would have painted every idle block as an error.
                // A fiction carries no control status, so the honest encoding is the absence of one, and
                // the guarantee that the absence is never read is the shader assertion.
                kind_status: [KIND_IDLE, 0, 0, 0],
                params: [0.45, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            });
            scene.counts.idle_blocks += 1;
        }
    }

    // ---- the recorded-proposal highlight ---------------------------------------
    // One raised quad per tile the view's own recorded proposals highlighted. This is the ONE piece of
    // the view that had no render path at all: `proposals[].highlighted_tiles` was parsed and dropped,
    // so the overlay's note — "the next ingestion pass re-derives which REAL loci fall inside the
    // highlight, and the player sees the overlap" — described a surface that did not exist.
    //
    // Drawn as a translucent slab ABOVE the ground and BELOW the blocks, so it reads as a region of
    // interest rather than as a thing standing in the city. A tile outside the grid is refused rather
    // than clamped: a highlight for a tile the grid does not have is a finding about the view.
    if options.highlights {
        for tile in highlight_tiles {
            let [x, z] = *tile;
            if x < 0 || z < 0 || x >= size || z >= size {
                continue;
            }
            scene.instances.push(Instance {
                pos_scale: [tile_world([x, z], size)[0], 0.02, tile_world([x, z], size)[2], 0.9],
                tint: [
                    theme::NEON[0] * 0.55,
                    theme::NEON[1] * 0.55,
                    theme::NEON[2] * 0.55,
                    0.35,
                ],
                // `y` is the reserved slot and is left 0: the highlight is not a status, and putting a
                // status code here would make an unreviewed proposal look like an evaluated control.
                kind_status: [KIND_TILE, 0, 0, 0],
                params: [1.0, 1.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            });
            scene.counts.highlights += 1;
        }
    }

    // ---- locus blocks and citizens ---------------------------------------------
    // Height comes from the view's own `height` field, which the overlay computed from the grade. This
    // module does not recompute it: two implementations of one derivation is §6.4's defect.
    for locus in &view.loci {
        let centre = tile_world(locus.tile, size);
        if options.blocks {
            let h = (locus.height.max(0.0) * 2.4 + 0.35).max(0.35);
            scene.instances.push(Instance {
                pos_scale: [centre[0], 0.0, centre[2], 0.85],
                tint: [0.10, 0.24, 0.34, 1.0],
                kind_status: [KIND_BLOCK, STATUS_MET, 0, 0],
                params: [h, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            });
            scene.counts.blocks += 1;
        }

        if options.avatars {
            // A multi-civilian locus is **fog by doctrine** (§30.2, "multi-civilian jobs"). It is
            // rendered as a single dashed placeholder rather than several figures, because drawing N
            // citizens would be the surface inventing N-1 of them.
            let (kind, status, flags) = if locus.multi_civilian {
                (KIND_FOG, STATUS_NOT_EVALUABLE, 1.0)
            } else {
                (KIND_AVATAR, STATUS_MET, 0.0)
            };
            scene.instances.push(Instance {
                pos_scale: [centre[0], locus.height.max(0.0) * 2.4 + 0.35, centre[2], 1.0],
                tint: [
                    theme::SILVER_BASE[0],
                    theme::SILVER_BASE[1],
                    theme::SILVER_BASE[2],
                    1.0,
                ],
                kind_status: [kind, status, 0, 0],
                params: [0.0, flags, 0.0, 0.0],
            });
            // Counted by what was actually emitted, not by the loop that emitted it. An earlier revision
            // incremented `citizens` unconditionally, so a multi-civilian locus — which emits a fog
            // placeholder and no figure at all — was reported to the HUD as a citizen.
            if locus.multi_civilian {
                scene.counts.fogged_loci += 1;
            } else {
                scene.counts.citizens += 1;
            }
        }
    }

    // ---- fog of war and out-of-scope walls -------------------------------------
    for region in &view.regions {
        let [x0, y0, x1, y1] = region.rect;
        // `rect` is inclusive tile coordinates; a zero-width rect is still a real one-tile region.
        let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) as f32 * 0.5, (y0 + y1) as f32 * 0.5);
        let w = (x1 - x0).abs() as f32 + 1.0;
        let d = (y1 - y0).abs() as f32 + 1.0;
        let wx = cx - size as f32 * 0.5 + 0.5;
        let wz = cz - size as f32 * 0.5 + 0.5;

        match region.kind.as_str() {
            "fog" if options.fog => {
                scene.instances.push(Instance {
                    pos_scale: [wx, 0.0, wz, w.max(d)],
                    tint: [0.5, 0.52, 0.56, 1.0],
                    kind_status: [KIND_FOG, STATUS_NOT_EVALUABLE, 0, 0],
                    params: [0.9, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
                });
                scene.counts.fog += 1;
            }
            "wall" if options.walls => {
                // A wall is an ABSENCE, and its extent is the region's own rect — scaled on Z too, so
                // it reads as a boundary rather than a post. The shader draws it near-black.
                scene.instances.push(Instance {
                    pos_scale: [wx, 0.0, wz, w],
                    tint: [0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0],
                    kind_status: [KIND_WALL, STATUS_NOT_EVALUABLE, 0, 0],
                    params: [2.6, 0.0, d / w.max(1.0), 0.0],
                });
                scene.counts.walls += 1;
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    }

    // ---- never-granted gates, on the boundary ----------------------------------
    // §6.4 places them "on the grid boundary". Which boundary tile each gets is this module's choice,
    // and it is a *presentation* choice with no doctrine meaning — evenly spaced along the near edge,
    // which is the edge the isometric camera looks across.
    if options.gates {
        let n = view.never_granted.len().max(1);
        for (i, _) in view.never_granted.iter().enumerate() {
            let t = (i as f32 + 0.5) / n as f32;
            let x = -extent + t * extent * 2.0;
            scene.instances.push(Instance {
                pos_scale: [x, 0.0, extent, 0.6],
                tint: [1.0, 0.05, 0.15, 1.0],
                kind_status: [KIND_GATE, STATUS_FAILED, 0, 0],
                params: [1.5, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            });
            scene.counts.gates += 1;
        }
    }

    // ---- decision monuments, on the perimeter arc ------------------------------
    if options.monuments {
        for (i, monument) in view.monuments.iter().enumerate() {
            // The HIG arc (SL-06): monuments arranged along a 120-degree arc facing the default
            // camera, which is §9.1's own placement rule rather than an aesthetic choice here.
            let a = -std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_3
                + (i as f32 / (view.monuments.len().max(2) - 1) as f32) * (2.0 * std::f32::consts::FRAC_PI_3);
            let r = extent + 2.2;
            // `answered` is the store's word for "this question is settled" — C05 and C09.
            let status = if monument.state == "answered" { STATUS_MET } else { STATUS_UNKNOWN };
            scene.instances.push(Instance {
                pos_scale: [(a.cos() * r), 0.0, (a.sin() * r), 0.55],
                tint: [theme::ACCENT[0], theme::ACCENT[1], theme::ACCENT[2], 1.0],
                kind_status: [KIND_NODE, status, 0, 0],
                params: [1.9, 0.0, 0.0, 0.0],
            });
            scene.counts.monuments += 1;
        }
    }

    // ---- control columns, on the far perimeter ---------------------------------
    // See the module doc: a column, not a volume, because the view carries no extent for a control.
    if options.volumes {
        for (i, control) in view.controls.iter().enumerate() {
            let t = (i as f32 + 0.5) / view.controls.len().max(1) as f32;
            let x = -extent + t * extent * 2.0;
            let status = status_code(&control.mechanical_status);
            scene.instances.push(Instance {
                pos_scale: [x, 0.0, -extent, 0.35],
                tint: [
                    theme::status_rgb_f(&control.mechanical_status)[0] * 0.55,
                    theme::status_rgb_f(&control.mechanical_status)[1] * 0.55,
                    theme::status_rgb_f(&control.mechanical_status)[2] * 0.55,
                    1.0,
                ],
                kind_status: [KIND_VOLUME, status, 0, 0],
                // A FAILED column carries the pulse value; the shader applies it only for FAILED, so
                // reduced motion is honoured in exactly one place.
                params: [2.2, pulse, 0.0, 0.0],
            });
            scene.counts.volumes += 1;
        }
    }

    // One stable partition at the end, rather than trusting the push order above. The loops interleave
    // opaque and translucent kinds — the region loop emits a fog volume and then a wall — so "opaque
    // first" cannot be maintained by ordering the pushes, and pretending otherwise is how the fog
    // became solid. `Iterator::partition` preserves the relative order of both halves, so the frame
    // stays a pure function of the view.
    let (opaque, translucent): (Vec<Instance>, Vec<Instance>) = scene
        .instances
        .drain(..)
        .partition(|instance| !is_translucent(instance.kind_status[0]));
    scene.opaque_count = opaque.len();
    scene.instances = opaque;
    scene.instances.extend(translucent);

    scene.sort_translucent_back_to_front(eye);
    scene
}

/// The hover/brush overlay for the tile under the cursor, and the current drag rectangle.
///
/// Separate from [`build`] because it changes every frame while the base scene does not — rebuilding
/// 600 instances to move one highlight would be the surface spending its budget on nothing.
pub fn overlay(bounds: Option<([i32; 2], [i32; 2])>, kind: &str, colour: [f32; 3], size: i32, pulse: f32) -> Vec<Instance> {
    let Some((a, b)) = bounds else { return Vec::new() };
    let (x0, x1) = (a[0].min(b[0]), a[0].max(b[0]));
    let (y0, y1) = (a[1].min(b[1]), a[1].max(b[1]));
    let (cx, cz) = ((x0 + x1) as f32 * 0.5, (y0 + y1) as f32 * 0.5);
    let w = (x1 - x0) as f32 + 1.0;
    let d = (y1 - y0) as f32 + 1.0;
    let half = size as f32 * 0.5;
    vec![Instance {
        pos_scale: [cx - half + 0.5, 0.0, cz - half + 0.5, w.max(d)],
        tint: [colour[0], colour[1], colour[2], 1.0],
        kind_status: [if kind == "brush" { KIND_BRUSH } else { KIND_HOVER }, STATUS_MET, 0, 0],
        params: [0.06, pulse, d / w.max(1.0), 0.0],
    }]
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    /// A view with one citizen, one fog region, one wall — built by hand so the tests do not depend on
    /// the live store's current contents (which change as the season progresses).
    fn view() -> CityView {
        // The fixture mirrors the REAL `seasons/plans/view.json`, field for field, including the ones
        // a summary would be tempted to flatten. Two shapes were got wrong on the first attempt and
        // both matter:
        //
        //   `never_granted` is a list of OBJECTS (`action`/`kanji`/`citation`), not a list of action
        //   strings — the kanji is the label the surface draws, so a string-only fixture would let the
        //   scene tests pass against a view the real reader rejects.
        //   `governor_base_version` is the stamp object, not an integer. It carries `versions[]`
        //   because C19 is about *every* ticket carrying one, and a fixture with a bare int would
        //   never exercise the coverage the HUD reports.
        //
        // An earlier draft used `governor_stamp`, a key the real view does not have. Serde ignores
        // unknown fields, so that fixture would have parsed while silently testing a view with the
        // required field missing from it. `the_fixture_carries_every_key_the_real_view_has` now holds
        // that class of drift, because this comment could not: the view grew three keys and the fixture
        // went stale in silence, exactly as the paragraph above warns and could not prevent.
        crate::city::parse_view_for_test(view_json()).expect("fixture parses")
    }

    /// The fixture's raw JSON, so a test can compare its KEY SET against the real view's.
    ///
    /// Split out from `view()` because `CityView` is deserialize-only — a round-trip through a serialised
    /// value is not available, and adding `Serialize` to the view would mean writing bytes the producer
    /// never writes, i.e. asserting against a shape that does not exist. Comparing the two JSON documents
    /// is the comparison that is actually about the artifacts.
