    // A `let` array of constants is a const-expression here, so `offsets[i]` has no defined value
    // even though `i` only ever runs 1..4. Unrolling is not a workaround for a compiler limitation:
    // a separable kernel is 18 taps, and 18 constant taps beat 18 dynamic ones. The weights stay
    // written out where they are read, so the kernel can be checked against its own definition.
    let step = post.dir * post.texel;
    var sum = textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv).rgb * 0.227027;

    let o1 = step * 1.0;
    sum += (textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv + o1).rgb
          + textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv - o1).rgb) * 0.194594;

    let o2 = step * 2.0;
    sum += (textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv + o2).rgb
          + textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv - o2).rgb) * 0.121621;

    let o3 = step * 3.0;
    sum += (textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv + o3).rgb
          + textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv - o3).rgb) * 0.054054;

    let o4 = step * 4.0;
    sum += (textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv + o4).rgb
          + textureSample(src_tex, src_samp, in.uv - o4).rgb) * 0.016216;

    return vec4<f32>(sum, 1.0);
}

@fragment
fn fs_composite(in: FullscreenOut) -> @location(0) vec4<f32> {
    let scene = textureSample(hdr_tex, post_samp, in.uv).rgb;
    let bloom = textureSample(bloom_tex, post_samp, in.uv).rgb;

    // Additive glow. `3DUI.MD` §13.2 pins the composite at 0.4; it is a uniform rather than a literal
    // so the value is registered in one place and a test can assert it.
    let lit = scene + bloom * post.intensity;

    // Tone map (Reinhard with a white point). The reason the scene pass is float: without this the
    // neon rim and the specular streak both clip to flat white and the material reads as plastic.
    let mapped = lit / (lit + vec3<f32>(1.0));

    // Linear out. egui's target format is sRGB, so the hardware applies the transfer curve — applying
    // it here as well would double-correct and wash the whole scene out.
    return vec4<f32>(mapped, 1.0);
}

// # What this file does NOT implement, stated rather than implied
//
// `3DUI.MD` §13.1 lists fourteen passes. This file implements five of them plus the paint pass:
// sky, geometry, bright-pass, separable blur, composite. Missing, and why:
//
//   - **Glass panel refraction** (§13.1 pass 13). The HUD is drawn by egui *after* this pass, so a
//     screen-space refraction of the panels would have to sample a target that does not exist yet.
//     The glass look is carried by the panels' own alpha and blur instead, which is what egui can
//     actually do.
//   - **A separate UI-compositing pass** (§13.1 pass 14), because egui IS that pass.
//   - **The authority-path ribbons with animated particles** (§6.3). They are geometry, not shading,
//     and the path data is not in the derived view — inventing it in the renderer would be the
//     surface deciding something the store did not say.
//
// Bloom is one blur pair at quarter resolution rather than a mip chain. That is a real quality
// difference and it is recorded in the README rather than described as the full pipeline.
```

#### `rust-ui/rust-toolchain.toml`

```toml
[toolchain]
channel = "stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc"
```

#### `rust-ui/Cargo.toml`

```toml
[package]
name = "laya-cua-ui"
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2021"

[dependencies]
# `wgpu` ONLY — `default-features = false` is load-bearing, not tidiness. eframe's default enables
# `glow`, and a binary carrying both renderers can fall back to the CPU path silently: the surface
# would build, run, and not be the thing 3DUI.MD section 13 specifies. With `glow` absent there is no
# fallback to make, so "is this the GPU pipeline?" is answered by the manifest rather than by a
# runtime flag someone can forget to set.
eframe = { version = "0.29", default-features = false, features = [
    # HIG accessibility surface (focus, screen-reader roles). The brief asks for HIG, and §12.4 makes
    # WCAG 2.2 AA a requirement, so this is a requirement rather than a nicety.
    "accesskit",
    "default_fonts",
    "wgpu",
] }
# The derived civilian view is JSON, and `serde_json` is already in the local cargo cache, so the
# panel parses the same file the validator wrote instead of re-implementing the rules in Rust. A
# second implementation of claim strength and the ladder refusals is the one thing most likely to
# disagree with the first, and a UI that disagreed with the validator would be worse than none.
serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1"
# Vertex and uniform structs must be plain-old-data to be uploaded. Written by hand this is
# `unsafe impl` blocks whose correctness nothing checks; `Pod`/`Zeroable` are derived instead.
bytemuck = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }

[dev-dependencies]
# The offscreen render test blocks on wgpu's async adapter request, and `pollster` is not in the local
# cargo cache while `futures-lite` is — so the dependency that already resolves wins over the one that
# does not. This is a test-only need; the shipping binary never blocks on an adapter.
futures-lite = "2"
# CPU-only WGSL parsing, so shader correctness is checkable with NO GPU present. That is the
# mechanical half of verification (rule 83); the offscreen render is the oracle half.
naga = { version = "22", features = ["wgsl-in"] }
```

#### `rust-ui/README.md`

```text
# laya / cua Rust UI

A small native desktop chat surface built with `eframe`/`egui`, following the authority boundary in `AGENTS.md`. The UI reloads and searches `AGENTS.md` for every request instead of stuffing the whole document into laya/cua's context window. On Windows, the project pins the installed MSVC Rust toolchain because the GNU toolchain requires a separate MinGW `dlltool.exe`:

- **laya / cua · chat** is the direct conversational mode: messages go to `LAYA_COMMAND` and responses appear in the same chat stream like a model conversation.
- **cua · act** does **not** call cua when a message is sent. It records a pending proposal.
- The conversational mode may discuss or propose work, but only an explicit approval invokes `CUA_COMMAND`.
- A human must review and click **Approve & run cua** before `CUA_COMMAND` is invoked.
- Rejecting a proposal records the refusal and never calls cua.
- The UI exposes the retrieved compatible features, gates/endpoints, commands, source path, selected sections, and exact 1-based AGENTS.md line ranges.
- Each user message becomes a ticket and automatically runs a visible forward pass (ticket → AGENTS.md grounding → Laya understanding → CUA proposal) and backward pass (reload → authorization → verification or refusal).
- A live activity feed records REQUEST, READ, DISPATCH, PROPOSE, RELOAD, APPROVE, RESULT, and REFUSED events with the exact file location used by each event.
- The bounded context pack includes the request plus applicable authority, evidence, doctor, and authorization rules.
- The UI is only the approval surface; a production broker must still verify identity, policy, action hashes, expiry, and single use.
- The CUA bridge uses PyAutoGUI with its fail-safe enabled; model-generated computer actions are stopped if the pointer reaches a screen corner or the adapter reports an error.

## The City tab

`City (isometric)` renders `seasons/plans/view.json` — the overlay's derived view, written by
`python overlay.py view` — as a playable isometric city. It is the surface `3DUI.MD` specifies, built to
that document's phases **B1–B4 and B6–B9**. Everything it draws has a doctrine source; the projection
parameters (`tilt`, `rotation`, `size`) are read from `view.grid` rather than hardcoded, and the four
billing-basis **names** and the C19 governor stamp arrive in the view, because a surface that spelled
doctrine for itself would be the exact defect section 31.1 names.

| Input | Action |
|---|---|
| hover | tooltip: the tile, and the region it is in with that region's citation |
| click | select a tile; with a service node tool active, propose one there |
| drag | propose a zone over the rectangle |
| `F` `G` `C` `L` | fog · residual risks · control volumes · labels |
| `Commit to plan store` | write the pending proposals to `seasons/plans/pending.json` |

**What this surface may never do, and the tests that hold it.** It *reports*; it never *adjudicates*.
A control's `mechanical_status` is copied from the view, never computed — and `status_colour` has an
explicit `Unknown` arm, so an unrecognised status renders as unknown rather than defaulting to green
(the same rule as section 9.7's no-default-to-PUBLIC, applied to a colour).

What it *is* allowed to do is refuse **spatially**: `spatial_verdict` tests a tile against the `regions`
the view already carries, which 3DUI.MD §4.3 assigns to the surface outright. That verdict is named
`SpatialVerdict`, carries the words "spatial only", and the disclaimer is painted **on the canvas** —
because the canvas is what a screenshot shows, and the governor's own verdict comes from
`python overlay.py adjudicate`.

Two consequences that are easy to get backwards and are both asserted:

- A **multi-civilian locus renders as fog**, not as a building. Whose income, whose evidence, whose
grade is an open question (§30.2), and drawing it solid would answer that question with geometry.
- The **risk layer R7–R11 is never folded into the controls C9–C20** (3DUI.MD §7.2). A test asserts the
  view keeps them in separate fields, so concatenating them would be a contract change rather than a
  rendering choice.

The one write path is the plan store, and it is pinned by a test: `seasons/plans/pending.json`, marked
`authoritative: false` and `adjudicated: false`, appended and never overwritten. Nothing here authorises
anything; only a governed merge promotes a plan into doctrine (rule 60).

### What is NOT built, stated rather than implied

The honest limit, and it is a real one: this is an **egui painter** doing true isometric projection, not
the **wgpu/WGSL pipeline** `3DUI.MD` §13 specifies. There is no bloom pass, no glass refraction, no
aurora ribbon, no instanced mesh and no WASM build (phase B10 and §13). Two reasons, not one:

* **The pillar ranks legibility above spectacle.** `3DUI.MD` P3 is "legibility over spectacle" and P6 is
  "no invented civilian facts". A painter satisfies both; bloom satisfies neither.
* **A GPU pass cannot be verified here.** Rule 36 says verify the **surface**, not the API behind it, and
  a shader pipeline nobody can look at is precisely the artifact that gets declared done on the strength
  of its own build log. The projection and the layout are pure functions with tests instead — including
  a round-trip over all 576 tiles that would catch the drift a shader would hide.

`3DUI.MD` §18 budgets ~32 working days for all thirteen phases. What exists is the readable, tested and
playable half. `ticket_civilian_overlay_005` records that scope honestly rather than closing.

## The Civilians tab

The header carries two surfaces, and they are separate deliberately: they read different stores, and a
panel that showed a derived view beside a live dispatch would invite reading one as evidence for the
other. `Civilians` never dispatches anything, which is why it is a **tab** rather than a third
`AgentMode` — every other `AgentMode` value can run a command, and putting a read-only surface in that
enum would make the two indistinguishable.

It renders `seasons/civilians/analysis.json`, the derived view written by `python civilians.py analyze`,
found by walking up from the executable or the manifest directory. **It does not re-implement any rule
in Rust**: claim strength, the ladder refusals and the two passes are computed by the validator, and a
second implementation of them is the thing most likely to disagree with the first. A UI that disagreed
with the validator would be worse than no UI.

What it shows, and why each one is on screen:

- **The derived-view warning**, with the store digest, because a view that presented itself as the
  store would be the §2.6 defect. Reload re-reads the file; it does not re-run the analysis.
- **The founding instruments** — each with its artifact, its **live hash check** (the view re-reads the
  bytes, so a stale badge is a finding rather than a cached field), its ladder and variant, its
  `grants_authority` value read from the record rather than asserted by the panel, its clause
  report, and per clause the rule it maps onto or the reason it is `UNMAPPED`.
- **Three provenance shapes, rendered differently**, because collapsing them is how a source nobody
  checked comes to look like a source with one variant. A named relay is a chain that continues; a relay
  of `NOT_STATED` is a chain that **stops**, shown with the date the absence was verified; and an
  unestablished variant count says which check **cannot be applied** rather than showing a zero. The
  field is `Option<usize>` for exactly that reason — it was `usize` with a default, which turned a
  `null` into `0` and would have rendered an unchecked source as a source with no variants.
- **Jobs, tickets, income, and promotions**, each with the control that governs it: a ticket records
  the governor version it ran under, and income is verified by a Governor record because a civilian
  cannot certify its own income.
- **Claims** with the computed level, the reason a line was withheld, and the assertion that was
  discarded — an asserted strength is reported, never honoured.
- **Both passes**, so a blocked arrow and a broken chain are visible rather than summarised.
- **The controls, as two statuses** (mechanical and identity), because rule 100 says they are different
  questions and one status for both is the defect.

A document that is not the view is an error, not an empty population. Note what that costs: every field
is `#[serde(default)]` and serde also accepts a JSON **array** by filling defaults, so a parse-error
test accepts `[]` happily. The reader therefore checks the marker the view itself carries
(`derived_view: true`), and `civilians::tests` asserts both facts — the guard, and the behaviour of the
parse that made the guard necessary.

Both adapters receive the prompt on stdin and return their response on stdout. The project-local `.venv` is the default runtime: chat uses `laya_adapter.py`, which loads `convaiinnovations/laya` and returns typed JSON understanding; approved actions use `cua_adapter.py`, which drives the installed CUA agent against the prepared local Ollama Qwen2.5-VL model. `LAYA_COMMAND` and `CUA_COMMAND` remain optional overrides; `CUA_MODEL` can override the local model.

## Run

The prepared runtime lives in `.venv` and is reproducible from `requirements.txt`:

```bash
.venv/Scripts/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
cargo run
```

The included `rust-toolchain.toml` selects `stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc` automatically. The equivalent explicit command is `cargo +stable-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc run`.

Example adapter configuration:

```bash
# Optional: override the prepared local CUA model.
export CUA_MODEL="ollama/hf.co/ggml-org/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M"
cargo run
```

The commands are started without a shell, so the executable and whitespace-separated arguments are passed directly. `Ctrl+Enter` sends the current message.
```

#### `migrate.py`

```python
"""Migrate AGENTS.md into the doctrine store, and rebuild it from the store afterwards.

    cd seasons/impl && python migrate.py status     # derived? drifted fragments? stale appendices?
    cd seasons/impl && python migrate.py check      # verify the partition, write NOTHING
    cd seasons/impl && python migrate.py migrate    # the one-time migration
    cd seasons/impl && python migrate.py generate   # regenerate the generated sections, then rebuild
    cd seasons/impl && python migrate.py rebuild    # assemble the store and rewrite the file

THE PRACTICE THIS ENFORCES. Rule 77 forbids hand-editing the god file, and after the migration that is
executable rather than aspirational: doctrine lives in `seasons/doctrine/frag_NN.json` and the file is
`rebuild` output. Editing a fragment is still a hand-edit of the SOURCE — the tool does not pretend
otherwise — so `status` REPORTS which fragments have been edited since the last rebuild.

AND TWO OF THE SECTIONS ARE NOT WRITTEN AT ALL. §23 (the record) and §24 (the implementation) declare a
`generated_by`, and `generate` re-derives them from the store and the source tree. `status` reports them
separately from hand-drift, because a stale generated section and an edited hand-written section are
different defects: the first means the file disagrees with reality, the second means someone changed the
doctrine.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import godplan as g
from godplan import appendix, doctrine
from godplan.canonical import sha256_hex


def _load_record(fragment_id: str) -> dict:
    path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{fragment_id}.json"
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _drifted() -> list[str]:
    """Hand-written fragments whose body no longer matches their recorded block hash.

    `block_sha256` describes the CURRENT body and is refreshed by `rebuild`, so this means "edited since
    the last rebuild" rather than "edited since the migration". The first version recorded the hash once
    at migration time, which would have flagged the same fragment forever after a legitimate rebuild — a
    drift report that never clears is one nobody reads.
    """
    out: list[str] = []
    for frag in g.load_fragments():
        recorded = _load_record(frag.fragment_id).get("block_sha256")
        if recorded and recorded != sha256_hex(frag.body.encode("utf-8")):
            out.append(frag.fragment_id)
    return out


def _stale_generated() -> list[str]:
    """Generated fragments whose body is not what their generator currently produces."""
    out: list[str] = []
    for frag in g.load_fragments():
        record = _load_record(frag.fragment_id)
        name = record.get("generated_by")
        if not name:
            continue
        generator = appendix.GENERATORS.get(name)
        if generator is None:
            out.append(f"{frag.fragment_id} (UNKNOWN GENERATOR {name!r})")
            continue
        if generator() != frag.body:
            out.append(frag.fragment_id)
    return out


def _regenerate() -> list[str]:
    """Rewrite every generated fragment from its generator. Returns the ids whose BODY changed."""
    changed: list[str] = []
    for frag in g.load_fragments():
        path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{frag.fragment_id}.json"
        record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        name = record.get("generated_by")
        if not name:
            continue
        generator = appendix.GENERATORS.get(name)
        if generator is None:
            raise SystemExit(f"   fragment {frag.fragment_id} names an unknown generator {name!r}; refusing")
        body = generator()
        if body != record.get("body"):
            changed.append(frag.fragment_id)
        record["body"] = body
        record["section"] = body.split("\n", 1)[0][3:]
        record["block_sha256"] = sha256_hex(body.encode("utf-8"))
        record["lines"] = f"0-{body.count(chr(10))}  (generated; span is indicative only)"
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
    return changed


def _refresh() -> None:
    """After a rebuild, record the current body hash and re-derive the line spans.

    The migration-time hash is PRESERVED as `migrated_block_sha256` rather than overwritten, so an edit is
    never erased from the record — it stops being *pending* and starts being *history*.
    """
    offset = 0
    for frag in g.load_fragments():
        path = doctrine.DOCTRINE_DIR / f"{frag.fragment_id}.json"
        record = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        current = sha256_hex(frag.body.encode("utf-8"))
        prior = record.get("block_sha256")
        if prior not in (None, current):
            record.setdefault("migrated_block_sha256", prior)
        record["block_sha256"] = current
        if not record.get("generated_by"):
            count = frag.body.count("\n")
            record["lines"] = f"{offset}-{offset + count}"
        offset += frag.body.count("\n")
        path.write_text(json.dumps(record, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


def _status(path: Path) -> int:
    audit = g.audit_current_god_file()
    frags = g.load_fragments()
    drifted = _drifted()
    stale = _stale_generated()

    print(f"   file          {path}")
    print(f"   bytes         {audit.bytes}")
    print(f"   DERIVED       {audit.is_derived}  — {audit.reason}")
    print(f"   fragments     {len(frags)}")
    print(f"   hand-edited since the last rebuild: {drifted or 'none'}")
    print(f"   generated sections out of date:     {stale or 'none'}")
    if drifted:
        print("   Those fragments were hand-edited. Run `rebuild` to propagate them, then RECORD it:")
        print("   a fragment edit is still a hand-edit of the source, and the tool says so out loud.")
    if stale:
        print("   Those sections disagree with their sources. Run `generate`. A generated section that")
        print("   is out of date is worse than a missing one, because it reads as current.")
    return 0


def _rebuild(path: Path) -> int:
    before = path.read_bytes()
    frags = g.load_fragments()
    drifted = _drifted()
    result = g.assemble(frags)
    path.write_bytes(result.output)
    _refresh()
    print(f"   REBUILD from {len(frags)} fragments")
    print(f"   propagated    {drifted or 'no fragment had drifted'}")
    print(f"   before  {sha256_hex(before)[:16]}…  {len(before)} bytes")
    print(f"   after   {result.content_hash[:16]}…  {len(result.output)} bytes")
    print(f"   changed {result.content_hash != sha256_hex(before)}")
    print(f"   drift after rebuild:  {_drifted() or 'none'}")
    print(f"   stale after rebuild:  {_stale_generated() or 'none'}")
    audit = g.audit_current_god_file()
    print(f"   DERIVED {audit.is_derived}  — {audit.reason}")
    return 0


def _generate(path: Path) -> int:
    print("   GENERATE  the sections that declare a generator")
    changed = _regenerate()
    print(f"   rebuilt from sources: {changed or 'nothing changed — the appendices already match'}")
    return _rebuild(path)


def _check(path: Path) -> int:
    raw = path.read_bytes()
    part = doctrine.partition(raw.decode("utf-8"))
    same = "".join(b.body for b in part.blocks) == raw.decode("utf-8")
    print(f"   file              {path}")
    print(f"   bytes             {len(raw)}")
    print(f"   lines             {part.line_count}")
    print(f"   blocks            {len(part.blocks)}  ({len(part.sections)} sections + preamble)")
    print(f"   preamble bytes    {part.preamble_bytes}")
    print(f"   fence lines       {part.fence_lines}  balanced={part.fence_balanced}")
    print(f"   phantom headings  {part.phantom_headings}  (inside fences, correctly ignored)")
    print(f"   reassembles       {same}")
    print("   nothing written — this was a check")
    return 0 if same and part.fence_balanced else 1


def _migrate(path: Path) -> int:
    report = doctrine.migrate(path)
    print("   MIGRATION")
    for key in ("god_file", "fragments", "sections", "legacy_bytes", "derived_bytes", "delta_bytes"):
        print(f"   {key:18s} {report[key]}")
    print(f"   legacy_sha256      {str(report['legacy_sha256'])[:16]}…")
    print(f"   derived_sha256     {str(report['derived_sha256'])[:16]}…")
    print(f"   doctrine lossless  {report['doctrine_lossless']}")
    return 0


MODES = {
    "check": _check,
    "migrate": _migrate,
    "status": _status,
    "rebuild": _rebuild,
    "generate": _generate,
}


def main(argv: list[str]) -> int:
    mode = argv[0] if argv else "status"
    if mode not in MODES:
        print(f"   usage: python migrate.py [{'|'.join(MODES)}]")
        return 2
    return MODES[mode](g.reconstruct.GOD_FILE)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main(sys.argv[1:]))
```

#### `run.py`

```python
"""godplan CLI — report the current state of the plan.

    python run.py

Prints four things, in the order the god file would ask for them:

  1. the store's integrity report   — rules 31, 65, 74, and the section 8 taxonomy
  2. the vocabulary collision report — the round-5 bare-token rule, with the collision it found
  3. the invariants                  — rule 55, shown as actual REFUSALS, both directions
  4. the derivation status           — rule 77, and whether the agents file is a derived object yet

Nothing here writes to the store. It reports.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import sys
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import godplan as g
from godplan import axes, authority, reconstruct as recon

RULE = "-" * 78


def report_store() -> None:
    print("1. STORE INTEGRITY")
    store = g.Store.load()
    store.validate()
    c = store.counts()
    print(f"   records={c['records']}  events={c['events']}  kinds={c['event_kinds']}  defects={c['defects']}")
    by_sev: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
    for d in store.defects:
        by_sev.setdefault(d.severity, []).append(f"{d.where}: {d.what}")
    if not by_sev:
        print("   no defects")
    for sev in ("blocking", "medium", "low"):
        for msg in by_sev.get(sev, []):
            print(f"   [{sev:8}] {msg}")


def report_vocabulary() -> None:
    print(f"\n{RULE}\n2. VOCABULARY — the bare-token rule")
    collisions = axes.ambiguous_tokens()
    if collisions:
        print(f"   DEFECT: {len(collisions)} token(s) claimed by more than one ladder")
        for token, kinds in sorted(collisions.items()):
            print(f"     {token!r:6} claimed by {', '.join(k.value for k in kinds)}")
        print("   Section 19.1 enumerates THREE axes; section 19.2 adds a fourth ladder, and")
        print("   the two graders share the tokens A/B/C/D while meaning different things:")
        print("   evidence grade A is the STRONGEST, unit grade A sits BELOW S.")
    for token in ("A", "gold"):
        try:
            axes.refuse_bare(token)
            print(f"   {token!r} was accepted — the rule is not working")
        except g.RefusedBareToken as exc:
            print(f"   refuse_bare({token!r}) -> {exc}")


def report_invariants() -> None:
    print(f"\n{RULE}\n3. INVARIANTS — shown as refusals, because that is what they are")
    checks = [
        ("advance(SSS)", lambda: g.Unit(g.Grade.SSS).advance()),
        ("graduate(A)", lambda: g.Unit(g.Grade.A).graduate()),
        ("certification = max(evidence)", lambda: axes.prohibited_max_certification({"x": g.EvidenceGrade.A})),
        ("gate.as_percentage()", lambda: g.ProceduralGate({}, "p").as_percentage()),
        ("evidence grade vs tier", lambda: axes.refuse_interchange(g.EvidenceGrade.A, g.CertificationTier.gold)),
        ("evidence grade vs unit grade", lambda: axes.refuse_interchange(g.EvidenceGrade.A, g.Grade.A)),
    ]
    for label, fn in checks:
        try:
            fn()
            print(f"   {label:32} ACCEPTED  <-- should have been refused")
        except g.Refused as exc:
            print(f"   {label:32} REFUSED   {type(exc).__name__}")
    # and the one that must be ACCEPTED
    u = g.Unit(g.Grade.SSS)
    u.graduate()
    print(f"   {'graduate(SSS)':32} ACCEPTED  -> status={u.status.value}")


def report_derivation() -> None:
    print(f"\n{RULE}\n4. DERIVATION — rule 77, is the agents file a derived object?")
    audit = recon.audit_current_god_file()
    print(f"   file      {audit.path}")
    print(f"   bytes     {audit.bytes}")
    print(f"   hash      {audit.content_hash[:16]}…")
    print(f"   DERIVED   {audit.is_derived}")
    print(f"   reason    {audit.reason}")
    real = g.load_fragments()
    real_result = recon.assemble(real)
    print(f"\n   The REAL doctrine store: {len(real)} fragments, rebuilt and compared to the file:")
    print(f"   fragments          {real_result.fragment_count}")
    print(f"   rebuild == file    {real_result.output == recon.GOD_FILE.read_bytes()}")
    print(f"   order-independent  {recon.verify_reconstruction(real, real_result.content_hash)}")
    print("\n   And the engine on a two-fragment sample, to show the determinism test itself:")
    sample = [
        g.DoctrineFragment("frag_b", 2, "Two", "## Two\nsecond body\n"),
        g.DoctrineFragment("frag_a", 1, "One", "## One\nfirst body\n"),
    ]
    forward = recon.assemble(sample)
    reverse = recon.assemble(list(reversed(sample)))
    print(f"   assemble(forward)  {forward.content_hash[:16]}…")
    print(f"   assemble(reversed) {reverse.content_hash[:16]}…")
    print(f"   deterministic      {forward.content_hash == reverse.content_hash}")
    print(f"   delete->rebuild    {recon.verify_reconstruction(sample, forward.content_hash)}")


def report_authority() -> None:
    print(f"\n{RULE}\n5. AUTHORITY — and the part that is NOT enforced")
    print(f"   {authority.PROCEDURAL}")
    led = g.Ledger()
    a = g.Artifact(
        artifact_id="artifact_1832",
        producer="investigator-07",
        provenance=("https://example.invalid/x",),
        certification_tier=g.CertificationTier.gold,
        reconstruction_passed=True,
    )
    print(f"   consider_for_merge(gold)   {authority.consider_for_merge(a)}   (consideration, not authority)")
    try:
        authority.authorize_merge(a, governor_actor=a.producer, governor_authenticated=True, ledger=led)
    except g.MergeRefused as exc:
        print(f"   authorize_merge(self)      REFUSED  {exc}")
    rec = authority.authorize_merge(
        a, governor_actor="governor-01", governor_authenticated=False, ledger=led
    )
    print(f"   authorize_merge(governor)  ALLOWED  identity_is_claim={rec.identity_is_claim}")
    print(f"   ledger chain verifies      {led.verify_chain()}")


if __name__ == "__main__":
    print("godplan — implementation of the plan in AGENTS.md\n" + RULE)
    report_store()
    report_vocabulary()
    report_invariants()
    report_derivation()
    report_authority()
    print(f"\n{RULE}\nTests: python -m unittest test_godplan")
```

#### `silver.py`

```python
"""silver.py — §22.2's two-part verification, run at the SILVER bar.

PART 1  PRESENCE       a mechanical comparison over RAW FETCHED BYTES. No model. Grade B.
PART 2  CLASSIFICATION laya, as a `choice` question with NAMED CRITERIA. Grade C, with the
                       probability recorded AS the strength — which §7.3 requires and which a
                       generative model's `CONFIRMED` cannot supply.

WHY THIS FILE WAS REWRITTEN. The first version ran ONE call convention and it was the wrong one:
it passed a plain string with the question saying "this passage", which §25.7 later measured at
accuracy 0.500 / ECE 0.4102, against 0.625 / 0.2385 for the dict-state form whose key is
backticked in the instructions. `§25.7` records that the first run's 0.375 was "partly my error".
**A calibration figure produced by a mis-called instrument is not a measurement of the instrument**,
so the convention is now DATA with all three variants scored on the same labelled control set in
one run, and the best one is chosen by the numbers rather than by memory.

    A  plain string, question says "this passage"            the mis-called first form
    B  dict state, backticked `passage` in the instructions   §25.7's measured-best form
    C  binary yes/no choice                                   §25.7 measured this as unusable

WHY `choice` AND NOT `noul`, read from laya's source (`agent.py:330-336`) rather than its docs:

    choice -> {"choice": <label>, "probabilities": {key: p}, "confidence": <entropy>}  label AND p
    noul   -> {"noul": p[1], "confidence": max(p, 1-p)}                                NO label, NO criteria

§22.3 said "a `choice` or `noul` question with named criteria". `noul` takes no criteria and returns
no label, so only `choice` can satisfy §19.7's two-field verdict. Recorded as a correction.

WHAT THIS SCRIPT REFUSES TO DO, stated so a reader cannot mistake the output for more than it is:

  * it does not decide whether the judgement is GOOD ENOUGH — it reports accuracy and ECE, and the
    verdict rule (§25.1: the judgement must be CALIBRATED) is applied in the report, not here;
  * it does not treat any label as authority: §19.4's boundary holds, and a classification is DATA;
  * it does not overwrite the first run's artifact. A changed source and a second convention produce
    a NEW artifact version (rule 2), so `evidence_silver_run.json` survives beside this one's output.

Run:  .venv/Scripts/python.exe silver.py
Out:  ../season_2026_s1/evidence/evidence_silver_run_3.json

WHY A THIRD ARTIFACT RATHER THAN AN EDIT OF THE SECOND (rule 2). Run 2 was written with a selection
rule that ranged over A, B and C and picked the best score — and C answers a BINARY question, so a
score could not compare it to a four-way one, and the rule chose an instrument that was not answering
the question being asked. Run 2 therefore carries a real defect and is preserved beside this one. Its
numbers are not withdrawn; its CHOICE is, and the correction is visible in the artifact that made it.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import sys
import time
import urllib.request
from pathlib import Path

RAW = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/githubusercontent/gsd-core/next/"
RAW = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/open-gsd/gsd-core/next/"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# PART 2's question, in three conventions. The criteria are IDENTICAL across all
# three: only the CALL FORM differs, so any difference in the scores is a
# difference the call form made and not a difference in what was asked.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
CRITERIA = {
    "agent_instruction": "it tells an AI assistant what to do or how to behave",
    "contributor_standard": "it sets a rule for a human writing code in this repository",
    "project_documentation": "it describes the project without instructing anyone",
    "other": "none of the above",
}

SPECIES_A = {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": (
        "Which kind of document is this passage? Judge the PASSAGE alone, "
        "not its filename and not the repository it came from."
    ),
    "criteria": CRITERIA,
}

# B is the measured-best form: the state is a DICT and its key is named in backticks, which is the
# shape every laya preset uses (§25.7).
SPECIES_B = {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": (
        "Classify the text in `passage`. Which kind of document is it? Judge `passage` alone, "
        "not its filename and not the repository it came from."
    ),
    "criteria": CRITERIA,
}

# C is the binary form, kept because §25.7 measured it as unusable and a claim about an instrument
# should be re-derivable rather than quoted.
SPECIES_C = {
    "type": "choice",
    "instructions": (
        "Is the text in `passage` an instruction to an AI assistant, or not? Judge `passage` alone."
    ),
    "criteria": {
        "agent_instruction": "it tells an AI assistant what to do or how to behave",
        "not_agent_instruction": "it does not",
    },
}

# A labelled control set. Eight passages, four classes, so chance is 0.250 and every class has more
# than one member. Each passage has a KNOWN species, which is what makes accuracy and calibration
# measurable rather than asserted.
CONTROL = [
    ("You are an AI assistant. Always answer in the user's language.", "agent_instruction"),
    ("Before answering, restate the user's goal in one sentence.", "agent_instruction"),
    ("Do not run any command that writes outside the working directory.", "agent_instruction"),
    ("CommonJS only. Use `node:test` and `node:assert`.", "contributor_standard"),
    ("Run `npm run lint` before every commit.", "contributor_standard"),
    ("All exported functions require a JSDoc block.", "contributor_standard"),
    ("GSD is a process framework that turns a specification into phases.", "project_documentation"),
    ("The repository contains a `bin/` directory and a `docs/` directory.", "project_documentation"),
]

# The real disputed passages — §22.5's scope question, one passage at a time.
REAL = [
    ("clinerules.core_rule",
     "GSD Core Rule: Never Edit Outside a GSD Workflow. All changes must go through "
     "a GSD workflow using /gsd:plan-phase."),
    ("clinerules.coding_standards",
     "Coding Standards. CommonJS only. Use node:test and node:assert. Use execFileSync, "
     "not execSync. All paths must pass validatePath()."),
    ("gemini.loop",
     "The loop is explore -> plan -> execute -> verify -> ship. Each phase carries a SPEC."),
    ("gemini.header",
     "This file ships only the context above - not the slash commands."),
]

# Claims Part 1 tests for exact presence in raw bytes. Quoted, not paraphrased.
PRESENCE = [
    ("gemini.loop_named", "GEMINI.md", "explore"),
    ("gemini.spec_word", "GEMINI.md", "SPEC"),
    ("gemini.self_partial", "GEMINI.md", "not the slash commands"),
    ("gemini.namespace", "GEMINI.md", "/gsd-plan-phase"),
    ("clinerules.core_rule", ".clinerules", "Never Edit Outside a GSD Workflow"),
    ("clinerules.namespace", ".clinerules", "/gsd:plan-phase"),
    ("clinerules.coding_standards", ".clinerules", "CommonJS only"),
]

# A benign repository conduct rule, used to re-measure laya's OWN guard preset. §25.7 measured the
# jailbreak head at 0.9765 on this text, which is the strongest single finding in the silver attempt:
# a control that fires on the benign case is not a control.
GUARD_PROBE = "Never edit files outside a GSD workflow."

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# THE TWO RULES THAT DECIDE HOW A LABEL IS READ — module level so a TEST can hold them.
#
# Both were wrong in an earlier version of this file, and both were wrong in the same direction: a
# number was read as more than it said. A control that exists only inside `main()` cannot be tested,
# so rule 44 — *a mitigation is not implemented until a test FAILS without it* — could not be met.
# They are pure functions here for that reason and not for elegance.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Which conventions compete. A and B ask the SAME four-way species question and differ only in call
# form, so their scores are comparable. C asks a BINARY question, so its score is not comparable to
# theirs — an earlier rule ranged over all three and picked C, i.e. it selected an instrument by its
# calibration when that instrument was not answering the question being asked.
SPECIES_CONVENTIONS = ("A", "B")

# A label below the floor is DIFFUSE and settles nothing; below the CONTROL MEDIAN it is FLAT — less
# decisive than a typical control call, INCLUDING the calls the instrument got wrong. A floor alone
# labelled all four real passages "PEAKED" at 0.12-0.14, which the control distribution (median
# 0.2019, mean 0.1184 when WRONG) does not support.
DIFFUSE_BELOW = 0.10


def dispersion_verdict(confidence: float, control_median: float) -> str:
    """Read laya's `confidence` as DISPERSION, never as certainty."""
    if confidence < DIFFUSE_BELOW:
        return "DIFFUSE"
    if confidence < control_median:
        return "FLAT — less decisive than a typical control call"
    return "PEAKED"


def usable_as_a_finding(verdicts) -> bool:
    """A row is a finding only when EVERY question asked of it came back PEAKED."""
    return all(v == "PEAKED" for v in verdicts)


# The sizes and hashes the FIRST run recorded, so a changed source is REPORTED rather than absorbed.
# A byte count that moved is a fact about the source; silently adopting the new one would bury it.
PRIOR_SOURCES = {
    "GEMINI.md": {"bytes": 2509, "sha256": "264c71c5c9d591e174a31dbd8af01d8b0e6389c7f43a013817b65cd6f9fbf82b"},
    ".clinerules": {"bytes": 1165, "sha256": "10872a5a7066ae13541ba5e1bf693d00cae84423c1a84ef325ba392559376da0"},
}


def fetch(name: str) -> str:
    req = urllib.request.Request(RAW + name, headers={"User-Agent": "godplan-silver/1.0"})
    return urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=30).read().decode("utf-8", "replace")


def main() -> int:
    out: dict = {
        "evidence_id": "evidence_silver_run_3",
        "type": "evidence",
        "schema_version": "1.0",
        "run_at": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ", time.gmtime()),
        "supersedes": "evidence_silver_run_2",
        "why_a_third_run": (
            "run 2's convention competition ranged over A, B and C by score, and C answers a binary "
            "question — so the rule selected an instrument by calibration that was not answering the "
            "four-way species question. Two corrections: the competition is now A vs B only, and a "
            "label whose entropy confidence is near zero is recorded as DIFFUSE rather than reported "
            "as a finding. The guard probe also measures BOTH call forms, because a bare string state "
            "never becomes the JSON the preset's instructions name."
        ),
    }

    # ---------------- PART 1 — presence, mechanical, over raw bytes ----------------
    sources: dict[str, str | None] = {}
    for name in ("GEMINI.md", ".clinerules"):
        try:
            sources[name] = fetch(name)
            print(f"[part1] fetched {name}: {len(sources[name])} bytes")
        except Exception as e:  # a refusal is reported, never silently skipped (rule 29)
            print(f"[part1] FETCH FAILED {name}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            sources[name] = None

    out["part1_presence"] = {
        "grade": "B",
        "question": "does this exact string appear in the raw fetched bytes?",
        "instrument": "exact substring over the fetched body; no model is applied to Part 1",
        "sources": {},
        "source_changes": [],
        "checks": [],
    }
    for name, body in sources.items():
        if body is None:
            out["part1_presence"]["sources"][name] = None
            continue
        measured = {"bytes": len(body), "sha256": hashlib.sha256(body.encode()).hexdigest()}
        out["part1_presence"]["sources"][name] = measured
        prior = PRIOR_SOURCES.get(name)
        if prior and (prior["bytes"] != measured["bytes"] or prior["sha256"] != measured["sha256"]):
            out["part1_presence"]["source_changes"].append({
                "source": name,
                "recorded_in_first_run": prior,
                "measured_now": measured,
                "verdict": "THE SOURCE MOVED between the two runs. Part 1 re-tests the CURRENT bytes, "
                           "and the earlier presence results are a fact about an earlier revision",
            })
            print(f"[part1] SOURCE MOVED {name}: {prior['bytes']} -> {measured['bytes']} bytes")

    for cid, src, needle in PRESENCE:
        body = sources.get(src)
        hit = (body is not None and needle in body)
        out["part1_presence"]["checks"].append(
            {"id": cid, "source": src, "needle": needle, "present": hit,
             "instrument": "exact string, no model"}
        )
        print(f"[part1] {'PRESENT ' if hit else 'ABSENT  '} {cid:34s} {needle!r}")

    # ---------------- PART 2 — classification, three conventions ----------------
    import numpy as np
    import laya
    import torch

    t0 = time.time()
    agent = laya.load(device="cuda")
    out["part2_laya"] = {
        "grade": "C",
        "package": getattr(laya, "__version__", "?"),
        "loaded_in_s": round(time.time() - t0, 1),
        "question_type": "choice",
        "why_choice_not_noul": "noul returns no label and takes no criteria (agent.py:330-336)",
        "criteria": list(CRITERIA),
        "conventions": {},
    }
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        out["part2_laya"]["device"] = torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)

    def classify(conv: str, passage: str) -> dict:
        """One passage, one call, in the convention named. Returns label + probability + timing."""
        t = time.time()
        if conv == "A":
            spec = {"species": SPECIES_A}
            r = agent.predict(passage, spec)["answers"]["species"]
        elif conv == "B":
            spec = {"species": SPECIES_B}
            r = agent.predict({"passage": passage}, spec)["answers"]["species"]
        else:
            r = agent.predict({"passage": passage}, {"species": SPECIES_C})["answers"]["species"]
        return {
            "label": r["choice"],
            "p_label": r["probabilities"][r["choice"]],
            "probabilities": r["probabilities"],
            "entropy_confidence": r["confidence"],
            "ms": round((time.time() - t) * 1000, 1),
        }

    def truth_for(conv: str, truth: str) -> str:
        # Convention C collapses four classes into two, so its truth is the collapsed one.
        return truth if conv != "C" else ("agent_instruction" if truth == "agent_instruction"
                                          else "not_agent_instruction")

    for conv in ("A", "B", "C"):
        conf, correct, rows = [], [], []
        for passage, truth in CONTROL:
            r = classify(conv, passage)
            expect = truth_for(conv, truth)
            ok = r["label"] == expect
            conf.append(r["p_label"])
            correct.append(1.0 if ok else 0.0)
            rows.append({"passage": passage, "truth": expect, **r, "correct": ok})
            print(f"[part2:{conv}] control {'OK  ' if ok else 'MISS'} truth={expect:22s} "
                  f"-> {r['label']:22s} p={r['p_label']:.4f} {r['ms']:6.1f}ms")
        acc = sum(1 for r in rows if r["correct"]) / len(rows)
        ece = float(laya.ece_score(np.array(conf), np.array(correct)))
        brier = sum((c - y) ** 2 for c, y in zip(conf, correct)) / len(rows)
        out["part2_laya"]["conventions"][conv] = {
            "call_form": {
                "A": "plain string; instructions say 'the PASSAGE'",
                "B": "dict state {\"passage\": ...}; instructions name `passage` backticked",
                "C": "dict state; binary agent_instruction vs not_agent_instruction",
            }[conv],
            "n": len(rows),
            "accuracy": round(acc, 4),
            "ece": round(ece, 4),
            "mean_brier": round(brier, 4),
            "distinct_labels_predicted": len({r["label"] for r in rows}),
            "rows": rows,
        }
        print(f"\n[part2:{conv}] CONTROL  n={len(rows)}  accuracy={acc:.3f}  ECE={ece:.4f}  "
              f"Brier={brier:.4f}  distinct labels={len({r['label'] for r in rows})}\n")

    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    # WHICH CONVENTION CLASSIFIES THE REAL PASSAGES — and a correction to the rule itself.
    #
    # The first version of this competition ranged over A, B AND C and picked the lowest ECE. Today
    # that picks **C**, which scores 1.000 — and C is a BINARY question (agent-facing or not). The
    # four-way species question the scope decision actually needs (agent instruction / contributor
    # standard / project documentation / other) CANNOT be answered by C at all.
    #
    # **So the rule was choosing an instrument by its calibration when that instrument answers a
    # different question.** A score is comparable only between instruments asked the same thing. C is
    # not a worse answer to A and B's question; it is a good answer to a different one, and the
    # selection rule was reading a higher score as a better fit. That is §4.5's conflation — a
    # qualification treated as interchangeable with the thing it is not — committed by the file whose
    # job is to check that nobody else does it.
    #
    # CORRECTED: A and B compete, because they ask the same four-way question and differ only in call
    # form. C is scored and reported separately as its own binary question, with its own bar, and is
    # never used to classify the real passages.
    # ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    scored = out["part2_laya"]["conventions"]
    best = min(SPECIES_CONVENTIONS, key=lambda c: (scored[c]["ece"], -scored[c]["accuracy"]))
    out["part2_laya"]["best_convention"] = {
        "chosen": best,
        "rule": "lowest ECE, then highest accuracy, COMPARED ONLY BETWEEN CONVENTIONS THAT ASK THE "
                "SAME QUESTION. A and B ask the four-way species question; C asks a binary one, so its "
                "score is not comparable to theirs and it is reported separately.",
        "competitors": list(SPECIES_CONVENTIONS),
        "excluded_from_the_competition": {
            "C": f"answers a DIFFERENT question (binary); scored accuracy="
                 f"{scored['C']['accuracy']}, ECE={scored['C']['ece']} as its own result, never as a "
                 "reason to prefer it for the four-way call",
        },
        "table": {c: {"accuracy": scored[c]["accuracy"], "ece": scored[c]["ece"]} for c in ("A", "B", "C")},
        "chance_for_four_classes": 0.25,
        "chance_for_binary": 0.5,
    }
    print(f"[part2] best SPECIES convention (A and B only): {best}  "
          f"(accuracy={scored[best]['accuracy']}, ECE={scored[best]['ece']})")
    print(f"[part2] C scored as its OWN binary question: accuracy={scored['C']['accuracy']}, "
          f"ECE={scored['C']['ece']} — not comparable to a four-way score, so not a competitor")

    # REPRODUCIBILITY, measured rather than asserted. The first run's stored artifact carries ONE
    # control set. If it is the same instrument on the same control set, convention A must reproduce
    # it row for row — and if it does not, the earlier numbers were a different call and are not a
    # baseline this run may be compared against.
    prior_path = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "season_2026_s1" / "evidence"
                  / "evidence_silver_run.json")
    if prior_path.exists():
        prior = json.loads(prior_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        prior_set = prior.get("part2_laya", {}).get("control_set") or {}
        mine = scored["A"]
        same_rows = [r["p_label"] for r in prior_set.get("rows", [])] == [r["p_label"] for r in mine["rows"]]
        out["part2_laya"]["reproducibility"] = {
            "against": prior_path.name,
            "prior_had_a_conventions_block": bool(prior.get("part2_laya", {}).get("conventions")),
            "prior_control_set": {k: prior_set.get(k) for k in ("n", "accuracy", "ece", "mean_brier")},
            "this_run_convention_A": {k: mine.get(k) for k in ("n", "accuracy", "ece", "mean_brier")},
            "per_row_probabilities_identical": same_rows,
            "verdict": (
                "REPRODUCES — the first run's stored control set IS this convention, and every "
                "per-row probability is identical, so the instrument is deterministic and the "
                "measurement is re-runnable"
                if same_rows and prior_set.get("accuracy") == mine["accuracy"] and prior_set.get("ece") == mine["ece"]
                else "DOES NOT REPRODUCE — the stored numbers are a different call, and §25.7's table "
                     "cannot be re-derived from the artifacts either way"
            ),
        }
        print(f"[part2] vs {prior_path.name}: stored accuracy={prior_set.get('accuracy')} "
              f"ECE={prior_set.get('ece')} | this run's A={mine['accuracy']}/{mine['ece']} | "
              f"identical per-row p={same_rows}")
    else:
        out["part2_laya"]["reproducibility"] = {"against": None, "verdict": "no prior artifact to compare"}

    # A LABEL IS NOT A FINDING UNTIL ITS DISPERSION IS READ (§25.7's own correction). `confidence`
    # from laya is a NORMALISED SHANNON ENTROPY over the option distribution (`1 - H(p)/log k`), NOT
    # a class probability — §25.7 found this by reading `agent.py`, and reading it as certainty
    # overstates every diffuse answer. So a near-zero confidence is the instrument saying *I have no
    # preference here*, and a label printed beside it would read as a verdict while being a coin toss.
    #
    # The threshold is stated as a rule rather than tuned: below it the row is DIFFUSE, which means
    # the passage is NOT decided by this instrument and the scope question stays OPEN.
    # AND A REFERENCE, because a floor alone cannot say whether a passage is decisive. When the four
    # real passages all cleared 0.10 while sitting at 0.124-0.138, a bare floor labelled them "peaked"
    # — a word the numbers do not support. The control set is the reference: it is the only place
    # where the dispersion of a KNOWN-correct call can be read. So the label is decided against the
    # control distribution as well, and the pair is reported rather than the floor alone.
    control_conf = [r["entropy_confidence"] for r in scored[best]["rows"]]
    control_conf.sort()
    control_median = control_conf[len(control_conf) // 2]
    control_correct = [r["entropy_confidence"] for r in scored[best]["rows"] if r["correct"]]
    control_wrong = [r["entropy_confidence"] for r in scored[best]["rows"] if not r["correct"]]
    reference = {
        "control_n": len(control_conf),
        "control_min": control_conf[0],
        "control_median": round(control_median, 4),
        "control_max": control_conf[-1],
        "mean_dispersion_when_correct": round(sum(control_correct) / len(control_correct), 4)
        if control_correct else None,
        "mean_dispersion_when_wrong": round(sum(control_wrong) / len(control_wrong), 4)
        if control_wrong else None,
        "reading": "a passage below the control MEDIAN is less decisive than a typical control call — "
                   "including the ones this instrument got WRONG",
    }
    print(f"[part2] control dispersion: min={reference['control_min']:.4f} "
          f"median={reference['control_median']:.4f} max={reference['control_max']:.4f} "
          f"mean|correct={reference['mean_dispersion_when_correct']} "
          f"wrong={reference['mean_dispersion_when_wrong']}")

    # EACH REAL PASSAGE IS PUT TO BOTH QUESTIONS, and the two answers are reported side by side and
    # NEVER combined. They are not two votes on one question: B asks WHICH of four species, C asks
    # only WHETHER it is agent-facing. C is the instrument the §22.5 scope question actually needs
    # ("is .clinerules addressed to agents?"), and it is also the better-calibrated of the two, so
    # omitting it because it lost a competition it should not have been entered in would be keeping
    # the defect the correction above was written to remove.
    control_median_of = {conv: sorted(r["entropy_confidence"] for r in scored[conv]["rows"])[
        len(scored[conv]["rows"]) // 2] for conv in ("A", "B", "C")}

    real_rows = []
    for cid, passage in REAL:
        species = classify(best, passage)
        binary = classify("C", passage)
        row = {
            "id": cid,
            "passage": passage,
            "species_question": {
                "convention": best,
                "asks": "which of four species (agent_instruction / contributor_standard / "
                        "project_documentation / other)",
                "label": species["label"],
                "p_label": species["p_label"],
                "probabilities": species["probabilities"],
                "dispersion": species["entropy_confidence"],
                "verdict": dispersion_verdict(species["entropy_confidence"], control_median_of[best]),
                "ms": species["ms"],
            },
            "binary_question": {
                "convention": "C",
                "asks": "is it an instruction to an AI assistant, or not — which is the §22.5 "
                        "scope question phrased directly",
                "label": binary["label"],
                "p_label": binary["p_label"],
                "probabilities": binary["probabilities"],
                "dispersion": binary["entropy_confidence"],
                "verdict": dispersion_verdict(binary["entropy_confidence"], control_median_of["C"]),
                "ms": binary["ms"],
            },
            "agreement": "AGREE" if (
                (binary["label"] == "agent_instruction") == (species["label"] == "agent_instruction")
            ) else "DISAGREE",
        }
        row["usable_as_a_finding"] = usable_as_a_finding(
            [row["binary_question"]["verdict"], row["species_question"]["verdict"]]
        )
        real_rows.append(row)
        print(f"[part2] {cid:26s} species={species['label']:22s} p={species['p_label']:.4f} "
              f"disp={species['entropy_confidence']:.4f} {row['species_question']['verdict'].split(' ')[0]:7s}|"
              f" binary={binary['label']:22s} p={binary['p_label']:.4f} "
              f"disp={binary['entropy_confidence']:.4f} {row['binary_question']['verdict'].split(' ')[0]:7s}|"
              f" {row['agreement']}")
    out["part2_laya"]["dispersion_reference"] = reference
    out["part2_laya"]["both_questions_note"] = (
        "the two instruments are reported side by side and NEVER combined: they answer different "
        "questions, and a score cannot compare them (section 4.5 — a qualification is not "
        "interchangeable with the thing it is not)"
    )
    out["part2_laya"]["passages"] = real_rows
    out["part2_laya"]["dispersion_rule"] = {
        "field": "entropy_confidence",
        "is": "a normalised Shannon entropy over the option distribution, NOT a class probability "
              "(agent.py:307 via confidence_from_probs)",
        "threshold": DIFFUSE_BELOW,
        "below_threshold": "DIFFUSE — the label is recorded but is NOT a finding, and the question it "
                            "was asked to settle remains OPEN",
        "second_reference": "below the CONTROL MEDIAN is FLAT — the instrument is LESS decisive here "
                           "than on a typical control call, including the calls it got wrong. A floor "
                           "alone labelled all four real passages 'PEAKED' at 0.12-0.14, which the "
                           "control distribution does not support.",
        "why_a_rule_and_not_a_tuning": "a threshold chosen by what made an answer look decisive would "
                                       "be selecting the instrument by the result it gave",
    }
    out["part2_laya"]["aggregate"] = {
        "n_species_agent_instruction": sum(
            1 for r in real_rows if r["species_question"]["label"] == "agent_instruction"),
        "n_binary_agent_instruction": sum(
            1 for r in real_rows if r["binary_question"]["label"] == "agent_instruction"),
        "n_questions_agree": sum(1 for r in real_rows if r["agreement"] == "AGREE"),
        "n_questions_disagree": sum(1 for r in real_rows if r["agreement"] == "DISAGREE"),
        "n_species_peaked": sum(
            1 for r in real_rows if r["species_question"]["verdict"] == "PEAKED"),
        "n_binary_peaked": sum(
            1 for r in real_rows if r["binary_question"]["verdict"] == "PEAKED"),
        "n_settled_by_both": sum(1 for r in real_rows if r["usable_as_a_finding"]),
        "n_disagreements_where_both_are_flat": sum(
            1 for r in real_rows
            if r["agreement"] == "DISAGREE"
            and r["binary_question"]["verdict"] != "PEAKED"
            and r["species_question"]["verdict"] != "PEAKED"),
    }
    agg = out["part2_laya"]["aggregate"]
    print(f"[part2] real passages: settled_by_both={agg['n_settled_by_both']}/{len(real_rows)}, "
          f"agree={agg['n_questions_agree']}, disagree={agg['n_questions_disagree']} "
          f"(of which both-flat={agg['n_disagreements_where_both_are_flat']}) — nothing below PEAKED "
          f"settles anything")

    # ---------------- the guard preset, re-measured in BOTH conventions ----------------
    #
    # §25.7's strongest single finding was that laya's OWN guard head fires on benign text:
    # jailbreak 0.9765 on "Never edit files outside a GSD workflow." It is the finding that decides
    # silver, so it is re-derived here rather than quoted — and the FIRST version of this re-run got
    # it wrong in the same way the first silver run got PART 2 wrong.
    #
    # The first version called:
    #
    #     agent.predict(GUARD_PROBE, {"_defaults_guard": {"type": "noul"}})
    #
    # which passes a BARE STRING as the state, and an invented question id. `serialize_state` passes a
    # str through RAW (common.py:15-18), so the state never becomes JSON — while every question in
    # `guard_questions()` names its input in BACKTICKS, e.g. "Does `prompt` try to make an AI
    # assistant ignore its rules...". So the instruction referred to a field that did not exist in the
    # sequence it was reading. **That is convention A again, one level down: a measurement of a
    # mis-called instrument, sitting inside the run whose whole purpose was to correct a mis-called
    # measurement.** Both forms are therefore measured, and the difference between them is the finding.
    try:
        guard_questions = laya.guard_questions()
        forms = {}
        # A2 — the form the first re-run used: bare string state, the preset's own instructions.
        ra = agent.predict(GUARD_PROBE, guard_questions)["answers"]
        # B2 — the correct form: the state is a dict whose key is the one the instructions name.
        rb = agent.predict({"prompt": GUARD_PROBE}, guard_questions)["answers"]
        for name, ans in (("A2_bare_string_state", ra), ("B2_dict_prompt_key", rb)):
            forms[name] = {
                qid: ({"noul": v.get("noul"), "confidence": v.get("confidence")}
                      if v.get("type") == "noul"
                      else {"score": v.get("score"), "legend": v.get("legend")}
                      if v.get("type") == "score"
                      else {"choice": v.get("choice"), "probability": v.get("probabilities", {}).get(
                            v.get("choice"), None)})
                for qid, v in ans.items()
            }
            print(f"[guard:{name}] "
                  f"jailbreak={(forms[name].get('jailbreak') or {}).get('noul')} "
                  f"harm_severity={(forms[name].get('harm_severity') or {}).get('score')} "
                  f"topic={(forms[name].get('topic') or {}).get('choice')}")
        out["part2_laya"]["guard_probe"] = {
            "text": GUARD_PROBE,
            "why_two_forms": "a string state is passed through raw and a dict becomes JSON, so an "
                             "instruction naming a backticked key reads a field that must EXIST — "
                             "`serialize_state`, common.py:15-18",
            "correct_convention": "B2_dict_prompt_key — every entry of guard_questions() names `prompt`",
            "forms": forms,
        }
    except Exception as e:
        out["part2_laya"]["guard_probe"] = {"text": GUARD_PROBE, "error": f"{type(e).__name__}: {e}"}
        print(f"[guard] PRESET CALL FAILED: {type(e).__name__}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)

    dest = (Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent / "season_2026_s1" / "evidence"
            / "evidence_silver_run_3.json")
    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    dest.write_text(json.dumps(out, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(f"\nwrote {dest}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())
```

#### `test_silver.py`

```python
"""Tests for silver.py — the two rules that decide how a laya label is READ, and the artifact they produce.

WHY THESE TESTS ARE ABOUT THE RULES AND NOT THE SCORES. The scores are a measurement of an instrument
and they will move when the instrument, the control set or the GPU changes; a test pinned to 0.223
would be a test that fails on a legitimate re-measurement, which is the stale-literal defect this
corpus keeps repairing. What must NOT move silently is how a number is turned into a claim:

  RULE 1  only conventions that ask the SAME question compete. C asks a binary one, so a score cannot
          compare it to a four-way one.
  RULE 2  a label whose dispersion is at or below the control median is FLAT and settles nothing.

Both were violated by an earlier version of this file and both violations pointed the same way — a
number read as more than it said. Rule 44 says a control is not implemented until a test FAILS
without it, so the negative controls below construct the violation rather than describing it.

Run:  python -m unittest test_silver
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import sys
import unittest
from pathlib import Path

sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import silver

ARTIFACT = (
    Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
    / "season_2026_s1"
    / "evidence"
    / "evidence_silver_run_3.json"
)
PRIOR = ARTIFACT.parent / "evidence_silver_run.json"

# The §10.2 citation index: a §N.M reference in a record must name a node in the canon. The registry
# is the canon itself, read from disk, so this cannot drift from the thing it checks. The NAME is
# resolved rather than assumed: this tree carries the god file as `GOD_AGENTS.md`.
from godplan.reconstruct import resolve_god_file  # noqa: E402

GOD_FILE = resolve_god_file(Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent)


class TestTheTwoRules(unittest.TestCase):
    """Rule 1 and rule 2 as pure predicates — no artifact needed, so a regression fails here first."""

    def test_only_same_question_conventions_compete(self):
        """The bug: a rule that ranged over A, B and C picked C, which answers a BINARY question."""
        self.assertEqual(silver.SPECIES_CONVENTIONS, ("A", "B"))
        self.assertNotIn("C", silver.SPECIES_CONVENTIONS)

    def test_a_score_cannot_compare_a_binary_to_a_four_way(self):
        """Negative control. The measured scores are exactly the shape that fooled the old rule: C
        scored HIGHER than both same-question conventions, so any rule keyed on score alone picks it."""
        scored = {"A": {"ece": 0.4964, "accuracy": 0.375},
                  "B": {"ece": 0.2230, "accuracy": 0.625},
                  "C": {"ece": 0.1553, "accuracy": 1.000}}
        best_by_score_alone = min(scored, key=lambda c: (scored[c]["ece"], -scored[c]["accuracy"]))
        self.assertEqual(best_by_score_alone, "C", "the trap must still be a trap")
        best_correctly = min(silver.SPECIES_CONVENTIONS,
                             key=lambda c: (scored[c]["ece"], -scored[c]["accuracy"]))
        self.assertEqual(best_correctly, "B")
        self.assertNotEqual(best_by_score_alone, best_correctly,
                            "if these ever agree the control has stopped testing anything")

    def test_dispersion_floor_labels_a_near_zero_confidence_diffuse(self):
        self.assertEqual(silver.dispersion_verdict(0.0025, 0.2019), "DIFFUSE")

    def test_dispersion_above_the_floor_but_below_the_median_is_flat(self):
        """The 0.12-0.14 cluster: above the floor, far below a typical control call."""
        self.assertTrue(silver.dispersion_verdict(0.1241, 0.2019).startswith("FLAT"))

    def test_only_above_the_control_median_is_peaked(self):
        self.assertEqual(silver.dispersion_verdict(0.7505, 0.2019), "PEAKED")

    def test_a_row_is_a_finding_only_when_every_question_is_peaked(self):
        """Negative control: one flat answer among two settles nothing, and the OLD rule — which read
        only the four-way verdict — would have called this row usable."""
        self.assertTrue(silver.usable_as_a_finding(["PEAKED", "PEAKED"]))
        self.assertFalse(silver.usable_as_a_finding(["PEAKED", "FLAT — less decisive than a typical control call"]))
        self.assertFalse(silver.usable_as_a_finding(["DIFFUSE", "PEAKED"]))


class TestTheArtifact(unittest.TestCase):
    """The artifact-level checks, because a rule cannot see whether a ropy run wrote it out."""

    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        if not ARTIFACT.exists():
            raise unittest.SkipTest(f"{ARTIFACT.name} not present; run silver.py")
        cls.art = json.loads(ARTIFACT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

    def test_part1_is_mechanical_and_needs_no_model(self):
        part1 = self.art["part1_presence"]
        self.assertEqual(part1["grade"], "B")
        self.assertNotIn("model", part1["instrument"].replace("no model", ""))
        checks = part1["checks"]
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(checks), 7)
        for check in checks:
            # every check states its instrument, and it is never a model
            self.assertIn("no model", check["instrument"])
            self.assertIsInstance(check["present"], bool)

    def test_part2_records_the_probability_as_the_strength(self):
        """§19.7's two-field verdict: a label AND a probability. A label alone is an assertion."""
        part2 = self.art["part2_laya"]
        self.assertEqual(part2["grade"], "C")
        self.assertEqual(part2["question_type"], "choice")
        for row in part2["passages"]:
            for question in ("species_question", "binary_question"):
                q = row[question]
                self.assertIn("label", q)
                self.assertIn("p_label", q)
                self.assertTrue(0.0 <= q["p_label"] <= 1.0)
                self.assertIn("dispersion", q)
                self.assertIn("verdict", q)

    def test_the_competition_in_the_artifact_excludes_the_binary_question(self):
        best = self.art["part2_laya"]["best_convention"]
        self.assertEqual(best["competitors"], ["A", "B"])
        self.assertIn("C", best["excluded_from_the_competition"])
        self.assertNotIn(best["chosen"], ("C",))

    def test_every_real_passage_is_put_to_both_questions(self):
        for row in self.art["part2_laya"]["passages"]:
            self.assertIn("species_question", row)
            self.assertIn("binary_question", row)
            self.assertIn(row["agreement"], ("AGREE", "DISAGREE"))

    def test_no_row_claims_a_finding_while_a_question_is_flat(self):
        """The defect this pins: a row reported as settled while one of its two answers was FLAT."""
        for row in self.art["part2_laya"]["passages"]:
            verdicts = [row["species_question"]["verdict"], row["binary_question"]["verdict"]]
            if row["usable_as_a_finding"]:
                self.assertEqual(verdicts, ["PEAKED", "PEAKED"], row["id"])
            else:
                self.assertFalse(silver.usable_as_a_finding(verdicts), row["id"])

    def test_the_dispersion_rule_names_its_second_reference(self):
        """A floor alone cannot say whether a passage is decisive; the control median is the reference
        that can, and it must be recorded rather than implied."""
        rule = self.art["part2_laya"]["dispersion_rule"]
        self.assertEqual(rule["threshold"], silver.DIFFUSE_BELOW)
        self.assertIn("control median", rule["second_reference"].lower())
        ref = self.art["part2_laya"]["dispersion_reference"]
        self.assertIn("control_median", ref)
        self.assertIn("mean_dispersion_when_wrong", ref)

    def test_the_binary_instrument_is_reported_separately_from_the_species_one(self):
        """They answer different questions; combining them would be the conflation the rule forbids."""
        self.assertIn("never combined", self.art["part2_laya"]["both_questions_note"].lower())

    def test_the_run_records_whether_the_first_run_reproduces(self):
        rep = self.art["part2_laya"]["reproducibility"]
        self.assertTrue(rep["prior_had_a_conventions_block"] is False or rep["prior_had_a_conventions_block"] is True)
        self.assertTrue(rep["verdict"].startswith(("REPRODUCES", "DOES NOT REPRODUCE")), rep["verdict"])

    def test_the_guard_probe_measures_both_call_forms(self):
        """§25.7's strongest finding decides silver, so it is re-derived — and the form matters: a bare
        string state never becomes the JSON the preset's instructions name."""
        guard = self.art["part2_laya"]["guard_probe"]
        self.assertIn("forms", guard)
        self.assertEqual(set(guard["forms"]), {"A2_bare_string_state", "B2_dict_prompt_key"})
        self.assertTrue(guard["correct_convention"].startswith("B2_dict_prompt_key"), guard["correct_convention"])
        for form in guard["forms"].values():
            self.assertIn("jailbreak", form)

    def test_the_verdict_is_never_stronger_than_the_dispersion_supports(self):
        """The whole point: 0 of 4 settled is a RESULT, and the artifact must say so rather than
        averaging the four into an impression of a decision."""
        agg = self.art["part2_laya"]["aggregate"]
        rows = self.art["part2_laya"]["passages"]
        self.assertEqual(agg["n_settled_by_both"], sum(1 for r in rows if r["usable_as_a_finding"]))
        self.assertEqual(agg["n_questions_agree"], sum(1 for r in rows if r["agreement"] == "AGREE"))
        self.assertEqual(agg["n_questions_agree"] + agg["n_questions_disagree"], len(rows))


class TestPriorArtifact(unittest.TestCase):
    """The first run survives beside the third, and the comparison is recorded in the third."""

    def test_the_first_run_is_preserved(self):
        self.assertTrue(PRIOR.exists(), "rule 2 — a changed source produces a NEW artifact version")
        prior = json.loads(PRIOR.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertNotIn("conventions", prior["part2_laya"],
                         "the first run carried ONE control set; §25.7's three-row table is prose")

    def test_the_third_run_supersedes_the_second(self):
        art = json.loads(ARTIFACT.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
        self.assertEqual(art["supersedes"], "evidence_silver_run_2")
        second = ARTIFACT.parent / "evidence_silver_run_2.json"
        self.assertTrue(second.exists(), "run 2's wrong CHOICE is preserved, its numbers are not withdrawn")


class TestCitations(unittest.TestCase):
    """Rule 31 — a citation of an absent node is worse than none, because it reads as provenance."""

    def test_every_section_cited_in_the_artifact_exists_in_the_canon(self):
        if not GOD_FILE.exists():
            self.skipTest("canon not present")
        canon = GOD_FILE.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")
        cited = set()
        for source in (ARTIFACT, Path(silver.__file__)):
            text = source.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            for n in range(1, 60):
                if f"§25.{n}" in text or f"25.{n}" in text:
                    cited.add(n)
        # §25 has 25.1-25.7 as of this writing. Asserting a range would be inventing one, so the
        # check is the weaker, honest one: the sections the file leans on hardest must be present.
        for n in (1, 2, 4, 7):
            self.assertIn(f"### 25.{n}", canon, f"§25.{n} is cited but not in the canon")

#### `c7_part1.py`

```python
"""C7 — scoring an outside reader against Part 1's seven presence checks.

    cd seasons/impl && python c7_part1.py

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. AGENTS.md §20.5 names C7 — *a reading that does not share the author's priors* — as
the only control aimed at the dominant threat, and §20.2 names the dominant threat as the author. §22.4
records C7 as refused on measurement: no lane could hold the context. This implements the narrow version
that DOES fit: Part 1 of §22.2 is a presence comparison over raw bytes, so it needs no project context at
all — the two source files total 3,728 bytes, and the whole brief is 1,627 tokens.

WHAT THIS FILE ENFORCES, and each is a rule rather than a preference:

  * A VERDICT IS TWO HALVES. A right PRESENT/ABSENT with a citation that does not contain the needle is
    UNSUPPORTED, never CORRECT. §19.7 requires a verdict to carry both a label and its evidence, and §11.4
    says a claim nobody could measure stays unresolved. Scored by value alone, a reader that guesses well
    would read as a reader that read well.

  * THE CONTROL IS A CONSTANT. `always PRESENT` is the degenerate strategy, and it is scored beside the
    readers. If a reader does not beat a constant, it carried no information — and §20.5's whole argument
    is that an unexercised control is indistinguishable from a control that does not exist, so the
    baseline has to be printed or the score is unreadable.

  * A LANE THAT DID NOT RUN IS `not_obtained`, NOT A FAILURE. §14 records this in the doctrine's own
    words: *a verification that never ran is a different fact from a verification that failed*. A 404
    attempt is preserved and scored as `not_obtained`, never silently dropped and never counted as wrong.

  * THE LOG'S MODEL FIELD IS A REQUEST, NOT AN INSTRUMENT. Measured: a 404 run still writes the requested
    model name into its own artifact, so a log can name a model that never executed. The instrument is
    recorded from the lane inventory, and the artifact is what is checked.

Ground truth is not read from a stored expectation; it is recomputed here from the fetched bytes, so this
file cannot agree with a stale result by accident.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import hashlib
import json
import re
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path

SEASONS = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
DELEGATION = SEASONS / "season_2026_s1" / "delegation"
RAW = DELEGATION / "part1-independent"

# The two sources, and the bytes each is checked against. Sizes are MEASURED here, never asserted.
SOURCES = {"FILE A": "GEMINI.md.raw", "FILE B": ".clinerules.raw"}

# The seven checks, verbatim from silver.py's PRESENCE list. Restated rather than imported because this
# file must be able to disagree with silver.py — importing its table would make a shared error invisible.
CHECKS = [
    ("1", "gemini.loop_named", "FILE A", "explore"),
    ("2", "gemini.spec_word", "FILE A", "SPEC"),
    ("3", "gemini.self_partial", "FILE A", "not the slash commands"),
    ("4", "gemini.namespace", "FILE A", "/gsd-plan-phase"),
    ("5", "clinerules.core_rule", "FILE B", "Never Edit Outside a GSD Workflow"),
    ("6", "clinerules.namespace", "FILE B", "/gsd:plan-phase"),
    ("7", "clinerules.coding_standards", "FILE B", "CommonJS only"),
]

# The readers, named by the MODEL THAT RAN — verified against `ollama list`, not against the log's model
# field, because a 404 run writes the requested name into its artifact. `not_obtained` lanes are scored as
# such and are not counted as wrong.
READERS = [
    {
        "id": "adi-qwen-7b",
        "model": "hf.co/AdvancedDataIntelligence/adi-qwen2.5-7b-ablit-glm5.2-GGUF:Q4_K_M",
        "log": "c7-part1-7b2.jsonl",
        "verdict": "c7-part1-verdict-7b2.txt",
    },
    {
        "id": "qwen2.5-vl-3b",
        "model": "hf.co/ggml-org/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct-GGUF:Q4_K_M",
        "log": "c7-part1-3b.jsonl",
        "verdict": "c7-part1-verdict-3b.txt",
    },
    {
        "id": "deepseek-r1-distill-7b (requested)",
        "model": "hf.co/ngxson/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-7B-abliterated-GGUF:Q4_K_M",
        "log": "c7-part1-7b.jsonl",
        "verdict": None,
    },
]

VERDICT_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*(\d)\.\s+\S+\s+(PRESENT|ABSENT)\s+line:\s*(.*?)\s*$", re.IGNORECASE)


def _norm(s: str) -> str:
    """Strip the markdown noise a reader adds around a quotation, without changing its words."""
    s = s.strip().strip('`').strip()
    s = s.lstrip(">").strip()
    s = s.strip('"').strip("'").strip()
    s = s.replace("**", "").replace("*", "").replace("`", "")
    return s.strip()


@dataclass
class Truth:
    cid: str
    label: str
    source: str
    needle: str
    present: bool
