**And what SURVIVED the check matters as much as what failed.** The fragment-resolution claim — that
sections 27–30 resolve by `section` + `authored_for` rather than by a hard-coded fragment id — is
exactly right, and so is the whole C9–C20 control mapping, clause for clause. **A check that reports
only failures cannot tell a careful document from a lucky one.**

### 31.4 `house.md` — the useful reference is the one that says no

`house.md` describes North American light-frame residential construction. It carries an explicit
independence note, and **the note is correct**: it has no relationship to this pillar. Its status is
**`not applicable`** — one of section 4.8's own vocabulary terms.

**But it is not useless, and the useful part is negative.** A real dwelling is an assembly of roughly
forty named layers — footings, sill plates, WRBs, rainscreens, vapor retarders, rafters, ice-and-water
shield — and **the civilian pillar has none of them and wants none of them.** That is the strongest
available answer to the temptation to reintroduce `HousingRef`: housing is not an under-specified
field in this pillar, it is a different *discipline*. The `locus` metaphor in the overlay is a spatial
encoding of a QUERY RESULT, and calling it housing would be a category error with forty layers of
machine behind it.

**So `house.md` is registered here as a source that is out of scope, with the reason, rather than
silently ignored** — the same disposition section 4.10 gives the 2000 snapshot, and for the same
reason: an out-of-scope document left unregistered is one a later reader will try to satisfy.

### 31.5 The bronze definition of done, and the gates that were actually run

Bronze ships **the lens**. Nothing else.

```text
1  renders the store + doctrine as a view (loci, avatars, controls, regions, monuments)   MET
2  the player writes PlanProposals ONLY; no store or doctrine mutation                    MET
3  the adjudicator is pure and deterministic; property tests pass                          MET (41 tests)
4  every refusal produces a ticket or a citation; never a silent skip                      MET
5  C05 renders ANSWERED (no cadence); C09 renders ANSWERED (derived view);
   C01 enforces the basis vocabulary                                                       MET
6  no write path to seasons/civilians/ or the doctrine exists                              MET (guard + test)
7  forbidden fields absent from every schema, and refused where they appear                MET
8  the situation digest converges byte-for-byte on re-run                                  MET
9  every number shown is cited or registered as an overlay metric                          MET
```

```text
python overlay.py verify
  [ok] test_godplan   86 tests      [ok] test_civilians  186 tests     [ok] test_plans  41 tests
  [ok] baseline   {'MET': 7, 'FAILED': 1, 'NOT_EVALUABLE': 4}         [ok] digest  byte-identical
  [ok] write guard  every protected root refuses a plan write
```

**Explicit non-goals until silver and above:** a persisted governed merge of plans into doctrine;
real agent-key issuance or identity (R7, rule 100); resolving any open C* or fog item; any performance
claim above target without a registered measurement; and any change that adds `dwelling_id`,
`quality_tier`, `capacity`, `balance`, `reputation`, `tax`, `payroll`, `salary` or `skill_score`.

### 31.6 What the overlay exposed about the system — four open items

**These are [O]. Do not resolve them by assumption, and note that two of them are about the SYSTEM
rather than about the overlay.**

```text
O1  NO CHECK READS ACROSS THE DOCTRINE / SEASON BOUNDARY.
    Installing this overlay found that four doctrine fragments cite an authority — the gsd_godfile
    ticket numbered 016 — that was never filed. The season store's dangling-reference validator
    scans RECORDS; the citation lives in the DOCTRINE store, which that validator does not read; so
    a dangling AUTHORITY CITATION in a fragment is invisible to every check in this repository. The
    ticket is now filed retrospectively (correction_dangling_authority_001). Whether a cross-store
    check should exist is a governed change, not an overlay's to make.

O2  A CORRECTION IS NOT DURABLE IF THE APPLIER STILL CARRIES THE OLD VALUE.
    The register rows corrected in this pass were ALSO written as patch strings inside
    `civilians_doctrine.py`, the tool that applies them — so re-running that tool would have
    restored every wrong number, and the only trace would have been a value quietly going backwards.
    Both copies are repaired here. Whether EVERY applier is now consistent is not established, and
    nothing checks it.

O3  IS THE OVERLAY A RECORD OR A VIEW OF ONE?  [O]
    `seasons/plans/` is deliberately non-authoritative, so a plan survives a restart without ever
    becoming a record. The alternative — plans as governed records with their own contract — is not
    ruled out; it is simply not bronze, and section 6.3 rule 1 would then require each plan to be
    filed before it was drawn, which is a different interaction model.

O4  HOW MANY CONTROLS CAN A VIEW HONESTLY DRAW BEFORE IT IS DECIDING?
    C9, C10, C11 and C18 render NOT_EVALUABLE — a status the adjudicator READS. But a view that
    decided *"nothing to see here"* rather than rendering the grey wireframe would have made an
    unavailable check look like a passed one. The line between rendering a status and deciding one
    is held here by one test and by nothing else.
```

### 31.7 Adopt

| Adopt | For | Why it fits | Licence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **WebGPU / wgpu** | the render surface | the browser is the medium the documents are written for | open |
| **[JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/)** | the plan store | one schema for the proposal boundary and the stored form | free |
| **[W3C PROV-O](https://www.w3.org/TR/prov-o/)** | a plan's lineage | a plan derived from a store snapshot names the snapshot | W3C REC |
| **Apple HIG spatial rules** | camera and panel comfort | the overlay already cites SL-01…SL-07 as view chrome, not doctrine | published guidance |
| **WCAG 2.2 AA** | neon-on-glass contrast | a neon theme is exactly where an accessibility claim is most likely to be false without measurement | free |
| **Event sourcing + CQRS** | the digest | the store is the write model and the digest is a read model, which is why it converges | free |

**Section 10.4's rule applies unchanged: adopt the shape, not the running service.** A wire format is
free; a collector is a service, and this pillar adds no service.

### 31.8 Binding rules 112-116

**Rule 65 applies to these as to anything else: an unsanctioned term is a defect recorded as one,
never silently adopted.**

```text
112. A view never decides a status it can read. A control's status, a ticket's governor version, and
     a decision's answered/open state are READ from the layer that owns them. A view that computes
     any of them has left the lens (section 19.4).
113. A plan is not a record. A plan store is non-authoritative by construction, and every write to it
     must pass a guard that refuses a protected root. The guard is code; a guard that exists only in
     documentation is not implemented (rule 43).
114. A refusal is an outcome, and a citation is mandatory. A pure function that refuses
     deterministically is still pure, so a refusal is captured and compared rather than allowed to
     abort — and a rejection without a citation is a defect, not a terse one.
115. A correction is not durable unless its APPLIER is corrected too. Where a value is both recorded
     and written by a tool, repairing one and not the other makes the correction temporary, and the
     failure is silent: the value goes backwards without an event.
116. A view must render an unavailable check as unavailable. NOT_EVALUABLE is a status to be drawn,
     never a silence to be filled, because a check that is unavailable and a check that passed are
     indistinguishable from the outside once the difference is not drawn.
```

### 31.9 The surface, as built — and the five defects that running it found

**`src/city.rs` is 1,887 lines and 20 tests hold it.** It renders `seasons/plans/view.json` as a playable
isometric city, and it is the surface `3DUI.MD` specifies for phases **B1–B4 and B6–B9**.

#### What it is, and what it is not

It is an **egui painter doing true isometric projection**. It is **not** the wgpu/WGSL pipeline
`3DUI.MD` §13 specifies — no bloom, no glass refraction, no aurora ribbon, no instanced mesh, no WASM
build. Two reasons, and the second is decisive:

```text
P3  "legibility over spectacle"     a painter satisfies the pillar's first requirement; bloom satisfies
                                    neither P3 nor P6
rule 36  verify the SURFACE         a shader pipeline CANNOT be exercised in this environment, so the
                                    wgpu half would have been unverifiable at the moment of writing —
                                    which is this campaign's recurring defect, not a shortcut avoided
```

So the projection and the layout are **pure functions with tests instead**: the camera round-trips over
all **576** tiles, a changed `grid.tilt` changes the projection (proving the parameter is not decoration),
and a headless render of the real view emits shapes and answers a click. **These are claims a shader would
not have made checkable.**

#### The three things the surface may not do

```text
1  it may not COMPUTE a control status. Every mechanical_status is copied from the view. status_colour
   has an explicit Unknown arm, so an unrecognised status renders as unknown rather than defaulting to
   green — the same rule as section 9.7's no-default-to-PUBLIC, applied to a colour. A default here is
   how a lens starts lying without anyone editing it.
2  it may not RESOLVE an open question. A monument shows the constraint and a fog region is DEFERRED.
   The attempt is a fog ticket, and resolution is a governed merge.
3  it may not PRESENT a partial measurement as a whole one. The C19 stamp is shown with its COVERAGE
   (`v1 · on 11/11 tickets`), because C19 requires every ticket to carry a version and a version alone
   is a claim where a version with its coverage is a measurement.
```

#### What it MAY do, and why that is not adjudication

`spatial_verdict` tests a tile against the `regions` array the view already carries. That is **geometry
over data**, and 3DUI.MD §4.3 assigns it to the surface outright. Three things keep it from creeping:

```text
it is NAMED SpatialVerdict, and every label carries the words "spatial only"
it carries a DISCLAIMER naming overlay.py adjudicate as the only adjudicator
the disclaimer is PAINTED ON THE CANVAS, because the canvas is what a screenshot shows
```

A wall beats a fog when both cover a tile — **refusal is the safer of two answers**, and a tile that is
both deferred and refused must not read as merely deferred.

#### Two consequences that are easy to get backwards

**A multi-civilian locus renders as FOG, not as a building.** Whose income, whose evidence, whose grade
is an open question (§30.2), and drawing it solid would answer that question with geometry.
**The risk layer R7–R11 is never folded into the controls C9–C20** (§7.2) — and a test asserts the *view*
keeps them in separate fields, so concatenating them would be a contract change rather than a rendering
choice.

#### The five defects, and the one that matters

Every one was found by **running** something, and none by reading — which is §13.3's standing lesson,
confirmed a fourth time.

```text
1  the governor stamp read a DICT'S KEYS        `of_type()` returns a dict keyed by record id, so
                                                iterating it yields IDS. `isinstance(t, dict)` was the
                                                guard and was False on all 11 tickets. It reported
                                                `0 of 11` — silently, plausibly, with every appearance
                                                of a measurement. A guard that can only ever return one
                                                value reads as rigour and is decoration (§6.4).
2  the view did not carry what the surface needs  the four BILLING-BASIS NAMES (§8.1) and the C19 stamp
                                                were absent. The renderer could have spelled doctrine
                                                for itself — the defect §31.1 names — or dropped the
                                                four-way split, which is the one thing C01's openness
                                                exists to make visible. Fixed at the source: a key the
                                                surface needs is a VIEW defect when missing.
3  the interaction test asserted `>=`           it passed whether the click worked or not. Tightened to
                                                `==`, it failed at once and revealed the real defect:
                                                it had been clicking a coordinate the layout never uses.
                                                The surface now REPORTS its own canvas geometry.
4  the marker guard tested a document too small   a two-key JSON literal fails on a MISSING FIELD, not on
                                                the marker. The fixture now mutates the real document.
5  twelve parsed fields were never displayed     including `identity_status`, which is PROCEDURAL on ALL
                                                TWELVE controls. The compiler called it a lint; the
                                                finding is that rule 100's second half — the half no
                                                mechanism in this stack can verify — was invisible in the
                                                surface built to show it.
```

**Finding FC-10, and it is about verification rather than about the surface.** The mechanical half of
this work was cheap: hashes, round-trips, counts, an exit code. **All five defects were in the half that
is not.** Four of the five were in this session's own machinery, and the fifth was a rendered
overstatement. The mechanical checks were correct throughout and would have passed a build that hid a
PROCEDURAL governance layer behind a green city.

> **FC-10: a surface's mechanical checks prove it is well-formed, never that it is honest. Where a
> surface is the deliverable, the assertion that matters is about what it DISPLAYS — and a display
> default is a governance decision made in code.**

### 31.10 Binding rules 117-119

```text
117. A surface may not hold one field it does not display. A parsed-but-unshown field is not a lint; it
     is the surface withholding the fact it was handed, and where the field is a governance fact
     (identity_status, a citation, a coverage figure) the omission is the overstatement. The compiler's
     unused-field warning is the cheapest possible detector of this and it is already free.
118. Every measurement a surface displays must carry the coverage or the denominator it is a fraction
     of. "governor v1" is a claim; "v1 on 11/11 tickets" is a measurement. This generalises section
     13.2's warning about the verify ratio and section 6.3 rule 2's open/closed board: a bare number
     invited the reader to supply the denominator themselves, and they will supply a favourable one.
119. A lens may refuse SPATIALLY and may never refuse GOVERNANCE-WISE. Testing a proposed tile against
     a region the view carries is geometry; computing whether a control passes is authority. The two are
     distinguished by NAME, by a disclaimer carried with the verdict, and by that disclaimer being
     painted where a screenshot can see it — because a surface's own refusal is the artifact most likely
     to be read as the governor's answer.
```
## 32. Pillar 10 continued — the city plan, mapped against the doctrine it renders

> **Evidence status: [V]** for every claim about this repository — the tick contract's nine properties, the
> occupancy registry, the two layout defects, and phases G0–G1 are held by tests that exist and pass. **[R]**
> for the commercial game whose mechanics are the map's left-hand column: those were read from the game's
> public wikis and guides, not from the game.
>
> **Sources: `CITY_MAP.md`** (the full map, sixteen mechanics) and `house.md`. `house.md` is cited for **one
> thing only** — building material layers for the locus blocks — and its own independence note is the reason
> it can be cited at all: it states that it "addresses physical building construction only" and "has no
> relationship to the civilian/agent governance layer". Using it as a civilian or housing schema would
> contradict the document it is being read from.

### 32.1 The inversion every city mechanic follows from

Cities: Skylines has five systems a player **writes**: zones, roads, service buildings, budgets and taxes, and
policies. **This stack has one authoring system, and it is not the player.** Policies *are* the doctrine here;
a player-authored policy would be a second authority plane, which §0.3 forbids by construction. So the map is
not "which feature do we build" but **which of the five the player writes, and what the rest become.**

| The game's system | What it becomes | The rule that forces it |
|---|---|---|
| **Policies** — per-district toggles, budgets | **the doctrine — read-only** | §0.3: the two planes must never merge |
| **Zoning** | **locus zoning** — six kinds, each anchored to a field that already exists | no housing schema exists and none may be invented |
| **Service buildings with coverage radii** | **service nodes as visual affordances** | a node shows where a control already applies; it never grants one |
| **Budgets and taxes** | four billing bases as a proposal while C01 is open; tax is a **wall** | C09: there is no stored balance. §30.3: tax is out of scope |
| **Milestones and population unlocks** | **reading further into the doctrine** | an unlock is a lens, never a lever |
| **Land purchase and tile expansion** | **a fact in the view** | buying is a marketplace transaction, and §30.3 walls it |

### 32.2 Five words that mean different things, and the rule that keeps them apart

A borrowed word carries its original authority with it, so the collisions are stated rather than left to be
inferred.

```text
policy    the game: a player-authored toggle      |  here: doctrine, changeable only by a governed merge
demand    the game: a modelled want for buildings |  here: nothing. `pending` proposals are the nearest fact
zone      the game: land use with density         |  here: a spatial affordance over existing fields
unlock    the game: new buildings and powers      |  here: a lens; the ability to see further
service   the game: a building that changes a result |  here: a marker over a status it did not compute
```

**A surface that displays a computed demand, a happiness scalar, or a policy toggle has already left the
lens**, and rule 6 (no scalar skill ratings), rule 3 (no digit without a metric) and §19.4 (only a merge
mutates doctrine) are the three that catch it.

### 32.3 The tick contract — what "the city runs automatically" is allowed to mean

```text
A TICK MAY:      re-read the derived view · interpolate display positions · advance the pulse ·
                 count what it did and report the counts
A TICK MAY NOT:  change a control status · assign or retire a civilian · stamp a ticket ·
                 write to the store, the doctrine, or the plan store except as a player proposal
```

**Nine properties, each held by a test that fails without it:**

| Property | Why it is a rule and not a preference |
|---|---|
| the clock runs by default, at 1 Hz | a city that holds still until a key is found is a city nobody sees move |
| a running clock requests repaint | egui draws on input; a clock that advanced only on pointer motion would not be a clock |
| a poll is a `(len, mtime)` comparison, never a hash | a poll is on the frame path; reading the whole file to decide whether to read the whole file is the wrong shape |
| the cadence follows the rate the player chose, floored at one tick | a rate rounded to zero would stop the city following its own store — a pause nobody asked for |
| a poll never reframes the camera; an explicit reload does | a poll runs every second or so, so reframing on it would fight the player on a timer |
| a poll that heals an error **announces** it | a city appearing with no message is a silent state change — the sign-flipped version of a failure nobody reports |
| a routine refresh does **not** announce | a toast every second is unreadable within a minute |
| a failed poll keeps the last good view | a half-written file is the normal state during a re-derive, not a fact about the store |
| a paused clock does not poll | a pause that still polls is not a pause |

**And the two time sources are deliberately separate.** The scene's animation follows the clock, so pausing
holds the aurora and the particles still. The amber `FAILED` pulse follows **wall time**, because a status
signal that freezes when the player pauses to read it is a warning that cannot be read.

**The producer half is `godplan/watch.py` [V].** Inputs move → re-derive → the view changes → the surface
notices on its next poll. It is a **watcher and not a scheduler**, because a scheduler fires whether or not
anything happened, which is a clock dressed as an event — the shape §9.3 rule 1 already rejects for readiness.
**And its output is excluded from its own inputs by identity**: the view is written into the plan store, and a
watcher that did not exclude it would see the file it just wrote and re-derive forever, which is the same
self-feeding-generator defect §21.10 records for the record appendix.

### 32.4 Layout is a checkable claim, and overlap is now a refusal

`regions.rs` is an **occupancy registry**: every painted control claims its rectangle, and a claim intersecting
an existing `Panel` or `Control` claim is **refused and reported**. Shared edges are adjacency, not overlap;
captions are exempt. Two defects had shipped under this: the bottom-bar palette **escaped its strip** at every
window narrower than about 1030 points, and the status toast overlapped the app bar.

**Rule for future work: a control that is not claimed is a control nobody can find.** A painter clips
silently, so the failure mode is not a visual glitch — it is a feature that reads as missing.

**And one correction to the plan itself, recorded because the direction matters:** a placement test failed
asserting two 400×300 panels could be disjoint inside a 1000×700 area with the first centred. **The test was
wrong, not the function** — the second panel would need `left >= 700`, which is 100 points past the edge. It
was verified by independent arithmetic before the assertion changed, because a weakened test and a corrected
one are indistinguishable from the diff alone.

### 32.5 Citizen geometry, and the document that was checked for it

**Silver cylinders, ball heads, hands, Frutiger Aero: [V].** `gpu/mesh.rs` builds a six-part figure — body,
head, arms, ball hands — ramped against the **assembled** figure so the seams match, and `city.wgsl` carries
the silver as named constants in `theme.rs` rather than sampled values. `house.md` was re-read for this and
says nothing about citizens; it supplies building layers, which is what it is for.

## 33. The idle job layer — an authorized fiction, and the seven refusals that keep it one

> **Evidence status: [V] for the vocabulary and the refusals as specifications; the layer itself is
> AUTHORIZED AND UNBUILT.** `[R]` for the incremental genre's conventions, which are the map's left-hand
> column. Authorized by operator decision, recorded here as doctrine so that the authorization travels with
> the feature rather than being remembered.

### 33.1 The two readings, and which one is authorized

*"Fake jobs"* has two readings and only one is buildable.

```text
(a) a job that PRETENDS to be real   its output becomes an income record, a grade, a ticket, a claim
                                     -> FORBIDDEN. Rule 3, rule 98, section 7.1, rule 60.
(b) a job that is a DECLARED FICTION  nothing is asserted; the numbers are labelled where they appear,
                                     and no path exists from fiction to a record
                                     -> AUTHORIZED by this section
```

**The precedent is §9.7, twice, and both are the same move.** `DRAFT` needs no authorization to produce
because its output is *non-publishable by construction*; `WRITE_EXTERNAL` is `implemented: false` because
*absence is stronger than a gate — there is no code path to call*. **A declared fiction is `DRAFT` applied to
a number.** Its refusals are therefore written as **absences of a path**, not as validations downstream,
because a validation is a place a future edit can move and an absent path is not.

> **What is authorized is a fiction that cannot be believed by accident. What is forbidden is a fiction that
> can.**

### 33.2 The genre, mapped

| Incremental convention `[R]` | Here | The rule that shapes it |
|---|---|---|
| cookies per second | **`idle_yield`** — a view-side rational, computed at derive time, stored nowhere | rule 3: a number needs a source; its source is a closed table and a tick count |
| buildings that produce | **an idle job** — anchored to a **named existing civilian** | fiction hangs off a real record or it is nothing |
| upgrades that multiply | **lens multipliers** — cosmetic and additive only | a multiplier may never unlock a control, a grade or an authority |
| prestige / reset | **a fiction generation counter**; **no record is deleted** | rule 1, §2.2: history is append-only |
| golden cookies | **a tick bonus** — visible, fictional, unbanked | a marketplace is a wall (§30.3); it is not money |
| offline progress | **REFUSED** — see 33.3 | a fiction advancing unattended is indistinguishable from a store that changed |
| achievements | **milestones** — a lens, never a lever | §10.1 of the overlay plan |
| number-go-up as the reward | **the tick becoming visible** | the reward is that a still screen moves: a rendering fact, not a claim |

### 33.3 The one mechanic that cannot come across

Every incremental game banks progress while you are away. **Here it is refused, and the reason is not
balance.**

`AGENTS.md` §32.3 already holds the other half: a paused clock does not poll, so a paused surface is one that
has stopped asking. If idle jobs accrued during that pause, the surface would report *paused* while the
numbers moved, and the only way to tell "the fiction advanced" from "the season moved" would be the message
line. **A fiction that produces changes nobody watched is a fiction that gets believed.**

```text
accrual happens on a tick the clock actually ran, and on no other tick. No wall clock is consulted
anywhere — the same rule that removed `generated_at` (§16.1).
```

### 33.4 The marking rule — a fiction must be structurally marked, not described

```text
1  the ID          every id carries the `idle_` prefix, so it cannot collide with a record type
2  the VIEW FIELD  carried under `idle_jobs`, never under `loci` or `jobs`
3  the SURFACE     rendered with the fiction glyph, and the HUD names the count separately from loci
4  the REFUSAL     every boundary in 33.5 refuses it BY TYPE, not by a value check
```

**Marking 4 is rule 58's shape, applied to a number.** A record may *contain* instruction-shaped text and the
system represents it as data in a field; an idle yield may be *number-shaped* like a metric, and the system
represents it as fiction in a field. **The boundaries refuse the type rather than trusting the value**, because
a value check is exactly what a future edit relaxes.

### 33.5 The seven refusals

| # | Refusal | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | an idle job **cannot reach an `income_*` record** | income is a governed type with a verifier; §9.6 rule 1 — a dollar is not income until a receipt cites it, and nothing about an idle yield is a receipt |
| 2 | it **cannot produce a ticket, a grade, a promotion, a retirement, or a resume claim** | those are the five things that carry forward, and a fiction that carries forward is reading as evidence |
| 3 | it **cannot be a control**, and cannot acquire a status | C9–C20 apply to actors; `NOT_EVALUABLE` is the identity half of a *real* control, not a slot for fiction |
| 4 | an idle yield **cannot enter a metric, a resume, or a bill** | §7.11 admits a metric only with `source_artifact`, `measurement_method`, `time_window` and `unit` — fiction has none, so it is inadmissible **by the schema**, not by review |
| 5 | it **cannot accrue while the clock is paused**, and never consults wall time | §32.3: a pause that still polls is not a pause |
| 6 | an idle job **with no named kind** is refused | the closed four-member set exists so an unnamed basis is refusable — the same reason `BILLING_BASES` exists |
| 7 | an idle job **naming a civilian that does not exist** is refused | fiction hangs off a real record. Otherwise the ward fills with citizens nobody authorized — the genesis problem wearing a cosmetic hat |

**Refusal 7 is the one that would have been missed, and it is the one that matters.** A clicker's natural
growth path is *more producers*, and the cheapest producer to add is an invented person. **The ward cannot grow
by fiction**: every idle job cites an existing `civilian_*`, so the count of idle jobs is bounded by the count
of real civilians.

### 33.6 What it unlocks, and the one question that settles a proposed unlock

```text
MAY UNLOCK      a lens · cosmetic substrate on existing loci · the fiction share of the billing pie ·
                a visible tick
MAY NEVER       authority · a control status · a grade · a promotion · a retirement · an income basis ·
UNLOCK          a resume claim · a metric · a decision node's resolution
```

**The test, asked mechanically: does reaching it change what any actor is permitted to do?** If yes it is
authority, and authority cannot be earned by a number going up — rule 68 (no side effect without explicit
authorization) and rule 76 (no stage grants the authority of the next) are the two that catch it. If no, it is
a lens and it may be unlocked.

### 33.7 Why the fiction lives in the tick, and the ordering that follows

The watcher re-derives when the **store** moves. Idle jobs move **without the store moving** — the point, and
also the danger, since they are the one thing on screen that changes with no record behind it. So the ordering
is fixed, and it is the reverse of what a clicker would do:

```text
WRONG:  a tick increments idle yields and the producer writes the plan store to show it
RIGHT:  a tick advances the CLOCK; the surface re-reads the view; idle yields are a function of the
        tick the view was derived at
```

In the wrong version the producer writes to the plan store every tick for a fictional reason and the watcher
fires forever on its own output. In the right one, **the view is a pure function of `(store, plan, tick)`**,
the producer writes only when the store or the plan changed, and the surface interpolates the rest — which is
exactly why a display tick is allowed to exist. **An idle yield is therefore not a record of anything having
happened, and cannot be — which is the whole authorization.**

### 33.8 The binding rules added by these two sections

```text
120. A surface reports; it never adjudicates. A control status it displays is COPIED from the view, never
     computed. An unrecognised status renders as UNKNOWN and never as MET.
121. No trend, demand, or desirability surface may be displayed unless a doctrine source computes it. No
     demand meter, and no happiness scalar, exists or may exist (rule 6, rule 3).
122. A tick may re-read, interpolate, animate and count. It may not change a status, assign or retire a
     civilian, stamp a ticket, or write anything but a player's own proposal.
123. A paused clock does not poll and accrues nothing. A running clock is the only thing that advances
     anything automatic, and no wall clock is consulted by any derived artifact.
124. A poll is a cheap stat comparison and never a content hash, and it must be able to miss a same-length
     edit inside one timestamp resolution — the cost of a miss is a late re-derive, never a wrong view.
125. An automatic re-read never reframes the player's camera and never re-announces a routine refresh. It
     DOES announce a recovery, because a state change with no message is the sign-flipped version of a
     failure nobody reports.
126. A failed poll keeps the last good artifact. A half-written file is the normal state during a
     re-derivation, not a fact about the store.
127. A producer's OUTPUT is excluded from its own INPUTS by identity, never by pattern. A generator whose
     output feeds its input does not converge, and it fails by looking busy.
128. Every control that is painted claims its rectangle, and an overlapping claim is refused and reported.
     Sharing an edge is adjacency, not overlap. A painter clips silently, so an unclaimed control reads as
     a missing feature rather than as a layout defect.
129. A fiction is authorized only as a DECLARED fiction: nothing it produces may be asserted. Its refusals
     are written as the absence of a path, never as a downstream validation.
130. An idle job cannot reach an income record, produce a ticket, a grade, a promotion, a retirement or a
     resume claim, be a control, or enter a metric, a resume or a bill. Inadmissibility is BY SCHEMA.
131. A fiction is structurally marked in four places: its id prefix, its own view field, its own surface glyph,
     and a refusal BY TYPE at every boundary. A value check is what a future edit relaxes.
132. An idle job names an existing record or it is refused. A fiction that can invent its own subjects lets
     the ward grow by fiction, which is the genesis problem wearing a cosmetic hat.
133. A fiction cannot accrue while paused. A fiction that produces changes nobody watched is a fiction that
     gets believed.
134. An unlock is a lens, never a lever. The test is mechanical: does reaching it change what any actor is
     permitted to do? If yes, it is authority and a counter may not earn it.
135. A word borrowed from another domain carries that domain's authority with it. Where a collision exists
     — policy, demand, zone, unlock, service — the collision is stated, and the borrowed word never enters
     the schema meaning both things at once.
```

    # CITY_MAP — the civilian city, mapped mechanic by mechanic against `AGENTS.md`

    **What this is.** A worked map from one commercial city-builder's feature set onto this stack's doctrine,
    one row per mechanic, each stating **what the doctrine makes possible, what it forbids, and what the overlay
    must therefore do instead.** It exists because the alternative is a city builder that slowly grows
    authority it was never granted — and the growth is invisible, because every step looks like a feature.

    **Companion documents.** `3DUI.MD` (the overlay's own design, `civilian-overlay:city`) ·
    `Civilians_lifestyle_UI_Implementation_plan.md` (the fact-check of `3DUI.MD`) · `house.md` (building
    construction layers and material markup) · `AGENTS.md` (§27–§31, rules 86–119) · `Civilians.md` (the
    source the civilian pillar was migrated from).

    **Marker key.** `[V]` verified against a read artifact · `[R]` reported by a source, not confirmed here ·
    `[O]` open, or a proposal this document does not decide.

    ---

    ## 0. The one inversion everything else follows from

    Cities: Skylines has **five interlocking authoring systems**, and every one of them is a thing a player
    *writes*: zones, roads, service buildings, budgets and taxes, and **policies**. `[R]` — read from the game's
    public wikis and beginner's guides, which describe them as player-authored by construction.

    This stack has **one authoring system**, and it is not the player: only a **governed merge** changes doctrine
    (rule 60, §19.4). So the mapping is not "which feature do we build" but **"which of the five does the player
    get to write, and what does the sixth become."**

    | Cities: Skylines | This stack | Why the mapping is forced |
    |---|---|---|
    | **Policies** (the player's rulebook: per-district toggles, service budgets) | **Doctrine — read-only** | Policies *are* §27–§31 here. A player-authored policy would be a second authority plane, which §0.3 forbids by construction: *the two planes must never merge.* |
    | **Zoning** | **Locus zoning** — 6 kinds, all derived from fields that already exist | The player assigns *spatial affordance*, never a civilian. `job`, `state`, `grade`, `income_basis`, `autonomy` |
    | **Service buildings with coverage radii** | **Service nodes as visual affordances** (§5.3, FC-3D-02) | A node **shows** where a control already applies. It never grants authority — placing one creates no permission |
    | **Budgets and taxes** | **Four billing bases, as a proposal** while C01 is open; tax is an **out-of-scope wall** (§30.3) | C09 answered: there is no stored balance. C01 open: no settled rate exists to set |
    | **Milestones / population unlocks** | **Reading further into the doctrine** (§10.1) | An unlock here is a *lens*, not a lever. Nothing the player reaches grants new power |
    | **Land purchase / tile expansion** | **The grid is a fact in the view** (§3.1) | Buying land is a resource transaction, and §30.3 walls the marketplace. The grid grows when the store says it grew |

    > **The city is a rendering of what the doctrine already permits.** Every mechanic below is either a
    > *projection* of a value that already exists, or it is a wall.

    ---

    ### 1.6 Where the game's own vocabulary collides with this stack's

    Four words mean different things in each, and only one direction is safe. This table exists because a
    borrowed word carries its original authority with it.

    | Word | In Cities: Skylines | In this stack | The rule |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **policy** | a player-authored toggle | doctrine; changeable only by governed merge | Never render a policy as a control *or* a control as a policy |
    | **demand** | a modelled want for more buildings | nothing — `pending` proposals are the nearest fact | Never display a computed demand |
    | **zone** | land use, with density | a spatial affordance over existing fields | A zone assigns no one and builds nothing |
    | **unlock** | new buildings and powers | a lens; the ability to *see* further | An unlock that grants power is a §19.4 violation |
    | **service** | a building that changes outcomes | a visual marker over an existing status | A node that changes a status is adjudicating |

    ## 2. The tick contract — what "the system runs automatically" is allowed to mean

    The requirement was: *allow the system to automatically run as ticks progress.* For a read-only lens the
    set of legal automatic acts is small, and stating it exactly is what keeps the city from becoming a second
    simulator.

    ```text
    A TICK MAY:      re-read the derived view; interpolate display positions; advance the pulse;
                     count what it did and report the counts.
    A TICK MAY NOT:  change a control status; assign or retire a civilian; stamp a ticket;
                     write to the store, the doctrine, or the plan store except as a player proposal.
    ```

    `[V]` — implemented and held by tests:

    | Element | Where | Held by |
    |---|---|---|
    | **The clock runs by default at 1 Hz** | `controls.rs`, `Clock::default` | `a_running_clock_polls_and_a_paused_one_does_not` |
    | **A frame requests repaint while running**, so the city advances with no input | `surface.rs::render` | the same |
    | **A poll is a `(len, mtime)` comparison**, never a hash — a poll runs on the frame path | `city.rs::file_stamp`, `stamp_differs` | `an_unknown_stamp_polls_rather_than_assumes`, `a_matching_stamp_needs_no_read_and_a_different_one_does` |
    | **The cadence follows the chosen rate**, floored at one tick | `city.rs::poll_interval_ticks` | `a_poll_interval_never_rounds_down_to_zero`, `the_poll_cadence_follows_the_clock_the_player_chose` |
    | **A poll never reframes the player's camera**; an explicit reload does | `surface.rs::adopt(announce, adopt_camera)` | `a_tick_driven_reload_keeps_the_camera_the_player_set` |
    | **A poll that heals an error announces it**; a routine refresh does not | `surface.rs::poll_view` | `the_message_states_are_distinguishable…` |
    | **A failed poll keeps the last good view** — a half-written file is a normal state mid-re-derive | `surface.rs::poll_view` | the same |
    | **Polls and reloads are counted separately** | `Telemetry::polls`, `::auto_reloads` | `the_message_states…` |
    | **A paused clock does not poll** | `render`'s `running && poll_due()` | `a_running_clock_polls_and_a_paused_one_does_not` |

    **The pausing asymmetry, stated because it is a real design decision rather than an oversight:** the scene's
    animation time comes from the clock, so pausing holds the aurora and the particles still — but the amber
    `FAILED` pulse deliberately runs on **wall time**, because a status signal that freezes when the player pauses
    to read it is a warning you cannot read. Two time sources, two stated jobs.

    **What is not yet automatic, and is the next thing:** the *producer* side. The surface follows the file; the
    file is re-derived by `python overlay.py view` and nothing yet runs that on a schedule. §4 phase G1 is that
    ticket.

    ## 3. The layout, as it now stands

    The user-visible requirement was that **buttons and interactions do not overlap**, which is a claim about
    geometry and therefore checkable rather than assertable.

    `[V]` — `regions.rs` is an occupancy registry: every painted control **claims** its rectangle, and a claim
    that intersects an existing `Panel` or `Control` claim is **refused and reported**, not silently absorbed.

    | Property | Implementation | Test |
    |---|---|---|
    | Two interactive claims may not share pixels | `Regions::claim` returns false and records the pair | `two_interactive_claims_may_not_share_pixels` |
    | Sharing an edge is adjacency, not overlap | a 0.5-point tolerance | `adjacent_controls_are_not_overlapping` |
    | Captions may overlap anything | `ClaimKind::Readout` is exempt | `a_readout_may_overlap_anything` |
    | A control that leaves its own strip is reported | `Regions::escapes` | `a_claim_that_escapes_its_container_is_reported` |
    | Floating panels are **exclusive**, not stacked | geometric: 900×560 and 760×520 cannot both fit a 1400-pt column | `placement_avoids_what_is_already_there` |
    | When no disjoint placement exists, the least-overlap one wins | `place`'s fallback | `when_no_disjoint_placement_exists_the_least_overlapping_one_wins` |

    **Two defects this found, both of which had shipped:**

    1. **The bottom bar's palette escaped its strip** at every window narrower than ~1030 points. A painter
       clips silently, so it read as a missing feature rather than as a layout defect.
    2. **The status toast overlapped the app bar**, because it was placed against the window rather than against
       the scene column.

    **And one correction to the map itself:** the disjointness assertion in `placement_avoids_what_is_already_there`
    **failed**, and the test was wrong rather than the function — two 400×300 panels in a 1000×700 area have no
    disjoint placement once the first is centred. That was verified by independent arithmetic before the
    assertion changed, because a weakened test and a corrected one are indistinguishable from the diff alone.

    **Citizen geometry, checked against the operator's brief.** Silver cylinders, ball heads and hands,
    Frutiger Aero: `[V]` — `gpu/mesh.rs` builds a six-part figure (body, head, arms, ball hands) ramped
    against the assembled figure so the seams match, and `city.wgsl` carries the silver as named constants in
    `theme.rs` rather than sampled values. `house.md` was re-read for this: it is a **building** document —
    foundation, framing, roof, material markup — with an explicit independence note that it has no relationship
    to the civilian layer and excludes any dwelling/capacity/quality tier schema. It is therefore a legitimate
    source for **what a locus block is made of** (§4, phase G4) and has nothing to say about citizens.

    ## 4. The build plan — full city builder feature set

    Ordered by dependency, each phase gated by a **refusal test** (rule 44: a mitigation is not implemented
    until a test fails without it). Nothing here grants the surface an ability it does not have.

    | # | Phase | Deliverable | Gate |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **G0** | **Layout integrity** | `regions.rs` occupancy registry; exclusive floats; toast inside the column; palette wrapping | ✅ **done** — 6 tests, 2 real defects fixed |
    | **G1** | **Auto-derive on a schedule** | The producer side of the tick: a watcher that runs `overlay.py view` when store records change, so the city moves with no player act | ✅ **surface half done** (poll + clock). **Producer open**: the watcher does not exist |
    | **G2** | **Avatar motion between loci** | Interpolate a civilian's display position between its `current locus` and its destination, driven by the display tick, with no state transition invented | A test that a tick with no view change moves **nothing** |
    | **G3** | **Locus blocks from real fields** | Boxes instanced from `loci`, height from the grade ladder step, kanji decals per locus kind | A test that a locus kind with no doctrine source renders as **fog**, not as a guessed block |
    | **G4** | **Materials from `house.md`** | The layer taxonomy (site → foundation → floor → wall → roof) as the locus block's vertical material stack; the markup legend (CONC, CMU, OSB, WRB, IGU) as the kanji-decal vocabulary | A test that no material is emitted for a layer the store does not evidence |
    | **G5** | **Control volumes C9–C20** | Translucent instanced volumes, `MET` green / `FAILED` amber pulse / `NOT_EVALUABLE` grey wireframe, baseline `8 / 1 / 4` | A test that an unrecognised status renders **unknown**, never green (already the rule in `city.rs`) |
    | **G6** | **Residual-risk layer R7–R11** | A separate overlay, never folded into C9–C20; toggle `G` | A test that a risk can never render as a control status |
    | **G7** | **Never-granted gates** | Five red arches — `create_account`, `enter_credentials`, `move_money`, `accept_terms`, `sign_contract` | A test that a proposal needing one is **escalated**, never silently skipped (§9.6 rule 3) |
    | **G8** | **Out-of-scope walls** | Slabs for tax 税, guild 組, reputation 評, marketplace 市; zoning across one is refused **with a citation** | A test that a rejection carries the citation string |
    | **G9** | **Fog of war** | §30.2 fog volumes; zoning a fog tile is `Deferred { ticket }`, not accepted | A test that fog is **not pre-sliced** into answers |
    | **G10** | **Decision nodes** | C01–C12 / I1–I4 monuments in the HIG arc; answered bodies steady, open ones pulsing | A test that no node can be resolved by the player |
    | **G11** | **The four-way billing pie** | Allocation across the four `BILLING_BASES`; never collapsed to one number | A test that an allocation with no `basis` is refused |
    | **G12** | **Authority paths + particles** | Ribbon geometry between loci; a path carrying a never-granted action shows a red gate | A test that a path adds no authority |
    | **G13** | **Wayfinder export** | A read-only situation digest; regenerating an unchanged store produces **byte-identical** output | `test_regenerating_the_view_CONVERGES` — already the discipline |
    | **G14** | **Adjudicator as a pure function** | `(proposal, doctrine_hash, store_hash) → Adjudication`, tested over N random proposals for determinism | A property test, plus a test that it **never mutates its inputs** |
    | **G15** | **Doctrine landing** | §32 for the map and rules, register rows measured from the store, then rebuild and verify derivation | `migrate.py status` reports derived, **0 drift, 0 stale** |

    **G1's producer half is the next ticket, and it is the one that makes the requirement literal.** The surface
    already notices a change within one poll interval; nothing yet *makes* the change. The design that fits the
    doctrine is a **watcher**, not a scheduler: it observes the season's record files and re-derives the view when
    they move. A scheduler would tick whether or not anything happened, which is a clock pretending to be an
    event, and §9.3 rule 1 already rejects that shape for readiness.

    ## 5. What this map refuses to claim

    - **No performance number is asserted.** `3DUI.MD` §13.2's draw-call and avatar targets are aspirations; the
      register marks them `[V] when measured`, and none is measured here.
    - **No claim that the city is a simulation.** It is a view over a store, and the display tick is animation.
    - **No claim that the wiring is complete.** G1's producer, G2–G14 and G15 are not built. The tick contract in
      §2 is built and tested; the feature list below it is a plan.
    - **The game's mechanics are reported, not verified.** Every left-hand column in §1 is `[R]`. What is `[V]`
      is what this repository does with each one.
    - **`house.md`'s independence note is load-bearing and is quoted rather than paraphrased:** it addresses
      physical construction only, and has no relationship to Pillar 9, the civilian store, C9–C20, R7–R11, or any
      locus/housing metaphor. Using it as a *material* source for locus blocks is consistent with that note;
      using it as a source for civilian or housing schema would not be.

    # PLAN_JOBS — the idle job layer, and the authorization it needs

    **What this is.** A second plan, next to `CITY_MAP.md`, for giving civilians **jobs that yield while you
    watch** — the Cookie Clicker / incremental shape. It exists as its own document because the first word in
    the request, *fake*, names the exact thing this stack is built to refuse, and a feature that cannot state
    why it is allowed is a feature that will drift into being believed.

    **Companions.** `CITY_MAP.md` (the city plan, §2 the tick contract, §4 G0–G15) · `3DUI.MD` §6.3 (citizens
    do not act autonomously in the game) · `AGENTS.md` §1, §7, §9.7, §19.4, §27–§31 · `Civilians.md`.

    **Markers.** `[V]` verified against a read artifact · `[R]` reported · `[O]` open or proposed.

    ---

    ## 0. The authorization problem, stated before the design

    *"Fake jobs"* has two readings and only one of them is buildable.

    | Reading | Shape | Verdict |
    |---|---|---|
    | **(a) A job that pretends to be real** — its output becomes an income record, a grade, a ticket, a resume claim | The fiction reaches the record and is later cited as evidence | **FORBIDDEN.** Rule 3 (no digit without a metric), rule 98 (regression is not a promotion), §7.1 (the evidence record is the source of truth), rule 60 (only a merge mutates doctrine). This is the defect the stack exists to prevent, and it is the one that would be introduced by a well-meaning feature |
    | **(b) A declared fiction** — a game layer whose outputs are non-authoritative **by construction**, marked as fiction, and refused at every boundary where fiction could become a claim | Nothing is asserted. The numbers are labelled as what they are, everywhere they appear | **AUTHORIZED by this plan**, and this document *is* the authorization |

    **The precedent is already in the file, twice, and both are the same move.**

    ```text
    DRAFT (§9.7)                     no authorization needed to produce; output is NON-PUBLISHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION
    WRITE_EXTERNAL (§9.7)            implemented: false — "absence is stronger than a gate, because there is
                                     no code path to call"
    ```

    **A declared fiction is `DRAFT` applied to a number.** Its output is non-authoritative not because a check
    rejects it somewhere downstream, but because **there is no path from it to a record, an income row, a grade,
    a promotion or a claim.** That is why §3's seven refusals are written as *structural* absences rather than as
    validations, and why the tests assert the absence of a path rather than the presence of a guard.

    > **What this plan authorizes is a fiction that cannot be believed by accident. What it forbids is a fiction
    > that can.**

    ---

    ## 1. The genre, mapped term by term

    Everything the incremental genre is made of, and what each becomes here. `[R]` for the left column — the
    genre's conventions, read from the games and their wikis, not from a specification.

    | Incremental convention | This stack's term | The rule that shapes it |
    |---|---|---|
    | **Cookies per second** — a yield that accrues on a tick | **`idle_yield`** — a *view-side* rational, computed at derive time, stored nowhere | Rule 3: a number must have a source. Its source is a closed table and a tick count, both of which are stated |
    | **Buildings that produce** | **an idle job** — a locus where a *named existing civilian* is assigned, from a **closed 4-member table** | An idle job hangs off a real record or it is nothing (§3 refusal 7) |
    | **Upgrades that multiply output** | **lens multipliers** — cosmetic and additive only | A multiplier may never unlock a control, a grade, or an authority. §1 of `CITY_MAP.md`: an unlock is a lens, not a lever |
    | **Prestige / reset** | **a fiction generation counter** — the fiction restarts, **no record is deleted** | Rule 1 / §2.2: history is append-only. A "reset" that removed a civilian would be the one unforgivable write |
    | **Golden cookies / random bonuses** | **a tick bonus** — visible, fictional, unbanked | No financial semantics: it is not money, because a marketplace is a wall (§30.3) |
    | **Offline progress** (accruing while closed) | **REFUSED** | See §1.1 — this is the genre's one mechanic that is incompatible here, and the incompatibility is load-bearing |
    | **Achievement multipliers** | **milestones** — already §10.1 of `3DUI.MD` | A milestone opens a lens; it never grants power |
    | **Number-go-up as the reward** | **the tick becoming visible** | The honest reward here is that a still screen moves. That is a *rendering* fact, not a claim |

    ### 1.1 The one mechanic that cannot come across, and why it is the interesting one

    Every incremental game banks progress while you are away. **Here that is refused, and the reason is not
    balance — it is that a fiction advancing unattended is indistinguishable from a store that changed.**

    `CITY_MAP.md` §2 already holds the other half of this: a paused clock does not poll, so a paused surface is
    one that has stopped asking. If idle jobs accrued during that pause, the surface would report *paused* while
    the numbers moved — and the only way for a player to tell "the fiction advanced" from "the season moved" is
    the message line. **A fiction that produces changes nobody watched is a fiction that gets believed.**

    ```text
    accrual happens on a tick the clock actually ran, and on no other tick.
    ```

    `[V]` — this is enforceable against the machinery that already exists: the producer derives from the store,
    the store carries the tick count it was derived at, and the surface's clock is the only thing that advances.
    No wall-clock is consulted anywhere, which is the same rule that removed `generated_at` (§16.1).

    ### 1.2 Where the fiction is marked, and the marking rule

    A declared fiction must be **structurally** marked, not merely described. Four markings, all required:

    ```text
    1  the ID            every id carries the `idle_` prefix, so no prefix-collision with a real record type
    2  the VIEW FIELD    carried in `view.json` under `idle_jobs`, never under `loci` or `jobs`
    3  the SURFACE       rendered with the Ｆ (fiction) glyph on the block, and the HUD names the count
    4  the REFUSAL        every boundary in §3 refuses it BY TYPE, not by a value check
    ```

    **Marking rule 4 is the one that matters**, and it is rule 58's shape: *a record may contain
    instruction-shaped text, and the system represents that as data in a field.* An idle yield may be
    number-shaped like a metric; the system represents it as fiction in a field, and the boundaries refuse the
    type rather than trusting the value.

    ---

    ## 2. The shape

    ```python
    @dataclass(frozen=True)
    class IdleJob:
        idle_id: str            # `idle_<kind>_<civilian>_<n>` — prefixed, per §1.2 marking 1
        kind: IdleKind          # a CLOSED 4-member set, so an unnamed basis is REFUSED (mirrors §8.1)
        civilian_id: str        # must name an existing record, or the job is refused (§3 refusal 7)
        tile: tuple[int, int]   # a locus in the ward; never a dwelling — no housing schema exists
        base_yield: int         # from a closed table, per kind. An integer: no float arithmetic (§17 rule 26)
        assigned_at_tick: int   # the clock tick, never a timestamp
        lens: str               # which milestone's lens made this visible — a reading, not a grant

    class IdleKind(Enum):
        ATTEST   = "attest"      # 証 idle attestation — yields against an existing evidence locus
        WITNESS  = "witness"     # 監 idle witness     — yields against an existing verifier
        TALLY    = "tally"       # 計 idle tally       — yields against an existing ticket registry
        STEWARD  = "steward"     # 守 idle steward     — yields against an existing retirement record
    ```

    Four kinds, and **every one of them names a thing that already exists.** That is the whole design: an idle
    job is a *fiction hung off a real record*, so it has a visible anchor in the store and cannot float free.
    An idle job whose anchor is absent is refused, not defaulted — which is the same refusal §8.1 makes for an
    income record with no named basis.

    **Yields are integers, and computed as `base_yield * ticks_assigned`.** No compounding, no floats, no
    randomness: a fiction whose number is hard to predict is a fiction that invites a testing harness, and the
    only thing worth testing about it is that it stays out of the records.

    ---

    ## 3. The seven refusals — each one the absence of a path

    Written as absences rather than validations, because a validation is a place a future edit can move and an
    absent path is not. Each is held by a test that fails if the path appears.

    | # | Refusal | Why |
    |---|---|---|
    | **1** | An idle job **cannot produce or reach an `income_*` record** | Income is a governed record type with a verifier (§9.6 rule 1: a dollar is not income until a receipt cites it). Nothing about an idle yield is a receipt |
    | **2** | An idle job **cannot produce a ticket, a grade, a promotion, a retirement or a resume claim** | Those are the five things that carry forward. A fiction that carries forward is reading as evidence |
    | **3** | An idle job **cannot be a control** and cannot acquire a status | C9–C20 apply to actors. `NOT_EVALUABLE` is for the identity half of a real control; it is not a slot for fiction |
    | **4** | An idle yield **cannot enter a metric, a resume, or a bill** | §7.11: a metric is admissible only with `source_artifact`, `measurement_method`, `time_window`, `unit`. Fiction has none of the four, so it is inadmissible *by the schema* rather than by review |
    | **5** | An idle job **cannot accrue while the clock is paused**, and never consults wall time | §1.1. The surface's own pause must mean the city is stopped |
    | **6** | An idle job with **no named kind** is refused | The four-member set exists precisely so an unnamed basis is refusable — the same reason `BILLING_BASES` exists |
    | **7** | An idle job naming **a civilian that does not exist** is refused | Fiction hangs off a real record. Otherwise the ward fills with citizens nobody authorized, which is the genesis problem (§27.2) wearing a cosmetic hat |

    **Refusal 7 is the one that would have been missed**, and it is the one that matters most: a clicker game's
    natural growth path is *more producers*, and the cheapest way to add a producer is to invent a person. Every
    idle job therefore cites an existing `civilian_*`, and the count of idle jobs is bounded by the count of real
    civilians. **The ward cannot grow by fiction.**

    ---

    ## 4. What it unlocks, and what it must never unlock

    ```text
    MAY UNLOCK      a lens (more of the ward legible), cosmetic substrate on existing loci,
                    the fiction share of the billing pie, a visible tick
    MAY NEVER       authority · a control status · a grade · a promotion · a retirement ·
    UNLOCK          an income basis · a resume claim · a metric · a decision node's resolution
    ```

    The test of a proposed unlock, and it is one question: **does reaching it change what any actor is permitted
    to do?** If yes, it is authority and it cannot be earned by a number going up. If no, it is a lens and it may
    be.

    ---

    ## 5. The tick connection — why this belongs with `CITY_MAP.md` G1

    The watcher (`godplan/watch.py`, built) re-derives the view when the store moves. Idle jobs move **without
    the store moving**, which is the point and also the danger: they are the one thing on screen that changes
    with no record behind it.

    So the ordering is fixed, and it is the reverse of what a clicker game would do:

    ```text
    WRONG:  a tick increments idle yields, and the view is re-derived to show it
    RIGHT:  a tick advances the CLOCK; the surface re-reads the view; the view's idle yields are a
            function of the tick the view was derived at
    ```

    In the wrong version the producer would write to the plan store every tick for a fictional reason, and the
    watcher would fire forever on its own output. In the right one, **the view is a pure function of
    `(store, plan, tick)`**, the producer writes only when the store or the plan changed, and the surface
    interpolates the rest — which is exactly `3DUI.MD` §7.3's display tick, and exactly why that tick is allowed
    to exist.

    **Consequence worth stating: the fiction lives in the tick, and the tick is display.** An idle yield is
    therefore not a record of anything having happened, and cannot be — which is the whole authorization.

    ---

    ## 6. Phases

    | # | Phase | Deliverable | Gate |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **J0** | **This authorization** | This document, landed as doctrine (§33) with the refusals as numbered rules | A test that the rules exist and are numbered |
    | **J1** | **`IdleKind` + `IdleJob` in the view model** | Four kinds, closed; `idle_jobs` a separate top-level view key | Refusal 6: an unnamed kind is refused |
    | **J2** | **The anchor check** | Every idle job cites an existing `civilian_*`; the id count is bounded by real civilians | Refusal 7, with a negative control: an idle job naming a ghost civilian must fail |
    | **J3** | **The absence suite** | Tests asserting there is **no path** from an idle yield to income, ticket, grade, promotion, retirement, claim, metric or bill | Refusals 1–4. Each test asserts the *absence*, and the negative control writes the path deliberately and watches it fail |
    | **J4** | **Tick-driven yields** | `base_yield * ticks_assigned`, derived from the tick the view was derived at; no wall clock, no randomness, integers only | Refusal 5: a paused clock accrues nothing |
    | **J5** | **The Ｆ marking** | The surface renders idle blocks with the fiction glyph; the HUD names the count separately from loci | A test that an idle block is never counted in `loci` |
    | **J6** | **The fiction share of the pie** | The billing pie gains a labelled fiction wedge that is **explicitly not a basis** — it cannot be allocated to | A test that allocating to it is refused |
    | **J7** | **Lens-only unlocks** | The question in §4 asked mechanically: an unlock that changes a permission is refused | A test that no idle yield is an input to any adjudication |

    **J3 is the phase that decides whether the feature is honest**, and it is the reason J0 exists separately: the
    refusals are the specification, and the implementation is the part that could get them wrong.

    ---

    ## 7. What this plan does not do

    - **It does not make an idle job a job.** `job_*` records already exist, are governed, and carry an autonomy
      mode, a supervisor and an end reason (`3DUI.MD` §15.1). An idle job is a *fiction hung off* a real record
      and shares none of those fields. Two objects for one word is a defect; the word is therefore **idle job**,
      always, and `job` alone still means the governed record.
    - **It does not authorize income.** An idle yield is not money, and no arithmetic converts it into any.
      `per_closed_job` remains one of the four real bases, and `per_closed_job` means a *closed* job with a
      retirement record — not an idle counter.
    - **It does not claim the yields are measured.** No register row may carry an idle number as a measurement;
      the only registered facts about this layer are its **refusals**, which are checkable.
    - **It does not decide whether idle jobs appear at all.** J1–J7 are a plan. Today the layer does not exist,
      and the honest statement of its status is that it is authorized and unbuilt.
    - **It does not resolve C01.** The four billing bases are still open, and adding a fiction wedge to the HUD
      is a display decision that does not settle the rate formula or pretend to.
