    ---
    
    # PLAN_CIVILIAN_CHAT — PocketJS human UI for civilian agents
    
    **What this is.** A plan that authorizes a human-facing UI, built on [PocketJS](https://pocketjs.dev/) (Rust core + JS guest), so a human can **connect to and chat with** civilian agents under Governor Base. It exists as its own document because “chat with agents” is the exact surface where authority, identity, and evidence most often leak by accident.
    
    **Companions.** `AGENTS.md` §0–§1 (precedence, evidence principle), §5 (contracts), §6 (tickets), §7 (resumes), §9.6–§9.7 (never-granted actions, fail-closed gates), §27–§30 (civilians), §31–§35 (overlay as lens, tick contract, idle fiction), `CITY_MAP.md`, `PLAN_JOBS.md`.
    
    **Markers.** `[V]` verified against PocketJS docs / this stack · `[R]` reported · `[O]` open or proposed · authorization is **operator decision**, recorded here so it travels with the feature.
    
    ---
    
    ## 0. The authorization problem (stated before the design)
    
    “Connect and chat with civilian agents” has two readings; only one is buildable under this stack.
    
    | Reading | Shape | Verdict |
    |---|---|---|
    | **(a) Chat as authority or evidence** — messages become tickets, grades, promotions, income, resume claims, or doctrine | Fiction or human prose reaches the record and is later cited as evidence | **FORBIDDEN.** Rule 3, §7.1, rule 60, §9.6 rule 1, rule 98 |
    | **(b) Chat as a declared human–agent channel** — messages are non-authoritative by construction, scoped by contract, logged only as operational evidence (grade B at best), and refused at every boundary where chat could become governance | Nothing is asserted as fact without a separate, governed path | **AUTHORIZED by this plan** |
    
    **Precedent already in the file (same move twice):**
    
    ```text
    DRAFT (§9.7)           no authorization needed to produce; output NON-PUBLISHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION
    WRITE_EXTERNAL (§9.7)  implemented: false — absence is stronger than a gate
    idle job (§33)         declared fiction; refusals are absences of paths
    ```
    
    **A human chat session is `DRAFT` applied to a conversation.** Its output is non-authoritative not because a downstream check rejects it, but because **there is no path from a chat message to income, grade, promotion, retirement, resume claim, or doctrine merge.**
    
    > **What this plan authorizes is a channel that cannot be believed as authority by accident. What it forbids is a channel that can.**
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. What PocketJS is (for this plan)
    
    PocketJS is a portable application runtime: Solid / Vue Vapor / Octane components compile to one native tree; a compact Rust core (`pocketjs-core`, `no_std`) owns layout, text, animation, and draw; the same logical UI targets browser (WASM), desktop, and constrained hosts.
    
    Relevant modules for this plan:
    
    | Module | Use here | Constraint from PocketJS |
    |---|---|---|
    | **ui** | Chat shell, civilian list, message list, compose | One thread, retained tree, no DOM |
    | **net** | Bounded HTTP to a backend that fronts civilians | Concurrent requests ≤ 2; body budgets; closed method set; no CONNECT/TRACE |
    | **(not fs / not credentials)** | — | Do not mount modules that would enable never-granted actions |
    
    The human UI is a **PocketJS guest app**. The Rust side of *this* stack remains the authority plane (Governor, tickets, civilians store). PocketJS does not become a second Governor.
    
    ---
    
    ## 2. Doctrine mapping (what the player/human may write)
    
    Same inversion as `CITY_MAP.md` §0: the human does not author policy.
    
    | Human action in the UI | Doctrine source | What it becomes |
    |---|---|---|
    | List / select civilians | Civilian store (read) | **Lens** — copy status from view; never compute grade or promotion |
    | Open a chat session | Contract + ticket (must exist or be proposed) | Session bound to an **authorized contract**; no contract → Deferred / refuse |
    | Send a message | Ticket procedure / evidence ladder | Message is **input under the contract**, not a claim; stored only if a ticket already authorized capture |
    | Receive agent reply | Agent execution under Governor Base | Reply is agent output under current authorization; UI displays, does not validate |
    | “Connect” | Actor identity | **PROCEDURAL** until real auth exists (R7, rule 100). UI may show a session label; it may not assert verified identity |
    | Escalate (credentials, money, terms, sign) | §9.6 rule 3 | **Gate for a human** — UI must surface escalate, never silently perform |
    
    **Precedence (§0.2) is unchanged:**
    
    ```text
    CURRENT GOVERNOR BASE
      > CURRENT CONTRACT
      > CURRENT TICKET
      > CURRENT WORLD / SYSTEM STATE
      > HISTORICAL SEASON INFORMATION
    ```
    
    Chat history is historical context. It **never** authorizes a tool, a spend, or a promotion.
    
    ---
    
    ## 3. Shape of the authorized system
    
    ```text
    ┌──────────────────────────── Human device ────────────────────────────┐
    │  PocketJS guest (Solid/Vue/Octane)                                   │
    │    · civilian directory (read from derived view)                     │
    │    · chat surface (compose + transcript)                             │
    │    · session banner: contract_id · ticket_id · governor_version      │
    │    · escalate affordances for never-granted actions                  │
    └─────────────────────────────── net (bounded) ────────────────────────┘
                                        │
                                        ▼
    ┌──────────────────────────── Backend (this stack) ────────────────────┐
    │  Session service (thin)                                              │
    │    · authenticate human: PROCEDURAL until real auth                  │
    │    · resolve civilian_id → existing civilian record only             │
    │    · require open Contract + Ticket (or issue proposal ticket)       │
    │    · stream messages as ticket inputs / agent outputs                │
    │    · never write income / grade / promotion / doctrine from chat     │
    │  Governor Base + civilian store + ticket store                       │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    ```
    
    **Structural markings (same discipline as idle jobs §33.4):**
    
    1. **ID** — session ids carry a `chat_` prefix; message ids `msg_`.
    2. **View field** — human chat state lives under a dedicated key (e.g. `human_chat`), never under `jobs`, `income_*`, or control status fields.
    3. **Surface** — UI labels the channel “human chat · non-authoritative”; transcript is not a resume view.
    4. **Refusal by type** — backend and schema refuse any path from `msg_*` to governed claim types.
    
    ---
    
    ## 4. The seven refusals (absences of paths)
    
    Each refusal is held by tests that fail if a path appears.
    
    | # | Refusal | Why |
    |---|---|---|
    | **1** | A chat message **cannot create or update an `income_*` record** | §9.6 rule 1 — a dollar is not income until a receipt cites it |
    | **2** | Chat **cannot produce a grade, promotion, retirement, or resume claim** | Those carry forward; chat is not evidence-grade-A and is not a certification act |
    | **3** | Chat **cannot be a control** and cannot change C9–C20 status | Overlay/city rules: status is copied from the store, never computed by a UI |
    | **4** | Chat text **cannot enter a metric or a bill** | §7.11 — metrics need source_artifact, method, window, unit |
    | **5** | Chat **cannot resolve an open C\* / I\* decision or merge doctrine** | Rule 60 / §19.4 — only a governed merge changes doctrine |
    | **6** | Chat **cannot perform never-granted actions** | §9.6 rule 3: create_account, enter_credentials, move_money, accept_terms, sign_contract → human gate only |
    | **7** | Chat **cannot invent a civilian** | Same as idle refusal 7: every session names an existing `civilian_*` or is refused |
    
    **Identity rule (rule 100 restated for chat):** any control that depends on actor authentication is **procedural** until an authentication mechanism exists. A successful login string is not proof of identity; the UI must not present it as verified.
    
    ---
    
    ## 5. Contract and ticket discipline for a session
    
    Before any message is accepted:
    
    1. **Contract** — human↔civilian chat runs under a contract that names: mission (chat scoped to topic X), scope (which civilian, which tools the *agent* may use), constraints (read-only vs allowed agent actions), resources, evidence, deliverable, stop (§5.2).
    2. **Ticket** — each session (or each bounded turn set) is filed **before** it runs (§6.3 rule 1). Closure requires evidence (at best operational record, grade B) or explicit `completed_but_unverified`.
    3. **Subcontracts** may only narrow (§5.3).
    4. **No silent new campaign every turn** — reuse open ticket under same legacy id (§6.3 rules 3–4).
    
    Human messages are **inputs** to the ticket. Agent replies are **outputs** under current Governor authorization. Neither is a completion claim until an external oracle or defined acceptance test says so (§1, §9.5).
    
    ---
    
    ## 6. PocketJS-specific engineering constraints
    
    | Concern | Plan rule |
    |---|---|
    | **Net module** | Use bounded `fetch` only; enforce timeout and maxBytes; no credential stuffing into headers beyond session token issued by *this* backend |
    | **No browser DOM assumptions** | Chat UI uses View / Text / focusable press patterns; works on WASM host first (lowest integration risk), desktop host second |
    | **Frame clock** | Treat network events as queued to frame boundaries (PocketJS model); do not mid-frame mutate authority state |
    | **Offline** | No offline “catch-up” that invents agent replies; pause = no poll of authority plane (align with §32.3 / rule 123) |
    | **Secrets** | PocketJS guest must not hold long-lived human credentials; session tokens short-lived; never-granted verbs stay unimplemented on the client |
    
    ---
    
    ## 7. Phases and gates
    
    Ordered by dependency. Each phase gated by a **refusal test** (rule 44: a mitigation is not implemented until a test fails without it).
    
    | # | Phase | Deliverable | Gate |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **H0** | **This authorization** | This plan landed as doctrine; refusals numbered | Rules exist and are numbered; no code path from `msg_*` to income/grade/doctrine |
    | **H1** | **Read-only civilian directory in PocketJS** | List civilians from derived view / API; no write | Selecting a missing `civilian_*` is refused (refusal 7) |
    | **H2** | **Session bootstrap** | Open session only with Contract + Ticket (or create **proposal** ticket, not active work) | No contract → Deferred with citation; no silent active ticket |
    | **H3** | **Message transport** | Bounded net; message schema with `chat_` / `msg_` ids; store only under ticket inputs/outputs | Refusals 1–4: absence suite (negative controls that deliberately try to write income/grade and fail) |
    | **H4** | **Transcript UI** | Compose + scroll; banner shows contract_id, ticket_id, governor_version, identity_status=PROCEDURAL | Surface does not compute control status (rule 112 / 120) |
    | **H5** | **Escalation UX** | Explicit UI for never-granted actions → “requires human gate” | Refusal 6: client has no code path that calls those ops |
    | **H6** | **Evidence labeling** | Any persisted chat evidence is `b_operational_record` (or weaker) with note that it is not oracle | Matches §9.5 pattern: do not dress self-chat as grade A |
    | **H7** | **Headless / CI determinism** | PocketJS headless host + fixture net: same inputs → byte-stable transcript render | Aligns with PocketJS frame-fold testing and this stack’s digest convergence |
    | **H8** | **Optional desktop/native host** | Same guest bundle on gpui/desktop host | No new authority; same refusals |
    
    **H3 is the honesty gate.** If any path from a message to a governed claim type exists, the feature is not authorized under this plan.
    
    ---
    
    ## 8. What this plan does not do
    
    - **Does not implement actor authentication.** Identity remains procedural (R7, rule 100).
    - **Does not authorize agent tool use beyond the current Governor profile.** Chat is not a capability grant.
    - **Does not resolve C01–C12 or fog items.** Chat cannot close open decisions.
    - **Does not add a second authority plane.** PocketJS is the UI runtime; Governor Base remains the authority plane (§0.3).
    - **Does not treat chat volume as skill evidence.** No “messages sent” metric on a resume (§7.11, rule 6).
    - **Does not ship WRITE_EXTERNAL or credential entry** from the guest.
    - **Does not claim performance numbers** until measured and registered (§10.2 discipline).
    
    ---
    
    ## 9. Binding rules proposed for the stack (after H0 lands)
    
    To be appended only by governed merge (not by this plan alone):
    
    ```text
    136. A human chat session is non-authoritative by construction. Message records
         may not create income, grade, promotion, retirement, resume claims, metrics,
         or doctrine changes. Inadmissibility is by schema and by absence of path.
    137. Every chat session names an existing civilian record and an authorized
         contract (or a proposal ticket). Inventing a civilian or chatting without a
         contract is refused.
    138. Never-granted actions remain unimplemented in the PocketJS guest. The UI
         may only escalate them to a human gate.
    139. Session identity is PROCEDURAL until an authentication mechanism exists.
         A UI must not present a login string as verified actor identity (rule 100).
    140. The chat surface is a lens: it copies civilian and ticket status from the
         store; it never computes control status or resolves open decisions.
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ## 10. Destination (checkable claim)
    
    > **A human may use a PocketJS UI to connect and chat with civilian agents only under an open contract and ticket, with messages marked and stored as non-authoritative operational traffic, with never-granted actions escalated, and with no path from chat into income, grade, promotion, resume, or doctrine.**
    
    That is the authorization. Implementation that violates any of the seven refusals is out of scope of this plan and must be refused, not patched downstream.
    
    ---
    
    ### How to use this next
    
    1. **Land H0** as doctrine (same pattern as §33 / §35 for idle jobs).  
    2. Implement **H1–H3** first; do not build a pretty transcript until the absence suite is green.  
    3. Keep PocketJS on the **browser/WASM host** until the backend contract/ticket boundary is proven.  
    4. Do not resolve open civilian questions (C01, C11, auth) inside the chat UI.
    
    If you want this turned into a concrete repo layout (crate names, API routes, Solid component sketch, or test list for the absence suite), say which phase to expand first.
    Updated plan: design baseline for the PocketJS civilian-chat UI, grounded in **Impeccable**, **Material Design 1**, and **Apple HIG**, with a **real-world images and textures** theme. Governance refusals from the prior plan are unchanged.
    
    ---
    
    # PLAN_CIVILIAN_CHAT — Design baseline (addendum)
    
    **Scope of this addendum.** Visual and interaction language for the PocketJS human UI only. It does not grant authority, resolve open civilian questions, or weaken the seven refusals. Register: **product** (tool that serves chat), not brand marketing surface.
    
    **Sources (design doctrine only):**
    
    | Source | Role in this baseline |
    |---|---|
    | **Impeccable** (Neo Kinpaku craft + DESIGN.md workflow) | Physical materials, OKLCH, anti-generic AI chrome, document-then-build |
    | **Material Design 1** | Material-as-metaphor, paper/surface, elevation/seams, 8dp metrics, bold intentional content |
    | **Apple HIG** | Purpose, agency, responsibility, familiarity; clear hierarchy; content over chrome |
    
    **Theme mandate (operator constraint):** **real-world images and textures** — photographed or scanned materials (paper, cloth, wood, metal, ink, stone), not pure vector flatness, not neon glassmorphism, not purple-gradient “AI tool” defaults that Impeccable explicitly rejects.
    
    ---
    
    ## D0. Creative north star
    
    **Name:** *Work desk, not dashboard.*
    
    The chat UI should feel like objects on a physical desk: paper transcripts, a metal or wood session plaque, cloth or board for the civilian list, ink for type. Motion is paper sliding and ink appearing — not bouncing UI confetti.
    
    **One memorable differentiator:** every primary surface carries a **legible real texture** (grain, fiber, leaf, oxidation) at a scale the eye can read; solid fills are for actions and rules only, never as the only surface language.
    
    This aligns:
    
    - Impeccable: “crafted object,” real texture on brand-bearing surfaces, mineral/lacquer restraint (adapted here to **desk materials**, not necessarily gold leaf).  
    - Material 1: material is the metaphor; surfaces and edges grounded in tactile reality.  
    - Apple: familiarity and purpose — build on what people already know from paper and tools.
    
    **Explicit non-goals for look:**
    
    - Glassmorphism / Liquid Glass as the primary product skin (Apple’s system material is not this app’s identity).  
    - Generic SaaS cards, equal-weight feature grids, sparkline decoration.  
    - Pure black `#000` panels without tint; Inter/Roboto as the only type.  
    - Status dots that pulse for decoration rather than state.
    
    ---
    
    ## D1. How the three systems map onto PocketJS
    
    PocketJS has **no DOM and no runtime CSS** — class strings compile into style tables; images and glyphs bake into the app package. Design tokens must therefore be:
    
    1. **Named in a `DESIGN.md`** (Impeccable workflow).  
    2. **Expressed as PocketJS class strings + baked image assets** (textures as `Image` / atlas, not CSS `background-image` filters).  
    3. **Measurable** (contrast, touch targets, texture resolution).
    
    | Concern | Material Design 1 | Apple HIG | Impeccable | PocketJS expression |
    |---|---|---|---|---|
    | Space | 8dp baseline; 48dp touch targets | Clear hierarchy; comfortable tap targets | Modular scale; purposeful restraint | Logical viewport (e.g. 480×272 class or desktop window); 8-unit spacing scale in classes |
    | Surface | Paper sheets, seams, steps (elevation) | Content primary; chrome secondary | Physical materials; texture where weight matters | Layered `View`s + baked paper/cloth/metal textures; elevation as edge/shadow tokens, not fake 3D clutter |
    | Type | Print-informed hierarchy | Plain language; clarity | Distinctive display + refined body; avoid Inter defaults | Baked fonts in PocketJS; display for session titles; body for messages |
    | Color | Bold, intentional; limited palette | System-aware contrast | OKLCH; tinted neutrals; solid vs material pair | Small OKLCH palette; texture assets for material role; solid for primary actions |
    | Motion | Motion provides meaning | Feedback without noise | One ease; reduced motion | PocketJS native animation tracks; message appear = paper settle, not bounce |
    | Interaction | Signifiers; consistent affordances | Agency, undo, forgiveness | Direct states; no decorative chrome | `focusable` + `onPress`; escalate never-granted actions with explicit human-gate copy |
    
    ---
    
    ## D2. Material metaphor (Material Design 1 → this app)
    
    Translate MD1 “paper” into **desk materials** so the theme stays real-world:
    
    | UI region | Material metaphor | Texture asset (examples) | Elevation / behavior |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | App shell / background | Desk surface | Wood grain, matte laminate, cork | Bottom sheet; never scrolls away |
    | Civilian directory | Index cards / cloth board | Card stock, linen, cork pinboard | List of discrete cards; seam between cards |
    | Transcript | Stack of paper | Off-white paper fiber, faint ruled lines optional | Newest message on top sheet; older sheets recessed one step |
    | Compose field | Notepad strip | Paper + slight shadow under edge | Sticky to bottom; keyboard/focus raises it one step |
    | Session banner | Metal or wood plaque | Brushed aluminum, stained wood, engraved plate | Fixed under status; carries contract/ticket ids as engraved text |
    | Primary actions | Ink / solid stamp | Solid color (not textured) for press clarity | High contrast; MD1: action is inflection |
    | Escalation / never-granted | Red wax seal or stamped warning paper | Matte red paper or wax texture | Separate sheet; never looks like a normal send button |
    | Agent vs human bubbles | Two paper stocks | Warm cream (human) vs cool gray paper (agent) | Same elevation; distinction by stock, not by neon |
    
    **MD1 rules kept:**
    
    - Seams: joined regions move together.  
    - Steps: overlapping sheets show depth with light, not arbitrary drop shadows.  
    - Touch targets ≥ 48dp equivalent; spacing ≥ 8dp between targets.  
    - Content bold and intentional: civilian name, message body, and session ids are the hierarchy — chrome is quiet.
    
    **PocketJS note:** textures are **baked images** (or atlas regions). Prefer small repeating tiles or carefully cropped photos; budget memory (PocketJS hosts include constrained devices). No full-screen 4K photo backgrounds.
    
    ---
    
    ## D3. Apple HIG principles → chat behaviors
    
    | Principle | Application in civilian chat |
    |---|---|
    | **Purpose** | Primary job: select a civilian, hold a scoped conversation under a contract. Everything else is secondary. |
    | **Agency** | Human controls send, scroll, end session, escalate. Agent replies never auto-trigger tools the human did not authorize via Governor. |
    | **Responsibility** | Privacy: no credential capture in-guest; identity shown as PROCEDURAL; chat not marketed as “verified.” |
    | **Familiarity** | Message list + compose is familiar; desk textures reinforce paper/tool metaphor rather than inventing a new interaction language. |
    | **Clarity** | Session banner always shows `contract_id`, `ticket_id`, `governor_version`, `identity_status`. |
    | **Forgiveness** | Destructive actions (end session, discard draft) confirm; send is undoable only if backend supports retract under ticket rules — do not fake undo. |
    
    Writing (Apple): short, action-oriented labels — “Send”, “End session”, “Needs human approval” — not clever microcopy.
    
    ---
    
    ## D4. Impeccable craft rules adapted to product register
    
    **Register:** product UI (serves the job), not brand landing page.
    
    From Impeccable practice:
    
    1. **Document before expanding** — maintain `DESIGN.md` + optional `PRODUCT.md` for this app; tokens are normative.  
    2. **Physical scene forces light/dark** — desk under warm task light → warm dark neutrals or warm paper light; do not default to pure OLED black.  
    3. **OKLCH palette** with tinted neutrals; material + solid pair for each brand accent (e.g. ink blue solid for actions; paper texture for surfaces).  
    4. **One easing curve** for UI motion (e.g. cubic-bezier similar to Impeccable’s single ease).  
    5. **Anti-slop bans** for this project: gradient text, rainbow borders, equal-weight card grids, decorative side stripes, Inter-only stacks, purple neon on black.
    
    **Optional brand accent (if needed):** prefer **ink, brass, or graphite** over kinpaku gold unless the product explicitly adopts Impeccable’s Neo Kinpaku brand. Gold leaf is allowed only if it remains a *real texture asset* and does not become generic “premium AI” chrome.
    
    ---
    
    ## D5. Texture and image pipeline (theme enforcement)
    
    **Rules:**
    
    ```text
    1  Every primary surface references a real texture asset OR an explicit solid token.
       “Primary surface” = shell, directory card, transcript sheet, compose strip, session plaque.
    2  Textures are photographs or scans of physical materials, color-corrected, tiling or fixed crop.
    3  Text contrast is measured on the composite (texture + overlay scrim if needed), WCAG AA minimum
       for body text (Impeccable / product baseline).
    4  Message body text sits on a scrim or quiet paper region so fiber noise never reduces legibility.
    5  No generative “AI texture” as the sole source without a human-selected physical reference.
    6  Assets are versioned and hashed; a missing texture fails the build or falls back to a named solid
       (fail closed for brand surfaces, not silent gray).
    ```
    
    **Suggested starter kit (replace with project photos):**
    
    | Token | Real-world reference |
    |---|---|
    | `tex.desk` | Oak or linoleum desk |
    | `tex.paper.human` | Cream wove paper |
    | `tex.paper.agent` | Cool gray bond paper |
    | `tex.card` | Manilla index card |
    | `tex.plaque` | Brushed aluminum or stained wood |
    | `tex.warning` | Red craft paper / wax |
    | `tex.cork` | Cork board (directory optional) |
    
    PocketJS: ship as packed images; reference from `Image` components or style table image ids.
    
    ---
    
    ## D6. Screen inventory (baseline layouts)
    
    All layouts: **content first**, texture second, chrome last.
    
    1. **Connect / session gate**  
       - Plaque: procedural identity, “not verified actor.”  
       - List of civilians as index cards on cork/desk.  
       - Empty state: real photo of empty desk + one sentence purpose.
    
    2. **Chat**  
       - Top: session plaque (contract, ticket, governor version).  
       - Middle: paper stack transcript (human/agent stocks).  
       - Bottom: notepad compose + solid Send.  
       - Escalation: separate warning sheet, not a green button.
    
    3. **Blocked / deferred**  
       - MD1 intentional empty: state why (no contract, refusal citation) on a single sheet; one primary action (“Request contract” / “Back”).
    
    Focus order and d-pad/touch: PocketJS `focusable` order matches reading order (plaque → list/messages → compose → escalate).
    
    ---
    
    ## D7. Motion (Material “meaning” + Impeccable single ease)
    
    | Event | Motion | Forbidden |
    |---|---|---|
    | Open civilian | Card lifts one step, transcript sheet slides in | Bounce, spin |
    | New message | Sheet settles onto stack (short ease) | Staggered confetti |
    | Send | Compose ink “stamps” then clears | Full-screen flash |
    | Escalation | Warning sheet steps up; dim desk behind | Aggressive shake |
    | Error | Plaque edge rule turns warning color | Modal spam |
    
    Respect reduced motion: cross-fade only, no large travel.
    
    ---
    
    ## D8. Design phases (extend H-phases)
    
    | # | Phase | Deliverable | Gate |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **D0** | `PRODUCT.md` + `DESIGN.md` for chat app | Audience, purpose, tokens, do/don’t | Tokens named; theme = real textures stated |
    | **D1** | Texture kit v1 | Baked assets + contrast checks on composites | AA body text on paper+scrim; memory budget noted |
    | **D2** | Shell + directory in PocketJS | Desk + cards; no chat yet | H1 (civilian list) + D1 textures |
    | **D3** | Transcript + compose | Two paper stocks; solid Send | H4 UI + legibility test on textures |
    | **D4** | Session plaque + escalation sheet | Procedural identity copy; never-granted UX | Refusals 6 + H5 |
    | **D5** | Motion + focus | Single ease; focus order test | Reduced-motion path |
    | **D6** | Audit | Impeccable-style critique: hierarchy, contrast, anti-slop | No banned patterns; WCAG AA |
    
    Design work **does not** unlock H3 absence suite; backend refusals remain the honesty gate.
    
    ---
    
    ## D9. Do / Don’t (design)
    
    **Do**
    
    - Use real paper, wood, metal, cloth textures on primary surfaces.  
    - Keep message text on quiet regions or light scrims.  
    - Show contract/ticket/governor on a persistent plaque.  
    - Use solid, high-contrast fills for primary actions.  
    - Measure contrast; document tokens in `DESIGN.md`.
    
    **Don’t**
    
    - Use neon gradients, glass blobs, or purple-on-black AI defaults.  
    - Hide procedural identity behind a “verified” badge.  
    - Put never-granted actions on the same visual tier as Send.  
    - Let texture noise reduce body text below AA.  
    - Invent civilians or chat without contract in the empty states (copy must match refusal 7).
    
    ---
    
    ## D10. Binding design rules (propose for governed merge with H0)
    
    ```text
    141. The civilian-chat PocketJS UI uses real-world material textures on primary
         surfaces; solid tokens are for actions and rules. Texture assets are versioned;
         missing required texture fails closed or falls back to a named solid.
    142. Visual language is product-register: desk/paper metaphor (Material 1),
         Apple HIG purpose/agency/clarity, Impeccable anti-slop and DESIGN.md tokens.
         Appearance grants no authority (rules 112, 120, 136–140 still apply).
    143. Session chrome must display contract_id, ticket_id, governor_version, and
         identity_status (PROCEDURAL until auth exists) without requiring a secondary screen.
    144. Body text on textured surfaces must meet WCAG AA on the composite (texture +
         scrim). Decorative grain must not carry information.
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ### Summary
    
    | Layer | Decision |
    |---|---|
    | **Theme** | Real-world images and textures (desk, paper, plaque, cloth) |
    | **Structure** | Material Design 1 sheets, seams, 8dp metrics, meaningful motion |
    | **Behavior & copy** | Apple HIG purpose, agency, responsibility, clarity |
    | **Craft & tokens** | Impeccable DESIGN.md, OKLCH, physical materials, ban AI-slop chrome |
    | **Runtime** | PocketJS baked assets + class strings; no DOM CSS |
    | **Authority** | Unchanged: lens only; seven refusals; chat non-authoritative |
    
    If you want a next artifact, the highest leverage is a concrete **`DESIGN.md` token table** (OKLCH values + texture filenames + PocketJS class map) for D0, still without writing app code.

    # PLAN_CIVILIAN_HOOK — Agent-side eligibility for human chat after AGENTS.md read
    
    **What this is.** A plan that authorizes a **civilian hook**: a narrow, machine-checkable binding that makes an existing civilian eligible for the PocketJS human-chat UI only after the agent process has completed a governed, evidence-linked read of `AGENTS.md`. It is a bridge between the authority plane (Governor Base + civilian store) and the chat lens (H1–H8), not a second Governor and not a chat implementation.
    
    **Companions.**  
    `AGENTS.md` §0–§1 (precedence, evidence principle), §5–§6 (contracts, tickets), §7 (resumes), §9.6–§9.7 (never-granted, fail-closed), §27–§30 (civilians), §31–§35 (overlay as lens, tick contract), `PLAN_CIVILIAN_CHAT` (Human_chat_ui.md), Document_orchestration.md (shared absence suite, Phase 0–2).
    
    **Markers.** `[V]` verified against stack doctrine / supplied plans · `[R]` reported · `[O]` open · authorization is **operator decision**, recorded here so it travels with the feature.
    
    ---
    
    ## 0. The authorization problem (stated before the design)
    
    “Connect the civilian to the human chat UI when AGENTS.md is read through by the agent process” has two readings; only one is buildable under this stack.
    
    | Reading | Shape | Verdict |
    |---|---|---|
    | **(a) Read as grant** — finishing a read of AGENTS.md *creates* a civilian, *opens* a chat session, *elevates* capability, or *writes* a claim | The read becomes authority or evidence | **FORBIDDEN.** §0.2–0.3, §1, rule 60, §9.6, §27 genesis rules, chat refusals 1–7 |
    | **(b) Read as eligibility signal** — a completed, ticketed, evidence-linked read of AGENTS.md is recorded as a **non-authoritative readiness fact** on an *already existing* civilian; the human chat UI may then open a session only under a separate Contract + Ticket | Eligibility is derived; authority stays in Governor Base | **AUTHORIZED by this plan** |
    
    **Precedent already in the file (same structural move):**
    
    ```text
    DRAFT (§9.7)              output NON-PUBLISHABLE BY CONSTRUCTION
    idle job (§33)            declared fiction; refusals = absences of paths
    human chat (H0)           messages non-authoritative by construction
    overlay tick (§32)        display tick may animate; may not change store or doctrine
    ```
    
    **A civilian hook is `DRAFT` applied to a readiness bit.** It does not authorize tools, spend, promotion, or doctrine. It only answers: *may this existing civilian appear in the human chat directory under a later contract/ticket?*
    
    > **What this plan authorizes is a pathless eligibility marker that cannot be mistaken for a capability grant. What it forbids is any path from “AGENTS.md was read” into authority, income, grade, or identity.**
    
    ---
    
    ## 1. Definition of the civilian hook
    
    ```text
    CivilianHook =
      a derived, non-authoritative record (or view field) that states:
        civilian_id          names an EXISTING civilian_* record
        agents_md_read       evidence-linked fact that a governed read completed
        read_ticket_id       the ticket under which the read ran
        governor_version     stamped at evaluation time
        identity_status      PROCEDURAL (rule 100) until real auth exists
        eligibility          true only if all gates below pass
    ```
    
    **What it is not:**
    
    - Not a capability grant  
    - Not a contract or ticket  
    - Not a resume claim or grade  
    - Not a genesis act (no new civilians)  
    - Not a chat session (session still requires H2 bootstrap)
    
    **What it enables (lens only):**
    
    - The human chat directory (H1) may list the civilian as *eligible for session proposal*  
    - Session open still requires Contract + Ticket (or proposal ticket only)  
    - Message transport still runs under H3 refusals
    
    ---
    
    ## 2. Doctrine mapping
    
    | Event | Doctrine source | What it becomes |
    |---|---|---|
    | Agent process completes read of AGENTS.md | Ticket + evidence ladder (§1, §6, §9.5) | Normalized observation → candidate → validator → evidence-linked claim that a read occurred |
    | Hook evaluation | Governor Base + civilian store | Eligibility bit copied into derived view under `civilian_hooks` (or equivalent); never under `jobs`, `income_*`, or control status |
    | Human sees civilian in chat directory | PLAN_CIVILIAN_CHAT H1 | Lens — status copied from view; no grade/promotion computed |
    | Human opens chat | H2 | Still requires Contract + Ticket; hook alone is insufficient |
    | Message send/receive | H3–H6 | Unchanged; seven chat refusals still hold |
    
    **Precedence remains (§0.2):**
    
    ```text
    CURRENT GOVERNOR BASE
      > CURRENT CONTRACT
      > CURRENT TICKET
      > CURRENT WORLD / SYSTEM STATE
      > HISTORICAL SEASON INFORMATION
    ```
    
    The fact “AGENTS.md was read” is historical/evidence context. It **never** authorizes a tool, a spend, or a promotion.
    
    ---
    
    ## 3. Shape of the authorized system
    
    ```text
    ┌──────────────────── Agent process ────────────────────┐
    │  Ticketed read of AGENTS.md                           │
    │    · governed ticket already open                     │
    │    · parser → observation → candidate → validator     │
    │    · evidence record: agents_md_read (grade ≤ B)      │
    └───────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                                │ evidence-linked claim only
                                ▼
    ┌──────────────────── Backend (this stack) ─────────────┐
    │  Hook evaluator (pure function of store + evidence)   │
    │    · civilian_id must already exist                   │
    │    · read_ticket_id must be closed or verified        │
    │    · no path to income / grade / doctrine             │
    │    · write eligibility only under dedicated view key  │
    │  Governor Base + civilian store + ticket store        │
    └───────────────────────────┬───────────────────────────┘
                                │ derived view only
                                ▼
    ┌──────────────────── PocketJS human UI ────────────────┐
    │  H1 directory shows eligible civilians                │
    │  H2 still requires Contract + Ticket to open session  │
    │  H3–H8 refusals unchanged                             │
    └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    ```
    
    **Structural markings (same discipline as idle jobs and chat):**
    
    1. **ID** — hook records carry `hook_` prefix; never collide with `civilian_*`, `job_*`, `msg_*`.  
    2. **View field** — lives under `civilian_hooks` (or equivalent), never under jobs, income, or C9–C20 status.  
    3. **Surface** — human UI may show “AGENTS.md read · eligible for chat proposal”; never “verified” or “authorized to act”.  
    4. **Refusal by type** — schema and tests refuse any path from `hook_*` to governed claim types.
    
    ---
    
    ## 4. The seven refusals (absences of paths)
    
    Each is held by tests that fail if a path appears. These extend the shared ten-refusal suite from Document_orchestration.md.
    
    | # | Refusal | Why |
    |---|---|---|
    | **1** | A hook **cannot create or update an `income_*` record** | §9.6 rule 1 |
    | **2** | A hook **cannot produce a grade, promotion, retirement, or resume claim** | Chat refusal 2; §7 |
    | **3** | A hook **cannot be a control** and cannot change C9–C20 status | Overlay rule: status is copied, never computed by this layer |
    | **4** | Hook data **cannot enter a metric or a bill** | §7.11 four-field requirement |
    | **5** | A hook **cannot resolve an open C\*/I\* decision or merge doctrine** | Rule 60 |
    | **6** | A hook **cannot perform or unlock never-granted actions** | §9.6 rule 3; client and agent side stay unimplemented |
    | **7** | A hook **cannot invent a civilian** | Same as idle refusal 7 and chat refusal 7: every hook names an existing `civilian_*` or is refused |
    
    **Additional hook-specific absences:**
    
    | # | Refusal | Why |
    |---|---|---|
    | **8** | Completing a read of AGENTS.md **does not open a chat session** | Session still requires H2 Contract + Ticket |
    | **9** | The hook **does not widen Governor profile or tool set** | Read tools confer nothing (§2.8); authority plane unchanged |
    | **10** | Eligibility **expires or is re-evaluated** when Governor version or civilian record changes | Stale eligibility is not authority |
    
    ---
    
    ## 5. Gates that must all pass before eligibility = true
    
    ```text
    1  civilian_id exists in the civilian store (genesis already satisfied)
    2  A ticket for the AGENTS.md read exists and is in a closed/verified state
       (or carries explicit completed_but_unverified if that is the acceptance path)
    3  Evidence record for the read is present and linked (grade at most operational / B)
    4  Governor version at evaluation time is stamped on the hook
    5  No never-granted action is requested by the hook path
    6  Identity remains PROCEDURAL (rule 100)
    7  Derived view write is under the dedicated key only
    ```
    
    Failure of any gate → eligibility false (or Deferred with citation). No silent true.
    
    ---
    
    ## 6. Contract and ticket discipline
    
    - The **read** of AGENTS.md runs under its own ticket (or an existing campaign ticket that authorizes the read).  
    - The **hook evaluation** is a pure derive step (like overlay view); it may run on ticket close or on a governed re-derive, but it does not create a new active work ticket by itself.  
    - Opening a **human chat session** remains H2: requires Contract + Ticket (or proposal ticket only). The hook is a precondition for *listing*, not a substitute for the session ticket.  
    - Subcontracts may only narrow (§5.3).
    
    ---
    
    ## 7. Phases and gates
    
    Ordered by dependency. Each phase gated by a **refusal test** (rule 44). Aligns with Document_orchestration Phase 0–2 and Chat H0–H2.
    
    | # | Phase | Deliverable | Gate |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **K0** | **This authorization** | Plan landed as derived doctrine under seasons/plans/; refusals numbered | Rules exist; no code path from `hook_*` to income/grade/doctrine |
    | **K1** | **Evidence shape for AGENTS.md read** | Observation → candidate → validator → evidence record for “read completed”; ticket linkage required | Missing ticket or missing evidence → no eligibility |
    | **K2** | **Hook model + schema** | `hook_` ids; dedicated view key; fields as in §1; `extra="forbid"` | Refusal 7: ghost civilian_id refused; unnamed civilian refused |
    | **K3** | **Absence suite** | Property tests for refusals 1–10; negative controls that deliberately try to write income/grade/session and fail | Shared suite with H3 / J3 / Land still green |
    | **K4** | **Evaluator as pure function** | `(store, evidence, governor_version) → eligibility`; no mutation of authority plane | Determinism test; never mutates inputs |
    | **K5** | **Wire to human chat directory (H1)** | Derived view exposes eligible civilians only; selecting ineligible is refused | H1 + refusal 7; no silent active ticket |
    | **K6** | **Session still gated by H2** | Hook true + no Contract → Deferred with citation | Explicit test: eligibility alone does not open session |
    | **K7** | **Re-evaluation / staleness** | Governor version change or civilian retirement clears or re-derives eligibility | Stale hook never treated as current authority |
    | **K8** | **CI / digest** | Re-derive from unchanged store → byte-identical view including hooks | Aligns with overlay and chat H7 discipline |
    
    **K3 is the honesty gate.** If any path from a completed AGENTS.md read into a governed claim type or an automatic chat session exists, the feature is out of scope of this plan.
    
    ---
    
    ## 8. What this plan does not do
    
    - Does **not** implement actor authentication (identity stays PROCEDURAL).  
    - Does **not** authorize agent tool use beyond the current Governor profile.  
    - Does **not** resolve open C*/I* or fog items.  
    - Does **not** create civilians (genesis remains separate).  
    - Does **not** open chat sessions (H2 still required).  
    - Does **not** treat “pages of AGENTS.md read” as a skill metric or resume claim.  
    - Does **not** add PocketJS code; the hook is backend/store/view only until H1 consumes the view.  
    - Does **not** claim performance numbers until measured and registered (§10.2).
    
    ---
    
    ## 9. Binding rules proposed for the stack (after K0 lands)
    
    To be appended only by governed merge (not by this plan alone):
    
    ```text
    145. A civilian hook is a non-authoritative eligibility marker derived from an
         evidence-linked read of AGENTS.md under a ticket. It may not create income,
         grade, promotion, retirement, resume claims, metrics, doctrine changes, or
         chat sessions. Inadmissibility is by schema and by absence of path.
    146. Every hook names an existing civilian record. Inventing a civilian via the
         hook is refused.
    147. Completing a read of AGENTS.md does not by itself open a human chat session.
         Session open still requires Contract + Ticket (or proposal ticket only).
    148. Hook eligibility is re-evaluated when Governor version or the civilian
         record changes; a stale hook is not current authority.
    149. The human chat directory may list hook-eligible civilians as a lens only;
         it copies status from the derived view and never computes control status
         or resolves open decisions (rules 112, 120, 136–140 still apply).
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ## 10. Destination (checkable claim)
    
    > **After an agent process completes a ticketed, evidence-linked read of AGENTS.md, an existing civilian may receive a pathless eligibility marker that allows the human chat UI to list that civilian for a later Contract + Ticket session. The marker creates no authority, no income, no grade, no session, and no doctrine change. All ten refusals remain absences of path.**
    
    That is the authorization. Implementation that violates any refusal is out of scope of this plan and must be refused, not patched downstream.
    
    ---
    
    ### How to use this next (orchestration alignment)
    
    1. **Land K0** with the same ticket that lands Security / Land L0 / Chat H0 (Document_orchestration Phase 0).  
    2. Implement **K1–K3** before any UI wiring; keep the shared absence suite in one test package.  
    3. Wire **K5–K6** only after H1/H2 exist; the hook is a precondition for listing, not a substitute for session bootstrap.  
    4. Do not resolve authentication, C01, or civilian genesis inside the hook tickets.
    
    If you want the next artifact expanded, the highest leverage is either:
    
    - the **K2 schema + absence-suite test list** (concrete JSON Schema / model fields and the ten negative controls), or  
    - the **exact view field shape** that H1 will consume (`civilian_hooks` array and eligibility predicate).

    **Implementation plan: High-security civilian organization (Neon-CIA / 1940s New York under control, hyper-intelligent scientist agents)**
    
    This plan is derived strictly from `AGENTS.md`. It does not invent authority, scalars, stored balances, housing schemas, tax/payroll systems, reputation scores, or any never-granted action. It treats the theme (faux Neon CIA aesthetic + 1940s New York “under control” + hyper-intelligent scientist civilians) as **narrative flavor and view chrome only**. Doctrine, stores, and controls remain those already defined in the civilian pillar (§27–§30), Governor Base precedence (§0.2–0.3), contracts (§5), tickets (§6), resumes (§7), retirement (§8), doctors (§9), and overlay constraints (§31–§35).
    
    Evidence markers follow the document’s own convention: **[V]** = already present / measured in the stack; **[O]** = open (do not resolve by assumption); **[R]** = reported / external convention.
    
    ---
    
    ### 0. One-sentence destination (fact-checked against §30.4)
    
    A high-security organization is a **population of privately promoted civilians**, each born by a genesis contract, controlled by an independent agent, earning only on contract-defined evidence-backed bases, advancing only when a distinct authorizer acts on computed evidence strength, and retiring explicitly — stored in MongoDB under the same append-only, evidence-first rules that already govern the civilian layer. The “Neon CIA / 1940s New York under control / hyper-intelligent scientist” framing is a **lens** (view, labels, monuments, kanji/glyph chrome); it grants no authority.
    
    ---
    
    ### 1. Precedence and non-negotiable constraints (must be enforced first)
    
    ```text
    CURRENT GOVERNOR BASE
      > CURRENT CONTRACT
      > CURRENT TICKET
      > CURRENT WORLD / SYSTEM STATE
      > HISTORICAL SEASON INFORMATION
    ```
    
    - Historical precedent (including any “1940s” or “Neon CIA” lore) **never authorizes** an action (§0.2, rule A of Seasons).
    - Subcontracts may only **narrow** (§5.3).
    - Promotion requires a **distinct authorizer** and computed (never asserted) support level (§7.3, rules 55/97/98).
    - Retirement is explicit; never inferred from inactivity (rule 99, §8).
    - No stored balance (C09 answered); income is a derived view over an evidence ledger with a named basis from the closed vocabulary (C01 still open as formula, but vocabulary is closed).
    - Actor authentication remains **procedural** until a real mechanism exists (rule 100 / R7). Mechanical controls may be implemented; they never prove identity.
    - Never-granted actions stay refused under every policy (§9.6 rule 3): `create_account`, `enter_credentials`, `move_money`, `accept_terms`, `sign_contract`.
    - MongoDB is used as the **store layer** that cannot be bypassed by application code (§9.2); JSON Schema / `$jsonSchema` validators are the natural fit already recommended in §5.8.
    
    Any proposal that widens scope, invents a scalar “intelligence” or “clearance” score, stores a balance, or lets one civilian authorize its own promotion is refused with a citation.
    
    ---
    
    ### 2. Core model mapping (existing vocabulary only)
    
    | Concept in the request | Maps to (existing) | Notes |
    |---|---|---|
    | High-security organization | Population of civilians under one Governor Base + season(s) | Not a new governance plane |
    | Privately promoted civilians | Civilians advanced by distinct-authorizer promotion records | Private = internal evidence chain, not public marketplace |
    | Independent agent per civilian | One agent identity per civilian; contracts / tickets issued to that agent | A2A-style delegation is already the recommended pattern (§6.5) |
    | MongoDB database | Append-only collections for civilians, contracts, tickets, evidence, promotions, retirements, seasons | Discriminated by `record` (or equivalent) field; schema-validated |
    | Neon / 1940s New York “under control” / scientist agents | View chrome, monument labels, locus kinds, idle-job fiction (if used), situation digest | Lens only (§31.1, rules 112–119, 135) |
    | Hyper-intelligent | Capability claims computed from evidence ladder A–E + support level | Never a scalar rating (rule 6) |
    
    Open questions that stay open (do not resolve): C01 (exact income-rate formula), C02 (who sets job scopes — only that scopes narrow), C06/C08 (season/campaign relationship), C07 (can a civilian be a supervisor — constraint already enforced: supervisor ≠ worker), C11 (agent-key issuance), C12 (relationship to god-file / AGENTS.md).
    
    ---
    
    ### 3. MongoDB store design (schema + enforcement)
    
    **Collections (minimal, append-oriented):**
    
    - `civilians` — genesis records, current state, grade/stage, supervisor_id (must ≠ civilian_id), agent_id, evidence references. No `balance`, no `reputation`, no `skill_score`, no `dwelling_*`.
    - `contracts` — seven-field envelope (§5.2) + authority, scope, resources, evidence, deliverable, stop. Status vocabulary already defined.
    - `tickets` — filed before run (§6.3 rule 1); status richer than open/closed; governor_base_version stamped.
    - `evidence` — source_type (prefer external oracle when available; currently all measured rows are `b_operational_record`), notes that refuse to dress self-verification as grade-A.
    - `promotions` / `retirements` — explicit records with distinct authorizer, computed support level, retirement reason from the closed taxonomy (§8.5).
    - `seasons` / `campaigns` — historical plane only; never consulted for permission.
    - `agent_bindings` — maps civilian_id ↔ independent agent_id (one-to-one); keys distinct per rule 75.
    - Optional read models (CQRS): derived balances, situation digests, overlay view.json equivalents. Never authoritative.
    
    **Enforcement layers (both required):**
    
    1. Application: Pydantic / equivalent models with `extra="forbid"`, field-echo guards, immutable_fields, support-level computation that discards asserted levels.
    2. Store: MongoDB `$jsonSchema` validators + write guards that refuse unknown kinds, missing required fields, self-authorization, never-granted actions, and any write into protected doctrine roots.
    
    **Indexes & integrity:**
    
    - Unique on civilian_id, contract_id, ticket_id.
    - Compound indexes for open tickets per civilian, evidence by civilian + grade.
    - Hash-linked or content-addressed evidence where feasible (append-only).
    - Adversarial probes that prove the validators actually evaluate (§9.2).
    
    **Idle / fiction layer (optional, already authorized by §33):**  
    If a “Neon ward” needs visible activity while the real board drains, use declared-fiction idle jobs only (`idle_` prefix, separate view field, no path to income/ticket/grade/promotion/retirement/resume/metric). Accrual only on a running display clock; never while paused; never invents civilians.
    
    ---
    
    ### 4. Independent-agent control model
    
    - Each civilian is bound to exactly one independent agent (agent key ≠ governor key ≠ human approval credential).
    - Work is issued only as **contracts** that narrow into **tickets**.
    - The agent may propose; the Governor Base (or distinct human/authorized principal) authorizes.
    - Cross-civilian interaction is only via contracts/subcontracts that narrow; no peer-to-peer authority side-channel.
    - Context doctor (Arm 3, §9.8) applies per agent window; headroom is measured by the runtime, never self-reported.
    - When an agent’s window is exhausted, results are labelled `completed_but_unverified` rather than silently continued.
    
    ---
    
    ### 5. Security & high-assurance controls (mapped to existing doctors & gates)
    
    | Control | Mechanism | Source |
    |---|---|---|
    | Fail-closed authorization | Governor Base profiles; unknown ops/profiles refused | §4.3 |
    | Distinct authorizer for promotion | Record + test that supervisor_id ≠ civilian_id and authorizer is present | rules 62, 97, 98 |
    | Evidence strength computed | `computeSupportLevel`; asserted levels → `ignoredAssertion` | §7.3 |
    | No inflation of capability claims | Resume-safe matrix; forbidden words; authorship unreachable by design | §7.5–7.10 |
    | External acceptance preferred | Oracle when available; otherwise honest `completed_but_unverified` | §9.5 |
    | Price / money gates | Integer cents, named basis, agent cannot clear money gates | §9.6 |
    | Never-granted actions | Structural absence or human gate | §9.6 rule 3 |
    | Drift / adversarial doctor | Schema verify + adversarial probe before runs | §9.2 |
    | Context headroom | Per-turn runtime signal; crossing budget → unverified | §9.8 |
    | Overlay / city view (if used) | Pure lens; never mutates store or doctrine | §31 |
    
    Actor authentication stays procedural. Any claim that “the agent is verified” is refused until a real mechanism (e.g., WebAuthn-class) is introduced and measured.
    
    ---
    
    ### 6. Phased implementation plan (gated, refusal-first)
    
    Phases are ordered by dependency. Every phase ends with a **refusal test** (rule 44: a mitigation is not implemented until a test fails without it). Bronze ships the lens + store; silver and above add governed merge and real identity only if later authorized.
    
    | Phase | Deliverable | Gate / refusal test | Status relative to stack |
    |---|---|---|---|
    | **P0** | Doctrine landing: this plan registered as a derived view; open C* questions left open; theme marked as chrome only | Test that no new authority plane or scalar rating appears | New |
    | **P1** | MongoDB schemas + `$jsonSchema` for civilians, contracts, tickets, evidence, promotions, retirements | Adversarial probe: bad writes refused at store layer; field-echo and self-authorization refused | Builds on §5.8, §9.2 |
    | **P2** | Genesis contract flow + civilian record creation | Five conditions + seven refusals already defined for genesis; no civilian without genesis | §27 / §30.4 |
    | **P3** | Independent agent binding (1:1 civilian ↔ agent) | Rule 75: keys distinct; test that one key cannot serve two roles | C11 still open for issuance method |
    | **P4** | Contract → ticket filing chain (filed before run) | Ticket open count vs closed count measurable; reuse not refiling | §6.3 (live data already shows the board-drain problem) |
    | **P5** | Evidence write + support-level computation | Asserted strength ignored; only evidence raises level | §7.3 [V] in ala-system |
    | **P6** | Private promotion path | Distinct authorizer required; regression classification blocks promotion (rule 98) | Existing promotion records already exercise this |
    | **P7** | Explicit retirement | Reason from closed taxonomy; no silent reopen | §8 |
    | **P8** | Derived income view (no stored balance) | Named basis only; unnamed basis refused; agent cannot clear money gates | C09 answered, C01 vocabulary closed |
    | **P9** | Doctors (drift + acceptance + context) run before any production batch | Health never ready → fail; oracle preferred | §9 |
    | **P10** | Optional Neon / 1940s scientist view (overlay / city surface) | Pure lens; statuses copied, never computed; fiction idle jobs if desired stay pathless | §31–§35 |
    | **P11** | Season / campaign closure gates | All tickets terminal or explicitly carried; lessons evidence-backed | §8.11 |
    | **P12** | Supply-chain & audit | SLSA-style attestations on delivered artifacts; OpenTelemetry signals; situation digest byte-identical on re-run | §5.8, §9.9, §31 |
    
    **Explicit non-goals until later governed decisions:**  
    resolving any open C* or I* item, real agent-key issuance mechanics, stored balances, tax/guild/reputation/marketplace systems, scalar “hyper-intelligence” scores, automatic promotion cadence, offline fiction accrual, or any write path from the overlay into civilians/doctrine.
    
    ---
    
    ### 7. Definition of done (bronze)
    
    - MongoDB collections enforce the schemas and refuse the listed defects.
    - Every civilian has a genesis record, an independent agent binding, and can only act inside narrowing contracts/tickets.
    - Promotion and retirement records exist and are exercised by tests that fail when the distinct-authorizer or explicit-reason rules are removed.
    - Evidence strength is computed; asserted levels are ignored and reported.
    - No path exists from any fiction/idle layer (if present) to income, tickets, grades, promotions, retirements, resumes, or metrics.
    - Situation / overlay views (if built) are pure lenses: statuses are read, never decided; re-deriving an unchanged store produces byte-identical digests.
    - All numbers that appear in dashboards or digests are either registered measurements or carry their coverage/denominator.
    - Actor-authentication-dependent controls remain labelled procedural.
    
    ---
    
    ### 8. Risks already named by the stack (do not paper over)
    
    - Live ticket board historically does not drain (227 open / 3 closed in measured data). Closing tickets with real evidence is the highest-leverage work; gates that nothing passes through are indistinguishable from missing gates (§6.3 rule 2).
    - Zero evidence-grade-A records in the measured corpus. Prefer external oracles; label self-closure honestly.
    - Identity remains string fields until authentication exists (rule 100). High-security claims must not over-state this.
    - Cross-store dangling citations and correction durability (O1/O2 in §31.6) apply equally to a MongoDB deployment.
    
    ---
    
    ### 9. Immediate next actions (executable)
    
    1. Land this plan as a derived, non-authoritative appendix (append-only correction style if it later needs revision).
    2. Write the MongoDB `$jsonSchema` validators and the corresponding application models with `extra="forbid"`.
    3. Implement the genesis + agent-binding + contract/ticket path with the existing refusal tests.
    4. Wire the evidence → support-level → promotion path so that rule 98 is exercised by real data, not only by prose.
    5. Only after the above is green, add the Neon/1940s scientist view as a pure lens.
    
    This keeps the organization high-security by construction: authority stays in Governor Base, evidence stays the source of truth, promotion stays private and distinct-authorizer-gated, each civilian stays under an independent agent, and the thematic skin never becomes a second legislator.

    # Revised L0 Candidate Implementation Plan
    ## Land / Earth / Genesis Corpus & Ontology

    **Status:** L0 candidate (non-authoritative plan artifact)

It becomes durable only after an L0 contract is authorized under current Governor Base, the artifacts are ingested under append-only rules, and the first retirement records exist. All subsequent work runs through current tickets.

    ---

    ### 0. Binding constraints (unchanged + strengthened)

    - Evidence record is the source of truth (§1). Model output is candidate only.
    - Two planes never merge (§0.2–0.3). Historical instruments never widen Governor Base.
    - Append-only; corrections are explicit objects (§2.5).

    - **No document is treated as a witnessed “genesis event.”** NASA Big Bang material is a scientific model; USGS Earth age is an evidence-derived estimate. Markers [V]/[R]/[A]/[O] preserve the difference.
    - Fundamental ontology rule:  
      **A relationship between two nodes must be explicitly evidenced. Semantic proximity is never evidence of legal identity, physical identity, ownership, jurisdiction, sovereignty, or causation.**

    ### 1. Corpus target (corrected count)

    **21 artifacts total.**

    **16 core**

    - 3 cosmic (NASA Big Bang; NASA Big Bang & Evolution; NASA History of the Universe infographic)
    - 3 Earth (NASA Facts About Earth; USGS Age of the Earth; USGS Time’s Ruler)
    - 1 physical-land (USDA NRCS National Soil Survey Handbook)

    - 2 submerged/OCS (43 U.S.C. §1301; 43 U.S.C. §1331)
    - 1 public-land definition (43 U.S.C. §1702)

    - 2 founding (Declaration of Independence; Articles of Confederation)
    - 1 Treaty of Paris 1783
    - 1 Constitution (NARA transcript + Art. IV §3 Annotated)

    **5 chronological sequence** (separate campaign)

    1. Land Ordinance 1785  
    2. Northwest Ordinance 1787  
    3. Louisiana Purchase Treaty 1803  
    4. Johnson v. M’Intosh, 21 U.S. 543 (1823)  
    5. Homestead Act 1862  

    Present-law claims on 43 U.S.C. §§1702 and 1331 must use the current House Office of the Law Revision Counsel prelim text (laws in effect as of July 6, 2026 for §1702 and July 29, 2026 for §1331, or later if updated at retrieval time). Retrieval date + hash are mandatory.

    ---

    ### 2. Three independent chains (corrected)

    ```
    COSMOLOGICAL GENESIS
    Universe → early universe → matter/elements → stars/galaxies → solar system → Earth
    (NASA / USGS sources only; trigger of expansion remains unknown)

    POLITICAL GENESIS
    colonial political entities → Declaration 1776 → independence → Articles of Confederation 
    (in force 1 Mar 1781 – 1789) → constitutional formation (signed 17 Sep 1787; government under 
    present Constitution from 1789)

    TERRITORIAL / LAND-ADMINISTRATION DEVELOPMENT
    historical territorial claims → international cession/recognition (Treaty of Paris 1783 as 
    historical_recognition_and_boundary_instrument, not current_boundary_definition) 
    → territorial government (Northwest Ordinance) → survey → federal land classification 
    → land administration → conveyance / reservation / other interests
    ```

    The political genesis of the United States government is **not** the same event as the development of the U.S. land-administration system. The agent must never treat the sequence as a single legal instrument progressively creating today’s territorial state.

    National Archives characterization (verified): The Articles of Confederation served as the United States’ first constitution and were in force from March 1, 1781, until 1789 when the present Constitution went into effect. The Treaty of Paris 1783 Article I recognizes the listed states as “free sovereign and Independent States”; Article II specifies boundaries at that time. It is therefore represented as a historical recognition-and-boundary instrument, not a current boundary definition.

    ### 4. Refined physical → legal ladder (must remain distinct objects)

    ```
    physical feature
    → geographic feature / region
    → administratively described area
    → survey tract
    → cadastral parcel
    → legal description
    → ownership/title interest
    → use/occupancy/right interest
    → public-land classification
    → governmental jurisdiction
    → territory
    → sovereignty
    ```

    BLM documents are especially valuable here: the 2009 Manual is the current edition of the surveying-instructions series; the 2017 Specifications govern descriptions used in federal land orders, executive orders, proclamations, Federal Register documents, and land-description databases. They teach the conversion of physical space into governmental spatial representation.

    **Examples**

    ---

    ### 6. Critical invariants (doctor-enforced)

    1. **Public lands under FLPMA**
       ```
       public_lands_under_FLPMA
       ≠ all land owned by the United States
       ≠ all land within the United States
       ≠ “public land” in ordinary language
       ```
       Scope is statute-specific (43 U.S.C. §1702(e)): land and interests in land owned by the United States within the several States and administered by the Secretary of the Interior through BLM, subject to statutory exclusions (including Outer Continental Shelf lands and lands held for specified Indigenous groups).

    2. **Submerged lands**
       ```
       physical_submerged_surface
       ≠ statutory_lands_beneath_navigable_waters (43 U.S.C. §1301)
       ≠ outer_continental_shelf (43 U.S.C. §1331)
       ≠ ordinary_private_land
       ```

    3. **Indigenous land / treaty / title / sovereignty** is a **separate branch**, never labeled a “complication.”

    4. **Category-error refusal**: a doctor must reject any attempt to treat a `scientific_model` as a `statute`, a `judicial_opinion` as a `physical_measurement`, or a historical instrument as a current boundary definition, before any substantive conclusion is reached.

    **Expanded Implementation Plan: Material Drawing + Manufacturing Origins**  
    *(house.md = exclusive drawing & layer authority · AGENTS.md = governance & refusal rules · Periodic table = closed elemental set · Industry standards = manufacturing comparison baseline)*
    
    ### 0. Governing Constraints (AGENTS.md vs Industry Practice)
    
    | AGENTS.md Rule / Principle | Industry Standard Practice | Comparison / Mapping |
    |----------------------------|----------------------------|----------------------|
    | Evidence record is source of truth (§1) | Batch tickets, mill certificates, ASTM/ISO test reports, chain-of-custody | Material may be drawn only when a store evidence record cites a real production artifact (or equivalent) |
    | Nothing invented; model output is candidate until validated | Mix designs, resin formulations, and process parameters are controlled documents | Renderer never invents a visual; composition & process must be declared |
    | Append-only history; corrections are explicit | Quality records are retained; non-conforming product is quarantined, not silently rewritten | Failed or corrected material batches produce a correction record, never an overwrite |
    | Surface reports; never adjudicates (rule 120) | Drawings show what was specified and verified; they do not certify performance | Drawing of a material never implies a grade, R-value, or strength claim |
    | No path from material to income / ticket / grade / promotion / retirement / resume / metric / bill without evidence (§33 refusals) | Material data sheets support claims only when cited in a formal submittal | Structural absence of paths is enforced by schema |
    | Closed vocabulary (callouts, layers) | ASTM / CSA / EN product standards + manufacturer proprietary marks | Only house.md legend + periodic-table elements admitted |
    
    Industry standards referenced (representative, not exhaustive):  
    - Concrete: ASTM C94 / C150 / C33, ACI 211, NRMCA guidelines  
    - Wood / engineered wood: APA, ASTM D5456 (LVL), CSA O86, EN 14374  
    - Gypsum: ASTM C1396, GA-1000 / GA-801  
    - Rigid foam: ASTM C578 (XPS/EPS), ASTM C1289 (polyiso), manufacturer process specs  
    
    ### 1. Drawing Rules Remain Unchanged (house.md)
    Vertical layer order, callout codes (CONC, CMU, PT, LVL, OSB, PLY, GYP BD, XPS/EPS/POLYISO, WRB, IGU, etc.), and functional purpose statements are taken verbatim from house.md. No new symbols or re-ordering.
    
    ### 2. How Each Core Material Is Made (Industry Process) + Elemental Grounding + Drawing Implication
    
    #### 2.1 Concrete (CONC) – Footings, foundation walls, slabs
    **Industry manufacturing process**  
    1. Raw materials: Portland cement (or blended), fine aggregate (sand), coarse aggregate (gravel/crushed stone), water, optional admixtures.  
    2. Batching by weight (preferred) at a central or transit-mix plant.  
    3. Mixing (central-mixed, shrink-mixed, or transit-mixed) until homogeneous.  
    4. Delivery in agitating trucks; placement before initial set.  
    5. Hydration: cement + water → calcium-silicate-hydrate gel that binds aggregates.  
    Typical volume: 10–15 % cement, 60–75 % aggregate, 15–20 % water (+ entrained air).
    
    **Dominant elements (periodic table)**  
    Ca, Si, O, Al, Fe (cement + aggregates); H, O (water); possible minor C, S, Cl from admixtures.
    
    **Drawing implication (house.md)**  
    Solid or hatched rectangular prism / wall volume in cool gray. Optional rebar shown as thin linear Fe-dominant elements. Thickness and height taken only from evidenced layer data. Never drawn with invented strength or slump values.
    
    #### 2.2 Dimensional Lumber & Pressure-Treated (PT, DF / SPF / SYP)
    **Industry manufacturing process**  
    1. Harvest → debark → saw into rough boards.  
    2. Kiln-dry to target moisture content.  
    3. Plane / grade / stamp.  
    4. For PT: vacuum-pressure impregnation with preservative (historically CCA; now typically ACQ, CA, or micronized copper systems).
    
    **Dominant elements**  
    C, H, O (cellulose + lignin); preservative metals (Cu, etc.) for PT.
    
    **Drawing implication**  
    Rectangular cross-section members. Subtle grain texture. PT receives distinct green-tint overlay or “PT” decal. Grain direction follows structural orientation in the layer.
    
    #### 2.3 Engineered Wood – LVL, OSB, Plywood (PLY), I-joists
    **Industry manufacturing process**  
    - **LVL**: Peel logs into veneers → dry → grade → apply phenolic adhesive → lay up with grain parallel → hot-press into billets → cut to size.  
    - **OSB**: Strand logs → dry strands → blend with resin + wax → orient in layers → hot-press.  
    - **Plywood**: Peel veneers → dry → cross-laminate with adhesive → hot-press.  
    - **I-joists**: Flanges (LVL or lumber) + web (OSB/PLY) bonded with exterior adhesive.
    
    **Dominant elements**  
    C, H, O (wood); C, H, O, N (phenolic / isocyanate resins); possible minor metals from catalysts.
    
    **Drawing implication**  
    - LVL: solid rectangular with subtle parallel-veneer lines on cut ends.  
    - OSB: flat panel with oriented-strand texture.  
    - PLY: edge shows alternating veneer layers.  
    - I-joists: classic “I” profile. All use house.md callouts only.
    
    #### 2.4 Gypsum Wallboard (GYP BD / GWB)
    **Industry manufacturing process**  
    1. Crush / grind natural or synthetic gypsum (CaSO₄·2H₂O).  
    2. Calcine (heat) to hemihydrate (“stucco”).  
    3. Mix stucco + water + additives (foam, starch, glass fiber, etc.) into slurry.  
    4. Deposit slurry between continuous paper facers on a forming line.  
    5. Set (rehydration), cut, dry in multi-zone kilns, edge-seal, stack.
    
    **Dominant elements**  
    Ca, S, O, H (gypsum core); C, H, O (paper facers); possible Si, Al from additives.
    
    **Drawing implication**  
    Thin interior face layer. Clean white / light-gray surface. Greenboard variant receives pale-green tint. Thickness (½″ or ⅝″) taken only from evidence.
    
    #### 2.5 Rigid Foam Insulation (XPS / EPS / POLYISO)
    **Industry manufacturing process**  
    - **EPS**: Expand polystyrene beads with steam (pentane blowing agent) → age → mold under steam/pressure into blocks or shapes → cut.  
    - **XPS**: Melt polystyrene crystals → inject blowing agent under pressure → extrude through a die → expand into continuous closed-cell board → cool / trim.  
    - **Polyiso**: Continuously mix isocyanate (A-side) + polyol blend + blowing agent (usually pentane) → pour between facers on a laminator → expand and cure into closed-cell board.
    
    **Dominant elements**  
    C, H (polystyrene or polyisocyanurate backbone); possible Cl, F, N, O from older or specialty blowing agents / fire retardants (modern formulations minimize high-GWP gases).
    
    **Drawing implication**  
    Sharp-edged rectangular boards (rigid) or cavity-filling volumes (spray). Distinct color coding common in industry (pink/blue XPS, etc.) may be used only as a visual aid, never as a performance claim. R-value annotation appears only when the store supplies a verified number.
    
    #### 2.6 Other Frequent Materials (brief)
    - **Steel rebar / connectors**: Iron ore → blast/electric furnace → alloying → rolling / drawing. Elements: Fe + C (± Mn, Si, Cr, etc.). Drawn as thin linear metallic elements.  
    - **WRB / housewrap / vapor barriers**: Extruded polyolefin films or asphalt-saturated felts. Elements: C, H (± additives). Drawn as thin continuous membrane.  
    - **Vinyl / PVC cladding or pipe**: Polymerization of vinyl chloride monomer + additives → extrusion or molding. Elements: C, H, Cl. Drawn per cladding or pipe geometry.  
    - **Aluminum**: Bayer → Hall-Héroult → rolling / extrusion. Element: Al. Drawn as smooth metallic surfaces (gutters, cladding, window frames).
    
    ### 3. Implementation Phases (Expanded)
    
    | Phase | Deliverable | Gate / Refusal Test |
    |-------|-------------|---------------------|
    | D0–D2 | Callout registry + fixed layer order + geometry/hatch library | Unknown callout or wrong order → fog |
    | M0 | Closed 118-element registry | Any non-IUPAC symbol refused |
    | M1 | Manufacturing-process registry (linked to each callout) | Process description missing → material not emitted |
    | M2 | Elemental composition table (from process) | Composition incomplete → refused |
