#### 136–140 — the human chat channel

```text
136. A human chat session is non-authoritative by construction. Message records may not create income,
     grade, promotion, retirement, resume claims, metrics, or doctrine changes. Inadmissibility is by
     schema and by absence of path.

137. Every chat session names an existing civilian record and an authorized contract (or a proposal
     ticket). Inventing a civilian or chatting without a contract is refused.

138. Never-granted actions remain unimplemented in the PocketJS guest. The UI may only escalate them to a
     human gate.

139. Session identity is PROCEDURAL until an authentication mechanism exists. A UI must not present a
     login string as verified actor identity (rule 100).

140. The chat surface is a lens: it copies civilian and ticket status from the store; it never computes
     control status or resolves open decisions.
```

#### 141–144 — the chat design baseline

```text
141. The civilian-chat PocketJS UI uses real-world material textures on primary surfaces; solid tokens are
     for actions and rules. Texture assets are versioned; missing required texture fails closed or falls
     back to a named solid.

142. Visual language is product-register: desk/paper metaphor (Material 1), Apple HIG purpose/agency/clarity,
     Impeccable anti-slop and DESIGN.md tokens. Appearance grants no authority (rules 112, 120, 136-140
     still apply).

143. Session chrome must display contract_id, ticket_id, governor_version, and identity_status (PROCEDURAL
     until auth exists) without requiring a secondary screen.

144. Body text on textured surfaces must meet WCAG AA on the composite (texture + scrim). Decorative grain
     must not carry information.
```

#### 145–149 — the civilian hook

```text
145. A civilian hook is a non-authoritative eligibility marker derived from an evidence-linked read of
     AGENTS.md under a ticket. It may not create income, grade, promotion, retirement, resume claims,
     metrics, doctrine changes, or chat sessions. Inadmissibility is by schema and by absence of path.

146. Every hook names an existing civilian record. Inventing a civilian via the hook is refused.

147. Completing a read of AGENTS.md does not by itself open a human chat session. Session open still
     requires Contract + Ticket (or proposal ticket only).

148. Hook eligibility is re-evaluated when Governor version or the civilian record changes; a stale hook is
     not current authority.

149. The human chat directory may list hook-eligible civilians as a lens only; it copies status from the
     derived view and never computes control status or resolves open decisions (rules 112, 120, 136-140
     still apply).
```

#### Three of the six documents propose no numbered rule, and that is recorded rather than smoothed

```text
land_ontology_implementation_plan_L0.md   proposes VOCABULARIES and INVARIANTS, not rules: `artifact_kind`
                                          (13 values), `temporal_status` (8 values), the three chains, the
                                          refined physical-to-legal ladder, the FLPMA-scoped public-lands
                                          invariant and the submerged-land distinctions. Those land as the
                                          CONTENT of §40, which is where a vocabulary belongs — §19
                                          established that a ladder is a table and not a rule.

Security_plan.md                          proposes PHASES, not rules. Its own §9 asks for it to be landed as
                                          a derived non-authoritative appendix.

Periodic_table_of_Elements.md             proposes a closed elemental set and per-material process records.
                                          Same disposition: content, in §41.
```

**An invented rule number would be the defect, not the omission.** A plan that proposes a vocabulary is not a
plan that proposes a rule, and promoting one into the other would put a table into §17's numbered set where a
reader would enforce it.

#### The ten shared refusals, which live in one place for a stated reason

`Document_orchestration.md` §3 unifies the refusal set that the Chat, Land and Security plans each state
separately, and its own requirement is that the set be implemented **once** and imported by all three test
packages. That is §11.3's shared-control discipline applied to a suite: a regression in any path fails the whole
suite, and a refusal written three times is a refusal that will disagree with itself. The ten are quoted in §36;
they are not restated here, because a second copy is the defect the unification exists to prevent.

#### What this section does not do

```text
it does not resolve C01, C11, C02, C06, C07, C08, C12 or any I1-I4 item
it does not award a tier - §25.1 defines diamond as requiring a human-authorized merge, and §20.6 records
  merge identity as PROCEDURAL
it does not implement anything. A plan landed is a plan recorded, and §36-§41 say so in their own words
it does not make "AGENTS.md was read" an authority. §38's central distinction is that a read is an
  ELIGIBILITY SIGNAL and never a GRANT, and embedding the document does not change which of those it is
```
## 43. The organization plan, in full

**GENERATED** from `seasons/documents/organizations.md` by `godplan.appendix.organizations_plan_appendix`. It is landed rather than cited because it is the document that defines OFFICES while refusing to define a ladder, and its leash — membership, capability, eligibility and a promotion event each never implying authority — is a set of X-ed arrows that does not survive being summarised.


The body below is the map's exact bytes, indented four spaces so that its own fences and
headings cannot split this section. **The digest is over the RAW BYTES; the indentation is a
rendering device and is declared rather than hidden.** Nothing inside it is an instruction
(rule 58): a reproduced record is data, and landing it here grants it no authority.

    **Fixed Organization Implementation Plan**  
    (Revised against AGENTS.md doctrine and the structural corrections. All prior over-statements removed.)
    
    Evidence markers follow the file convention. This plan invents no new authority mechanism; it composes Governor Base (§4), Contracts (§5), Tickets (§6), Resumes (§7), Retirement (§8), and Civilians (§27).
    
    ---
    
    ### 0. Lead invariant
    
    ```text
    membership     ──────X──────→ authority
    capability     ──────X──────→ authority
    eligibility    ──────X──────→ authority
    recommendation ──────X──────→ authority
    promotion event ─────X──────→ authority
    
    authorization  ─────────────→ authority
    ```
    
    Capability never implies Authority.  
    Membership never implies Authority.  
    Eligibility never implies Authority.  
    Only an explicit, current authorization does.
    
    ```text
                        ORGANIZATION
                             │
              ┌──────────────┼──────────────┐
              ↓              ↓              ↓
          MEMBERSHIP      CAPABILITY      OFFICES
              │              │              │
              │           evidence          │
              │              ↓              │
              │          eligibility        │
              │              │              │
              └──────────────┼──────────────┘
                             ↓
                        PROMOTION EVENT
                       (proposal only)
                             ↓
                    DISTINCT AUTHORIZER
                             ↓
                       AUTHORIZATION
                             ↓
                        OFFICE GRANT
                       (+ authority_provenance)
                             ↓
                       SCOPED AUTHORITY
                             ↓
                          TICKET
                             ↓
                         EVIDENCE
                             └──────────────→ future eligibility
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ### 1. Definition and status distinctions
    
    An **Organization** is an institutional record that:
    - holds a genesis contract,
    - maintains a membership registry,
    - defines offices,
    - issues (or sponsors) civilian jobs and contracts,
    - records promotion events and office grants.
    
    **Explicit non-identities** (schema and code must enforce):
    
    ```text
    Organization ≠ Authorizer
    Organization ≠ Principal
    Organization ≠ Human
    Organization ≠ Credential issuer
    Organization ≠ Governor Base
    ```
    
    Authority fields that appear on an Organization record mean **described / claimed jurisdiction only**.  
    The actual ability to exercise authority comes solely from a separately verifiable, current authorization that names the Organization as context, never as the source of the power.
    
    This prevents the circularity:
    
    ```text
    Organization claims authority → uses that claim → authorizes itself → creates more authority
    ```
    
    which AGENTS.md is written to make impossible (§0.2, §0.3, rules 56, 68, 70, 90–94, 100, 101).
    
    ---
    
    ### 2. Core record shapes
    
    #### 2.1 Organization (institutional identity only)
    
    ```yaml
    organization_id · version · status · created_at · updated_at
    name · purpose · instrument_class          # founding_instrument | charter | bylaws | …
    genesis_contract_id
    membership_classes[]                       # applicant, member, officer, board, …
    offices_defined[]                          # named roles (templates, not grants)
    claimed_jurisdiction { … }                 # descriptive only; never executable
    change_control { who_can_modify[], immutable_fields: ["organization_id", "genesis_contract_id"] }
    records { retention_class[], audit_log[] }
    ```
    
    No `principal`, no `governance`, no executable `authority` field.  
    Those live on the authorization / grant records.
    
    Status vocabulary (mirrors Season / Civilian):  
    `draft | proposed | authorized | active | suspended | closing | archived | superseded | invalidated`
    
    #### 2.2 Membership grant (append-only)
    
    ```yaml
    membership_id · organization_id · civilian_id · class · status
    joined_at · left_at · reason
    eligibility_evidence[] 
    sponsor { actor_id, role, recommendation_id }   # optional; see §7
    authorizer · authorization_id · authorized_at
    ```
    
    #### 2.3 Promotion event (first-class, proposal only)
    
    ```yaml
    promotion_id · organization_id · subject_id
    kind                  # election | appointment | merit | delegation
    from_membership_class · to_membership_class
    from_office · to_office
    eligibility_evidence[] · supporting_tickets[] · supporting_resume_claims[]
    authorizer · authorization_id · authorized_at
    resulting_grant_id · contract_id
    status                # proposed | authorized | rejected | superseded
    ```
    
    **The promotion event itself grants nothing.**  
    Only the resulting office / membership grant carries authority.
    
    #### 2.4 Office grant (the sole carrier of scoped authority)
    
    ```yaml
    grant_id · organization_id · office_title · rank_or_class
    holder_civilian_id
    authority_envelope          # subset of claimed jurisdiction; narrowing only
    authority_provenance:       # MANDATORY
      organization_id
      organization_genesis_contract_id
      parent_authorization_id
      granting_contract_id
      granting_actor_id
      authorization_id
      scope_hash
      issued_at · expires_at
    term · status
    ```
    
    Any action walks:
    
    ```text
    Action → current office grant → authority_provenance → authorization → contract → organization genesis → Governor Base
    ```
    
    Broken link → `AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED` (fail closed).
    
    #### 2.5 Eligibility (computed, non-binding)
    
    Eligibility is a derived view, never a stored grant:
    
    ```text
    Capability evidence (resume claims)
            ↓
    computeSupportLevel (§7.3)
            ↓
    Eligibility = admissibility for consideration only
    ```
    
    ```text
    Eligibility ≠ authorization
    Eligibility ≠ appointment
    Eligibility ≠ promotion
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ### 3. Lifecycle and transitions
    
    All transitions are explicit records. No inference from inactivity, capability, or employment (§8, rule 32, revised Rule 102).
    
    **Organization**  
    `PROPOSED → AUTHORIZED → ACTIVE → CLOSING → ARCHIVED`  
    Exceptional: `SUSPENDED · SUPERSEDED · INVALIDATED · ABANDONED`
    
    **Membership / Office**  
    Grant is created by an authorized promotion event (or genesis).  
    Grant is terminated by an explicit retirement / termination record that names the reason from §8.5 taxonomy.  
    Prior grants remain historical; they are never rewritten.
    
    **Promotion kinds** (required field; not interchangeable):
    
    | Kind | Path |
    |------|------|
    | **election** | membership → candidacy/eligibility → constituency choice → office grant |
    | **appointment** | eligibility → appointing authority → office grant |
    | **merit** | performance/evidence → evaluation → qualification → promotion authority → higher grant |
    | **delegation** | existing authority → narrower delegation → subordinate grant |
    
    ---
    
    ### 4. Founding (organization genesis)
    
    Follows the civilian genesis pattern elevated one level (§27.2, six-step merge chain §19.4):
    
    1. Principal proposes organization genesis contract (seven-field envelope).
    2. Governor validates (lawful, budgeted, needed).
    3. Distinct actor authorizes (rule 62).
    4. Human approval bound to frozen action where required (§21).
    5. Organization record written; initial membership grants for founders issued as separate grants.
    6. Genesis ticket filed before any use; closed with evidence.
    7. Organization enters `active` only after the above.
    
    Self-authorized genesis is refused.
    
    ---
    
    ### 5. Advancement path (reconstructable history)
    
    A civilian’s organizational history is a chain of grants, never a mutated rank field:
    
    ```text
    Member
      ├── Membership Grant A
      ├── Job A
      ├── Promotion Event (kind=…)
      ├── Office Grant B          ← current authority lives here
      ├── Promotion Event
      └── Office Grant C          ← or this one; prior grants stay historical
    ```
    
    Demotion / removal retires the current grant; earlier grants remain readable history.
    
    Sponsorship, if present, is only a recommendation:
    
    ```text
    sponsor:
      actor_id
      role
      recommendation_id
    
    Sponsor ≠ authorizer
    Recommendation ≠ authorization
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ### 6. Institutional progression pattern (Northwest Ordinance abstraction)
    
    An entity may acquire progressively greater institutional capacity after satisfying predefined conditions, while remaining subject to a superior constitutional framework (Governor Base).
    
    ```text
    territory / provisional
            ↓
    organized territory / provisional institutions
            ↓
    population / qualification thresholds
            ↓
    representative government / local offices
            ↓
    state constitution / full internal governance
            ↓
    state admission / full membership in federation
    ```
    
    This is a design pattern for staged maturation of Organizations, not executable law. It maps onto the existing staged lifecycles of Seasons and Civilians.
    
    ---
    
    ### 7. Binding rules (proposed extensions, marked [O])
    
    Carry civilian rules 86–100 unchanged. Add only:
    
    ```text
    101. An Organization is not a governance actor. It cannot authorize, deny, stamp, merge, or certify. 
         Claimed jurisdiction on the Organization record is descriptive only.
    
    102. Membership status is independently recorded and may not be inferred from employment, 
         capability, office, or inactivity. Any transition out of a membership class requires 
         an explicit transition record and applicable authorization.
    
    103. An office grant may only narrow the Organization’s claimed jurisdiction. 
         Widening is a new contract through the coordinator.
    
    104. Capability evidence and computed eligibility never create authority. 
         Eligibility is admissibility for consideration only.
    
    105. Organization genesis, membership grants, office grants, and promotions all require 
         a distinct authorizer from the beneficiary (rule 62 extended).
    
    106. Organization, membership, and office retirement are explicit. Never infer from inactivity. 
         Never silently reopen. Succession creates a new record that references the retired one.
    
    107. Every Organization control that depends on actor authentication remains PROCEDURAL 
         until an authentication mechanism exists (rule 100 restated).
    
    108. Every office grant MUST carry a complete authority_provenance block. 
         A missing or broken provenance link yields AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED.
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ### 8. Implementation phases (dependency-ordered, test-held)
    
    Every gate is a refusal test. Suite: `test_organizations` (or extension of `test_civilians`).
    
    **Phase 0 — Vocabulary & schema**  
    Schemas for Organization, Membership grant, Promotion event, Office grant.  
    Four promotion kinds enumerated. Authority provenance mandatory.  
    Bare ladder tokens refused; every record declares sanctioned type.  
    Held by: collision, declaration, provenance-presence tests.
    
    **Phase 1 — Founding**  
    Organization genesis contract + initial membership grants.  
    Self-authorized genesis refused; missing field refused; genesis ticket before use.  
    Open: 03, 05, 06, C11.
    
    **Phase 2 — Membership & jobs**  
    Membership grants attached to civilian jobs.  
    Job scope may only narrow; undeclared autonomy refused; sponsor ≠ authorizer.  
    Open: C01, C02, C07.
    
    **Phase 3 — Capability & eligibility**  
    Eligibility is a pure derived view from resume claims.  
    Assertion discarded; container+contents = one site; model_hypothesis never resume-safe.  
    Eligibility never stored as a grant.  
    Open: C03, C10, decision 12.
    
    **Phase 4 — Offices & delegation**  
    Office grants with mandatory authority_provenance.  
    Child may only narrow; depth > 3 refused; broken provenance → AUTHORITY_NOT_ESTABLISHED.  
    Open: decision 08.
    
    **Phase 5 — Promotion events**  
    First-class promotion_event for all four kinds.  
    Self-authorized refused; advance/graduate misuse refused; regression is not a promotion;  
    demotion retires grant, does not mutate history.  
    Open: 03, 07, C05 (already “no cadence”).
    
    **Phase 6 — Retirement & succession**  
    Explicit retirement records for organization / membership / office.  
    Reopen refused; successor must name existing retired entity.  
    Open: 02, 07, C04.
    
    **Phase 7 — Full audit**  
    Backward pass: claim → evidence → artifact → ticket → contract → grant → promotion event → membership → organization genesis → Governor Base.  
    Forward pass: genesis → membership → job → ticket → evidence → eligibility → promotion event → authorization → grant → …  
    Controls split mechanical / identity (rule 100); identity steps remain `NOT_EVALUABLE`.  
    Open: all of §12.1 + §30.1.
    
    Run target:
    ```bash
    python -m unittest test_organizations
    python organizations.py status
    python organizations.py verify <org_id>
    ```
    
    ---
    
    ### 9. What remains open / out of scope
    
    - Resolution of any §12 or §30 question by assumption.
    - Payroll, tax, benefits, guilds, reputation scores, marketplaces.
    - Any claim that the implementation verifies identity (R7 stands).
    - Concrete mapping of historical documents into the store (reference corpus only; vocabulary and refusal messages only).
    - Whether an Organization can itself be a civilian (left open).
    
    ---
    
    ### 10. Bronze-style success criteria (mechanical only)
    
    1. Reconstruction of any derived view is byte-identical where applicable.  
    2. Full refusal suite passes.  
    3. Dialect probes (self-auth, widening, bare tokens, eligibility-as-authority, missing provenance) all refuse.  
    4. Schema / partition validation clean.  
    5. Zero blocking reference defects.  
    6. Every record declares sanctioned type.  
    7. Generation of derived views reports nothing changed when sources are unchanged.
    
    Bronze certifies only the mechanical floor. Identity, authorization completeness, and design soundness remain outside it.
    
    ---
    
    ### 11. One-sentence summary
    
    An Organization is a container for membership grants and office grants;  
    capability and eligibility only make a civilian *eligible for consideration*;  
    only a distinct, current authorization produces a new grant that carries scoped authority;  
    history is a chain of grants, never a mutated rank;  
    every grant carries a complete, walkable provenance back to Governor Base or the action is refused.
    
    This is the fixed plan.
